docs.text:
一、開課目的：
This course integrates advanced technical knowledge of CMOS process technology
with essential leadership and innovation skills required for future leaders in
the semiconductor industry. Students will explore the frontiers of CMOS scaling,
3D integration, EUV lithography, and device architecture, while also developing
competencies in strategic thinking, project management, and team leadership
within high-tech R&D environments.

二、課程對象:
Graduate students in Electrical Engineering, Materials Science, Applied Physics,
or related disciplines; Students intend to pursue career in semiconductor
industry, especially in the area of process technology development and
manufacturing.

三、課程目標：
By the end of the course, students will be able to:
1.Explain key challenges and innovations in advanced CMOS technology nodes
2.Analyze the integration of device, process, and design co-optimization
strategies.
3.Apply principles of innovation leadership, communication, and decision-making
in a technical team context.
4.Evaluate technology roadmaps and R&D strategies from leading semiconductor
companies.
5.Present technical and strategic proposals effectively to diverse audiences.

四、課程內容大綱：
1. Introduction: Technology Leadership in Semiconductor Innovation
2. Advanced CMOS Scaling: Moore’s Law, More-than-Moore / Leadership in
Technology Transitions
3. FinFETs to GAA/Nanosheet Transistors/Strategic Visioning
4. Process Integration at Nanoscale: EUV, Patterning, and Material Challenges
/ Cross-functional Teamwork
5. 3D Integration, Heterogeneous Integration, Advanced Packaging / Decision-
making under Uncertainty
6. Design-Technology Co-Optimization (DTCO) and System-Technology Co-
Optimization (STCO)/ Systems Thinking for Leaders
7. Reliability, Yield, and Manufacturability in Advanced Nodes/ Risk Management
in R&D
8. Sustainability and Energy Efficiency in Semiconductor Manufacturing/ Ethics
and Responsibility
9. Midterm Paper and Case Study Presentation / Team Collaboration &
Communication
10. Technology Roadmapping and Innovation Strategy/ Innovation Management
11. AI and Data-Driven Approaches in Process Control / Leading Digital
Transformation
12. IP, Trade Secrets, and Global Competition/ IP Strategy & National Interests
13. Talent and Organization in High-Tech R&D / Building and Leading R&D Teams
14. From Lab to Fab to Product: The Commercialization Pathway / Entrepreneurial
Leadership
15. Case Studies: TSMC, Intel, Samsung, and Startups /Learning from Real-World
Leaders
16. Final Team Project Presentation/ Influencing and Presenting Ideas

五、擬用教科書，參考書或教材來源：

- FinFETs and Other Multi-Gate Transistors, edited by J.-P. Colinge
- Semiconductor Manufacturing Handbook – Hwaiyu Geng

- Selected papers and articles

docs.text:
1. Course Description
The objective of this course is to provide students an overview of VLSI designs,
particularly about how we manage to integrate billions of transistors to perform
complex functions. This course focuses on three major topics: logic design,
electronic design automation, and computer architecture. Students will learn the
layered abstraction of design technology from the ground up, including
combinational/sequential circuits, gate-level design, physical layout, micro-
architecture, and processor cores.

2. Teaching method
In-class lectures.

3. Syllabus
This course is partitioned into three parts for a sixteen-week semester, and each
part will have its own exam for evaluation.

Part 1. Logic design and hardware description language (HDL)
CMOS logic gates, combinational logic, CMOS latches and flip-flops, sequential
blocks, and memory.

Part 2. Electronic design automation (EDA)
Cell-based design, timing and power analysis, clock tree and power grid, floorplan
and routing.

Part 3. Computer architecture
RISC-V instruction set architecture (ISA), single-cycle processor, pipelined
processor, and memory hierarchy.

4. Evaluation (TBD)
Part-1 Exam (33%)
Part-2 Exam (33%)
Part-3 Exam (34%)

5. Website
eeclass.nthu.edu.tw

6. Reference book (not required)
CMOS VLSI Design: A Circuits and Systems Perspective, 4th Edition, Neil Weste,
David Harris, Addison Wesley, 2010
Digital Design and Computer Architecture, RISC-V Edition, Sarah Harris, David
Harris, Morgan Kaufmann, July 2021

7. Usage of generative AI tools
If report writing is assigned, generative AI tools are conditionally allowed if
the student clearly states how the texts are generated.

docs.name: 半導體化學品材料與製程應用
docs.nameEn: Chemical Material and Process Application in Semiconductor
docs.text:
1.課程說明

最基本的半導體廠內所用化學品介紹起並敘述工廠內如何做好污染防治，讓良率提高，包括有氣體還
有化學液體和管路如何做好，在無塵室裡如何做到class等級由10000變1000再變成100，如何做到
迷你環境的class 1。

接下來就介紹各模組所用的化學品及其相關的製程如晶圓潔淨(wafer clean)製程: 晶圓清潔之目
的係移除所有表面污染物：微粒、有機物、金屬與原生氧化物。每一個製造步驟，皆可能污染晶圓表
面之元件。因此完成一整個 ULSI 製造步驟，估計每個晶圓至少需經過濕式清潔100次以上，課程內
容包括有RCA清潔:SC-1,SC-2,Piranha 混合溶液的介紹與使用方法，再配合一些新的清洗設備，
比如超音波/刷洗/噴灑/熱DI等。

蝕刻(etch)製程部分: 半導體製程包括兩種基本形式的蝕刻製程，乾蝕刻與濕蝕刻乾蝕刻，乾蝕刻
根據所需移除材料的類型而分類，三種主要的蝕刻材料分類包括有金屬蝕刻、介電質蝕刻及矽蝕刻，
除因基材不同而使用適當氣體種類外，亦詳細講解蝕刻工程師在發展配方時所要檢查的十大項目:
蝕刻速率、蝕刻輪廓(profile) 、蝕刻偏差(etch bias) 、選擇性、均一性(uniformity) 、殘
留物、聚合物形成、電漿引起的破壞、微粒污染及缺陷、蝕刻速率。

至於濕蝕刻方面，主要是講解BOE(Buffer Oxide Etch), 在半導體如STI製程上的應用與控制。再
介紹化學機械平坦(CMP)製程上有關的化學反應、研磨墊高分子材料,pattern loading等。還有針
對氧化物、鎢金屬、銅金屬所使用的研漿(slurry)與其製程作介紹。

至於在黃光(Litho)製程方面，從g/i-line光反應一直講到248光阻和193光阻，再講解 EUV光阻在七
奈米以下的黃光製程應用。另一方面，再從有機光阻再介紹到金屬氧化物類的無機光阻。光阻配方中有
acid diffusion和quencher角色對光阻性能的影響有詳細的講解，至於BARC的化學組成和作用亦屬
於黃光製程的重點，另外還有特殊的降低LER, 增加選擇比等等的處理劑，最後有時間再介紹先進製程
上的雙層/三層黃光製程。

2.指定用書 (Text Books): none

3.參考書籍 (References): none

4.教學方式 (Teaching Methods): 在課堂上直接授課, 平時請學生自願上台表達或分組討論來增
加平時分數。

5.教學進度 (Course Schedule):

A.半導體廠內化學品種類及其應用與廠內污染控制(5 weeks)

●1st week: 化學材料安全及廠內常用的氣體液體化學製程
●2nd week: 半導體廠內污染控制及廠務設備介紹
●3rd week(小考): 無塵室的規劃設置與潔淨度(如class 100)的控制
●4th week: 晶圓潔淨(wafer clean)所用的化學品
●5th week(小考): 晶圓潔淨的化學製程和小考或分組討論

B.半導體廠內乾式/濕式蝕刻(dry/wet etch)所用的化學品及其相關的製程(3 weeks)
●6th week: 十大蝕刻參數的介紹與製程配方建立的相關性
●7th week: 乾蝕刻的應用及相關底層蝕刻的化學
●8th week(小考): 濕蝕刻的應用及相關的化學和小考或分組討論

C.半導體廠內化學機械平坦(CMP)所用的化學品及其相關的製程(2 weeks)
●9th week: 傳統平坦化和化學機械平坦所用的化學品及製程
●10th week(小考): CMP 研漿(slurry)與底層基材的關係，研磨墊片(PVA)介紹和小考或分組討
論

D.半導體廠內黃光(Litho) 所用的化學品及其相關的製程(6 weeks)
●11th week: i-line/KrF光阻光化學/BARC化學介紹
●12th week: 製程設備中常見的問題與解決如substrate poison, airborne contamination,
standing curve etc.
●13th week(小考): track中光阻每一製程步驟的目地介紹和小考或分組討論
●14th week: ArF光阻光化學和分子設計
●15th week:immersion 光阻設計及所遇到問題和解決方法
●16th week(小考): CAR type 和無機金屬EUV光阻的介紹和小考或分組討論

6.成績考核 (Evaluation):
A.小考或分組討論分享(50%)
B.出席, 分組或個人的平時或上課小作業(50%)

7.AI使用規則: 本課程無涉及AI使用 Not applicable

docs.name: 論文研究
docs.text:
一、課程說明：在指導教授之指導下，就各別選定之題目進行有系統研究，期獲得在該領域知識與技術
上之成果。

二、教學方式：學生在教授研究室學習各種研究技巧，解決研究上遭遇之問題。

四、成績考核：由論文素質，研究態度決定。

docs.name: 微影光罩
docs.text:
本課程為教導學生半導體之光罩技術，先進之光罩技術為半導體技術中之重要一環，舉凡三奈米或二奈
米世代，便含有一百片以上之先進光罩，光罩品質之精良與否或好壞會直接影響產品之良率，並且光罩
中之CD或overlay控制更直接影響製程之精良與否。並課程會以深入淺出之講授，教導學生了解光罩技
術，並從而具有光罩研究之基本能力。

列印講義

參考書籍 Photomask Fabrication Technology, B.G.Eynon Jr., B. Wu

教學方式 課堂講授

教學進度

1 Introduction - Material, Patterns, mask structure,Fabrication flow, products,
issues
2 Data preparation - MDP flow, Pattern fracturing
3 Data preparation - Job DEKS, MDP process time
4 Pattern Generation - Mask writing system, Pattern quality control
5 Pattern Generation - Data system
6 Pattern Transfer - Process, Plasma etching fundamentals
7 Pattern Transfer - Cr etching, MoSi etching
8 期中考
9 Metrology - Introduction, CD metrology, AFM, Overlay
10 Back end process - Introduction, inspection
11 Back end process - Repair
12 Back end process - Clean
13 Resolution Enhancement Technology - Fourier Optics, scalar imaging
14 Resolution Enhancement Technoloyg - OPC, PSM, Optimization
15 Next Generation Mask - EUV mask, pellicle, inspection
16 期末考

成績考核 期中考試(40%), 作業(20%), 期末考試(40%)

以科技管理學院「企業導師領航計畫」為主軸，藉由本課程推動「企業導師領航計畫」，讓本院學⽣提早認知 職涯發展，此課程中由本院及本校傑出企業家校友擔任導師，提供經驗交流及傳承，引領本院⼤⼆以上學⽣ 了解產業趨勢及就業市場，培養未來競爭⼒。具體⽽⾔，本課程的導師來⾃⾼科技、⾦融、證券、投資、⽣ 物科技、製造、⽂創、法律各領域，藉由導師們豐富實務經歷、產業專業、職場⽣存法則，讓參與課程的同 課程內容依照『科管院企業導師領航計畫』進⾏，本計畫邀請多位傑出熱⼼校友擔任企業導師，⽬前參與本 計畫的導師共有 17 位，每位導師⾄多帶領 3 位學⽣，為期⼀學年執⾏職涯發展探討。 課程內容及活動⽅式將根據導師專⾧領域與學⽣需求彈性調整，課程內容可能涵蓋導師授課、企業參訪或邀 請專家演講，詳細內容視各位導師⽽訂，本課程的⽬的為讓修課學⽣儘早了解職涯發展的重要性。 ● 指定⽤書(Text Books) 由企業導師指定。 ● 參考書籍(References) 由企業導師推薦。 ● 教學⽅式(Teaching Method) 1. 修課對象: 本課程限定科管院⼤⼆以上學⽣選課修讀，包含其他學院雙主修學⽣(不包含輔系、雙專⾧)。 2. 修課期間: 本課程為⼀學年課程，分為上下學期各 0.5 微學分，⼀學年計⼀學分。 3. 課程要求: 1.) 【企業導師配對機制】 I. 須參加說明會，始有機會參與導師配對。 II. 說明會時間地點：開學第⼀週 9/2 週⼆中午 12:00~13:00 於台積館⼀樓孫運璿演講廳舉辦 III. 說明會報名網址：https://forms.gle/dND3xekMRQ5JEtYX7 IV. 因衝堂無法參加說明會，仍需報名；說明會當天 23:59 前補看課程說明影⽚並回答測驗。課程說明 影⽚連結於會後提供。 V. 須繳交資料，於 9/8 上午 8:00 前⾄連結完成：https://forms.gle/USL51uXjxJvzZ4Ss5 VI. 執委會審查繳交資料，根據導師志願序與其他綜合表現，將學⽣與企業導師分組配對。 VII. 助教於 9/12 發信通知配對結果，未配對成功者無法選修本課程。 VIII. 配對成功者，須在 9/14 完成課程加選程序。 2.) 【必出席之團體活動】 I. 導師⽣相⾒歡：9 ⽉ 17 ⽇ 18:00~21:00。 II. 企業參訪：暫定參訪某科技公司，開學第⼀週公布⽇期與時間。 III. 企業參訪結束後三天內完成個⼈⼼得報告，⼀⼈⼀篇 300 字內。 IV. 以上活動，全體學⽣必須參加，缺席者學分不通過。 V. 只接受衝堂請假，且必須補看指定影⽚撰寫⼼得報告。 3.) 【必出席之⼩組活動】 I. 每學期⾄少兩次⼩組活動，由各組導師⽣共同討論訂定；例如：職涯座談、演講、展覽、履歷⾯ 試加強、參與導師公司會議或計畫、⼀⽇實習、執⾏專案等。 II. ⼩組活動結束後三天內完成⼩組活動紀錄，⼀組⼀篇 300 字內附團體照⼀張（可由⼀⼈代表撰寫 或所有組員共筆，但字數限制不變）。 ● 成績考核(Evaluation) 企業導師根據學⽣出席狀況及表現，核給通過或不通過。授課教師有最終成績審核權利。宜注意如學⽣未滿 ⾜上述每學期兩次全體活動(衝堂者有補課機制)、⼩組活動兩次之要求，本課程將不予通過。 ●『科管院企業導師領航計畫』導師名單: https://career-ctm.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/406-1380-293944,r4772.php?Lang=zh-tw ●『科管院企業導師領航計畫』宣傳影⽚: https://youtu.be/5fN_rW1Lo3I

docs.name: 癌症十六問
docs.nameEn: Sixteen Questions to Ask about Cancer
docs.text:
● 課程說明(Course Description)

癌症是現代社會裡最致命的疾病，大部分的人碰到癌症時，總是聞之色變，將之視為絕症。但並不
是每
種癌症都這麼可怕，也有許多診斷與治療的方法，因此本課程希望能夠讓學生具備有更多與癌症相
關的
正確知識，同時，也可增進跨領域的交流，讓更多不同專長的學生投入癌症研究的相關新藥、診斷
技
術、與醫材的開發。

● 指定用書(Text Books)

本課程為自編講義

● 參考書籍(References)

1. 癌症大祕密：醫師很想說、你很想問的65個問題 出版社：如何
2. 細胞反叛 出版社：天下文化

● 教學方式(Teaching Method)

教學方式主要以課堂理論講述與影片分享為主，前半學期會與學生介紹癌症發生的原因與目前常見
的檢
測及治療方法。在前二節課理論介紹完後會請每位學生提出想問的問題，再由學生投票決定18個希
望被
回答的問題。問題會分配在第9-16週由同學分組回答，每週回答二題，同學報告之後再由老師補充
相關
資料。希望能藉由這種互動的方式，瞭解學生想知道的問題是什麼，同時也會開放課堂討論，達到
教學
相長的目的。

● 教學進度(Syllabus)

1. Week 1第一問：癌細胞是怎麼跑進身體裡的？
2. Week 2第二問：癌症的轉移是怎麼發生的？
3. Week 3第三問：健康檢查真的可以預防癌症嗎？
4. Week 4第四問：什麼是化療？什麼是放射線療法?
5. Week 5第五問：什麼是免疫療法？什麼是標耙治療？
6. Week 6第六問：什麼是精準醫療？
7. Week 7第七問：有可能靠改變飲食或腸道菌治療癌症嗎？
8. Week 8第八問：期中考
9. Week 9-16 第九到十六問：第三周時請每個同學提出想問的問題一題，並開投票決定要回
答那些問題，由同學分組每週回答四題，並開放大家討論。

● 成績考核(Evaluation)

1. 出席 10%
2. 課堂討論與分組回饋單 20%
3. 期中考試 35%
4. 口頭報告 35%

● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website)

eeclass數位學習平台

本校公布之「大學教育場域AI協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採取有條件開放，以下說明
如何使用生成式AI於課程產出

學生須於課堂作業或報告中的「標題頁註腳」或「引用文獻後」簡要說明如何使用生成式AI進行議
題發想、文句潤飾或結構參考等使用方式。若經查核使用卻無在作業或報告中標明，教師、學校或
相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。本門課授課教材或學習資料若有引用自生

docs.name: 醫療與社會：導論
docs.text:
一、課程說明
對於醫科系的學生來說，瞭解「醫療與社會」的關係對於進入生醫領域工作是一種關鍵的知識裝
備。然而，要能掌握這兩者之間的關連，一則需要從社會學的觀點來認識它們之間的基本關係，二
則需要理解兩者一起發展的幾種新興趨勢，三則需要瞭解兩者之間的張力（例如：共生或制衡）。本
課程正是針對上述三個目標，分為三個模組：
1. 從社會學的觀點來認識「醫療與社會」，以「社會學的想像力」來理解社會的醫療化、醫
療的專業化，對於健康不平等之影響（第2至5週）。
2. 對比台灣在地的關鍵案例與歐美新興趨勢，作為討論近幾十年「醫療與社會」關係的重要
議題的基礎（第6至10週）。
3. 透過「醫療與社會」之間的張力，來認識其中的制衡或共存關係，並依此理解其中涉及哪
些重要社會制度（第11至14週）。

二、指定用書
本課程無指定教科書，但各週均有指定閱讀。各週指定閱讀均出自以下書目：
1. Mills, C. Wright，1995，《社會學的想像》，台北：巨流，頁31-55。
2. Giddens, Anthony，1995，《批判的社會學導論》，台北：唐山，頁1-22。
3. Bauman, Z.，2000，〈前言〉，《社會學動動腦》，台北：群學，頁1-22。
4. Conrad, Peter. 許甘霖等譯，2015，《社會的醫療化：論人類境況如何轉為可治之
症》，台北：群學。
5. 成令方編，2008，《醫療與社會共舞》，台北：群學。
6. 工作傷害受害人協會，2013，《拒絕被遺忘的聲音》，台北：行人。
7. 科技、醫療與社會（STM），2011，第12期，RCA專題
8. 梁志鳴，2019，〈論跨領域法律解釋是用之原則與挑戰：以美國在地慣習與全國水準之辯
證及我國醫療常規與醫療水準之論戰為例〉，《中研院法學期刊》，22。
9. 吳志政，2008，以疫學手法作為民事因果關係認定之檢討，東吳法律學報，20卷1期，頁
205 – 236。
10. 陳重仁，2012，〈《別讓我走》與生命政治的美麗新世界〉，《中外文學》，41(2):
15-54。
11. 王景智，2007，〈何處是兒家？：《別讓我走》中「家」的變奏與衍異〉，《中外文
學》，36(2): 221-246。
12. Gosta Esping-Andersen (古允文譯)，1999，〈導言〉、〈第二章：社會政策的去商品
化〉，《福利資本主義的三個世界》，台北：巨流
13. Lee, Sang-Yi et al. 2008. The National Health Insurance system as one
type of new typology: The case of South Korea and Taiwan. Health Policy, 85, 1,
105 – 113.
14. ISA論壇，2018，〈ISA論壇：照顧的全球危機〉，Global Dialogue 8.2: 20-40.
15. Hochschild, Arlie Russell. 2001.“Global Care Chains and Emotional
Surplus Value.” Pp. 130-146 in On the Edge: Globalization and the New
Millennium, edited by T. Giddens and W. Hutton. London: Sage Publishers.
16. 藍佩嘉，2008，《跨國灰姑娘：家務移工與台灣新富雇主》，行人文化。導論、結論。頁
17-52、315-336。
17. 劉香蘭、古允文，2015，〈台灣照顧分工的重組：兩個女性世代生命歷程的比較〉，《女
學學誌：婦女與性別研究》，36期，頁49-104。
18. 林國明，1997，國家與醫療專業權力：臺灣醫療保險體系費用支付制度的社會學分析，臺
灣社會學研究 1: 77-136.
19. Sismondo, Sergio. 王業翰等譯，2022，《醫藥幽靈：大藥廠如何干預醫療知識的生
產、傳播與消費》，新竹：國立陽明交通大學出版社。

三、參考書籍
另外，同學在準備期中、期末報告時，亦歡迎參照下面參考書目：
1. Waddington, Keir著；李尚仁譯. 2014. 《歐洲醫療五百年：醫學與分化（卷二）》。
2. 楊倍昌，2011，《資本主義與當代醫療》，台北：群學。
3. 賴宗成、陳琮淵，2015，《藥向前行：台灣藥品行銷發展》，台北：巨流。
4. Greene, Jeremy 林士堯譯，2018，《便宜沒好藥？一段學名藥和當代醫療的糾葛》，台
北：左岸。
5. 經典雜誌編著，2006，《臺灣醫療四百年》。台北：綠色陣線協會。
6. Griffin, G. (2009) ‘Science and the Cultural Imaginary: The Case of
Kazuo Ishiguro’s Never Let Me Go’, Textual Practice, 23: 645–63.
7. Whitehead, A. (2011) ‘Writing with Care: Kazuo Ishiguro’s Never Let Me
Go’, Contemporary Literature, 52: 54–83.
8. 成令方、林鶴玲、吳嘉苓譯，2001，《見樹又見林：社會學作為一種生活、實踐與允諾》
（Forest and the Trees: Sociology as Life, Practice and Practice，Allan Johnson
著），台北：群學出版。
9. Porter, Roy（王道還譯），2005，《醫學簡史》。台北：商周。
10. 張苙雲，2008，《醫療與社會》。台北：巨流。
11. 葉明叡、劉曦宸編，2023，《以健康之名？10道公衛政策倫理難題，培養公民思辨力》，
台北：聯經。
12. 科技、醫療與社會（STM），2015，第20期，議題與討論。
13. ＊林文源與「記疫」團隊，2022，《記疫：臺灣人文社會的疫情視野與行動備忘錄》，台
北：大塊文化出版。
14. ＊國科會人文處，「醫病．社會．人文研究」專題電子書59，《人文與社會科學簡訊》。
https://web.nstc.gov.tw/hssnq/ebook59/mobile/index.html

四、教學方式
本課程各週皆有指定閱讀，同學需先行閱讀並且以小組為單位進行導讀，老師則會講解並引導討
論。此外，本課程也有安排其他形式的授課（指，紀錄片討論、邀請演講、醫學人文劇），同學則需
在課後繳交反思心得。最後，本課程要求學生以小組為單位，完成一份關於「醫療與社會」之報
告，安排期中提案與期末呈現。

五、教學進度

週 課程內容 指定閱讀
1 課程簡介：內容進度與評分標準
2 社會學的想像力（Mills; Giddens; Bauman）
3 社會的醫療化（社會的醫療化，第1、6、7章）
4 醫療的專業化（醫療與社會共舞，第2篇）
5 健康不平等（醫療與社會共舞，第6篇）
6 紀錄片：《奇蹟背後》(2002) 拒絕被遺忘的聲音
7 RCA案例討論（STM，2011，12專刊）
8 期中各組報告（初次）提案：請先閱讀其他組的提案說明書
9 邀請演講：科技X健康X性別（講者提供指定閱讀）
10 醫學人文劇：石黑一雄《別讓我走》(2010)（陳重仁，2012；王景智，2007）
11 制衡I：不同因果觀的交錯—醫療訴訟（梁志明，2019；吳志正，2008）
12 制衡II：全民健保是社會福利嗎？（Lee, SY 2008；林國明，1997）
13 共存I：醫療上空的幽靈—製藥業（醫藥幽靈，導讀/譯序、第1章）
14 共存II：照護前提—文化脈絡中的照顧（藍佩嘉，2008；劉香蘭,古允文，2015）
15 期末分組報告（一） （請先閱讀其他組的期末書面報告，並擔任評論）
16 期末分組報告（二） （請先閱讀其他組的期末書面報告，並擔任評論）

六、成績考核
課程參與20%：出席率，10%（隨機點名三次）。組內互評，10%。
文本導讀20%：以小組為單位，針對3-5、11-14週擇一進行15-20分鐘導讀。
個人心得20%：第7、9、10週內容擇二撰寫，各10%
小組報告40%：期中提案20%、期末報告20%

七、可連結之網頁位址(相關網頁)
將放置於本校數位學習平台

八、生成式人工智慧倫理聲明： 「有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式AI於作業或報告」
基於透明與負責任的原則，本課程鼓勵學生利用AI進行協作或互學，以提升本門課產出品質。根據
本校公布之佈的「大學教育場域AI協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採取有條件開放，請註
明如何使用生成式AI於作業或報告，說明如下：
1.學生可於課堂作業或報告中的「標題頁註腳」或「引用文獻後」簡要說明如何使用生成式AI
進行議題發想、文句潤飾或結構參考等使用方式。然而，在本課程的「個人心得」、「小組報告」
中，學生不得使用生成式AI工具撰寫作業。若經查核使用卻無在作業或報告中標明，教師、學校或
相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。
2.修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。

docs.name: 癌症生物學導論
docs.text:
課程簡述

這門課將深入探討癌症的生物學與遺傳學，從單一細胞到複雜系統，完整追蹤癌症的發展歷程。這門課會從癌症的基礎講到最新的治療方法，讓學生對癌症有更全面的了解。

課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」
Tumorigenesis, Oncogenes, Tumor Suppressor Genes, metastasis, Cancer Therapy.
腫瘤生成、致癌基因、抑癌基因、轉移、癌症治療。

課程大綱
● 課程說明(Course Description)
這門課會深入探討癌症的生物學和遺傳學，從細胞層面到複雜的系統，完整追蹤癌症的發展過程。課程重點包含：
R26; 細胞和個體生物學、遺傳學基礎
R26; 癌症的本質
R26; 細胞癌基因的影響
R26; 生長因子、受體和訊號傳導路徑
R26; 腫瘤抑制基因
R26; 細胞凋亡、細胞永生化和腫瘤發生
R26; 多步驟腫瘤發生
R26; 基因體完整性
R26; 異型細胞互動
R26; 血管新生
R26; 侵襲和轉移
R26; 腫瘤免疫學、免疫治療
R26; 癌症的合理治療策略
這門課會從癌症的基礎講到最新的治療方法，讓學生對癌症，以及現代治療方法有更全面的了解。

● 指定用書(Text Books)

docs.text:
Brief Course Description:
This is a ground basis lecture for providing basic knowledge regarding biochemical
and biophysical activities of a living cell.
Learning goal:
- Learn about different cellular structures and determinants of cellular
morphology
- Describe how cells generate energy and communicate with each other
- Recognize modern technologies used for cell biology
- Understand the mechanisms behind clinically relevant or disease-associated
mutations

Keywords:
Membrane Structure; Cell Signaling; Cell Communities; DNA and Chromosomes; Cell
Division Cycle; Cytoskeleton

================================
Detailed Course Syllabus
================================
Course Description:
Cell Biology is a required course for students who major in Medical Science.
This course will be taught in English.

Text Books:
Essential Cell Biology, Fifth Edition. Alberts, Hopkin, Johnson, Morgan, Raff,
Roberts, and Walter. Garland Science

References:
Cell Biology, Seventh Edition. Gerald and Karp. Wiley

Lecture

11 Membrane Structure; Ch 12 Transport Across Cell Membrane; Ch 15 Intracellular
Compartments and Transport; Ch 16 Cell Signaling; Ch 20-1 Cell Communities:
Cancer.

and Chloroplasts; Ch 5 DNA and Chromosomes Ch 6 DNA Replication, Repair, and
Recombination; Ch 7 From DNA to Protein: How Cells Read the Genome; Ch 9 How Genes
and Genomes Evolve; Ch19 Sexual Reproduction and the Power of Genetics; Ch 18 The
Cell Division Cycle.

Ch 3 Energy, Catalysis, and Biosynthesis; Ch 4 Protein Structure and Function; Ch
10 Modern Recombinant DNA Technology; Ch 17 Cytoskeleton; Study of assigned topics
and consultation on cell biology research and experimental methods

docs.text: 第 1 頁，共 3 頁 科目課程簡介 課目名稱：(中文) 人體解剖學虛擬實作 (英文) 3D Organon Virtual Reality (VR) Human Anatomy 授課老師：張壯榮、彭明德、莊永仁、李佳霖 學分數： 1 學分 上課時間：Wed. 13:20-14:10 or 14:20-15:10 修課資格：大學部二年級以上 (需修習過人體生理與解剖學) 課程目標： 雖然大體解剖學實驗一直以來是解剖學的重要教學方法，但並不是每間 學校都有大體解剖學實驗的軟硬體設備與師資（包括大體老師）；且對 部分學生而言，實驗課會對其造成很大的心理壓力。近年來電腦科技的 進步及新教學方法與教材的研發，開始利用虛擬實境（Virtual Reality, VR）的解剖學教材，來補充或部分取代大體解剖學實驗。 授課方式: 以解剖學虛擬實境教材進行教學，其具備下列以下功能：可以觀察人體 的局部（例如頭、胸、腹部等，亦即局部解剖學）；也可單獨觀察某個系 統（例如呼吸、循環、消化、神經等系統，亦即系統解剖學）；可以搜尋 與定位特定的器官構造；有不同角度的切面，且可放大切面觀察細節； 可以將數個切面組合以觀察各器官構造之走向、相對位置與關係；互動 式解剖（可將器官構造移開、放回、旋轉等）；可將器官構造著色與標記； 可以與同部位的 X 光、MRI 或 CT 影像一起觀察比對；內含器官構造之 說明、影片與動畫。 授課進度表 Date Chapter and Topics Teacher 1 9/03 助教時間/ The Skeletal System Membranes Dr. CR Chang 2 9/10 The Skeletal System Dr. CR Chang 第 2 頁，共 3 頁 3 9/17 The Urinary System Dr. CR Chang 4 9/24 The Muscular System Dr. MD Perng 5 10/01 Special Senses Dr. MD Perng 6 10/08 The Endocrine System Dr. MD Perng 7 10/15 Midterm Exam I 8 10/22 The Cardiovascular Dr. YJ Chuang 9 10/29 The Lymphatic System System Dr. YJ Chuang 10 11/05 The Respiratory Dr. YJ Chuang 11 11/12 全校運動大會(停課一天) 12 11/19 Midterm Exam II 13 11/26 The Nervous System Dr. JL Lee 14 12/03 The Nervous System and Body Metabolism Dr. JL Lee 15 12/10 The Digestive System The Reproductive System Dr. JL Lee 16 12/17 Final Exam 縮短為 16 周教學說明：扣除開始的準備周及微調整體實作時間，調整為 16 周。

II 107: Human Anatomy & Physiology Lecture: Mon 15:30-18:20 Lecturers: Prof. Chuang-Rung Chang, Prof. Ming-Der Perng, Prof. Yung-Jen Chuang, Prof. Jia-Lin Lee COURSE DESCRIPTION: Human Anatomy and Physiology is intended for Department of Medical Science majors. Course (10710DMS 370300) encompasses both, anatomy and physiology of the human body. It includes cell structure and function and basic concepts of A&P. The focus of this course (A&P) is on the basic concepts, cellular level, Integumentary, Muscular, Nervous, Endocrine, Cardiovascular, Lymphatic, Respiratory, Digestive, Urinary and Reproductive systems. Course Outcomes: Students will be able to 1. Recognize and understand anatomical and physiological terminology 2. Know major organic and inorganic chemicals as they relate to the human body 3. Describe cellular structure and cellular activity 4. Discuss anatomical and physiological features of Integumentary, Muscular, Nervous, Endocrine, Cardiovascular, Lymphatic, Respiratory, Digestive, Urinary and Reproductive systems. 5. Apply the concept of homeostasis to human physiological activity 6. Evaluate select pathological conditions as they relate to normal functioning of the above-named systems TEXTBOOK: Essential of Human Anatomy and Physiology 12th edition by Elaine N. Mariem, Pearson Education. ISBN: 978-1-292-21611-9 Author(s): Elaine N. Marieb, PhD, Professor, Holyoke Community College LS Bldg. The book continues to offer just the right balance of anatomy, physiology, and clinical coverage to make the content complete, but not overwhelming. New clinical photos in the Homeostatic Imbalance feature help students visualize diseases and disorders, and new integrated Concept Links help students make connections across topics and body systems. A new, more modern design makes the book more accessible than ever, and new specific references to Mastering A&P direct students to study tools and resources that reinforce their understanding of chapter concepts. docs.nameEn: Medical Measurement in the Application of Music Healthcare
docs.text: 課 程 名 稱 生理量測與音樂健康照護 開課教師 授課對象 學分數 授課時數 （h） 開授系所 蘇郁惠、蘇美如 戚居暘 大學、研究所 選修、2學分 32 醫學科學系 授課時間、地點 週四 10:10-12:00 生科二館 課程說明 一、音樂對身心健康有多項益處。研究顯示聆聽或創作音樂能活 化大腦多個區域，促進情緒、記憶與社交連結，並有助釋放正向 化學物質，音樂甚至可能改變大腦結構。音樂介入已被應用於減 輕焦慮、憂鬱與慢性病症狀，但相關研究多為初步階段，需更多 嚴謹科學實證。美國國立衛生研究院（NIH）與國家補充與綜合健 康中心（NCCIH）推動「聲音健康」 (Sound Health)倡議，研究音 樂對大腦的影響及臨床應用。自2019年起研究涵蓋帕金森氏症、 中風、慢性疼痛及兒童大腦發展等。NCCIH支持項目含音樂對早 產兒神經發育、帕金森氏症患者步態與心血管病患健康的影響。 NIH於2023年與合作機構開發針對神經退化疾病的音樂介入方案。 三、提升音樂健康照護之科學實證研究能力，照護對象涵蓋安寧 緩和、認知障礙與老年癡呆症、帕金森氏症步態、精神疾病、中 風、嬰幼兒安撫、演奏傷害者。 四、生理量測與音樂健康照護-生醫專題海報競賽，分為表演藝術 醫學組、音樂健康照護組，採學生分組方式於期中分享主題、期 末繳交分組海報暨口頭簡報。 五、本課由音樂教育、醫學工程、物理治療等三領域教師合開。 課程含跨高齡科技領 域說明 本課程包含以音樂來改善高齡者逐漸退化的聽覺、動覺、認知等 生理感官機能，並支持高齡者提升生理、溝通、娛樂及學習。 成績評量 評分項目：出席率20%、提問10%、期末個人延伸報告20% 創意構想生醫專題海報競賽 50%，評分項目：創造力、跨域力、 學理性、Slogan 學生使用AI的規則：有條件開放 本課程鼓勵學生在透明與負責的原則下，適度使用AI工具進行課業協作。學生應在作 業或報告的標題頁註腳或引用文獻部分簡要說明AI工具的使用情況，並遵循學校的相 關指引。如未明確標註，教師有權重新評分或不予計分。 周次/日期 講題 授課老師 (1)09/04 課程介紹 蘇郁惠(清大音樂科技與健康研究中心主 任)、戚居暘(清大醫科系兼任助理教授) (2)09/11 實證醫學的基礎(等級、分類、IRB) 戚居暘(清大醫科系兼任助理教授) (3)09/18 實證醫學的設計(實驗設計、統計分析) 戚居暘(清大醫科系兼任助理教授) (4)09/25 音樂治療成效評估之生理量測 戚居暘(清大醫科系兼任助理教授) 蘇美如(中原大學醫工系主任) (5)10/02 高齡者的音樂治療:認知神經科學的觀點 蔡振家(臺大音樂學研究所副教授) (6)10/09 中風後步態復健之音樂介入科學實證 戚居暘(清大醫科系兼任助理教授)、蘇郁 惠(清大音樂科技與健康研究中心主任) (7)10/16 精神疾病之音樂介入科學實證 陳正哲(臺大新竹分院精神科主治醫師)、 蕭忻(臺大新竹分院職能治療師) (8)10/23 表演藝術醫學研究暨典範機構 戚居暘(清大醫科系兼任助理教授)、蘇郁 惠(清大音樂科技與健康研究中心主任) (9)10/30 表演藝術醫學常採之生理量測 戚居暘(清大醫科系兼任助理教授) 蘇美如(中原大學醫工系主任) (10)11/06 各組報告主題分享 各組推派一位組員報告 (11)11/13 音樂家之肩背痛問題評估 蘇炯睿(奇美醫院復健科音樂家特別門診主 治醫師)；戚居暘(清大醫科系兼任助理教 授) (12)11/20 利用音樂與人工智慧之導入，進行新型態 的智慧健康照護 蔡明耀(量子音樂創辦人及董事長) (13)11/27 安寧緩和暨科學實證音樂介入 彭仁奎(臺大醫院安寧緩和部醫師)及團隊 (14)12/04 以演奏者視角探討演奏傷害之預防及實踐 顏竹君(中山大學音樂系助理教授) (15)12/11 期末分組競賽(1-4組) -表演藝術醫學組 蘇郁惠(清大音樂科技與健康研究中心主 任)；戚居暘(清大醫科系兼任助理教授) 蘇美如(中原大學醫工系主任) (16)12/18 期末分組競賽(5-8組) -音樂健康照護組 蘇郁惠(清大音樂科技與健康研究中心主 任)；戚居暘(清大醫科系兼任助理教授) 蘇美如(中原大學醫工系主任)

docs.name: 精準醫療與基因檢測概論
docs.nameEn: Introduction of Precision Medicine and Genetic Testing
docs.text:
一、課程說明:
介紹細胞治療與基因檢測在精準醫療時代的重要性，熟悉基細胞治療與基因檢測的原理與將來的應用，
並介紹基因大數據相關資料庫與AI技術如何應用在基因與疾病間關聯性的分析，提供學生了解現代精準
醫療的發展方向。

二、指定用書 本課程將以教師講義與期刊或其他參考資料為主。

三、參考書籍 課堂指定相關論文

四、教學方式 口頭授課與互動討論為主，並會邀請產業人士來演講授課，
了解精準醫學與基因檢測的未來發展。

五、教學進度(課程主題)
(A)、精準醫療與基因體學概論
(B)、基因檢測技術與檢測試劑的發展與應用
(C)、基因檢測在大健康產業的應用
(D)、序列多形性與全基因組疾病關聯分析
(E)、基因與疾病資料庫介紹
(F)、基因檢測實驗室認證與法規
(G)、基因檢測在癌症治療的應用
(H)、基因檢測在臨床藥物的應用
(I)、精準醫療的商品行銷策略
(J)、細胞治療與法規
(K)、外泌體的理論與臨床應用
(L)、大數據資料在基因檢測的應用

六、成績考核
課堂參與: 包含出席,討論與課後作業(30%)。另外共需繳交兩次報告，
期中報告(佔30%)以及期末報告(佔40%)。

https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw/

docs.name: 基因諮詢概論
docs.text:
課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus

● 課程說明(Course Description)
該課程內容含括醫學遺傳學、高通量定序與資料分析、諮商理論與技巧、遺傳統計學、癌症遺傳學、母
胎醫學檢測與罕見疾病遺傳等相關內容，並透過臨床資料與案例的介紹，來更了解基因資訊如何在不同
的臨床方面的應用與解讀，本課程是與國家衛生研究院師資共同開設，會邀請相關領域的專家參與授
課，使學生具備有基因諮詢的基本知識。

● 指定用書(Text Books)
本課程將以教師上課講義與期刊論文為主。

● 參考書籍(References)
A Guide to Genetic Counseling, 3rd Edition
Vivian Y. Pan (Editor), Jane L. Schuette (Editor), Karen E. Wain (Editor), Beverly
M. Yashar (Editor)
ISBN: 978-1-119-89208-3, November 2024, Wiley-Blackwell

● 教學方式(Teaching Method)
口頭授課與互動討論為主，並會邀請臨床醫師來演講授課，更實務的了解基因諮詢的實踐。

● 教學進度(Syllabus)
教學的單元如下:
1. Overview of genetic counseling (蔡惠如研究員, 國衛院)
2. Introduction to statistical methods (蔡惠如研究員, 國衛院)
3. Overview of epidemiology (蔡惠如研究員, 國衛院)
4. Introduction to genetic epidemiology (林達雄教授 馬偕醫院)
5. Bioinformatic resources for medical genetics (曾大千教授 清大)
6. Genetic techniques and analysis I (曾大千教授 清大)
7. Genetic techniques and analysis II (曾大千教授 清大)
8. Ethical issues in clinical genetic counseling (雷文玫副教授 陽交大)
9. Risk calculations for genetic counseling (蕭自宏助理教授 台中榮總)
10. Practical skills in genetic counseling I (簡穎秀教授 台大)
11. Practical skills in genetic counseling II (許育光教授 清大)
12. Application of genetic counseling in cancer (蔡世峰研究員 國衛院)
13. Application of genetic counseling in rare disease (蔡世峰研究員 國衛院)
14. Application of genetic counseling in reproductive health (孫孝芳教授, 成功大
學)

● 成績考核(Evaluation)
課堂參與: 包含出席與討論(20%)。期中考(佔40%)以及期末報告(佔40%)。

docs.name: 工程導論
docs.text: 工程導論課程大綱 一、本課程前兩週為工學院大一學生之共通課程，隨後進入四大主題課程（每主 題各為期三週），由不同學系教師分別講授。 二、工程導論課程之授課教師如下： ◼ 化學工程學系－林育正老師 ◼ 動力機械工程學系－李明蒼老師 ◼ 材料科學與工程學系－許瑋麟老師 ◼ 工業工程與工程管理學系－洪一峯老師：114/9/3 更新成績考核。 三、成績考核： ◼ 各主題課程各佔總成績之 25%，合計為 100%。 ◼ 各主題課程之成績評量方式略有不同，請參閱各授課教師之課程大綱以 了解詳細規定。 國立清華大學課程大綱－化工系 林育正教授 課程簡述 本課程旨在引導工學院大一學生建立低碳與永續能源的基本認知，涵蓋再生能源、發電碳排放、 碳足跡計算等主題。學生將學習如何分析不同能源形式的碳排強度，並進行簡易計算與小組討 論。透過實作與案例探討，培養學生對低碳轉型的理解與工程應用敏感度。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」 低碳能源 Low-carbon energy;碳足跡計算 Carbon footprint calculation;永續發展 Sustainable development;發電碳排 Electricity emissions;工程減碳 Decarbonization in engineering 課程大綱 ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程透過六堂課引導學生了解低碳與永續能源的核心議題，從基礎能源知識出發，進一步探討 碳排放與碳足跡的計算方式。學生將學習如何查找資料並估算各種能源與電力來源的碳排強度， 並進行小組簡報與討論，以提升跨領域整合與溝通能力。 ● 指定用書(Text Books)：無指定教科書，教師將提供講義及補充資料。 ● 參考書籍(References)：無指定教科書，教師將提供講義及補充資料。 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method)：講授與互動討論; 小組作業與簡報; 線上資料查詢與實作練習 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 1.低碳能源與電力概論 2. LCA 碳足跡計算方法介紹 3. 碳足跡計算結果與分析報告 ● 成績考核(Evaluation)：書面報告（60%）及口頭報告（40%），佔總成績 25% ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output 可參考下列網頁範例 See the following web page for examples. https://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1208-248357.php?Lang=zh-tw 國立清華大學課程大綱－動機系 李明蒼教授 課程簡述 機械工程涵蓋四個基礎專業領域：熱流與能源、機電控制、機械結構與材料力學，以及設計製 造。機械工程技術的應用範圍廣泛，包含光機電、生醫、動力、能源、微奈米科技等。本課程 將介紹機械工程的專業與應用，以及討論近年快速興起的人工智慧以及永續發展目標 (Sustainable Development Goals, SDGs)等議題與機械工程的相關性。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」 機械工程(Mechanical Engineering)，光機電系統(Opto-mechatronic systems)，人工智慧 (Artificial Intelligence)，永續發展目標(Sustainable Development Goals, SDGs) 課程大綱 ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程將介紹動力機械工程的專業與應用，以及討論近年快速興起的人工智慧以及永續發展目 標(Sustainable Development Goals, SDGs)等議題與動力機械工程的相關性。 ● 指定用書(Text Books)：無 ● 參考書籍(References)：課程投影片 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method)：課堂講授 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 1. Power Mechanical Engineering: Fields, Scales and Applications 2. Virtual vs. Reality; PME: Now, the Future, and Sustainability 3. Mini project ● 成績考核(Evaluation)：小實作專題（100%），佔總成績 25% ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output 可參考下列網頁範例 See the following web page for examples. https://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1208-248357.php?Lang=zh-tw 國立清華大學課程大綱－材料系 許瑋麟教授 課程簡述 本課程首先介紹材料科學與材料工程的關聯性、材料科學與工程與在科技與產業上的角 色、能源及環境永續發展的關係。接著介紹材料科學與材料工程的基礎：材料科學工程學習材 料之結構、性質與製程，並研究三者之間的關聯性。材料結構包括晶體結構與微結構，材料性 質涵蓋機械性質、物理性質與化學性質，材料製程則包括熔煉、鍛造、軋延、熱處理等傳統製 程。第三部分則進一步介紹數種現代工業中重要材料技術與實際應用情形: 如積層製造技術 (如 選擇性雷射熔融與電子束熔融等)、以及熱噴塗技術 (如電漿噴塗與高速氧燃燒噴塗) 等進階製 程。這些技術能應用於國防與航太元件、能源轉換裝置、生醫植入物與高溫防護塗層等領域， 展示了現代材料技術如何支援高階產業發展並因應極端環境需求。最後介紹半導體材料相關製 程，以晶圓代工產業之乾蝕刻製程為例，體現材料科學對現代科技發展的深遠影響。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」 材料結構，材料製程，材料性質 (機械性質、物理性質、化學性質) ，積層製造技術，熱噴塗 技術，半導體材料製程 Material Structure, Material Processing, Material Properties (Mechanical, Physical, Chemical), Additive Manufacturing Technology, Thermal Spray Technology, Semiconductor Material Processing 課程大綱 ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程介紹材料科學與工程的基礎概念，包括材料的結構、性質與製程及其相互關係，並延伸 至現代材料技術如積層製造、熱噴塗與半導體製程。課程同時探討材料技術在國防、航太、能 源、生醫等高階應用中的重要角色，說明其對科技與永續發展的關鍵影響。 ● 指定用書(Text Books) Materials, 3rd Edition, Engineering, Science, Processing and Design, eBook ISBN: 9780080982816 ● 參考書籍(References) Thermal Spray Fundamentals, eBook ISBN: 978-0-387-68991-3 Dry Etching Technology for Semiconductors, eBook ISBN: 978-3-319-10294-8 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 投影片上課 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 1. 材料的重要性 (Importance of Materials in human society) 2. 材料科學與工程基礎 (The basics of Materials Science & Engineering) 3. 進階材料技術應用 (Applications of Advanced Materials Technology) ● 成績考核(Evaluation) 出席率（20%）及期末考（80%），佔總成績 25% ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 本課程無涉及 AI 使用 Not applicable 可參考下列網頁範例 See the following web page for examples. https://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1208-248357.php?Lang=zh-tw 國立清華大學課程大綱－工工系 洪一峯教授 課程大綱 ● 課程說明(Course Description)： ※最佳化與工業工程 介紹工業工程部分的技術，包含生產管理概念、作業研究、線性規劃及整規劃之建模技術，並 利用套裝軟體求解數學規劃模型。 ● 指定用書(Text Books) ： None ● 參考書籍(References) ： None ● 教學方式(Teaching Method)： 課堂講授（class lectures） ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 1. 作業研究 2. 線性規劃 3. 整數規劃 4. 生產管理 ● 成績考核(Evaluation) 114/9/3 更新 課堂學習心得(15%)、數學規劃軟體專案作業(50%)、期末考(35%)，佔總成績 25%

程，以晶圓代工產業之乾蝕刻製程為例，體現材料科學對現代科技發展的深遠影響。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」 材料結構，材料製程，材料性質 (機械性質、物理性質、化學性質) ，積層製造技術，熱噴塗 技術，半導體材料製程 Material Structure, Material Processing, Material Properties (Mechanical, Physical, Chemical), Additive Manufacturing Technology, Thermal Spray Technology, Semiconductor Material Processing 課程大綱 ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程介紹材料科學與工程的基礎概念，包括材料的結構、性質與製程及其相互關係，並延伸 程。第三部分則進一步介紹數種現代工業中重要材料技術與實際應用情形: 如積層製造技術 (如 選擇性雷射熔融與電子束熔融等)、以及熱噴塗技術 (如電漿噴塗與高速氧燃燒噴塗) 等進階製 程。這些技術能應用於國防與航太元件、能源轉換裝置、生醫植入物與高溫防護塗層等領域， 展示了現代材料技術如何支援高階產業發展並因應極端環境需求。最後介紹半導體材料相關製 程，以晶圓代工產業之乾蝕刻製程為例，體現材料科學對現代科技發展的深遠影響。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」 材料結構，材料製程，材料性質 (機械性質、物理性質、化學性質) ，積層製造技術，熱噴塗 技術，半導體材料製程 Material Structure, Material Processing, Material Properties (Mechanical, Physical, docs.text:
1. Course Description (課程說明)
Primary aim
This course is aimed to equip the upperclassmen in the undergraduate engineering
program with language skills and knowledge necessary to succeed in the
engineering disciplines. Primarily focused on the academic speaking, the course
is designed on basis of interactive, communicative, and task-based
approaches.
In the course, students will analyze engineering-specific texts, evaluate
academic and technical sources, and apply engineering-related vocabulary across
a variety of academic tasks. Ultimately, students will create and deliver an
academic poster presentation to demonstrate organizing, visualizing, and
communicative skills. By mastering these academic skills, students are expected
to participate in discussions, conduct research, and present their studies with
clarity and confidence.
Subsidiary aim
Furthermore, this course is designed to enhance students’ abilities to
comprehend and interpret academic texts. Students will be guided to identify
main ideas by deciphering long, complex sentences in the academic writing.
Finally, they will be taught to write concise and succinct headings and
sentences for their poster presentations and apply these skills to their final
poster presentations.

2. Textbooks (指定用書)
Rowe, Nicholas .(2017)Academic & Scientific Poster Presentation: A Modern
Comprehensive Guide

3. References (參考資料)
(1) W. F. Smith and J. Hashemi, "Foundations of Materials Science and
Engineering", 6th Ed., McGraw-Hill, ISBN 978-1-260-09203-5
(2) N. J. Tro, "Chemistry-A Molecular Approach", 5th ed.2021, Person.

(5) Writing for presentation Week13-14
(6) Preparing for poster presentations Week15
(7) Poster presentation Week16

6. Evaluation (成績考核)
(1) Attendance and participation (35%)
(2) Homework: poster proposal (20%)
(3) Invitation letters and thank-you letters (10%)
(4) Final poster presentation (35%)

7. Guidelines for Students Use of the Al 人工智慧使用規範
Certain assignments in this course can be done using generative artificial
intelligence.
In the assignments permitting the use of AI tools, you must clearly identify
which parts of the assignments were AI generated and how AI helped you.
Additionally, you are responsible for the information based on AI queries in
your submitted assignments.
If permitted, you are allowed to use generative AI tools for the following
activities:
-brainstorming ideas
-looking up some words
-finding information about your topics

If not permitted, by default, you are not allowed to seek AI assistance,
particularly for the following activities:
-posting answers on online discussion boards
-doing exercises focusing on basic language skills, such as paraphrasing,
reducing and combining sentences.

docs.text: 經濟學原理一 課程大綱 Instructor: 余朝恩 Email: chaoenyu@mx.nthu.edu.tw 本門課程簡介經濟學的基本原理。經濟學不是一門教人自私的社會科學，而 是研究個人、廠商和組織如何做選擇的社會科學。 本課程主要介紹理性消費者和廠商決策的最適化，以及市場如何運作和達成 均衡的原理。本課程也將介紹在不同市場結構下，廠商的訂價和合作競爭等 決策行為。最後，本課程將分析政府在經濟社會運作中可以和應該扮演的角 色（或者不扮演）。鑑於近年來各國對公平、正義的呼聲日益高漲，本課程 也將針對部分大眾對於經濟學的迷思進行答辯和剖析。本門課程也將以數理 套裝軟體和 Python 程式設計展示經濟分析常用的繪圖和運算。 評分方式： 兩次期中考(10/13 和 11/17)，一次期末考(12/15)，佔總成績 80%; 課堂小考佔 20%，缺考扣分。 教科書： Hubbard and O'Brien (2022), Economics, Pearson Education Limited, 8th edition (滄海圖書) Steven Pinker (2022), 理性：人類最有效的認知工具, 商周出版社. 考試規則： (1) 考試時禁止使用手機。 (2) 請同學務必參加考試。考試時應按時進入試場，遲到逾 20 分 鐘者不得入場，遲到或缺席者以「缺考」處理。 生成式人工智慧倫理聲明：禁止使用 經仔細考量後，本課程授課教師認為不宜於此門課程當中使用生成式人工智慧於課堂學習當 中。因本課程的內容於生成式 AI 中尚有諸多錯誤，且容易影響學生對基礎核心知識之判讀。 根據本校公布之佈的「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採取禁止使 用，以下為相關的監管機制 • 修讀本門課程之學生應注意本門課不得繳交使用生成式人工智慧所產出的作業、報告 或個人心得。若經查核發現，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評 分或不予計分。 • 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。

docs.text: 1 11410ECON100102 Principles of Economics I Instructor: Prof. Hui-chen Wang (王惠貞) Fall 2025 (114上) Office: 台積館 810 Classroom: TSMC (台積館) 224 Office Hours: TBA Lecture Time: R5R6R7 (150 minutes on Thu 13:20-16:20) Email: huichenwang@mx.nthu.edu.tw Principles of Economics (I) Syllabus (Preliminary) Course Description This course offers an introduction to microeconomic theories and applications. We will discuss the basic economic concepts and theories concerning market functions and the choices of individual decision makers, including people and firms. This course is offered in English. Learning Objectives After successful completion of this course, students will be able to (1) define and discuss the key economic concepts including the basic principles of rational choices, (2) identify and analyze the fundamental microeconomic issues using verbal, graphical and simple mathematical techniques, and (3) apply economic thinking to daily decisions and events. Course Requirements and Policies Examinations There will be an in-class midterm exam and a final exam. The exams are not strictly cumulative; however, previously tested concepts may be covered in the final exam to the extent that they are the bases of a current topic. The format of the examinations will be a combination of multiple-choice questions and short written problems. The midterm and final exam dates will be announced in the first class meeting. All students must take the exams at their scheduled times. Make-up exam policy: No make-up exam will be given for the midterm exam. The weight for a missed midterm exam, if excused, will be reallocated to the final exam. Make-up exam for the final exam will only be given under unexpected, extremely unusual and justifiable circumstances. Students who miss an exam due to an unexpected emergency should inform professor Wang within 24 hours from the missed exam and provide official documentation for the absence within one week. Pop quizzes: Short, unannounced quizzes will be given throughout the semester. For each student, the lowest score of all quizzes given in the semester will be excluded from the calculation of quiz average. It is important to note that NO makeup quiz may be given for any reason since the one quiz waiver (indicated above) already takes into account the occasional illness or unexpected personal situations that may prevent you from taking a quiz. However, under extremely unusual and justifiable circumstances 2 (official documentation required), extra quiz waivers may be granted on a case- by-case basis, at professor Wang’s discretion. Homework assignments: Problem sets will be assigned throughout the course. Your homework will not be graded; however, all students are expected to complete all assignments in a timely manner for effective learning and preparation of the tests. Attendance and Participation: Students are required to attend the lectures regularly. Participation in class discussion is expected and appreciated. You will be held responsible for all assignments, tests, and any announcement made in class, even in your absence. Your attendance and participation may affect your overall course grades on the margin. Grading Course letter grades will be assigned based on the weighted sums of the graded components of your performance: Midterm exam: 40 % Final exam: 45 % Quizzes: 15% The grades are not negotiable. No individual request for extra credit work will be taken. Textbook Glenn P. Hubbard and Anthony P. O'Brien (2022), Economics: Global Edition 8/e. Pearson. (ISBN-13: 978-1292430645) Our class discussion and test coverage may include some material not from this textbook. Class Communication and Resources TA Office hours: In addition to Professor Wang’s office hours (see header), there will be weekly office hours held by one of our teaching assistants. The time and location of the TA office hours will be announced separately on eeclass (see next). eeclass: In addition to in-class communication, email and office hours, we will utilize the eeclass digital course tool maintained by the university. Class announcements, lecture slides (student version), homework assignments, answer keys, grades and other course-related material will be posted. You are expected to check your email as well as your eeclass account regularly to remain up to date. Note: The posted version of the lecture slides will be incomplete by design with spaces to be filled out in class. You are expected to print out the slides in advance and bring them to the class. Keep in mind that the lecture slides will not remove the need for your class attendance and note taking efforts Regulation on AI Usage The usage of AI is irrelevant in this course since student learning will be assessed by in-class closed-book tests. 3 Tentative Course Outline Topics Textbook Chapters 1. Introduction 2. How Market Works: Demand and Supply; Market Equilibrium; Economic Efficiency and Government Intervention; Elasticity 3. Consumer Choices: Budget, utility, and consumer’s demand 4. Production Theory: Output and cost 5. Market Structure and Profit Maximization: Perfect Competition; Monopoly and Price discrimination; Monopolistic Competition and Oligopoly 1-2 3, 4, 6 10 11 12, 15, 13-14

docs.text: ECON100103 經濟學原理一 課程大綱 Instructor: 李翎帆 Office: 台積館 703 Email: lilf@mx.nthu.edu.tw Office Hours: 週二 12:00-13:30 經濟學是研究理性個人如何做選擇的社會科學。本課程主要介紹消費者與廠商如何做決策。在消 費者理論方面，本課程將探討影響消費者購買行為之因素與其決策準則。在生產者理論方面，將 介紹在不同市場結構下，廠商的生產與定價決策行為。此外，也將分析政府在經濟社會所扮演之 角色。 主要用書: M. Parkin, Economics, 14th edition (雙葉書廊) 評分方式 : 本學期總成績由一次期中考試(50%)和一次期末考試(50%)評定，時間如下： 期中考: 2025/11/03。 期末考: 2025/12/15。 考試規則 : (1) 考試時禁止使用手機。 (2) 請同學務必參加考試 ，考試當天缺席者以 〝缺考 〞處理。 若遇不可抗拒之因素需 請事假 ，於考試前向授課教師申請補考，無法事後申請補考。 課程相關連結 : 清華大學 eLearn https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw/ 授課內容 : 1. 經濟學基本概念 (Ch.1, ch.2) 2. 供需均衡與彈性 (Ch.3) ➢ 分析在完全競爭市場下，商品 (或服務) 的價格如何決定 3. 價格彈性(ch.4) ➢ 價格變動與消費數量之間的關係 4. 效率與平等(ch.5) ➢如何分配資源 5. 市場機能與政府干預 (Ch.6) ➢市場管制 ➢最低工資 6. 消費者決策 (ch.8, ch.9) ➢效用和需求 ➢消費者在既有的資源(財富)下，如何選擇市場上個別商品的消費量 7. 生產者決策 (ch.10, ch.11) ➢ 介紹廠商生產理論與成本分析 8. 競爭與獨佔 (ch.12, ch.13) ➢ 介紹在不同市場結構下廠商的訂價決策行為 9. 外部性與公共財 (ch.16, ch.17) ➢ 分析在市場經濟發生缺陷時(市場失靈)，政府可以介入市場提升社會福利 ➢ 分析政府設立關稅對一國福利之影響

docs.text: 經濟學原理一 Fall 2025 教師: 唐震宏 E-mail: jhtang@mx.nthu.edu.tw Office: TSMC727 有關加簽的常見問題 1. 如果有加簽需求的同學，請在加簽期間登入學校系統提出要求。 2. 教室有容量限制，我能加簽的名額等於教室容量減去已選課人數。如果有加簽需求的 人數超過可加簽人數，原則上以大四同學優先，再來依序是大三、大二、大一。若同 一順位要求加簽人數超過空位 (例如有 N 個空位，但有 N+1 位大四同學要加簽)，則 以亂數抽籤決定。 課程概述 本課程目的在介紹經濟學的基本分析工具與核心議題。內容以市場機制之運作為主軸， 包括經濟學的基本概念，如機會成本、比較利益、專業分工，以及個體經濟學的議題，如 供給與需求、市場均衡、消費者行為、生產者行為、和產業組織等。 課程目標 本課預期能協助同學 (1) 瞭解經濟學基本原理；(2) 應用經濟理論分析經濟問題。 參考用書 1. Mankiw, N.G. (2024), Principles of Economics, 10th Edition, Cengage Asian Edition. 授課方式 1. 授課以教師講解為主，歡迎同學隨時發問並提出意見。 2. The lectures are taught in Chinese (Mandarin). Students who have diffi- culties in understanding Chinese are advised not to take this course. 1 3. 上課投影片會在上課前公布在 eeclass: http://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw。投影片的內 容是演講的重點與綱要，但不可能是文理清晰邏輯通順的文章。建議同學上課時記下 重要的邏輯推論及實例，或是準備一本課本，方便日後複習。 4. 如果你常來聽課，遇到聽不懂的地方，或是不會答的題，我有責任，也很樂意回答你 的問題，讓你明白。但有些同學平常不來上課，自己看課本講義又看不懂 (或是不想 費神)，然後考前發 email 給我問問題，或是考前才來課堂上，利用下課來問一大堆我 早已反覆講過多次的內容，把我當成函授學校或是私人家教。占用我的時間，也排擠 掉其他同學發問的時間，甚至影響到正常上課。這對我或是對其他同學，應該都是不 公平吧？所以如果你有缺課，又想補上進度，請你自己想辦法。 5. 考試命題範圍以上課投影片為準，所有在課堂上講解過的內容都包含在內。大致上與 課本一致，但會有所增減。 放假與上課時間 • 放假：10/10 (雙十節) • 上課：九月 (5、12、19、26)、十月 (3、17、24、31)、十一月 (7、14、21、28)、十二 月 (5、12、19)。 成績計算、考試時間、及相關規定 1. 期中考 50%，期末考 50%。 2. 期中及期末考時間：10/24、12/19，3:30–5:20pm。 3. 上述考試時間若無法出席參加考試，請依本校請假辦法辦理。任何事假歉難同意，且 無法給予補考。公假需出示本校派遣單位核發之公假單，喪假需請家長、監護人、或 直系尊親屬來信 (電郵) 代為請假，病假需請校醫或醫院開立證明，否則視同無假缺 考。因懷孕、分娩或為撫育三歲以下幼兒而核准之事病假及產假視同病假。 4. 考試以中文或英文出題，可以中文或英文回答。如果你自認中/英文不好，請自己加 強中/英文閱讀能力。 2 課程進度 • 經濟學簡介 • 供給與需求 • 市場均衡 • 價格彈性 • 效用與消費者的選擇 • 期中考 • 生產者決策的基礎 • 競爭市場的供給線 • 市場機能與經濟效率 • 獨占 • 不完全競爭市場 • 要素市場 • 期末考 3

Perlo§ (2020). Course Description: This course is o§ered in English and is the Örst part of an one-year course of Microeconomics which is a requirement for Economics program. Knowledge of calculus will be expected as it is used frequently for solving problems. The course starts with the introduction of supply and demand, and it studies how a consumer makes choices about which good to consume. After understanding consumer theory, the demand curve and its properties can then be analyzed in a more rigorous manner. Moreover, we will discuss how to measure the consumer welfare and provide policy implications. In the second half of the course, we study how Örms make choices on how much to produce for both short and long- run analysis. Similar to the consumerís problem of maximizing utility, Örms minimize their costs, and the properties of the cost function will be studied. We then introduce the most important mode of market structure, namely the perfect competition and discuss how Örms and consumers interact in such environment. Lastly, we extend the partial analysis of an economy to a general equilibrium setting and discuss the economic welfare of such setting. We will focus on topics including data, probability distributions, sampling, estimation, and conclude with hypothesis testing. We will also start familiarizing ourselves with basic programming as we use visualization and simulations to introduce statistical concepts. docs.name: 統計學一
docs.text:
一、課程概述（Course Description / Outline）
本課程為統計學的入門課程，適合商學院學生修習，旨在建立學生分析資料與解讀數據的基礎能力。
內容涵蓋統計的核心理論與基本應用方法，從資料的整理與視覺化、敘述統計（如集中趨勢與離散程
度指標），到機率理論、常見機率分配（如二項分配與常態分配）、抽樣理論、信賴區間估計與假設檢
定等。本課程重視資料素養的培養，並會在課程中透過軟體進行實作，使學生能從資料中萃取關鍵資
訊，做出有根據的統計推論與判斷。課程結合理論、操作與應用，為學生未來深入學習計量經濟學、
商業資料分析或從事實證研究提供必要的理論基礎與分析能力。

二、教學目標及預期成效（Goals and Learning Outcomes）
本課程旨在引導學生掌握統計學的基本概念與分析邏輯，理解並運用統計方法處理資料，進行合理的
推論與解釋。課程設計結合理論與實務，透過課堂講授與操作練習，培養學生的資料素養與量化思考
能力。學生將學會如何以統計方法解析問題、檢定假設，並能將所學應用於日常生活與商業決策情境
中。
預期成效：
1. 能整理資料並製作圖表，執行基礎統計分析與結果解釋；
2. 理解敘述統計與機率分配的基本概念，具備計算與應用能力；
3. 能進行信賴區間估計與假設檢定，具備基礎推論能力；
4. 理解統計在生活與商業應用中的角色，具備分析與判斷資料的能力。

三、課程內容（Course Content）
本學期課程內容將預計涵蓋下列章節：
1. Describing Data with Graphs.
2. Describing Data with Numerical Measures.
3. Describing Bivariate Data.
4. Probability.
5. Discrete Probability Distributions.
6. The Normal Probability Distribution.
7. Sampling Distributions.
8. Large-Sample Estimation.

（課程進度將依上課情況進行調整）

四、課程特色及執行方式（Course Features and Teaching Approach）
>> 課程融合理論與實務，透過實際資料與統計工具進行操作演練；
>> 注重資料素養與邏輯表達，鼓勵學生從生活或產業議題出發，進行統計探究；
>> 透過學校教學平台協助進行教材布達、作業繳交與課堂互動。

五、指定教材與參考書目（Textbook）
指定教材： Mendenhall, Beaver, and Beaver (2020). Introduction to Probability
and Statistics, 15E (SI Edition). ISBN: 9780357114469。 http://www.gau-
lih.com.tw/tier/front/bin/ptdetail.phtml?Part=BX0162&Category=100106344

參考書目：
Camm, J., Cochran, J., Fry, M., Ohlmann, J., Anderson, D., Sweeney, D., &
Williams, T. (2024). (2024). Statistics for Business and Economics (15th ed.).
Cengage.
(https://eshop.tsanghai.com.tw/products/ps0507pc)
Lind, D. A., Marchal, W. G., & Wathen, S. A. (2021). Statistical Techniques in
Business and Economics, 18th Edition, McGraw-Hill Education.
Wickham, H. & Grolemund, G. (2017). R for Data Science. O'Reilly Media.

docs.text:
一、課程說明(Course Description)

不論是營利或非營利事業，亦不論是組織規模的大小，「成本」經常是管理者做決斷時所需要
的關鍵性資訊。本課程主要的目的，在循序漸進地介紹與討論各類成本計算的方法與成本管理的理
論，引導學生瞭解處於動態環境下的組織，如何運用成本會計的技術進行規劃、控制及做決策。

docs.text: 1 Cost and Managerial Accounting(I) 成本與管理會計(I) College of Technology Management, National Tsing Hua University (Spring 2025) Instructor: 沈瑜峰 Shen Yu-Feng Office Hour: By appointment E-mail: shenyf@mx.nthu.edu.tw Class time: 15:30-18:20, Wednesdays, W7W8W9 Classroom: TSMC 台積 205 Course Objective: The goal of cost and managerial accounting is to acquaint students of management with the fundamental tools of management accounting, but also to promote their understanding of the dramatic ways in which the field is changing. The emphasis throughout the course is on using accounting information in managing an organization. In this course, the traditional tools of managerial accounting, like product costing, budgeting, and performance evaluation, will be augmented and updated with contemporary approaches such as activity- based costing, customer profitability analysis, value-chain analysis, target costing, balanced scorecard, and strategic cost management. Prerequisite: Accounting(I)、(II)。 Topics Cost Concepts for Decision-Makers 1 Managerial Accounting 2 Job Order Costing 3 Process Costing 4 Activity-Based Costing Decision-Making Concepts 5 Cost-Volume-Profit 6 Cost-Volume-Profit Analysis: Additional Issues 2 7 Incremental Analysis 8 Pricing Planning and Control Concepts 9 Budgetary Planning 10 Budgetary Control and Responsibility Accounting 11 Standard Costs and Balanced Scorecard 12 Planning for Capital Investments Performance Evaluation Concepts 13 Statement of Cash Flows 14 Financial Analysis: The Big Picture Required Materials: Weygandt, J. docs.name: 財務報導與實務
docs.text: 1 Financial Reporting： Theory and Practices College of Technology Management, National Tsing Hua University (Fall 2025) Instructor: 沈瑜峰 Shen Yu-Feng Office Hour: By appointment E-mail: shenyf@mx.nthu.edu.tw Class time: 12:10-15:10, Wednesdays, WnW5W6 Classroom: TSMC 台積 205 Course Objective: This course is designed to provide a strong conceptual, analytical and procedural foundation for the study of financial reporting and practice. The historical development of accounting thought and the role of financial accounting in today’s economy are investigated. Socioeconomic, political, legal, and ethical influences on financial reporting are considered. Discussions include procedures to record, summarize, and report results of business events; content and presentation of financial statements and specific reporting issues related to cash and receivable. An overview of financial statement analysis is also presented. International issues are addressed as appropriate. The aims and objectives of the course are to: • stimulate theoretical enquiry into financial accounting issues • develop the student’s knowledge and understanding of financial accounting • prepare students for further academic study in accounting and related areas • enable students in the pursuit of a professional accountancy qualification • equip students for employment in areas where an understanding of accounting issues and tools is helpful. Prerequisite: Accounting(I)、(II)。 Topics Module 1 Theory and Conceptual Framework Module 2 Depreciation Policy and Analysis and Interpretation of Statements of Changes in Financial Position Module 3 Accounting Information And Disclosure 2 Module 4 Financial Accounting and Reporting Standards Module 5 Corporate Reporting and Accounting for Multinational Corporations Module 6 Contemporary Issues in Accounting Required Materials: Higson, A. W. (2002). Corporate financial reporting: Theory & practice. Supplementary Reading: Lee, T. A. (2007). Financial reporting and corporate governance. John Wiley & Sons. Ding, Y., Lebas, M. J., & Stolowy, H. (2013). Financial accounting and reporting: A global perspective. Cengage Learning. Beyer, A., Cohen, D. A., Lys, T. Z., & Walther, B. R. (2010). The financial reporting environment: Review of the recent literature. Journal of accounting and economics, 50(2-3), 296-343. Barth, M. E., & Landsman, W. R. (2010). How did financial reporting contribute to the financial crisis?. European accounting review, 19(3), 399-423.

docs.text: ECON 3033 Econometrics I National Tsing Hua University Fall 2025 Instructor: Eric S. Lin Contact Information: Office: CTM 712, Email: slin@mx.nthu.edu.tw, Phone: 574-2729 Time and Location: Wednesday 12:00-3:00 pm, CTM 103 Office Hours: By appointment Course Webpage: Course materials will be available on the web through eeclass. Teaching Assistant: You are lucky to have XX to be your TA. Teaching Assistant Hours: TBA TA will hold the office hours and also be available for consultation on homework. Course Description: There are two sequences for undergraduate econometrics. This course is the first part of the introduction to econometrics sequence. We will review probability and statistics at the first beginning and then introduce the basic idea of regression models. You are expected to have a firm grasp of the types of empirical research designs that can lead to convincing analysis and be comfortable working with actual data sets. Although the aim will remain on the underlying theory, students will be given several opportunities to gain “hand on” experience with real data set through homework assign- ments. I would encourage students to make use of my office hours (or TA’s office hours) during the semester and not wait until the day before the exam. If you are having difficulty with concepts early on, then it is likely that your difficulties will snowball and that there will be insufficient time to deal with your puzzles close to the exams. So please make use of my office hours to sort out difficulties as they arise. Prerequisites: Calculus, Probability, and Statistics Syllabus Fall 2025 Required Textbook: Basically, I will hand out weekly lecture notes which are the summary of textbooks.  Stock, J. H. and M. W. Watson, 2020, Introduction to Econometrics, 4th edition, Addison-Wesley. Of course, there are lots of textbooks related to this course. If you have enough time, it would be also beneficial to check out some of the following references. References: Note that you don’t need to buy the following books. The book list is just for your reference.  Gujarati, D. N., 2003, Basic Econometrics, McGraw-Hill. It is the former textbook in this course.  Wooldridge, J. M., 2003, Introductory Econometrics: A modern approach, South- Western. It is a very popular undergraduate level textbook adopted in US. This book gives a huge amount of empirical examples and illustrates econometric concepts intuitively.  Maddala, G. S., 2001, Introduction to Econometrics, 3rd edition, Wiley. This book is well written and in general is deeper than our textbook. You could also find some fancy topics in Maddala’s book such as bootstrap, Jackknife and GMM.  Kennedy, P. A., 1998, A guide to Econometrics, 4th edition, MIT Press. This book tries to verbally explain difficult econometric ideas and avoids heavy math.  Pindyck, R. S. and L. R. Rubinfeld, 1998, Econometric Models and Economic Forecasts, McGraw-Hill. Ths is my econometric textbook when I was a junior. It is quite easy to read.  Ramanathan R., 2002, Introductory Econometrics with Applications, 5th edition, South- Western. This book provides a number of practical applications. It is also self-contained. In Chapter 14, the author demonstrates the various steps involved in carrying out an empirical research project.  Johnston and DiNardo, 1997, Econometric Methods, 4th edition, McGraw-Hill. If you are sort of familiar with matrix algebra, it is a nice book to build up the foundation of econometrics. It also serves the bridge to compensate the gap between undergraduate and graduate level econometrics. – 2 – Syllabus Fall 2025 Software: You are welcome to use any econometric packages such as Stata, R, Eviews, or Limdep. Grading: Several problem sets will be passed out during the semester. Although there are benefits to be obtained from working in groups I would advise against students free-riding off other students. docs.text: 1 ECON 3131 Syllabus: Globalizing Economy I Spring 2024 General Information. Instructor: Elaine Chyi Email: ylchyi@mx.nthu.edu.tw Office Hours. Weds. 3-5 pm or by appointment. (Email is the best way to reach me.) Classroom: TSMC #223 Course Home Page: eLearn 數位學習平台 Course objective and design. The growing economic openness expressed in the globalization of independent economic systems has created problems as well as opportunities in new and unexpected ways. In particular, globalization has allowed many counties to emerge from underdevelopment, as well as increase world production and employment. Outward-oriented policies brought greater prosperity to much of East Asia, transforming it from one of the poorest regions of the world about sixty years ago. Multinational firms have been the driving force behind these transformations, favoring the international division of productive processes and the spread of technologies and know-how. This course focuses on the aspects of economic globalization, such as the role of multinational firms as major participants of the globalizing world, global trade, and foreign direct investment, by providing an analytical framework for students to understand decisions of multinational firms. This course is primarily lecture style in around 80 percent of the semester. There will be some class activities, such as coursework or case discussion, held. A final team project with presentation in class is required. Grading. The final grade will be determined by classwork and homework (30%) and a final report and presentation of projects (70%). Course Material. − Head, Keith, Elements of Multinational Strategy, Berlin, Springer. − Related Articles from various books, issues of the Economists, NYT and economic journals. docs.text: 11410ECON316100 Public Finance (I) Instructor: Prof. Hui-chen Wang (王惠貞) Fall 2025 (114上) Office: 台積館810 Classroom: TSMC (台積館) 224 Email: huichenwang@mx.nthu.edu.tw Lecture Time: WnW5W6 (150 minutes on Wed 12:10-15:10) Office Hours: TBA Public Finance (I) 財政學一 Syllabus (Preliminary) Course Description This is the first course in the two-semester undergraduate sequence of Public Finance. Public Finance is the branch of economics that studies the role of the public sector in the economy, and the approach is primarily based on microeconomics. In this semester, we will have a focus on the expenditure side of public finance. The course will begin with an introduction to the public sector and basic economic tools, followed by the economic reasons and outcomes of government interventions. We will then look at what the public sector actually does using examples from the expenditure policies in the United States and in Taiwan, and how it affects individual decision-making and welfare. This course is offered in English. Learning Objectives After successful completion of this course, students will be able to (1) define and discuss the key economic concepts pertinent to the public sector, (2) analyze the fundamental issues in public finance using microeconomic theories and tools, (3) have a basic understanding of the important public expenditure policies in the world, and (4) apply economic thinking to the issues in the public expenditure policies in Taiwan. Prerequisite Principles of Economics I and II. Textbook and References Teaching material will be primarily drawn from the following textbooks: Hyman, David N. (2021), Public Finance: A Contemporary Application of Theory to Policy, 12th Edition. Cengage. (ISBN-13: 978-0357442159.) Rosen, Harvey S. and Ted Gayer. (2014). Public Finance. 10th global edition. McGraw-Hill/Irwin. ISBN-13: 978-0077154691 Some material that is not in the textbooks may be presented in the lectures. Course Requirements and Policies Examinations There will be two in-class examinations: one midterm exam and one final exam. The exams are not strictly cumulative; however, previously tested concepts may be covered in a later exam to the extent that they are the basis of a current topic. The midterm and final exam dates will be announced in the first class meeting. 2 All students must take the exams at their scheduled times. Make-up exam policy: No make-up exam will be given for the midterm exam. The weight for a missed midterm exam, if excused, will be reallocated to the final exam. Make-up exam for the final exam may be given under unexpected, extremely unusual and justifiable circumstances. Students who miss an exam due to an unexpected emergency should inform professor Wang within 24 hours from the missed exam and provide official documentation for the absence within a week. Pop Quizzes: Four short quizzes will be given in the semester. These quizzes will not be pre-announced. For each student, only the highest three quiz scores of the four will count towards the course grade calculation. NO makeup quiz may be given for any reason. However, under extremely unusual and justifiable circumstances (official documentation required), additional quiz waiver(s) may be granted on a case-by-case basis, at professor Wang’s discretion. Homework assignments: Problem sets will be assigned throughout the course. Your homework will not be collected nor graded; however, all students are expected to complete all assignments in a timely manner for effective learning and preparation of the tests. Attendance and Participation: Students are required to attend the lectures regularly. Participation in class discussion is expected and appreciated. You will be held responsible for all assignments, tests, and any announcement made in class, even in your absence. Your attendance and participation may affect your overall course grades on the margin. In addition, we reserve the right to impose penalty in terms of course grades if high frequency of unexcused absences is observed for a student. Grading Course letter grades will be assigned based on the weighted sums of the graded items: Midterm exam: 40% Final exam: 45 % Quizzes: 15% (5 for each of the three highest quiz scores) Your grades are not negotiable. No individual request for extra credit work will be taken. Class Communication and Resources TA Office hours: In addition to Professor Wang’s office hours (see header), there will be weekly office hours held by one of our teaching assistants. The time and location/format of the TA office hours will be announced separately on the eeclass learning platform (see next). Digital learning platform: We will utilize eeclass (https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw) digital learning platform maintained by the university. Announcements, slides, assigned problem sets, solutions, grades and other material related to the course will be posted. Please check the designated platform regularly to remain up to date. You are expected to check your email as well as your eeclass account regularly to remain up to date. Note: The posted version of the lecture slides will be incomplete by design with spaces to be filled out in class. You are expected to print out the slides in advance 3 and bring them to the class. Keep in mind that the lecture slides will not remove the need for your class attendance and note taking efforts. Regulation on AI Usage The usage of AI is irrelevant in this course since student learning will be assessed by in-class closed-book tests. Tentative Course Outline 1. INTRODUCTION AND ANALYTIC TOOLS (Ch. 1~2) 2. RATIONALE FOR A GOVERNMENT A. Externalities (Ch.3) B. Public Goods (Ch.4) 3. PUBLIC CHOICE AND POLITICAL ECONOMY (Ch. 5) 4. GOVERNMENT EXPENDITURE A. Income Redistribution and Programs for the Poor (CH. 7) B. Social Insurance I: Health Care (Ch. 9) C. Social Insurance II: Social Security (Ch. 8)

docs.text: 1 China’s Public Finance and Economic Development 中國大陸財政與經濟發展 Instructor: Pi-Han Christine Tsai Email: pihantsai@mx.nthu.edu.tw Course Description: This course provides a foundational understanding of China’s public finance and examines the country’s economic development through the lens of its political and fiscal institutions. We begin with an overview of China’s fiscal reforms, tracing their historical evolution and assessing their current implications. The core of the course focuses on the structure and dynamics of China’s political and fiscal systems. In addition, we will explore a range of contemporary issues in public finance, including expenditure allocation (e.g., education, healthcare, and pension systems), intergovernmental fiscal relations, the budget cycle, government debt, and land finance. The course concludes with a forward-looking discussion on the future trajectory of China’s economic development. Ethics Statement on Generative Artificial Intelligence: Grounded in the principles of transparency and responsibility, this course allows students to leverage AI for collaboration and mutual learning, thereby enhancing the quality of their midterm critical reports. In accordance with the published Guidelines for Collaboration, Co-learning, and Cultivation of Artificial Intelligence Competencies in University Education, this course adopts the following policy: Conditionally open. Students may briefly explain how generative AI was used for topic ideation, sentence refinement, or structural reference in the footnotes of the title page or after the bibliography in their final reports. However, students are not permitted to use generative AI tools for writing the reports. If such usage is discovered without proper disclosure, instructors, the institution, or relevant units have the right to reevaluate the report, or withhold scores. Students enrolled in this course agree to the above ethics statement by registering for the class. Course Objectives: 1. To learn the development of China’s fiscal policies and their economic outcomes. 2. To understand China’s budget system and intergovernmental fiscal arrangement. 3. To be able to analyze the causes and results of current public economic issues and problems in China. Textbooks and Related Materials: No textbook is required, but students are encouraged to read the supplemental materials. Please also refer to the instructor’s PPT. Additional reading materials will be announced during the semester. 1. Chen, T., and Kung, J., 2009. “Do Land Revenue Windfalls Create a Political Resource Curse? Evidence from China.” Journal of Development Economics 123: 86-106. 2. Han, L., and Kung, J., 2015. “Fiscal Incentives and Policy Choices of Local Governments: Evidence from China.” Journal of Development Economics 116: 89-104. 3. Jin, Hehui, Qian, Yingyi, Weingast, Barry R. 2005. “Regional Decentralization and Fiscal Incentives: Federalism, Chinese Style”, Journal of Public Economics 89: 1719-1742. 4. Justin Lin, and Zhiqian Liu, 2000. “Fiscal decentralization and economic growth in China”, Economic Development and Cultural Change, 49(1), 1-21. 5. Li, H., and Zhou, L., 2005. “Political Turnover and Economic Performance: the Incentive Role of Personnel Control in China.” Journal of Public Economics 89: 1743-1762. 6. Shah, Anwar, Shen, Chunli. 2006. “The Reform of the Intergovernmental Transfer System to 2 Achieve a Harmonious Society and a Level Playing Field for Regional Development in China”, World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 4100. 7. Shen, Chunli, Jin, Jing, Zho, Heng-fu. 2012. “Fiscal Decentralization in China: History, Impact, Challenges and Next Steps”, Annals of Economics and Finance 13-1: 1-51. 8. Shiyu Li and Shuanglin Lin, 2011, “The size and structure of China’s government debt,” Journal of Social Sciences, Vol. 48, No. 3, 527-542. 9. 蘭小歡, 2021, 置身事內：中國政府與經濟發展, 北京市紀文景文化傳播有限責任公司 Grading Policy: Class Participation 15% Midterm Exam 20% News Report or Critical Report 30% Final Debate Competition 35% Assessment Components (1) Class Participation (15%): • Attendance (10 Points): Attendance will be checked randomly three times during the course. To receive full credit for attendance, students must be present for at least two of these checks. Each attendance check is worth 5 points. • Participation in Discussions (5 Points): Active and meaningful participation in class discussions is essential and valued. Engagement in discussions will be worth 5 points towards the class participation grade. (2) Midterm Exam (20%): scheduled for 10/9. (3) News Report or Critical Report (30%): • News Report: Starting from Week 2, two students each week will present a recent news article or event related to China’s public finance and related phenomena. Students are expected to provide background or historical context and analyze the issue from an institutional perspective. Each presentation should be approximately 15–20 minutes in length. • Critical Report: Students will select a public policy or phenomenon related to China for critical analysis. The report should be 3–5 pages in length (including figures, tables, and references). Deadline: 11/6. (4) Final Debate Competition (35%): Each group will consist of five students, whether participating in the final debate or the in-class presentation. The presentation should last 60 minutes, followed by 30 minutes of Q&A. • Structured Debate or Final in-class Presentation (30%): Students will either participate in a structured debate on a public policy in Taiwan related to Mainland China, or deliver an in-class presentation comparing institutions or policies between Taiwan and Mainland China. • Experience Report (5%): Submit a 1-page report detailing your experience and learning outcomes from the debate. Deadline: 12/20. Course Content and Tentative Teaching Schedule (subject to change) Week 1: 9/4 Introduction Week 2: 9/11 Political Institutions 3 Week 3: 9/18 Political accountability Week 4: 9/25 Fiscal Institutions I Week 5: 10/3 Fiscal Institutions II Week 6: 10/9 Revenues and China’s Taxation System Week 7: 10/16 Midterm Exam ; Public Expenditure (I): Education Week 8: 10/23 Public Expenditure (II): Health Week 9: 10/30 Public Expenditure (III): Social Welfare Week 10: 11/6 Government Debts • Cause of a government debt crisis • Land finance • Local government financing vehicles Week 11: 11/13 Discussion on China’s Fiscal Risks and Crises Week 12: 11/20 Group Presentations Week 13: 11/27 Group Presentations Week 14: 12/4 Group Presentations Week 15: 12/11 Group Debate Week 16: 12/18 Group Debate

docs.name: 數理經濟學一
docs.text: 數理經濟學一 Fall 2025 Friday 12:30–15:20 @ TSMC 205 教師: 唐震宏 E-mail: jhtang@mx.nthu.edu.tw Office: TSMC727 課程介紹 數理經濟學是什麼？ 數理經濟學是一門經濟學的分支，其目的在為經濟分析提供嚴謹的架 構，尤其當經濟理論過於複雜而超過口語或圖形的表達範圍時，數理經濟學提供分析 的工具。除了在經濟理論的發展中發揮了關鍵的作用，數理經濟學也普遍應用於經濟 學的各個領域，提供數學工具對經濟現象進行建模及分析，進而發展出明確且可檢驗 的理論假說。 本門課的目標是什麼？用到那些數學工具？ 經濟學家視研究目的及分析難度來選用適當 的數學工具，常用的包括微積分、線性代數、微分方程、最優化理論、和機率論等。經 濟系的同學在大二的個體經濟學都上過 Perloff 的教科書，對微積分、靜態優化等應 該都不陌生。所以本門課將建立在這個基礎上，以總體經濟學的內容及其所使用的數 學工具為主要教學目標，會用到微積分、線性代數、靜態最適化、基礎微分方程、差 分方程。我們希望用這些數學工具來幫助同學學習總體經濟學，就如同 Perloff 的課 本用微積分來幫助同學學習個體經濟學。 數理經濟學有什麼用？ • 幫助學習及深入瞭解經濟理論：學習使用代數等數學工具的輔助，以及使用抽象 簡潔的數學表達，有助理解複雜的經濟理論，提高學習效率，並為未來學習更進 階的經濟理論奠定基礎。 • 提高分析和解決問題的能力：數理經濟學可以幫助學生將複雜多變的經濟問題 化繁為簡，並應用適當的模型進行分析，進而培養解決問題的能力。 • 培養跨領域的數學技能：數理經濟學需要使用微積分、線性代數、微分方程、最 優化理論等數學工具，而數學是科學之母，這些數學工具也都普遍應用在大數據 分析、機器學習、和人工智能等其他領域。尤其現在人工智能的時代已經來臨， 1 學習人工智能已不再是理工科系的專利。經濟主修的同學熟練應用數學工具可 以培養數學技能，除了提高經濟理論的學習效率，也有助於渉獵其他領域。 數理經濟學適合那些同學選修？ 選不選修數理經濟學要根據學生自身的興趣、職業規劃和 學術需求等因素來考慮。如果學生對數學和統計比較感興趣，且想將這些技能應用於 經濟學分析中，那麼選修數理經濟學會是一個不錯的選擇。這些技能可以幫助學生更 深入地理解經濟學理論和應用，並提高升學或就業競爭力。 但如果學生對數學和統計沒有太大的興趣，或者想在其他領域發展自己的職業生涯， 那麼選修數理經濟學可能不是必需的。學生可以根據自己的興趣和職業規劃選擇相應 的選修課程，以發揮自己的潛力。 課程目標 本課程預期能協助同學瞭解及學習 1. 如何應用數學工具有效學習經濟理論 2. 如何應用數學工具模型化並解決經濟問題 參考用書 C & W 是主要的教科書，其他參考書會隨主題進行介紹. • Chiang, A.C. and K. Wainwright (2004). Fundamental Methods of Mathematical Eco- nomics, 4th Ed. 放假與上課時間 • 放假：10/10 (雙十節) • 上課：九月 (5、12、19、26)、十月 (3、17、24、31)、十一月 (7、14、21、28)、十二 月 (5、12、19)。 2 成績計算與考試時間 • 作業 (4 次) 20%、期中考 40 %、期末考 40%。 • 期中及期末考時間：10/24、12/19，12:30–15:20。 課程進度 1. Linear system of equations 2. Determinants 3. Linear economic models (C & W, Chs.4, 5) 4. Comparative-static analysis (C & W, Chs.6, 7, 8) 5. Euclidean spaces 6. Eigenvalues and eigenvectors 7. Static optimization (C & W, Chs.9, 11, 12, 13) 3

docs.text: 1 ECON412100 國際經濟學一(International Economics (I)) 課程大綱 (temporary) Instructor: 李 宜 助教: TBA Office: 台積館 812 Email: ylee@mx.nthu.edu.tw Office: Office Hours: M 12pm-1pm Office hour: 在全球化的潮流下，近 30 年來世界各國紛紛降低貿易障礙，加速商品貿易的流量。 此外，國際間生產分工的方式，已從過去產品之間的分工，逐漸轉為生產同一種商品 在不同製程上的分工。在貿易自由化與國際分工的趨勢下，加速商品、人才與資金的 跨國移動，提升國家與國家間生產活動的關聯性。透過國際貿易，各國可專注於本國 較具生產優勢的商品，在國際市場換取本國生產成本較高的商品，進而提升本國的生 產效率與福利。雖然自由貿易可提升一國福利，但同時也可能對一國所得分配造成不 均度惡化。因此，各國政府在制定貿易相關政策時多受到許多爭議。 本課程主要介紹當前國際貿易理論模型，分析國家間為何會進行貿易，以及自由貿易 與貿易政策(如:關稅)下對一國福利的影響，期望學生未來能對國貿相關議題有初步認 識及相關分析能力。 主要用書: International Economics Theory and Policy, by Paul Krugman, Maurice Obstfeld and Marc Melitz (KOM) [華泰書局代理] 評分方式: 本學期成績評定內容涵蓋： (1) 作業: 本課程將依照授課進度不定期發放作業，學生由 6 人組成小組， 每組繳交一份作業。作業需於指定日期(時段)繳交，逾期不收。 (2) 期中考: 期中考於 2025,10,21 課堂中舉行 (3) 期末考: 期末考於 2025, 12,16 課堂中舉行。 學期總成績計算方式如下: A =﹝作業(30%)，期中考(35%)，期末考(35%)﹞ B =﹝作業(30%)，期中考(25%)，期末考(45%)﹞ 學期總成績將取 A 與 B 兩者中較高者(Max{A,B})。 考試規則: (1) 考試時禁止使用手機。 (2) 請同學務必參加考試，考試當天缺席者以〝缺考〞處理。若遇 不可抗拒之因素需請事假，需於考試前向授課教師請假申請補考。 2 授課大綱: 1. Introduction 2. 李嘉圖模型 (KOM: Ch.3) ➢ 以國家間生產技術的差異解釋國家間貿易形成的原因 3. 特定要素模型 (KOM: Ch.4) ➢ 分析自由貿易在短期間對一國不同生產要素擁有者所得之影響(如:雇 主 vs 勞工) ➢ 分析勞工的跨國移動(如:外國白領人才、藍領勞工、移民)在短期與長 期下對一國所得分配的影響 4. HO 模型 (KOM: Ch.5) ➢ 以國家間生產資源分佈差異解釋國家間貿易形成的原因 ➢ 分析自由貿易在長期下對一國不同生產要素擁有者所得之影響 ➢ 分析勞工的跨國移動(如:外國白領人才、藍領勞工、移民)在長期下對 一國所得分配的影響 5. 經濟成長與國際貿易 (KOM, Ch.6) ➢ 當國家生產技術進步或生產資源增加，對一國貿易條件與福利之影響 6. 外部規模經濟與國際貿易 (KOM: Ch.7) 7. 內部規模經濟、不完全競爭與貿易 (KOM: Ch.8) ➢ 解釋產業內貿易發生的原因 ➢ 解釋個別廠商出口決策與對外投資(國際分工)的行為 ➢ 分析廠商國際分工對勞動市場的影響(FT: Ch. 7) 8. 貿易政策 (KOM: Ch.9) ➢ 關稅的經濟效果-大國 v.s. 小國 ➢ 關稅與配額比較: 完全競爭市場 v.s. 不完全競爭市場 ➢ 出口補貼、傾銷與其他非關稅貿易政策工具 9. 貿易干預的理論基礎 (KOM: Ch.10,11,12) ➢ 介紹政府限制貿易的理由與工具

docs.text: ECON 504200 Machine learning and econometrics: concepts and procedures (機器學習與計量經濟: 概念與程序) National Tsing Hua University 1st semester, 2025-2026 Time: 3:30pm - 6:20pm, every Tuesday (T7T8T9) except September 23. Make-up class will be arranged. Venue: TSMC 205 Office hours: By appointment Instructor: CY (Chor-yiu) SIN (Office: CTM-804, Email: cysin@mx.nthu.edu.tw, Phone: 03-516-2134) Course description: Since Varian (2014), people have been believing that machine learning uses data to predict some variable as a function of other variables, while econometrics use statistical methods for prediction, inference, and causal modeling of economic relationships. However, nowadays some tend to believe that machine learning is the new generation nonparametric statistical and econometric methods, branded as machine learning (Chernozhukov et al. 2017). While academically rigorous theorems are much appreciated, they are not the focus of this course. Instead, this course starts with basic concepts of machine learning and econometrics; and ends with procedural computer codes. Students are required to be familiar with at least one software such as Python, R or C++. This course discusses the basic concepts with examples in economics and management. Hands-on exercises with the software “Python”. Course topics: 1. Revision on (a) prediction with linear regression (b) classification with logit/probit model 2. The essential tools in computer age statistical inference: (a) Monte-Carlo simulation; (b) Bootstrapping; (c) Cross-validation (CV) 3. Linear model selection and regularization: (a) Ridge regression; (b) Elastic net; (c) Lasso; (d) Best subset regression plus CV/information criterion (IC) 4. Tree-based methods and boosting: with an introduction to gradient boosting 5. Baic topic in deep learning: Feedforward neural network 6. Baic topic in deep learning: Recurrent neural network (RNN) and Long short-term memory network (LSTM) 7. Intermediate topic in deep learning: Convolutional neural network (CNN). 8. Intermediate topic in deep learning: “You only look once” (YOLO) 9. Introduction to basic generative adversarial network (GAN); 10. Introduction to reinforcement learning (RL) 11. Generalized linear model: with an introduction to support vector machine (SVM) 12. Re-sampling approach to (a) Interval estimation; (b) P-value Textbooks and papers: (1) Chernozhukov, V., Chetverikov, D., Demirer, M., Duflo, E., Hansen, C., Newey, W., 2017. Double/debiased/Neyman machine learning of treatment effects. American Economic Review: Papers and Proceedings 107, 261-265. (2) Efron, B., Hastie, T., 2016. Computer age statistical inference: algorithms, evidence and data science. Cambridge, U.S.: Cambridge University Press. (3) Hansen, B.E., 2022. Econometrics. New Jersey, U.S.: Princeton University Press (4) James, G., Witten, D., Hastie, T., Tibshirani, R., Taylor, J., 2023. An introduction to statistical learning with applications in Python. New York, U.S.: Springer Science+Business Media (https://www.statlearning.com/) (5) Varian, H.R., 2014. Big data: new tricks for econometrics. The Journal of Economic Perspectives 28, 3-27. Assessment: Attendance and participation in discussions 40%, mid-term examination 30%, final examination: 30%. (Only grades will be given for each part of the assessment. Student leave applications must be submitted in-person to the instructor.) Attitude taken in this course: Be humble, careful and simple, positive and gentle. Needless to say, be logical. - End -

docs.text: 1 Family Economics Spring 2023 M7M8M9 Classroom: TSMC(台積館) Room 428 Course Description: This course focuses on research on family and demographic economics. Students will be introduced to a wide range of research topics related to family and demographic economics and learn to develop the ability to conduct research in this field. The study of families and households is an important research area given the increasingly complex organization of families, which have produced substantial effects on behavior of households and welfare of children as well as spouses. We will focus on the theoretical modeling and empirical investigation of how individuals sort into families (cohabitation, marriage and divorce) and of the major economic outcomes determined in a family context (such as spousal time allocation, labor supply (particularly the changing role of women in the labor force), fertility, consumption, investments in children and intergenerational transfers. Of particular importance are the various classes of household models and their testable implications on family decisions. We will also investigate family laws and policies from the economic perspective and draw insights from research studies in sociology and demography on the family. Method of Instruction: Lecture/Discussion Course Website and Communication: Courses materials are available on our course website in the eeclass system (eeclass 數位學習 平台). Readings, usually academic articles, will be assigned throughout this course. Students are expected to participate in the discussion of papers covered in each topic. The links for the papers and selected articles and lectures notes will be posted on the course website. So please make sure to regularly check the course website. Instructor: Crystal Wong (黃賀寶) Office: TSMC (台積館) Room 704 Office Hours: By Appointment Email: hpwong@mx.nthu.edu.tw 2 Requirements: This course is intended for students interested in learning and conducting demographic research. Knowledge of calculus, and statistics are required. (We will discuss both theoretical and empirical studies on the subject and you will be required to provide critiques of these works.) In-Class Presentation (in English) Each student would be assigned a paper on the reading list and present it in class. The presentation should be about 40 minutes long. docs.text: Macroeconomic Analysis I Fall, 2025 Instructor: Ching-Yi Lin Class Meeting: M567 Office Hours: M 12:00-13:00 Office: TSMC 831 Email: lincy@mx.nthu.edu.tw The objective of this course is to familiarize graduate students with quantitative methods in advanced macroeconomics and introduce some fundamental workhorse models and methods of formal macroeconomics analysis. The main difference between undergraduate and graduate macroeconomics is the use of models that are explicitly dynamic and stochastic. Dynamic general equilibrium (DGE) macroeconomics by providing microeconomic foundation for macroeconomics has emerged in recent years and been adopted by most modern research in macroeconomics as a leading approach. Course material will be drawn from several sources. Suggested text is “Advanced Macroeconomics, David Romer” and “Barro and Sala-i-Martin, Economic Growth, Appendix”. Evaluation: Homework and quizzes:20% Midterms: 40% Final: 40% Course Outline: 1. Differential Equations 2. Useful Results in Calculus 3. Useful Results in Matrix Algebra 4. Static Optimization 5. Dynamic Optimization in Continuous-Time Economic Models 6. Dynamic Programming 7. The Solow Growth model (Romer ch1) 8. Infinite-Horizon and Overlapping-Generations Models (Romer ch2) 9. Real Business Cycle Model

docs.text: 1 National Tsing Hua University Department of Economics Theory of Public Economics I, Fall 2025 Time: Wednesday 9-12noon Classroom: 732 TSMC Building Professor: Wu, Shih-Ying Office: 711 TSMC Building, Tel: ext 62031, E-mail: wus@mx.nthu.edu.tw Office hours: by appointment Introduction: The course will analyze issues in public economics, which can be categorized into four parts: (1) tax effects on economic behaviors; (2) issues on the income and wealth inequality in Taiwan and the world; (3) individual charitable donations; and others. The part of tax effects will investigate the tax effects on individuals’ economic behaviors, mainly including business investment and tax compliance. The part on inequality will discuss empirical evidence on income and wealth inequality and examine various rationales for the increasing inequality around the world since the 1980s. It will also analyze the negative impacts of income and wealth inequality on the society and evaluate possible remedies, especially tax policies, to alleviate the increasing inequality. The part on individual charitable donations will discuss the theoretical rationales underlying individuals’ charitable giving and analyze the buzzing empirical studies based on field experiments in the past decade. Besides, depending on students’ interest, the topics in some weeks listed below can be adjusted. Prerequisite: Undergraduate-level intermediate microeconomics Readings: The readings for this course are mainly journal articles and working papers. Lecture notes for most of the weeks will be available on the website of eeclass. Grading: A take-home exam will comprise 30%, a term paper will comprise 40%, and critical presentations and comments for assigned papers (2-3 times, depending on the enrollment) will comprise the remaining 30% of the course score. 2 Format for critical presentation: 50 minutes including Q&A. The time for presentation is short but the assignment is usually a full paper including background, theoretical framework, econometric specification, data, results and discussion.
