docs.name: 學士論文一
docs.text:
人文社會學院學士班 「學士論文」修課說明與規定

一、為鼓勵同學整合前三年所受的專業訓練、培養獨立研究的能力，特增設此課程，也同時期盼同
學在畢業前能夠凝聚出具體成果，預先為深造或就業做好準備。

二、在每學年上學期開設「學士論文一」( 1學分) 、下學期開設「學士論文二」( 2學分)，並於
第二學期結束前繳交成果報告一份至系辦公室存檔。

三、採師生一對一指導方式，限人社系大四學生選修，有意選修者須在大三下學期結束前事先徵得
指導教授同意，才得選修。

四、論文完成時得舉行論文口試，口試委員2位，並依口試委員之意見作修改。

五、鼓勵有意選修「學士論文」之同學，在大三下學期(三月間)以同一研究為主題申請「大專學生
參與國科會專題研究計畫」獎勵方案。

docs.name: 當代中國社會與電影
docs.text:
暫定

一、課程簡介：

新世紀以來，中國加入WTO之後，綜合國力快速增長，中共透過黨國主控的市場經濟將經濟發展的結果轉換成兩
個

支撐黨國延續的重要支柱：（1）強化集權能力的數位列寧主義，（2）以民族主義為內核，結合軍事硬實力與統
戰銳

實力的混合戰略，放棄「韜光養晦」，積極對外投射政治軍事經濟力量，以實現「中華民族偉大復興」的政治號
召。

中國利用全球建制力量深陷對抗宗教極端主義的反恐戰爭和欠缺適應經濟金融治理所導致的全球經濟大衰退之
中，趁

勢而起。

與此同時，中國社會也正處在快速變遷的過程中，變化的速度與往往令人驚奇，而有時其大膽的程度又令人
瞠

目結舌。但是，八九鎮壓肅殺氣氛稍稍緩和後朝向多元開放的民間社會，在習近平接掌大位之後似乎卻有逆轉的
情

況。維權律師被大抓捕、婦運同運被整肅、連學術界一息尚存的自由主義氣氛也在強調政治正確之下完全蒸發。
在美

中多層次對抗的同時，中國社會卻也面臨前所未有的險峻挑戰，未富先老、所得不均、福利體制尚待建立等標示
著中

國正深陷「中等收入陷阱」，而香港抗暴起義和港中政府的壓制和起源武漢的Covid19疫情全球蔓延也暴露了中共
的

專政治理模式的危機。

中國社會這一切卻又跟台灣息息相關：一度在中國找到「第二春」的台商徬徨尋找下一個生產基地，曾經關
係

緊密的兩岸社運忙著救援昔日夥伴，台生台師在優惠待遇下西進，中共銳實力全面滲透台灣基層社會。這門課意
圖提

升學生的中國識讀能力，在夾雜真假訊息中辨別真相，在混沌中搜尋方向，也能透過社會科學基本訓練來了解中
國社

會。我們將透過紀錄片觀賞、課堂（與課後）討論、以及閱讀、大量的閱讀來發展理解分析中國社會的基本框
架。面

對這樣的衝突要如何去認識中國呢？

電影是理解中國發展的鮮活教材。本課程將藉由影像為媒介，透過導讀與討論，將中國置於其發展的歷史脈絡，
觀看

與解讀中國社會在歷經共產主義革命、文化大革命、改革開放、與全球化的面貌與軌跡，試圖從鮮活的電影故事
中，

探索這個社會最隱密的身世之謎。

課程內容選擇關於中國改革開放以來最具代表性的影片與導演、以及重要的紀錄片。除了藉此指認中國社會結構
深刻

的變遷與矛盾外，也凸顯個人與人性在其中呈現的形貌與遭逢的扭曲與衝擊。課程的目的在使修課同學對於當代
中國

過去、現在與未來能有多面向的認識與深度的理解。

本課程沒有預設學科背景，但對當代中國社會的好奇心則是必要條件，長短不拘的中國遊歷經驗會有幫助，但沒
有這

個經歷也完全不是問題。社會科學訓練不是前提，但以身為度和同情了解的能力是必要的裝備。

二、指定書目與延伸閱讀：

莫里斯‧邁斯納，2005，《毛澤東的中國及其後毛：中華人民共和國史》。香港：香港中文大學出版社。（譯自：

Meisner, Maurice. 1999. Mao’s China and After: A History of the People’s Republic, 3rd edition. New York:

Free Press.）

羅德里克‧麥克法夸爾（Roderick MacFarquhar），沈邁克（Michael Schoenhals）著，關心譯，2009，《毛澤
東

最後的革命》。台北：左岸文化。（譯自：Roderick MacFarquhar and Michael Schoenhals. 2006. Mao’s Last

Revolution. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press.）

Elizabeth C. Economy. 2018. The Third Revolution: Xi Jinping and the New Chinese State. Oxford: Oxford

University Press.）

其他參考書目：

docs.name: 漢字學習
docs.text:
● 課程說明(Course Description)
本課程針對國際生學習漢字設計，除了認識並練習漢字書寫之外，最重要的是降低學生對於漢字
的焦慮，協助學生運用漢字生動性、系統性、邏輯性的特點，達到觸類旁通，倍增漢字量的成效。
課程主要內容分為三大部分：
一、寫字：認識漢字架構、書寫方式並充分練習。15%
二、記字：認識部首、部件，藉造字方法及字源以系統性增加識字量。75%
三、查字：利用數位工具輔助學習漢字。10%

● 指定用書(Text Books)：無，教材為教師自編。

● 參考書籍(References)
許慎，《圈點說文解字》，臺北：萬卷樓，2002
周碧香、陳玉明、馬偉怡、戚恕平《漢字好好教 好好教漢字—華語師培與漢字教學》，臺北：五南，
2024
馬燕華，《漢字入門》，北京：北京語言大學出版社，2017
黃沛榮，《漢字教學的理論與實踐》，臺北：樂學書局，2009
游國慶，《趣味的甲骨金文》，臺北：國立故宮博物院，2012

● 教學方式(Teaching Method)
理論講述與討論(60)%(說明：教師講述漢字理據，分組討論議題)
行動實作與報告(40)%(說明：包含平時學生分組實作及期中報告)

● 教學進度(Syllabus)
第一部分 概念（3週）
第一課 漢字簡史
第二課 漢字認、記、寫的學習策略
第三課 漢字架構與寫字
第四課 漢字查字及自學資源
第二部分 認識漢字、倍增漢字（14週）
第五課 從「人」學起
第六課 從「人體」學起
第七課 從「動物」學起
第八課 從「植物」學起
第九課 從「山川氣象」學起
期中考
第十課 從「飲食」學起
第十一課 從「服飾」學起
第十二課 從「房子」學起
第十三課 從「工具」學起
第十四課 從「交通」學起
第十五課 綜合探討
期末考

● 成績考核(Evaluation)
出席率與課堂參與 25%
課後功課 20%
期中考 25%
期末考 30%

● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website)
中華語文知識庫──漢字源流 http://chinese-linguipedia.org/search_source.html
漢語多功能字庫 https://humanum.arts.cuhk.edu.hk/Lexis/lexi-mf/
萌典 https://www.moedict.tw
MDBG https://www.mdbg.net/chinese/dictionary

● 學生使用 AI 的聲明 (Student use of AI)：有條件開放 Conditionally open)

基於透明與負責任的原則，本課程鼓勵學生利用AI進行協作或互學，以提升本門課產出品質。根據
本校公布之佈的「大學教育場域AI協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採取有條件開放，如何使用
生成式AI於作業或報告，說明如下：

學生須於課堂作業或報告中的「標題頁註腳」或「引用文獻後」簡要說明如何使用生成式AI進行議
題發想、文句潤飾或結構參考等使用方式。然而，在本課程的「個人反思報告」、「小組採訪作業」
中，學生不得使用生成式AI工具撰寫作業。若經查核使用卻無在作業或報告中標明，教師、學校或
相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。

本門課授課教材或學習資料若有引用自生成式AI，教師也將在投影片或口頭標注。

修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。

docs.text: 114 上 國立清華大學清華學院國際學士班課程大綱 科號 Course Number 1110IBP 100201 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Size of Limit 20 中文名稱 Course Title 聽力與口說(一)A 英文名稱 Course English Title Listening and Speaking (1) 任課教師 Instructor 陳慶華 上課時間 Time F3F4 星期五/10:10-12:00 上課教室 Room 教 102 提醒您：請遵守智慧財產權，勿使用非法影印教科書 Please respect the intellectual property rights, do not use illegal copies of textbooks. 課程簡述 (Brief course description) 聽說技能是外籍生學習中文的難點。聽與說是不可分的，所以聽與說之教學應同時進行。 此課程將介紹聽力理解與口說的要領。課程進行將逐項介紹聽與說之各項技能，並逐項訓 練，將聽說之理論體現於課室教學中。 訓練聽力理解時，以「聽」為主，以「說、讀、寫」為輔。聽力課程採五種教學方式： 聽辨訓練、聽讀訓練、聽寫訓練、聽說訓練、聽測訓練。教學過程劃分為聽前、聽時及聽 後等三大步驟，再細分為若干項教學策略，如提問、聽時交換資訊、推論等策略。 訓練口說時，以「說」為主，以「聽、讀、寫」為輔。採任務型訓練方式，如:角色扮演、 採訪、戲劇、辯論等策略。 授課方式 老師講授、師生互動、小組討論、活動練習、任務型教學 成績考核 出席 + 課堂參與 Attendance & Class Participation：30% (1)上課表現 15%（上課態度、會話練習、手機使用等） (2)出 缺 席 15% (包括遲到) 缺席一次扣一分。 期中考（筆試+口試）Midterm (written & oral)：35% 期末考（成果+口語表達）Final Exam (written & oral)：35% 課程進度表 (會依照教學需要 而做調整或修改） 週 進度 1 聽力課與口說課之概述及授課方式之介紹 2-3 聽力技能訓練:初級階段 4-5 聽力技能訓練:中級階段 6-7 聽力技能訓練:高級階段(運用網路廣播節目) 8 期中考 (聽力測驗 ) 9-10 任務型說話訓練:語音、詞彙 11-12 任務型說話訓練:句子、篇章 13-14 任務型說話訓練:聽後說說看或辯論 15 成果展(分組短劇表演、說故事比賽、訪談) 16 期末考(個人演說) 備註 Remarks 選修限制:當代中文四「中高一」以上，包括中高一。

docs.text: 114 上 國立清華大學清華學院國際學士班課程大綱 科號 Course Number 11410IBP 100301 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Size of Limit 20 中文名稱 Course Title 華語發音與正音 A 英文名稱 Course English Title Mandarin Pronunciation 任課教師 Instructor 陳慶華 0939-590201 helenchen37@yahoo.com 上課時間 Time F1F2 (星期五/8:00-9:50) 上課教室 Room 教 102 課程簡述 (Brief course description) 發音是外籍生學習中文時首當其衝的難點，即使已學到高級程度發音仍難準確。 此課程重在訓練學習者中文發音的準確程度，力求學習者音準調正。課程進行時， 首先詳細介紹華語的聲、韻、調，讓學生感知且真正明白。之後藉由各種發音訓練， 讓學生熟悉中文的字調、語調、語氣，並能正確表達。並時時糾音、正音。以字正腔圓 為最終目標。 授課方式 老師講授、師生互動、小組討論、活動練習、任務型教學 成績考核 出席 + 課堂參與 Attendance & Class Participation：30% (1)上課表現 15%（上課態度、會話練習、手機使用等） (2)出 缺 席 15% (包括遲到) 期中考（筆試+口語表達）Midterm (written & oral)：35% 期末考（筆試+口語表達）Final Exam (written & oral)：35% 課程進度表 (會依照教學需要 而做調整或修改） 週 進度 1 華語語音概說與發音檢測 2-3 華語聲調(一聲/二聲/三聲/四聲/輕聲)、[一/不]與[三聲]變調 4-5 華語韻母發音與練習/正音(Finals) 6-7 華語聲母發音與練習/正音(Initials) 8 期中考 筆試(華語發音基本知識) +口試(朗讀與師生對話) 9-10 華語的輕重音與語音的變化 11-12 華語易混淆音之對比與練習 13-14 朗讀的要領與練習 15 成果展(分組話劇表演) 16 期末考 筆試(華語發音基本知識)+口試(華語口語與表達)

docs.text: 國立清華大學清華學院國際學士班課程大綱【甲組-華語與專業學科】 科號 11410IBP 100800 中文名稱 <生命教育> 英文名稱 < Life Education> 任課教師 陳淑娟、顏秀芬 上課時間 Time 週二 15:30-17:20 一、課程之教學目標 從全人教育的人與自己、人與他人、人與環境、人與宇宙四個面向，為此生命教育課程架構。 期能達成 1. 增進對於個人生命的探索、認識與價值的重視。 2. 立志效學典範、楷定生命方向、探索生命意義。 3. 提升學習者主動關懷周遭生命、建立良好人際關係,涵養積極因應未來生活挑戰之態度。 4. 透由實踐利他的服務過程，創造生命價值，對生命充滿希望與熱誠。 5. 透由正念的練習, 開展平靜、安定、專注、善良、感恩的心，提升專注力與情緒管理。 二、教學方法 教師講述、影片教學、分組討論、分組報告 三、教學進度 周次 日期 課程名稱 備註 1 課程與評量/分組/相見歡 總說: 親手鑄造自己美好的未來 課程與評量/相見歡/認識自他 2 正念、覺知、身體掃描 正念: 覺知呼吸 3 科技的的真相 - 網路電子科技可以帶給我們快樂嗎? 正念: 身體掃描 4 身心出走、留白的幸福、打開五感– 沒有網路電子科 技我快樂嗎? 正念: 感恩練習 5 觀功念恩 正念: 慈心祝福 6 感恩禮讚 正念: 立姿伸展/正念行走 7 我的學思歷程 - 陳淑娟老師 正念: 壓力事件 8 期中報告：幸福專賣店 9 期中報告：幸福專賣店 10 正念溝通 正念: 仁慈時刻(找資源) 11 正念聆聽 正念: 正念行走 12 壓力的因應：有覺察地回應 VS 慣性反應 正念: 換位練習 13 壓力的因應：有覺察地回應 VS 慣性反應 正念: 覺知呼吸 14 期末報告：敘說幸福感恩願景實踐計畫 正念: 一次一件事 15 期末報告：敘說幸福感恩願景實踐計畫 16 幸福感恩禮讚+課程回饋與總結 四、參考資料 ⚫ Gandhi, Mahatm 著，C. F. Andrews 編。1987。甘地 : 他就是印度。台北巿：北辰文化。 ⚫ Yunus,Muhanmmad，Alan Jolis 著，曾育慧譯。2007。窮人的銀行家：尤努斯打造無貧世 界。台北市：聯經。 ⚫ 塔爾‧班夏哈 (Tal Ben-Shahar)作，李芳齡譯。2013 幸福的魔法：更快樂的 101 個選擇 台 北市 : 天下雜誌 ⚫ 塔爾‧班夏哈 (Tal Ben-Shahar)作，譚家瑜。 2012 更快樂:哈佛最受歡迎的一堂課(新版) 台 北市 : 天下雜誌 ⚫ 嚴長壽。2008。做自己與別人生命中的天使。台北市：寶瓶文化 ⚫ 常少波。2013。從電腦天才到世界慈善家：比爾．蓋茲全傳。文經閣出版社。 ⚫ 釋一行 (Nhat Hanh, Thich)作, 何蕙儀譯。一行禪師說佛陀故事。台北市 : 法鼓文化, 民 94. ⚫ 張尤娟。1999/03。慈心飲食,保育大地--販賣誠信的里仁商店。新觀念 125 期，頁 94-96。 ⚫ 威爾.鮑溫 Will Bowen 著，陳敬旻譯(2008)。不抱怨的世界。台北市 : 時報文化 ⚫ Nichols, Michael P.,著, 邱珍琬譯(1989)。傾聽 : 人際關係中溝通的藝術。台北市 : 遠流 ⚫ 喬．卡巴金 Jon Kabat-Zinn Ph.D. 2013。正念療癒力：八週找回平靜、自信與智慧的自己 （卡巴金博士二十年經典增訂版）台北市:野人出版社。 五、成績考核 一、平時成績 30% 1.出席 20% (本學期點名 10 次，每次 2 分，準時上課者 2 分，遲到者 1 分。事先請假第一次缺席不扣分， 之後每次扣 2 分。無故三次缺席者，出席成績以 0 分計算。) 2 課堂參與度(課堂參與度+不使用手機 10 分) 二、口頭報告 : 50 % ◆ 小組報告 20% ◆ 個人期末報告 20 % 三 、平常作業: 20% ◆ 我想認識你 10% ◆ 幸福銀行 10% 四、 期末回顧心得學習單 10% 作業說明: (一) 小組報告: 形式：透過多媒體方式呈現 報告時間：每組 15-18 分鐘 【幸福專賣店】以小組為單位彙整，向全班介紹日常生活中，讓自己感受到幸福的方法， 如：一本好書、一首動人的歌曲、一部發人省思的電影、一個心靈沉澱的角落……等。 以主題性、整體性、故事性…等方式，彙整成一個報告跟全班分享。20 % (二) 個人報告: 形式：透過多媒體方式呈現 報告時間：每人 3-5 分鐘 【幸福感恩禮讚】敘說幸福感恩願景實踐計畫。 如：為父母做一件令他們歡喜的事、父母生命故事的訪談並製成小影片、為師長擦黑板一周 書寫自己生命故事、與有誤會的同學道歉等。 20 % (三) 平常作業: 【幸福銀行】發送幸福存摺，一天挪出個 10 分鐘，想出並記錄讓你心懷感激的 5 件事。 10% (四) 平常作業: 【我想認識你】認識全班同學(記下名字+學號+系級) 訪問 3 個問題，並記下他的答案 10% (五) 期末回顧心得學習單 10%

docs.text: 1 National Tsing Hua University (NTHU) Course Title: International Etiquette and Cross-Cultural Communication Course Description: 1. This course is primarily initiated to help NTHU students acquire knowledge and understanding of international etiquette in terms of its norms and practices. 2. Major teaching emphasis will be developing "2Cs": Culture & Career. Culturally speaking, students will be taught to create a basic global perspective & cross-cultural sensitivity, and, on the career front, to familiarize themselves with tips on job interviews & international business meetings /travels. 3. In addition to lectures/discussions, videos & field trips will be introduced, depending on availability, to enable students to learn in a fun & friendly environment. Teaching Objectives: To help students possess top-notch manners & social skills, which come from quality etiquette guidance and will make them stand out from any peers personally & professionally. Teaching Syllabus: 1. Basic etiquette in clothing, Food, Housing, Transportation, Education & Entertainment. 2. The difference and competition between Western Christian civilization and Eastern Buddhist culture. 3. Etiquette models of Asian and Western countries. 4. Survival tips for job interviews. 5. Cultivation and practice of Sense of Humor. 6. Etiquette in the international business world. Teaching Methods: Lecture, Discussions, Appreciation, Simulation, Visit Evaluation: Study Assignments (20%), Class Attendance and Discussions (including in classroom and online) (40%), Individual Reports (including oral and written) (20%) and Group Reports (20%). Textbook: 《The Practical Use of International Etiquette》(2020) References: Magazine/periodical articles and other designated reading requirements 2 Course schedule: Week 1: Course introduction Week 2: Self-introduction of students (selected by drawing lots) Week 3: Basic Introduction to Etiquette in Food, Clothing, Housing, Transportation, Education & Entertainment (1) Week 4: Basic Introduction to Etiquette in Food, Clothing, Housing, Transportation, Education & Entertainment (2) Week 5: The difference and competition between Western Christian civilization and Eastern Buddhist feudalism Week 6: Etiquette models and cultural background of Asian countries (1) Week 7: Etiquette models and cultural background of Asian countries (2) Week 8: Etiquette models and cultural background of Western countries (1) Week 9: Etiquette models and cultural background of Western countries (2) Week 10: Midterm report (written individually) Week 11: Field Trip (further coordination is required) Week 12: Case study of international celebrities' etiquette Week 13: Etiquette in school and in the workplace Week 14: Survival Tips for job interviews Week 15: Fine Line between Sense of Humor & Cultural Faux Pas Week 16: Etiquette in the business world Week 17: Final report (1) (by study groups in the form of role-playing) Week 18: Final report (2) (by study groups in the form of role-playing) Regarding AIGC using: Ethics Statement on Generative Artificial Intelligence Grounded in the principles of transparency and responsibility, this course encourages students to leverage AI for collaboration and mutual learning to enhance the quality of course outputs. In accordance with the published Guidelines for Collaboration, Co-learning, and Cultivation of Artificial Intelligence Competencies in University Education, this course adopts the following policy： Conditionally open Students may briefly explain how generative AI was used for topic ideation, sentence refinement, or structural reference in the footnotes of the title page or after the bibliography in their assignments or reports. However, in the "personal reflection report" and "group interview assignment" of this course, students are not allowed to use generative AI tools for writing assignments. If usage is discovered without proper disclosure, instructors, the institution, or relevant units have the right to reevaluate the assignment or report or withhold scores. If the course materials or learning resources have been derived from generative AI, the instructor will also indicate this in the slides or orally. Students enrolled in this course agree to the above ethics statement if registering for the class.

業、報告或個人心得。若經查核發現，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業 或報告重新評分或不予計分。 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。 ● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website) 教師個人作品網站: shihfen.myportfolio.com

Classroom: EDU 教 115 Telephone #: 03-5715131-72817 0930625770 Email: thtseng@mx.nthu.edu.tw ■Course Description: This course provides an introduction to the leisure, tourism and hospitality industry. It also introduces and explains the importance of tourism, explaining the effects of supply and demand on the economy, culture and the environment. Students will be able to approach various facets of tourism, including: ecotourism; urban tourism; community-based tourism; agricultural tourism; religious tourism; tourism planning, management and policy; and the future of tourism. A multifaceted understanding of tourism allows students to critically evaluate and apprehend tourism policies and activities on economic, social, and environmental domains. ■Course Module Objectives: 1. Jerome McCarthy, coauthor of Basic Marketing and Essentials of Marketing. While the four Ps are an oversimplification, they do provide a neat, simple framework in which to look at marketing and put together a marketing program. The four Ps are product, place, promotion, and price. The product includes not only the actual physical attributes of the product but also product plan- ning, product development, breadth of the line, branding, and packaging. Planning the product should consider all these aspects in order to come up with the “right” product. Place is really concerned with distribution. What agencies, channels, and institutions can be linked together most effectively to give the consumer easy access to the purchase of your product? Where is the “right” place to market your product? Promotion communicates the benefits of the product to the potential custom- ers and includes not only advertising but also sales promotion, public relations, and personal selling. The “right” promotional mix will use each of these promotional techniques as needed for effective communication. Price is a critical variable in the marketing mix. The “right” price must both satisfy customers and meet your profit objectives. Mill and Morrison3 have added another “three Ps” that they believe are particularly relevant to tourism. Programming involves special activities, events, or other types of programs to increase customer spending or to give added appeal to a package or other tourism service. As noted in Chapter 15, tourism policy views programs as a strategic consolidation of a range of different activities designed to ensure a clear focus for development and marketing efforts. The second of the additional three Ps concerns people. This P is intended to stress that tourism is a “people business”—that we must not lose sight of the importance of providing travel experiences that are sensitive to the human side of the visitor as well as to the functional requirements. The final P is defined as partnership. This highlights the high degree of interdepend- ency among all destination stakeholders, as well as the need for alliances and working relationships that build a cooperation—sometimes with competitors as well as col- leagues. docs.text: Forms in Nature I. Abstract This course explores the rich and varied forms found in nature, alongside the mathematical and physical ideas that illuminate them. We begin with projective geometry, examining how perception shapes our understanding of the world. From there, we investigate archetypal patterns including symmetry, curves, waves, spirals, and fractals. Each topic is paired with hands-on activities, enabling students to experience the intersection of beauty and science through direct engagement with the natural world. II. Introduction Our journey begins by investigating natural forms—from the geometric order of crystals to the spirals found in shells and galaxies. Alongside these visual and structural patterns, we study the mathematical and physical frameworks that reveal their underlying logic: projective geometry, crystallography, calculus, trigonometric functions, Fourier analysis, and fractal geometry. The course emphasizes experiential learning, integrating artistic practice with scientific exploration. Activities such as pendulum drawing, curve sketching, and modeling celestial motion highlight the unity between nature, mathematics, and art. III. References The references are listed as below 1. What Is Mathematics? An Elementary Approach to Ideas and Methods 2nd Edition ISBN-10 0195105192 2. Projective geometry, H. S. M. Coxeter. ISBN 0387406239 3. Understanding Physics, Cassidy, Holton, and Rutherford, ISBN 1-4757-7698-5 (e-book) 4. Geometry of Grief: Reflections on Mathematics, Loss, and Life, Michael Frame (2021), ISBN-10 022680092X IV. Syllabus Week 1: Introduction and Overview (9/1) Overview of the course Syllabus and evaluation What we are going to do in the semester Week 2: Perceiving the world (9/8) Vision: How human vision works Euclidean Geometry: the five postulates (focus on the 5th) Projective Geometry: parallel lines, viewing from higher dimension Hands-on: Games of lines and points Week 3: Perspective Drawing (9/15) Perspective Drawing: from 3D to 2D Desargues’ Theorem Cross ratio Presenting Infinity Hands-on: Perspective drawing Week 4: Duality and equivalence (9/22) Cartesian and Homogeneous Coordinates Point-line duality and more Desargues theorem revisited Hands-on: Duality in pairs Week 5: Symmetry and Crystal Structures (9/29) Crystals patterns: cubes, honeycomb Unit cell, lattice structures Symmetry: mirror, glide, rotation axes Crystallography and diffraction (Fourier series) Hands-on: Symmetry modeling and crystal patterns Week 6: Holiday: Full Moon Festival (10/6) Week 7: Changes and Curves (10/13) Meanders and turning Tangents and curvature Instantaneous speed and motion Hands-on: Walking on curves and sketching tangents Week 8: Midterm Examination (10/20) Week 9: Rhythms (10/27) Vibrations: pendulums and springs Simple harmonic motion Period and amplitude Hands-on: Measure periods with pendulums Week 10: Waves (11/3) Sound waves, water waves Reflection, refraction, diffraction Principle of least action Hands-on: Tones and scales Week 11: Periodic Motion (11/10) Derivatives of Trigonometric functions Physical meaning: velocity and acceleration Basics of differential equations for motion Hands-on: Pendulum drawing and analysis Week 12: Wave-like Patterns (11/17) Zebra stripes, fish patterns, sand dunes Moire pattern and Turing pattern Self-organization and emergence Hands-on: Drawing fractals Week 13: Campus Tour (11/24) Looking for natural forms: leaves, veins, branches, spirals Self-similarity in nature Hands-on: Drawing and analyzing forms Week 14: Spirals (12/1) Shells, galaxies, whirlpools, pinecones Fibonacci sequence, golden angle Growth spirals and logarithmic spirals Hands-on: Construct and sketch spirals Week 15: Fractals (12/8) Koch curve, Sierpinski triangle, Cantor cubes Natural fractals: ferns, trees, lightning Fractal dimension: concept and examples Hands-on: Draw fractals and estimate dimension Week 16: Final Examination and Course Reflection (12/15) V. Evaluation 1. Initial attendance 4%: Students who want to take this course are required to attend for the first two weeks (9/1, 9/8). 2. Participation (Week 3-16 except Week 6, 8, 16) 22% 3. Midterm Examination 20% 4. Final Examination 30% 5. Hand-on activities 20% 6. Bonus 4% 7. An A+ indicates the students achieve all goals beyond expectation. Students with two unexcused absences in the whole semester will not receive grade of A+. VI. Grading Policy for Attendance This policy is designed to promote fairness, responsibility, and clarity throughout the semester. Attendance and participation are essential to the course experience. For consistency, attendance is graded separately from in-class activities and presentations, and make-up opportunities are limited to specific circumstances. 1. Initial Attendance (Week 1-2) These first two weeks are for orientation and course adjustment. 1. Each week counts for 2% of the final grade (total: 4%). 2. Absence results in zero attendance points. 3. Students absent for both weeks will not be eligible for extra enrollment approval. 2. Regular Instruction Weeks (Week 3-16 except Week 6, 8, 16, 22%) 1. Each week’s attendance counts for 1% of the final grade. 2. Absence for any reason results in zero for both attendance and any activities conducted that week. Students with valid documentation (illness, bereavement, or official leave) may still submit “questions for today” and discussion on e-Learn in time (1%). 3. If the session includes a hands-on activity, students with valid documentation (illness, bereavement, or official leave) may still submit the report or assignments for the hands- on activity in time. Such reports will be graded at 70% of the original score. 3. Examination (Midterm 20%, Final 30%) 1. Absence from the midterm exam results in a score of zero. 2. Students with valid documentation (illness, bereavement, or official leave) may request a make-up exam. 3. Make-up exams will be graded at 70% of the original score. 4. It is the student’s responsibility to contact the TA in advance to schedule the make-up exam. VII. The use of AI is conditionally open. You may use AI to check the grammar of your reports, but NOT for writing or generating articles. VIII. The content above may be subject to change based on actual circumstances. Updated information will be announced in class or on e-Learn.

docs.name: 漢字與中國文化
docs.text:
● 課程說明(Course Description)
本課程帶領學生認識反映在漢字中的中國歷史文化，認識中國歷史演進進程，了解其對漢字的影
響。並藉由學習漢字本義及引申義的發展，促進漢字記憶與應用。能具備漢字與中華文化相關知
識，增進跨文化溝通能力。

● 指定用書(Text Books)
許進雄著，2020《文字學家的甲骨學研究室：了解甲骨文不能不學的13堂必修課》。台灣商務。
林西莉 (Cecilia Lindqvist) 著，2016《漢字的故事》。貓頭鷹出版社
自編教材

● 參考書籍(References)
許進雄著，2013《中國古代社會：文字與人類學的透視》。臺灣商務印書館
許進雄著，2018《漢字與文物的故事》系列四書。臺灣商務印書館
方麗娜著，2017《華人社會與文化（增訂版）》。正中書局
洪燕梅著，2013《漢字文化與生活》。臺灣商務印書館
王明嘉等28人《漢字的華麗轉身：漢字的源流、演進與未來的生命》。大塊文化
王力主編 《中國古代文化常識》。北京語言大學出版社
王貴元著 2008《漢字與歷史文化》。中國人民大學出版社

● 教學方式(Teaching Method)
一、主題闡釋與討論 (60%) (說明：分組研討)
二、行動實作與報告 (30%) (說明：個別研討實作)
三、其他 (10%) (說明：隨堂參與)

● 教學進度(Syllabus)
週次 進度
1 說明授課方式、進度規劃及介紹漢字與中國文化的關聯

基於透明與負責任的原則，本課程鼓勵學生利用AI進行協作或互學，以提升本門課產出品質。根據
本校公布之佈的「大學教育場域AI協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採取有條件開放，如何使用
生成式AI於作業或報告，說明如下：

學生須於課堂作業或報告中的「標題頁註腳」或「引用文獻後」簡要說明如何使用生成式AI進行議
題發想、文句潤飾或結構參考等使用方式。然而，在本課程的「個人反思報告」、「小組採訪作業」
中，學生不得使用生成式AI工具撰寫作業。若經查核使用卻無在作業或報告中標明，教師、學校或
相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。

本門課授課教材或學習資料若有引用自生成式AI，教師也將在投影片或口頭標注。

課程說明 (Course Description)
課程簡述:

華語電影賞析課程旨在透過觀賞各種精選華語電影，提升學生的華語聽說能力並深化對華人文化的理解。課程設
計以學生的語言程度為基準，選取語速適中且情節豐富的電影。透過小組討論、角色扮演和文化解讀等互動性活
動，學生不僅能學習新詞彙和語法，還能提高他們的思維和文化認知水平，最終達到全方位的語言學習和文化體
驗。

課程目標:

本課程設計旨在透過觀賞華語電影來達到以下教學目標，並讓學生在輕鬆自然的環境中學習：
（一） 語言能力提升：學習新的日常辭彙和語法，增強聽力和口語溝通技能。
（二） 文化理解：增進對華人社會和文化的興趣及理解。
（三） 批判性思考：透過討論電影的主題和情節，激發學生的批判性思考和想像力。

一、授課教師：丁威仁
二、課程學分數：3
三、上課時間：週一567
四、上課地點：教305
五、教學方式 (Teaching Method)

（一）選片原則：
為了最大化教學效果，選片將遵循以下原則：
（一） 語言和適應性：選擇近年的華語電影，語速適中，適合學生的語言程度。
（二） 題材多樣性：涵蓋各種題材和主題，促進學生的多元性。
（三） 角色塑造：選擇角色鮮明，能引發學生興趣的電影。
（四） 情節和價值：挑選情節引人入勝且富含教育意義的電影。
（五） 語言純淨：避免選擇含有過多非華語或不當言詞的影片。
（六） 節奏適宜：避免選擇步調緩慢或獨白過多的影片。
（七） 文化接近性：避免選擇文化背景過深，難以為學生理解的電影。
（二）教學內容：
（一） 影片預看：學生課前先觀看影片，了解基本內容，並記下不明白的詞彙和語法。
（二） 課程開場：介紹電影背景和主要內容，采取分段觀賞和解釋的方法來深入分析。
（三） 小組討論：通過設計的提問引導學生小組討論，並書寫答案。
（四） 文化解讀：深入探討電影中的文化價值觀，與學生本國文化進行比較。
（五） 任務解鎖：透過解鎖教師要求任務來鞏固所學，並激發創意。
（三）教學流程
（一） 觀影前：討論電影名稱和預期內容，設定學習目標。
（二） 觀影：學生在課堂上觀看影片，使用目標語言字幕來增進語言學習。
（三） 加強學習：重複觀看關鍵段落，進行深入討論和語言練習。
（四） 後續活動：進行角色扮演和其他互動性活動，以應用所學並增進語言實踐。

通過這種結構化和互動性強的課程設計，學生將能夠在輕鬆的環境中有效學習華語，同時深入了解華語電影的文
化和語言特點。

六、每週教學進度 (Syllabus)
學期週 課程進度
第一週9/1 課程簡介
第二週9/8 公播電影觀賞
（《可不可以，剛好你也喜歡我》）
第三週9/15 電影賞析（一）：字詞解釋
第四週9/22 電影賞析（二）：字詞解釋與情節分析
第五週9/29 教師節補假
第六週10/6 中秋節放假
第七週10/13 電影賞析（三）：鏡頭語言及其他
第八週10/20 專題演講（暫定）
第九週10/27 主題辯論賽
第十週11/3 分組討論與活動（一）：塔羅與我
第十一週11/10 專題演講之公播電影觀賞
第十二週11/17 專題演講（暫定）
第十三週11/24 分組討論與活動（二）：分組故事創作
第十四週12/1 分組討論與活動（三）：拍攝劇本討論
第十五週12/8 拍攝週
第十六週12/15 期末成果發表（播放且評分）
七、成績考核 (Evaluation)

出席百分之三十
分組討論、活動與辯論賽百分之四十
期末成果發表百分之三十

Chinese Opera, Folklore, Ritual, change 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) 1. 學生能從不認識戲曲，到發現戲曲的精彩故事、豐富內涵，尤其偶戲的世界性，學生可 以與母國流行的偶戲互為映照。 2. 學生能在跨文化比較的討論中，認識其他國家表演藝術、節慶、敬神的傳統與內涵，互 相理解與尊重。 3. 能夠看懂戲曲表演的門道，對於唱腔的音樂性，也有一定程度的理解與感受。 4. 對於民俗活動在非常態時期的風靡與虔敬，有一定程度的理解，並因此熟悉漢人社會組 織與神明出巡的不同作法與含義。 ● 參考書籍(References) 伏木香織、羅斌：《閩南布袋戲在東南亞與台灣》，台北：臺原出版社，2014 年。 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 1. 課堂講述 2. 5C 教學法 3. 實作體驗教學法 4. 田野調查法 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 日期 課程主題 內容【說明】 備註 9/2 課程說明 教師課程說明、學生自我介紹。 9/9 布袋戲的掌上風雲 臺灣布袋戲（古典、金光、霹靂）、東南亞 布袋戲 9/16 布袋戲表演實作 布袋戲表演實作 實作體驗 9/23 跨文化比較（一） 著重表演藝術：介紹母國被列為文化資產／ 國寶的傳統表演藝術，賞析表演內涵、在母 國藝術的意義。 學生報告 9/30 皮影戲的光影變化 臺灣皮影戲（古典與現代）、東南亞皮影戲 皮影戲講座及實作 實作體驗 10/7 京劇的傳入與創新 京劇的表演體系（聯合國口述及非物質文化 遺產）、京劇在臺灣 10/14 京劇表演實作 京劇容妝及表演實作 實作體驗 10/21 跨文化比較（二） 著重當代變遷：以母國傳統民俗或表演藝術， 在當代社會產生的變貌，以及這些傳統在當 代維繫的意涵 學生報告 10/28 北管戲曲與客家戲曲 台灣民間音樂戲曲的業餘組織及廟會參與 11/4 華人的多神信仰 台灣三月瘋媽祖、王爺代天巡狩、新竹東寧 宮下元節（國曆 12 月 4 日）眾神遶境，及印 尼三寶壟三保大人遊神等。 11/11 民俗與陣頭 說明民俗儀式的產生背景，及相關的陣頭。 以竹塹中元城隍祭、台南武陣為主。 田野調查 11/18 跨文化比較（三） 著重大型節慶：思考母國是否將原本以民俗 docs.name: 連續介質力學
docs.text:
Introduction to Continuum Mechanics

Unit 0 Course Overview
Positioning: Seminar-style, topic-oriented course that builds on classical
continuum mechanics and extends to modern research on active matter in biological
systems.
Prerequisites: Calculus, linear algebra, partial differential equations, and basic
thermodynamics.
Learning Goals:
1. Master conservation laws and tensor language in continuum
mechanics.
2. Derive macroscopic field equations from microscopic active
processes.
3. Critically assess the relevance of active-matter models for
tumors, bacteria, and cell–matrix interactions.

Unit I Introduction to Biological Active Matter
Definition and scope of active matter in living systems
Comparison of active (energy-consuming) versus passive transport
Case studies: tumor microenvironments and bacterial niches
Energy dissipation as a hallmark of activity

Unit II Fundamental Equations for Chemotactic Systems
Keller–Segel model: construction, assumptions, and limitations
Coupling between particle density and chemical concentration fields
Non-linear diffusion in high-density regimes
From run-and-tumble kinetics to continuum descriptions

Unit III Active Transport in Porous Media
Biological porous environments (matrices, gels, tissues): definition and
measurement
Effective-medium theories for complex geometries
Modified transport equations under confinement
Darcy’s law and its extensions for active particles

Unit IV Bacterial Navigation in Complex Environments
Flagellar mechanics and motility strategies in restricted spaces
Run-and-tumble statistics in hydrogel networks
Mean free path in confined geometries
Environmental control of chemotactic efficiency

Unit V Continuum Models of Tumor Growth
Mass and momentum conservation for proliferating cell populations
Pressure feedback and its influence on growth rates
Nutrient diffusion/consumption coupling
Interface dynamics between tumor and healthy tissue

Unit VI Phase Separation and Coexistence in Active Systems
Mechanical interpretation and driving forces of phase separation
Force balance at ordered/disordered interfaces
Stability analysis of phase boundaries
Applications: tumor rims and bacterial colonies

Unit VII Extracellular Matrix as a Dynamic Medium
ECM modeled as a complex porous continuum
Matrix remodeling by tumor cells and bacteria
Two-way feedback between cell migration and matrix architecture
Memory effects and time delays

Unit VIII Multicomponent Active Systems
Mixture-theory framework for multiple cell populations
Interaction between active and passive constituents
Stress tensors with active source terms
Modeling tumor heterogeneity and phenotype switching

Unit IX Numerical Methods for Complex Biological Media
Finite-element techniques: interface tracking and adaptive meshing
Phase-field methods for growing domains and topology changes
Moving-boundary handling strategies
Multiscale coupling between microscopic and macroscopic levels

Unit X Hard-Sphere Models and Incompressibility Constraints
Volume-exclusion effects in dense active systems
From particle-based models to incompressibility conditions
Pressure buildup in densely packed tumor spheroids
Local volume fraction versus global force balance

Unit XI Gradient-Flow Structures and Energy Dissipation
Variational formulations for active systems
Energy functionals including chemical potentials
Stability estimates and convergence results
Gradient-flow view of chemotactic aggregation

Assessment
1. Mid-Term Project (40 %): Numerical simulation or theoretical
derivation (teams of two).
2. Final Report (60 %): Choose either a tumor or bacterial system;
integrate theory and simulation in a 10–12-page report with oral presentation.

Recommended Texts and References (Mathematical Focus)
Morton E. Gurtin, Lee Fried & Anil Anand, The Mechanics and Thermodynamics of
Continua, Cambridge University Press, 2010.
C. Truesdell & W. Noll, The Non-Linear Field Theories of Mechanics (3rd ed.),
Springer, 2004.
Michael E. Gurtin, An Introduction to Continuum Mechanics, Academic Press, 1981.
J. D. Murray, Mathematical Biology II: Spatial Models and Biomedical Applications
(3rd ed.), Springer, 2003.
Pierre Ciarlet, Mathematical Elasticity (Vols. I–III), North-Holland, 1988–2000.
H. G. Othmer, Mechanics of Cell Motility (Lecture Notes, Univ. of Minnesota).
S. H. Strogatz, Nonlinear Dynamics and Chaos (2nd ed.), CRC Press, 2018.
M. C. Cross & P. C. Hohenberg, “Pattern Formation Outside Equilibrium,” Rev. Mod.
Phys. 65, 851–1112 (1993).
S. Ramaswamy, “Active Matter,” J. Stat. Mech. 054002 (2017).
L. D. Landau & E. M. Lifshitz, Fluid Mechanics (2nd ed.), Elsevier, 1987; Theory
of Elasticity (3rd ed.), Elsevier, 1986.

docs.text:
● 課程說明(Course Description)
If T is a non-self-mapping, the equation Tx=x does not necessarily have a
solution. In which case, the best approximation theorems explore the existence
of an approximate solution, and the best proximity point theorems analyze the
existence of an approximate solution that is optimal. If the fixed point
equation Tx=x does not possess a solution, then d(x,Tx)>0 for all x. In
such a situation, it is our aim to find an element x such that d(x,Tx) is
minimum in some sense. The best approximation theory and best proximity pair
theorems are studied in this direction.

docs.name: 作業研究一
docs.text:
Course Description:

Operations research (OR) is the study of a scientific approach to decision-making
that typically involves allocating scarce resources in order to maximize or
minimize some function. OR has many applications in engineering,
science, economics, and industry. Thus the ability to solve OR problems is
crucial for both researchers and practitioners. Being able to solve real life
problems requires understanding and modeling the problem correctly and applying
appropriate optimization tools/skills. In this course, we will demonstrate how
to formulate, analyze and solve mathematical models of real-world problems.
Specifically, we will cover linear programming (including simplex algorithm,
duality and sensitivity analysis), network flow problems, integer programs,
nonlinear programs and inventory theory, with the amount of
emphasis depending on the time available. Some optimization commercial packages
will be used to assist understanding of and to gain insight into OR. Students
are expected to be able to build their own formulations, to critically evaluate
the impact of assumptions and to choose an appropriate solution technique at the
end of this course.

Text Books:

Hillier, F.S. and Lieberman, G.J. (2009) Introduction to Operations Research.
McGraw Hill. 10th edition.

本課程範圍為作業管理(Operations Management)中特殊與生產密切關係的生產計劃與管制系統
（PPC，Production Planning and Control System），將著重探討PPC的整體架構及其功能，

能規劃，製造資源規劃(MRPII)，作業排程，限制理論(TOC/DBR)，生產活動管制與生產線平衡等，
並將以作業或個案輔助學習。線上課程請參考清華大學開放式課程OCW
(http://ocw.nthu.edu.tw/ocw/index.php?page=course&cid=136&)。

docs.text: 1 Course: IEEM510300 Stochastic Processes Semester: Fall 2019 Number of credit hours: 3 Instructor: Professor Kuo-Hao Chang (chang@mx.nthu.edu.tw) Room 713R. Phone (03) 5742337 Lecture Time: Friday 2:20-5:20 pm Office Hours: Thursday 2-3:30 pm or by appointment TA office hours: TBA or by appointment Prerequisites: IEEM203000 (Engineering Statistics) or equivalent basic probability course. Textbook: Introduction to Probability Models, 10th Ed. by Sheldon M. Ross, Academic Press, 2009 (or the newest version). Student Learning Objectives: To develop an ability to model dynamical processes as stochastic processes; To develop an understanding of important qualitative characteristics of stochastic processes; To develop an ability to analyze basic stochastic processes. Course Topics Chapter 3. Conditional Probability and Conditional Expectation Chapter 4. Markov Chains Chapter 5. The Exponential Distribution and the Poisson process Chapter 6. Continuous-time Markov Chain (CTMC) Chapter 7. Renewal theory and its applications Chapter 8. Queueing Theory Student presentation (1 week) Grading Elements, Weighting and Scale: Grade Element Weighting Midterms (I and II) 40% Final 20% Quiz 10% Class Exercise 15% Final Project 15% General Policies: This course will adopt the “flip-classroom” mode, that is, lecture videos will be provided on a weekly basis before the class time. Students are required to watch the videos and bring their questions to the classroom. The instructor will answer the questions until everything is CLEAR. Quiz will be conducted to ensure that students have a full understanding about the teaching materials. Finally, class exercises will be provided with students to practice in class in groups. Discussion about the exercises are expected. 2 Class Exercises: You will team up with up to 3 team members, work on class exercises together and present your answers on a luck-draw system. The exercises are designed to improve your understanding of the class materials and give you a chance to learn and interact with your classmates. The same team will be give the same grade based on the correctness of the answer and the presentation if any. Homework: Homework will be assigned roughly weekly while I will not collect them. You are also encouraged to discuss homework with your classmates and learn from each other Quizzes: Quizzes are given on a weekly basis. All the quiz problems are strongly related (or identical) with the homework problems. You should fully understand every homework problem in order to get good grades for the quiz. Exams: Exams will cover material discussed in class. The two midterm and final examinations are close book and notes. No make up exams! Final exam is cumulative. The exact date of midterm exams is given as below (additional information). Final Project: The goal of the project is to learn about an application area where stochastic process models have been successfully used to model realistic situations. You should choose an area you are interested in (such as manufacturing, inventory management, transportation, health care, finance, insurance, telecommunication, software reliability, etc.), study the related literature (paper, book etc.), and do some computational work. This will be a team project (four team members at most) for which you are required to prepare a project report (around 10 pages, not counting cover and reference list), written at a level that your classmates could read. Specifically, the report should include: (1) A background introduction of the application area (2) The description of your stochastic model. You should justify the appropriateness of stochastic modeling being used to model systems/processes in the chosen area. (3) Work out numerical examples to demonstrate the use of stochastic process models in solving realistic problems and provide the managerial insights through your examples. A complete reference list is required. The final report (and the presentation slides) will be collected in class before your presentation starts, and plus, each team will make a 15-minute presentation in the last two weeks of this semester. More details about the order of presentation will be announced later.

docs.text:
Course Description:
This course introduces the common used Human Factors Testing and evaluation
methods in ergonomic research studies. The students will learn how to define
ergonomic research question(s), get themselves familiar with data measurement
equipment, design valid experiments to test research hypotheses, analyze data,
and interpreter their findings. The class will (1) introduce/review human
factors/ergonomic research methods (2) present cases for students to learn in
depth (3) discuss the principles, functionalities, and applications of selected
lab equipment (4) provide chances for students to familiarize themselves with
the equipment through actual experiment design practices. Through the training
of this class, the students will be able to equip themselves better for their
graduate research studies in the area of ergonomics.

Text Books:
Relevant materials will be provided during class

References:
Bridger, R., Introduction to ergonomics. CRC Press.
Wickens, C.D., Gordon, S.E., Liu, Y., & Lee, J., An Introduction to
Human Factors Engineering. Pearson.
Sanders, M.S., & McCormick, E.J., Human Factors in Engineering and
Design. New York: McGraw-Hill.

Teaching Method:
Lectures, cases studies, discussions, presentations

Syllabus:
1. Course Introduction
Overview of human factors and ergonomics (HFE) principles and course objectives.
2. Experimental Design in HFE Research
Key concepts and best practices for designing experiments in HFE.
3. Research Methods and Study Design in HFE
Detailed exploration of commonly used methodologies in human factors and
ergonomics research.
4. Subjective Measurement Methods for HFE Applications
Introduction to tools such as Likert-scale questionnaires, NASA-TLX, Borg Scale,
or SART for assessing subjective workload or perceptions.
5. Physiological Measurement for HFE Applications
Use of physiological tools such as EMG systems to evaluate muscle activity for
ergonomic assessments.
6. Kinematic and Kinetic Measurements for HFE Modeling and Analysis
Application of motion tracking systems, force plates, or other biomechanical
tools to analyze human movement or physical forces.
7. Psychophysics and Behavioral Evaluation Methods
Study of visual or motor performance assessment tools such as eye tracking
analysis or Fitts’s Law.
8. Physiological Evaluation Techniques
Analysis of autonomic nervous system indicators, such as heart rate variability
(HRV), for workload or stress assessment.

*Please note: The syllabus is subject to change at the instructor’s discretion.
Depending on the course’s progress, topics will be covered as fully as possible,
or selectively emphasized based on relevance. Students are also required to
complete multiple term projects/presentations.

Evaluation:
Assessment will be based on participation, quizzes, group/case discussions, and
team projects/presentations.

Regarding AI Usage:
The use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) and AI-assisted technologies
is permitted only for language polishing in the written report. Use for content
creation or any other inappropriate purpose is strictly prohibited. Any use of
AI tools must be clearly and properly acknowledged.

Students will examine both theoretical and practical aspects of how people interact with digital systems, focusing on perceptual and cognitive processes that inform the development and assessment of user interfaces. Core subjects include interface architecture, usability analysis, accessible design, and the use of multiple input and output modalities, such as tactile, visual, spoken language, and auditory feedback. 一、課程說明 (Course Description)
This course provides an introduction to Factory Physics: a systematic discussion
of the underlying behavior of manufacturing systems with three major parts. The
first part discusses The Lessons of History including Manufacturing in America,
Inventory Control: From EOQ to ROP, The MRP Crusade, The JIT Revolution, and What
Went Wrong. The second part illustrates Factory Physics including A Science of
Manufacturing, Basic Factory Dynamics, Variability Basics, The Corrupting
Influence of Variability, Push and Pull Production Systems. The third part
describes Principles in Practice including A Pull Planning structure, Shop Floor
Control, and Production Scheduling. Students are required to make a group
presentation (including ppt and video) for a survey of state-of-the-art progress
of Production and Operations Management in terms of hardware, software, system,
technology and idea.

二、指定用書 (Textbooks)
Factory Physics, 3rd edition, Wallace J. Hopp and Mark L. Spearman, Waveland
Press, 2008

Lecture, Question and Answer, Discussion, Presentation

docs.text: 2025/8 1 國立清華大學課程大綱-研究所 科號 IEEM5381 組別 學分 3 人數限制 20 上課時間 W2W3W4 教室 Room 726, Engineering Building I 科目中英文名稱 專利分析與智財管理 Patent Analysis and Intellectual Property Management 任課教師 張瑞芬 (Prof. Amy J.C. Trappey) ※下列各欄由任課教師提供※ 依 IEET 與評鑑精神,本系擬定之核心能力如下,教師請勾選本課程所欲培養之核心能力,並根據此建立 核心能力達成指標, 以課程評分量表(Rubrics)作為評估方法, 並依據此評分量表確認及評估教學成效, 是否作後續教學改進之用。(課程對應之核心能力並非要求”全選”, 無對應到的核心能力”可以不選”) 此科目對應之 系所課程規畫 所欲培養之核 心能力 Core capability to be cultivated by this course ■ 工工專業與系統分析能力 IE profession and systems analysis skills 30 % ■ 獨立研究及解決問題的實作能力 Capability of independent research and problem solving 50 % □ 領導、溝通與團隊合作能力 Leadership and coordination abilities 0 % □ 自我充實能力 Capability of self-development and enrichment 0 % ■ 國際觀視野、國際化互動與表達能力 Global interaction and communication skills 20 % 一、課程說明 (Course taught in full English) Intellectual properties (IPs) have become the most critical resources for enterprises worldwide. According to AON IP Assets Briefing (Aug. 2021), nearly 90% of the value of S&P500 companies lies in intangible assets, with major portion being IPs. Effective management of IPs, such as patents for R&D innovations, trademarks for corporate identity, and copyrights for multi-media content, is therefore essential for sustaining competitiveness and growth of a successful enterprise. Patent documents, in particular, serve as rich repositories of technical innovations, the inventive core concepts, and claimed legal rights. The rapid global increases in patent applications and subsequently grants, alongside the rising importance of licensing, infringement litigation, and IP-driven mergers and acquisitions, have created significant challenges for professionals to review and foreseeing the patent landscapes and future R&D trends. Researchers, patent engineers/consultants, business managers, and specialists in IP-related finance, law, and strategies must all be equipped to conduct large-scale patent searches, interpret complex documents, and extract actionable insights in a timely matter. This course will provide both the theoretical foundation and practical methods for Patent Analyses and IP Management (PA-IPM), focusing on patent and IP information retrieval, analysis, and IP knowledge, landscape, and trend discoveries. Students will learn how to apply advanced information and knowledge management techniques, e.g., AI and language modeling, for PA-IPM. Through lectures, case studies, and hands-on exercises, students will develop the ability to analyze, interpret, and apply IP knowledge in both research and business contexts. 2025/8 2 Key learning components include (not limited to):  Patent portfolio landscape: Analyzing technological development trends through patent portfolio visualization to understand the evolution of emerging technologies and their assignees.  IP knowledge representation: Structuring and visualizing patent knowledge using ontology frameworks to support potential collaborative innovations and patenting.  Patent data analysis (Macro and Micro): Assessing the innovation capabilities and competitiveness of countries, industries, and enterprises.  Patent text mining: Applying classification, clustering, and topic modeling techniques to understand invention content, compare claim scopes, prevent infringement and strengthen IP protection.  Intelligent innovation systems: Integrating patent analytics into R&D decision-making to identify mainstream R&D paths and guide corporate innovation strategies. 智慧財產已被公認為全球企業占比最高的重要無形資產。智慧財產類別、智慧財產權 法令、智慧財產管理等議題，尤其與研發技術相關的專利權保護、與企業識別相關的 商標權保護，皆為企業知識與經營管理不可忽視的一環。以專利文件為例，無論在技 術詞彙、創新概念、申請專利範圍等標準要項中，均蘊藏了豐富的技術知識與智財內 涵。近年全球專利申請或獲准數量激增，以及專利授權和專利侵權訴訟等企業競合互 動的興盛，無論對研發人員、專利工程師、經營管理者，亦或專門從事專利申請、侵 權訴訟、甚至企業併購資產評估等財、法、商專業人員，在即時大量專利檢索、解讀、 掌握關鍵性專利資訊與技術知識上，皆面臨相當高的挑戰。本課程除智財管理的基本 知識外，將對全球專利資料庫中專利文件搜尋與分析、數據資訊淬取、智財知識表述 等資訊和知識管理技術與應用，將進行理論與實務的教授和演練。同學在此課程中， 除了能學習到基礎關鍵知識外，更能對數據分析方法與其在智財管理應用上，進行實 做練習，例如： - 製作專利地圖：探討領域技術發展趨勢。透過專利組合分析與圖示，瞭解新興科 技之發展。 - 智財專利知識表述：將專利與智財知識的架構，透過本體論進行關聯化與視覺化 表述，有助於協同創新產品與技術開發之進行。 - 專利數據宏觀與微觀分析方法：辨識國家產業、各企業之創新能力與競爭力。 - 專利文字探勘(分類、分群、主題模型等)分析法：協助專利發明內涵之理解、範圍 主張比對、侵權防範、智權保護。 - 智慧型研發創新系統平台整合應用：發掘主流創新趨勢，引導企業創新研發。 二、Textbook 教科書 張瑞芬、張力元、吳俊逸、樊晉源 (2021)，專利分析與智慧財產管理 - 以資訊技術與 知識管理方法為手段(2 版)，華泰文化。 https://www.hwatai.com.tw/webc/html/book/show.aspx?isbn=9869941788 三、References 參考資料 To be provided. 科號 IEEM5381 組別 學分 3 人數限制 20 上課時間 W2W3W4 教室 Room 726, Engineering Building I 科目中英文名稱 專利分析與智財管理 Patent Analysis and Intellectual Property Management 2025/8 3 任課教師 張瑞芬 (Prof. Amy Trappey) 五、教學 軟體 IQ+, Clarivate Derwent Innovation (DI), USPTO, WIPO, TIPO, EPO PATSTAT, EB lab (in-house) patent analytic modules. 六、教學 方式與規 範 課堂講解、課堂討論與分組報告。 - During class, the instructor will lecture, ask questions, and engage in discussion with students. - Your class participations will be graded as a part of the overall grading. - Only water/coffee/tea are allowed during the class. Eating foods are prohibited. - Cells, computers, other electronic devices can be used only during in-class exercises, when online resources are needed. - Generative AI tool can only be partially used for editing/refining your self-written reports and assignments ** 生成式 AI 有條件開放之規範註明：所有作業、報告皆需自己撰寫。 七、教學 進度 No. Core Topic Textbook *TA 1, 2 智慧財產簡介、專利趨勢分析 Introduction and overview of Intellectual Property (1) * Patents, Trade Marks, Designs, Copyright and related rights, Confidential Information, Plant Variety Protection, Geographical Indications, and Traditional Knowledge Ch1; WIPO Annual Report (IP Indicators) (9/3, 9/10 -EPIP) 3 專利商業手段簡介 Introduction and overview of Intellectual Property (2) * The Intellectual Property Laws * IP in the Global Economy Ch2; WIPO Annual Report (IP Indicators) (9/17) 4 專利分析與研發策略、專利地圖製作 * Macro patent landscape/map * Clarivate Derwent Innovation introduction and training Ch 3; IP.com -- InnovationQ Plus, IQ+ (9/24) 5 專利資料庫與檢索技巧、各國專利資料庫簡介 * Patent databases and search techniques * USPTO, EPO Patstat, TIPO, WIPO Ch 4; Patent databases; Clarivate DI training (Dr. CY Fan / Dr. CY Wu, 10/1) 6 專利地圖分析流程 (練習) * Patent landscape/map/analysis tool training and practice Ch 5 (10/8) 7 專利資訊分析知識平台 專利地圖分析-實務練習 * WordMap, citation map, TFM training * Python CPU/GPU IP Server Training Ch 6 (10/15) 2025/8 4 8 專利地圖分析製作 Assessment I working session (1) Patent portfolio analysis cases: UAV and Bike Sharing (WPI and APMC2023 papers) * TAs (STPI Conf. 10/22) 9 Introduce ELEBC Patent Micro-analysis Platform (tutorial) – Keyword extraction, text mining, tech mining, word cloud, TFM, LDA modules. * TAs (10/29) 10 ＊＊ Assessment I: 1. 專利資料檢索及專利地圖分析-期中報告繳交 WORD (docx) Report specification: font size 12, single-spaced, maximal 10~15 page limit with additional pages of reference list). 2. docs.text:
一、課程說明 (Course Description)
Due to its practical value and contribution, Project Management is becoming
increasingly important and receiving high attention from enterprises and
organization. International certificates are becoming popular, such as Project
Management Professional (PMP) and Certified Associate in Project Management
(CAPM). This course introduces the concepts, theories, techniques, and
applications of project management, including both organizational behavior issues
and quantitative methods. In addition to teach What and How, this course also
investigates Why. Students will learn the definition, selection, planning,
execution, management, measurement, and closure of projects. Important topics
include Organization Strategy and Project Selection, Organizational Structure and
Culture, Defining the Project, Estimating Project Times and Costs, Developing a
Project Plan, Managing Risk, Scheduling Resources and Costs, Reducing Project
Duration, Being an Effective Project Manager, Managing Project Teams,
Outsourcing, Progress and Performance Measurement, Project Closure. Student will
develop individual project proposal and form groups to analyze and evaluate
famous projects.

Mastery of project management could make you competitive in the job market.

Project Management: The Managerial Process,
E. W. Larson and C. F. Gray, 7th Edn, McGraw Hill, 2017

docs.text: 課程資訊 (Course Information) 科號 Course Number 11410IEEM552300 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 40 中文名稱 Course Title 決策分析 英文名稱 Course English Title Decision Analysis 任課教師 Instructor 許嘉裕(HSU, CHIA-YU) more information 上課時間 Time R2R3R4 上課教室 Room ENG I 工一 701 此科目對應之系 所課程規畫所欲 培養之核心能力 Core capability to be cultivated by this course ■ 工工專業與系統分析能力 (30%) Professional skills in industrial engineering and engineering management, the ability of system analysis (30%) ■ 創新研究能力 (20%) The ability of innovative research (20%) ■ 領導與協調能力 (25%) The ability of leadership and coordination (25%) ■ 自我充實能力 (15%) The ability of self-enrichment (15%) ■ 國際互動能力 (10%) The ability of international interaction (10%) 課程簡述 (Brief course description) 學習有系統地分析策略決策問題、架構目標、評估方案的預期結果和可能的風險、探討決策方案的執 行，而從問題架構、 資料收集、資訊整理、決策分析乃至決策輔助的完整思維過程，提供系統化數 位化之決策依據與實行策略。除介紹各種決 策分析方法和工具外，並利用演講、個案討論、上機實 做和實證案例研究，討論決策者及群體決策時可能發生的決策陷阱 和問題，進而探討其中的組織領 導、變革管理與策略性決策思維等議題。 課程大綱 (Syllabus) Course keywords: 決策分析，決策品質，數位決策，營運管理 課程說明(Course Description)： 學習有系統地分析策略決策問題、架構目標、評估方案的預期結果和可能的風險、探討決策方案的 執行，而從問題架構、資料收集、資訊整理、決策分析乃至決策輔助的完整思維過程，提供系統化 數位化之決策依據與實行策略。除介紹各種決策分析方法和工具外，並利用演講、個案討論、上機 實做和實證案例研究，討論決策者及群體決策時可能發生的決策陷阱和問題。 指定用書(Text Books)： 簡禎富（2014），決策分析與管理:紫式決策分析以全面提升決策品質(第二版)，雙葉書廊，台北。 簡禎富（2022），《藍湖策略：發展智慧化管理科技與數位決策，超越藍海紅海循環宿命》，天下 雜誌出版社，台北。 參考書籍(References)： 1. 個案研究及講義 2. 簡禎富（2019），《工業 3.5：台灣企業邁向智慧製造與數位決策的戰略》，天下雜誌出版社， 台北。 教學進度(Syllabus): ※ 課程簡介 ※ 決策的重要性與決策本質、決策問題類型 ※ 紫式決策分析架構：勢、策、形 ※ 系統性決策與多屬性決策 ※ 分析層級程序法 ※ 資料包絡分析法 ※ 完全不確定決策 & 風險下的決策與資訊的價值 ※ 數位決策&智慧製造 ※ 生成式 AI 於決策應用 ● 生成式人工智慧倫理聲明:「有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於作業或報告」 ※根據本校公佈之的「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採取「有條件開 放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於作業或報告」，說明如下: 學生可於課堂作業或報告中的「標題頁註腳」或「引用文獻後」簡要說明如何使用生成式 AI 進行 議題發想、文句潤飾或結構參考等使用方式。然而，若經查核使用卻無在作業或報告中標明，教 師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。 本門課授課教材或學習資料若有引用自生成式 AI，教師也將在投影片或口頭標注。 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。

docs.text: 1 IEEM 554600 Sustainable Engineering and Management 永續工程與管理 Instructor: Ming-Chuan Chiu, 邱銘傳 Ph.D. E-mail: mcchiu@ie.nthu.edu.tw Office Phone: (03)574-2699 FAX: (03)572-2204 Office Location: 923 ENG I Office Hours: Wed 10:00-11:59 am and by appointment Class Times: W789 Class Location: Eng I 901 Class TA: 張芷瑄 chihsuan@gapp.nthu.edu.tw,石文德 aa29960939@gmail.com Office: 913 ENG I TA Office hour: Monday afternoon at 913 Ext:33949 Class Web: eeclass (https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw/course/22208) FB 社團: www.facebook.com/groups/1544856802791801 Course Objective Carbon neutrality and sustainability have become a global trend and had a great impact on design, manufacturing, service, supply chains, corporate governance, etc. This course provides students the basic knowledge about these issues and enables them to develop preliminary skills of applications for industries. 永續環保理念已成國際趨勢，在設計、生產、服務、供應鏈、公司治理等多方面的永續議題也受到重 視。本課程目標為使學生對這些永續內容具備基礎知識，在管理面與工程面介紹現今重要議題與未來發 展趨勢，並提供相關實踐作法(Best Practice)，協學生進而發展初步的應用技能與產業接軌能力。 Textbook 永續工程與管理, 中國工業工程學會, 2022, 前程文化 Grade Construction: You will be evaluated based on a broad spectrum of assignments. Your grade will be determined in the following fashion: ● Final Projects – 20% ● Examinations – 40% ⮚ Midterm 20% ⮚ Final Exam 20% 2 ● Assignments/Homework – 30% ● Class Participation – 10% Grading Policy: The major lesson to be learned in this course is that it is ok to make mistakes. If you feel frustrated that something isn’t working out, don’t worry! Design projects will be evaluated on the basis of effort and how well you followed the design process, and not whether the “correct” result was obtained. When it comes time to put together final grade, the following grade cutoffs will be applied. %Range 100 – 90 89 – 85 84 – 80 79 – 77 76 – 73 72 – 70 69 – 60 59 – 50 49 – 1 Letter A+ A A- B+ B B- C D E Class Policies The following are some ground rules to help us progress steadily through the semester: 1. Attendance is mandatory for all class periods. Because this class meets for 1.5~2 hours each session, significant material is covered each class session. You need to be present to learn and contribute to your team's success. Course grade will be dropped to the next lower grade (such as from A - to B+) for every three classes missed Also, the course grade will be dropped to the next lower grade if there is a pattern of tardiness. Missing class due to family vacation is not an excused absence. If possible, send the e-mail to me (mcchiu@ie.nthu.edu.tw) before class if you are sick or injured and will not be attending class. 2. If you have an excused absence that results in missing a quiz or other major assignment, you must discuss this with me prior to the quiz. 3. Late assignments (i.e., those not turned in at the beginning of the class period they are due) are graded out of 80%. Assignments turned in late will be graded, but with a 20% grade reduction for every week beyond the due date. 4. The instructor will discuss any exam or assignment grade within 48 hours (excluding weekends and holidays) of its return, after which time the discussion is closed. 5. The Design and Computer labs cannot be made up if they are unique and involve team work. 6. Students are responsible for any missed handout and homework assignment for any unexcused missed class. 7. Changes to assignments will be announced in class and supersede what is on the syllabus (the syllabus may be updated periodically without prior notice, please check iLMS weekly for updates). If you miss a class for an excused absence, it is your responsibility to ensure that you have the proper assignment. 8. Teams are expected to address team member problems (such as missed meetings or not completing work). However, do not let a small team issue or problem develop into a major conflict. Contact the class instructor to help address and correct the problem early! 3 9. Excellent team work can improve your project grade by as much as 2% per design project. Students earning high peer evaluation scores will see a project grade boost, and students earning a low peer evaluation scores will see a grade decrease. 10. Cell phones are to be turned off or in silent mode when in class. No IM and newspaper during the class. docs.text:
一、課程說明 (Course Description)
精實生產(Lean Production)又稱豐田生產系統(Toyota Production System, TPS)，近年來廣為
全球製造業與服務業採用，搭配企業流程再造(Business Process Reengineering, BPR)或改善活
動，成功地消除浪費、減少在製品、縮短生產週期時間、提升達交率、提升品質、降低成本、提高生產
力、並強化國際競爭力。精實生產與標準化是企業進行自動化、數位化與智慧製造的基石。本課程將教
導學生精實生產與管理以及企業流程再造之理論基礎與實務應用，學生將學以致用，在精實實驗
室進行實作以提升生產力，並分組執行一小型精實改善專案並上台報告。

docs.name: 博士班專題
docs.text: Course Title: Special Topics I Brief course description: This seminar course aims to broaden students' perspectives on cutting-edge research topics in industrial engineering & management, operations research, production management, and artificial intelligence (AI). Through invited talks from distinguished scholars and industry experts, students will gain exposure to the latest research developments and real-world applications, fostering both academic insight and practical awareness. All students need also to present their research idea and share the insights from their reviews. The course also emphasizes critical thinking, academic dialogue, and research ideation. Course Syllabus: Several invited speakers from academia or industry will deliver a seminar on current topics. Representative themes include, but are not limited to:  Optimization and systems engineering in industrial settings  Operations research and decision analysis  Applications of AI and machine learning in manufacturing and supply chain  Smart manufacturing, Industry 4.0/5.0 Active participation and Q&A with the speaker are highly encouraged to cultivate academic communication skills. Each student needs to provide a one-page summary report for post-seminar discussions. Course Requirements and Evaluation:  Seminar Response Reports (30%): Each student will prepare summary and commentary reports for assigned seminars.  Attendance and Participation (30%): Regular attendance is mandatory unless approved by the instructor. Engagement in discussions is essential.  Final Reflection or Research Proposal (40%): Students will submit a final report regarding a topic reflecting on what they have learned, along with a preliminary research idea (including introduction and motivation for the chosen topic, challenge, comparison of major works, and future research direction).

docs.text:
● 課程說明(Course Description) :
本課程強調與說明機率模式與統計方法在工業工程的各種應用。目的在讓學生瞭解統計原理及技
巧，並應用於工程問題分析。此外，本課程將搭配使用統計軟體來進行統計分析，使學習者可快速
學會如何操作及做正確解讀統計軟體報表，以奠定日後從事分析研究工作及管理時之需。
This course emphasizes and illustrates the use of probabilistic models and
statistical methodology that is employed in countless applications in industrial
engineering. It gives the student an understanding of the logic behind
statistical techniques as well as practice in using them.

docs.text: 課程資訊 (Course Information) 科號 Course Number 11410IEM 561600 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 40 中文名稱 Course Title 決策分析 英文名稱 Course English Title Decision Analysis 任課教師 Instructor 許嘉裕(HSU, CHIA-YU) more information 上課時間 Time RaRbRc 上課教室 Room ENG I 工一 904 此科目對應之系 所課程規畫所欲 培養之核心能力 Core capability to be cultivated by this course ■ 工工專業與系統分析能力 (30%) Professional skills in industrial engineering and engineering management, the ability of system analysis (30%) ■ 創新研究能力 (20%) The ability of innovative research (20%) ■ 領導與協調能力 (25%) The ability of leadership and coordination (25%) ■ 自我充實能力 (15%) The ability of self-enrichment (15%) ■ 國際互動能力 (10%) The ability of international interaction (10%) 課程簡述 (Brief course description) 學習有系統地分析策略決策問題、架構目標、評估方案的預期結果和可能的風險、探討決策方案的執 行，而從問題架構、 資料收集、資訊整理、決策分析乃至決策輔助的完整思維過程，提供系統化數 位化之決策依據與實行策略。除介紹各種決 策分析方法和工具外，並利用演講、個案討論、上機實 做和實證案例研究，討論決策者及群體決策時可能發生的決策陷阱和問題，進而探討其中的組織領 導、變革管理與策略性決策思維等議題。 課程大綱 (Syllabus) Course keywords: 決策分析，決策品質，數位決策，營運管理 課程說明(Course Description)： 學習有系統地分析策略決策問題、架構目標、評估方案的預期結果和可能的風險、探討決策方 案的執行，而從問題架構、資料收集、資訊整理、決策分析乃至決策輔助的完整思維過程，提 供系統化數位化之決策依據與實行策略。除介紹各種決策分析方法和工具外，並利用演講、個 案討論、上機實做和實證案例研究，討論決策者及群體決策時可能發生的決策陷阱和問題。 指定用書(Text Books)： 簡禎富（2014），決策分析與管理:紫式決策分析以全面提升決策品質(第二版)，雙葉書廊，台 北。 簡禎富（2022），《藍湖策略：發展智慧化管理科技與數位決策，超越藍海紅海循環宿命》， 天下雜誌出版社，台北。 參考書籍(References)： 個案 A：驚爆十三天（看電影學決策陷阱） 個案 B：創意電子 個案 C：聯發科和山寨 個案 D：旺宏電子公司個案-製造策略決策 個案 E：飛馬葡萄酒廠 大數據和數位決策參考書：簡禎富、許嘉裕（2014），資料挖礦與大數據分析，前程文化，新 北市。 教學方式(Teaching Method) ： 1. 作業 (原則上 2 人一組) 2. 軟體實做 (原則上 2 人一組，上課完成) 3. Take-home exam (個人) 4. 期末報告 (4~6 人一組) 5. 有條件開放 AI ，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出。 教學進度(Syllabus)： ※ 課程簡介 ※ 決策的重要性與決策本質、決策問題類型 ※ 紫式決策分析架構：勢、策、形 ※ 系統性決策與多屬性決策 ※ 分析層級程序法 ※ 資料包絡分析法 ※ 完全不確定決策 & 風險下的決策與資訊的價值 ※ 數位決策&智慧製造 ※ 生成式 AI 於決策應用 ● 生成式人工智慧倫理聲明:「有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於作業或報告」 ※根據本校公佈之的「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採取「有條 件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於作業或報告」，說明如下: 學生可於課堂作業或報告中的「標題頁註腳」或「引用文獻後」簡要說明如何使用生成式 AI 進行議題發想、文句潤飾或結構參考等使用方式。然而，若經查核使用卻無在作業或報告中標 明，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。 本門課授課教材或學習資料若有引用自生成式 AI，教師也將在投影片或口頭標注。 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。

docs.text: 課程資訊 及 課程大綱 課程名稱 (中文) 資訊安全實作一 課程名稱 (英文) Information Security Implementation I 科號 11410IIS 500000 授課教師 指導教授 上課時間 開課年級 資安所一年級、二年級 學分數 2 人數限制 先修科目 課程簡述 Brief Course Description (required) 本課程將由指導教授帶領，就資訊安全相關課程的理論與技巧，因 應個別學生之選題，應用在相關領域問題上並進行深入研究，以培 養解決資安問題之實作能力與閱讀學術論文的能力，並於期末繳 交心得報告。 關鍵字 資 訊 安 全 , Information Security 課程大綱 Detailed Course Syllabus 一、課程說明(Course Description) 本課程鼓勵學生就所習得之資訊安全相關課程的理論與技巧，因 應個別學生之選題，應用在相關領域問題上並進行深入研究，且 以研究簡報或撰寫報告之方式，以專門導向問題與指導教授共同 研究，以培養解決資安領域問題之實作能力，以及閱讀學術論文 的能力。 二、指定用書(Text Books) 由指導教授指定 三、參考書籍(References) 由指導教授指定 四、教學方式(Teaching Method) 學生在教授研究室學習各種研究技巧，解決研究上遭遇之問題。 五、教學進度(Syllabus) 由指導教授自行安排。 六、成績考核(Evaluation) 由研究報告素質、研究態度決定。 七、可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website) 核心能力 Core capability 請勾選 此科目對應之系所課程規畫所欲培養之核心能力 Core capability to be cultivated by this course 權重（百分比） Percentage v 具備檢索文獻、閱讀論文、與撰寫論文的能力。 To be able to search literatures, read and write academic papers. 20 % v 具有策劃及執行研究計畫、撰寫研究報告及簡報研究成果 的能力。 To be able to plan and execute research projects, write research reports, and present research results. 20% v 瞭解與資訊安全相關之產業脈動與最新的資訊安全進展。 To understand the most recent technological and industrial advancements regarding information security. 20% v 瞭解資訊安全對於全球性社會、經濟、文化等層面的影響 與責任。 To understand the social, economical, cultural effects of information security and related technologies on the global level. 20% v 尊重學術、工程倫理、及智慧財產權。 To respect academics, engineering ethics, and intellectual property. 20%

docs.text: 課程資訊 及 課程大綱 課程名稱 (中 文) 次世代行動網路 課程名稱 (英 文) Next Generation Mobile Networks 授課教師 邱德泉助理教授 上課時間 T5T6R6 台達102 (如果要連續 3 小時上課，請一併提供理由。) 開課年級 碩士班 學分數 3 人數限制 40 先修科目 計算機網路概論 課程簡述 Brief Course Description (required) 近年來由於邊緣智慧的崛起伴隨著智慧物聯網的新世代來臨，有別於 傳統架構，終端裝置本身將產生大量具價值數據，若能即時處理這些 資料，並搭配人工智慧模型 萃取出有用資訊，相信將能實現一系列具 前瞻性的次世代網路服務應用，例如:元宇宙、自動化 無人載具系統、 無線腦機互動及工業 5.0 等等;由此可預期次世代行動網路將是實現 邊緣計算基於 「將運算從雲端移近至終端」之嶄新架構，順理融合人 工智慧後演化成邊緣智慧框架—將能就近 實現智慧物聯網具低延遲 需求之關鍵學習任務。 關鍵字 第五代行動網路, 邊緣運算, 邊緣智慧, 行動網路安全 課程大綱 Detailed Course Syllabus 一、課程說明(Course Description) 近年來由於邊緣智慧的崛起伴隨著智慧物聯網的新世代來臨，有別於 傳統架構，終端裝置本身將產生大量具價值數據，若能即時處理這些 資料，並搭配人工智慧模型 萃取出有用資訊，相信將能實現一系列具 前瞻性的次世代網路服務應用，例如:元宇宙、自動化 無人載具系統、 無線腦機互動及工業 5.0 等等;由此可預期次世代行動網路將是實現 邊緣計算基於 「將運算從雲端移近至終端」之嶄新架構，順理融合人 工智慧後演化成邊緣智慧框架—將能就近 實現智慧物聯網具低延遲 需求之關鍵學習任務。本課程承接上述兩門課程，開始從 5G 行動網 路 與其應用簡介、5G 核心網路架構介紹、邊緣運算網路介紹並以 MEC 當作探討個案、邊緣智慧介 紹、5G 資安議題探討，宜先修過 計算機網路概論、無線網路、行動電信網路等基礎課程。 本課程將基於計算機網路課程繼續延伸探討四大議題: (1) 第五代行動網路 (2) 邊緣運算 (3) 邊緣智慧 (4) 行動網路安全 Based on the Computer Networks course, this course will further explore the following four topics: (1) The 5th Mobile Network (2) Edge Computing (3) Edge Intelligence/AI (4) Mobile Network Security 二、指定用書(Text Books) 參考教育部下世代行動通訊技術人才培育計畫聯盟教材進行課程及模 組實驗 三、參考書籍(References) 參考5G 行動寬頻人才培育計畫之推廣教材及模組 影音連結如下： https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCjvy2yZI6c_e7v91Y3e52Vg/playlists 四、教學方式(Teaching Method) 以投影片教學 五、教學進度(Syllabus) 1. 5G Introduction 2. 5G Architecture 3. 5G Core Networks 4. SDN and NFV in 5G 5. Edge Computing 6. MEC in 5G Introduction and use cases 7. AI at the Edge 8. docs.name: 企業家精神與創業管理
docs.text: National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 科號 Course Number 11410IMBA400200 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Size of Limit 25 中文名稱 Course Title 企業家精神與創業管理 英文名稱 Course English Title Entrepreneurship and New Venture 任課教師 Instructor Yu-Wei Hsu 許祐維 教師聯絡方式 Contact Information Email: yhsu.edu@gmail.com 上課時間 Time Tuesday T2T3T4 上課教室 Room TBD (@TSMC Building) 先修科目 Prerequisite(s) 本課程對應之學習目標與核心能力 Aligned Learning Goals and Learning Objectives Entrepreneurial mindset- ideas origination, opportunity realization, economic thinking, risk taking and be passionate. Business Plan- to work in a team to put together a sound Business Plan. Leadership- Build up observation skills to provide sound feedbacks and challenges on others’ views and business proposals. 課程目標 Course Objectives To understand the essential mindset and mental models of a successful entrepreneur- a startup entrepreneur or a corporate entrepreneur. To learn and practice the necessary tools in starting up a business- the entrepreneurial process, business planning, Business Plan, etc. To build up strong interactive capability in business group discussion- to provide useful feedbacks, to challenge ideas and to help driving others to be successful. 課程說明 Course Description This course is useful for students who are especially interested to run a startup company. We will discuss entrepreneurship from the essential mindset and mental models through to key useful tools in starting up a company. Even though you may not plan or expect to run a startup, this course could help you build up the key competence to be a corporate entrepreneur who realize career advancement through entrepreneurial mindset and with competence in related tools. Participants are expected to get actively engaged in class discussions, to provide feedbacks at the end of each lecture, to work in groups on Business Plan and to provide feedbacks on others’ Business Plan presentations. No mid term nor final term exam is designed while we emphasize on the Business Plan preparation and reviews that stress on interactive participations. Additionally, considering Business Plan that involves the utilizing of AI assisted tools or services is encouraged with condition. National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus Policy on use of AI:(2) Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output. 指定用書 Textbooks William D. Bygrave, Andrew C. Corbett, Andrew Zacharakis, “Entrepreneurship Asia Edition 5/e”. 參考書籍 References Charles Koch, “Good Profit” 教學方式 Teaching Approach - Each session will consist of lectures as well as group discussions (except on the two weeks when Business Plan presentation and reviews are scheduled). Group discussion could be case study discussion or continuously working through a part of the group Business Plan in accordance with the weekly topic. Also, Site Visit or Invited Speech will be arranged as shown in the Course Schedule. - Time will be given for reflection at the end of selected sessions for the participants to provide feedbacks and summarize key learning in a concise manner. 評分標準 Grading Class participation and group discussions: 25% Lecture reflection: 25% - By the end of selected lectures (or within given days), a feedback form is to be submitted with feedbacks and key learning. docs.text: National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus Course Number: IMBA400600 Course Title: Financial accounting 2026 (Fall 2025) Instructor: Hsieh, Chih-Cheng Contact Info: chih-cheng.hsieh@pwc.com Time: 9:10~12:00 (Monday) Classroom: TSMC Building Room 428 COURSE DESCRIPTION The global accounting environment has been evolving around greater transparency and comparability through continuous amendments to existing guidance and challenges emerge in different areas, e.g. continuing development of ESG, cloud computing and respective variations and fluctuations of global and domestic economics. The two main-stream financial reporting frameworks (International Financial Reporting Standard (“IFRS”) and Generally Accepted Accounting Principle in the United States (“US GAAP” or “GAAP”) have been working on enhancing respective guidance on accounting treatments and disclosures in respect to the abovementioned topics, as well as continuously working on aligning newly announced “co-developed” guidance, though discrepancies still exist. However, new accounting guidance was continuously being discussed and communicated to minimize potential discrepancies. The Taiwanese-IFRS (“T-IFRS”) has caught up with the global trend since 2018. Continuing the trend, the course is designed to educate students on these matters: 1. provides students with a basic understanding of accounting (primarily IFRS); 2. provides high level understanding of accounting principles when reviewing financial statements based upon IFRS; and 3. analyses various factors and methods that would be adopted in identifying the financial statements at risk. COURSE OBJECTIVES 1. To introduce students to understand information / underlying implication from a company’s financial statements. 2. To introduce students to analyze the accounting transactions on financial reports and business decision. 3. To orient students to organize the operating, investing, and financing activities of a company. TEACHING METHOD Instructor-led discussion, case study, team presentation, and etc. TEXTBOOKS Jerry J Weygandt, Paul D. Kimmel and Donald E. Kieso --- Financial Accounting with IFRS 5th Edition COURSE REQUIREMENTS AND GRADING POLICY 1. Participation – group presentation and question-raising: 30% 2. Group case – group presentation: 50% 3. docs.text: １ 科目名稱：『國際華語教育發展』課程綱要 Development of International Chinese Education (IMS 500100) 114 學年度第 1 學期 (Fall, 2025) 授課老師： 信世昌 hsins@ntnu.edu.tw LINE ID: hsinscc 學 分： 跨院華語組必修、華文所選修; 3 學分 教 室： 清大校本部綜合二館 2 樓 ____ 教室 時 間： 每週四下午 3:30pm – 6:20pm ============================================================= 課程目的： 本課程的主要目的是從宏觀的角度來探討華語文教育的國際化及其在全球的發展， 並且從國際環境、語文政策、師資培育、課程與教學制度、機構組織等方面切入，此外 並一併探討語言的興盛與衰退，內容包括： 1. 探究影響語言興盛與衰退的因素為何 2. 瞭解華語國際化與多元化之變遷 3. 探討海內外華語文教育與僑教之發展與現況 4. 了解全球華語推廣機構及重要活動 5. 討論如何推動全球的華語文教育 教學方式: 以課堂討論、專案分析、文獻資料研讀為主，並擬邀請專家參與特定主題之討論。 本課並採專題研判方式，根據國內外華語文教育的相關情勢，深入探究其成因與發展之 道。此外，若干與華語文教育有關的特殊問題，也將一併深入討論。 學習評量方式: 文章導讀 (講義與教材) 20% 分組專題報告與資料彙集 30 % 期末報告 (專案 Project 或專題論述) 40% 課程參與 (出席, 討論與服務) 10% (加分 Bonus:於本學期報名參加本課認可之華語教學研討會,每次酌加總分1~2分) 註：出席 (缺席請事先請假，無故曠課每小時扣總分 1 分) 教材: ※ 本課講義 (雲端 Moodle 平台 PDF 檔) ※ Crystal, David (2015) English as a Global Language. docs.name: 華語文教材教法
docs.nameEn: Pedagogies of Teaching Chinese as a Second Language
docs.text:
課程目標：

本課程以概念為本，方法為主，理論為輔。上課內容著重概念、實作、創新、合作，及反思。學生
必須在學期間進行教學設計專題，專題之外，本課程活動亦包括聽講、研讀專書和研討之外。
學生修完本課程之後應能：
1. 理解第二語言教學理論和方法並能與教學實務連結；
2. 掌握不同級別華語文教材特性及教學之重點；
3. 具備華語文教學活動設計和編寫教案之能力；
4. 善用並發展具針對性和實用性之教學策略。

授課方式：
本課程主要教學對象為華語文教學學程學生，上課內容以教學方法為主；理論為輔；強調「做中學」、創
新、實用，以及合作學習。
學生除聽講和研討之外，學期間需完成導讀、翻轉報告、學習者分析、教案專題、教案實踐演練等個人和
分組作業、教案之設計在本課程教師的督導下循序完成。

海內外各級華語文教材

docs.name: 華語教學之跨文化溝通
docs.nameEn: Cross-cultural Communication for Teaching Chinese as a Second Language
docs.text: 《華語教學之跨文化溝通》 授課教師：宋怡南 ynsung@gmail.com 時間地點：12:10-15:10 GEN II 綜二 二、課程內容與學習 語言與文化的關係密切，跨文化溝通知識及能力屬華語教學專業知能之 一。華語教師必須充分了解語言與本國文化之間的連結，在生活中與自我經驗 中觀察文化，進而能適當的將之展現在教學中；另一方面，教師在面對來自世 界各地不同背景的學生，必須有足夠的文化敏感度，對各國文化及其相關影響 抱持尊重的態度，進而幫助學生從其母語文化出發，認識目標語的文化，結合 跨文化交際知能，獲得完整之語言溝通能力。 本課程《華語教學之跨文化溝通》由理論與實務出發，首先界定語言與文 化的關係及其定義，介紹語言與文化的研究方法，綜合探討華語教學中合適的 文化範圍。其次在語言交際和跨文化溝通的目的和基礎上，探討語言與文化接 觸與衝擊，經由各種語言現象所反映的文化背景，理解背後不同文化的交際模 式和核心價值。同時選取五類於跨文化溝通中具代表性及差異性的語言主題， 如：借字、禮節語言、禁忌語和委婉語等，通過與不同文化之受訪者對談，真 實觀察跨文化交際衝突和適應過程。最後由本學期探討主題出發，規劃具備華 語教學效能之主題文化課程單元。 三、課程要求 （一）閱讀與討論 課前閱讀教材並於班上積極參與討論，有助於在短時間內 取得最大收穫。請妥善規劃每次出席，課堂參與度將是學期成績的重要參考。 （二）跨文化個案訪談 分組後找到本學期五次文化主題訪談的對象，對象請 鎖定在臺學華語的外籍人士，國籍不拘，華裔背景請排除。 【訪談對象介紹】配合投影片介紹訪談對象：本人華語學習背景所來自國 家/鄰近地區的歷史宗教政治文化背景母語特色華語在該國的發展狀況對 臺灣文化的印象。 【五次訪談與分享】根據大綱上所列主題進行訪談，應輪流分工，於課上口頭 分享後繳交一份 4 頁的訪談書面報告 ※訪談請依照各週規劃之主題，依次完成。每次訪談均需全組到齊，盡量採 實體形式以利觀察跨文化溝通，不可合併主題訪談。書面報告均須附上分工 狀況與全組合照。 （三）華語教學主題文化課程單元設計 根據本學期訪談及探討的主題出 發，練習規劃不同主題之文化課程單元，報告包含海報票選與課堂講述兩部 分，期末前有一次主題簡報。 評量項目（總分 100％）  出席與閱讀討論（個人） 20%  訪談對象介紹（分組） 10%  個案採訪報告（分組） 40% （共 5 次，每次 8%）  期末主題文化課程設計（分組） 30% （簡報佔 5%） 四、每週進度（暫訂） 週 授 課 主 題 活 動 內 容 一 課程介紹與主題討論 語言學習與文化衝突經驗 二 語言與文化的關係 民族價值核心與文化對比 三 語言與文化的研究方法 活動：訪談注意事項 四 跨文化交際理論與實務 序曲：訪談對象介紹 1 五 從造詞心理、親屬稱謂看文化 序曲：訪談對象介紹 2 六 先人的智慧：各類熟語探討 活動：訪談行前討論 七 文化接觸之一：借字 第 1 次訪談與分享 八 文化接觸之二：混合語 第 2 次訪談與分享 九 誰最有禮貌：禮節語言的運用 第 3 次訪談與分享 十 語言的力量：咒罵語、髒話 活動：教學現場的文化議題 1 十一 佛曰不可說：禁忌語與委婉語 第 4 次訪談與分享 十二 男女大不同：性別語言 活動：教學現場的文化議題 2 十三 非語言符號：動作、表情、服飾… 期末主題文化課程簡報 十四 語言教學與文化課程設計 終曲：第 5 次訪談與分享 十五 ～期末主題文化課程單元設計報告與回饋～ 十六 ～期末主題文化課程單元設計報告與回饋～ 五、課程閱讀清單 課程主題指定閱讀文獻，已公告於本課程平台上。請按照進度完成閱讀與 筆記，帶至課堂上討論。

docs.name: 書報討論：國別化教材編寫
docs.text: 1 書報討論：國別化教材編寫 Seminar: Compiling Country-Specific Teaching Materials 一、教師資訊： 授課教師：陳淑芬 電子信箱：chensf@gapp.nthu.edu.tw 辦 公 室：綜二館 A607 聯絡電話：35167 二、課程資訊： 上課時間： 週四 10:10 --- 1:00 上課地點：綜二 608 Office Hours: 週四、週五下午 1 – 3 （請來信預約） 三、課程說明： 本課程旨在瞭解國別化教材之編寫原則，並培養學生從事國別化教材之研究 能力，進而撰寫國別化華語教材。透過系統性與階段性的學習指導，協助學生進 行國別化教材相關之學位論文寫作。本課程有三大學習目標： (1) 確立碩士/博士論文問題意識與研究方法。 (2) 培養國別化教材相關之研究能力。 (3) 培養論證架構的能力與論文寫作能力。 四、參考資料： Brown, J. D. 1988. Understanding Research in Second Language Learning. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press. Fantini, A. E. (1997). New Ways in Teaching Culture. Alexandria, VA: Teachers of English to Speakers of Other Languages, Inc. Kramsch, C. (1988). “The cultural discourse of foreign language textbook”. In A. Singerman (ed.), Towards a New Integration of Language and Culture (pp. 63-68). Middlebury, VT: Northeast Conference. Kramsch, Claire. (1993) Context and Culture in Language Teaching. Oxford: Oxford University Press. Kroeber, A. L., and Kluckhohn, C. (1952). Culture: A Critical Review of Concepts and Definitions. Cambridge, Massachusetts: Peabody Museum. Moran, P. R. (2009). Teaching Culture: Perspectives in Practice. Beijing: Foreign Language Teaching and Research Press. Nemetz-Robinsin, G. L. (1988). Crosscultural Understanding. New York: Prentice-Hall. Oswalt, Wendell H. (1970). Understanding Our Culture. An Anthropological View. New York: Holt, Rinehart and Winston. 2 Seelye, N. (1993). Teaching Culture: Strategies for Foreign Language Educators. Lincolnwood: National Textbook Company. 五、教學方式 上課以報告和討論的方式進行。由學生上台報告最近所研讀國別化教材相關 的文獻，及論文書寫進度，出席同學需要輪流提問以及評論。上課前三日需將全 文寄給評論的同學和任課老師。 六、成績考核： 課堂報告 + 書面報告：40% 提問與同儕評論：30% 期末報告： 30% 七、學生使用 AI 的聲明： 根據本校公布之佈的「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」， 本門課程採取有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於作業或報告，說明如 下： 學生可於課堂作業或報告中的「標題頁註腳」或「引用文獻後」簡要說明 如何使用生成式 AI 進行議題發想、文句潤飾或結構參考等使用方式。然而， 學生不得使用生成式 AI 工具撰寫期末研究報告。若經查核使用卻無在作業 或報告中標明，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或 不予計分。 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。 備註：限碩二以上準備寫畢業論文學生選修。 3 論文撰寫相關書籍： 上野千鶴子著，涂紋鳳譯，《如何做好研究論文？成為知識生產者，從提問到輸 出的18個步驟》，臺北：三采，2021。 安伯托．艾可（Umberto Eco）著，倪安宇譯，《如何撰寫畢業論文：給人文學科 研究生的建議》，臺北：時報，2019。 何德華，《華語教學研究方法與論文寫作》，臺北：正中書局出版，2009。 吳鄭重：《研究研究論論文：研究歷程之科P解密與論文寫作SOP大公開》，臺北： 遠流出版，2016。 孟樊，《論文寫作方法與格式》，新北市：威仕曼文化，2012。 美國現代語言協會編著，《MLA 論文寫作手冊，第9版》，臺北：書林出版有限 公司，2022。 張可婷譯，Diana Ridley 著，《一步步教您做文獻回顧》，新北：韋伯文化，2010。 畢恆達，《教授為什麼沒告訴我？——論文寫作的枕邊書》，臺北：學富文化事 業，2005。 陳信助，《研究方法易上手》，臺北：學富文化，2020。 彭明輝，《研究生完全求生手冊：方法、秘訣、潛規則》，臺北：聯經，2017。 葉至誠，《研究方法與論文寫作》，臺北：商鼎文化，2011。 蔡柏盈，《從字句到結構：學術論文寫作指引》，臺北：臺灣大學出版中心，2015。 顏志龍，《傻瓜也會寫論文（量化+質化增訂版）： 社會科學學位論文寫作指南》， 臺北：五南圖書，2018。 參考資源： 1. 學校授權資源（可至清大圖書館---資料庫檢索/期刊檢索中檢索所需工具） A. 愛如生的《中國基本古籍庫》、《中國方志庫》、《歷代別集庫》、《譜 牒庫》、《典海平台》 B. 讀秀 C. CNKI 中國期刊全文數據庫 D. 華藝線上圖書館 2. 國家圖書館期刊文獻資訊網：https://tpl.ncl.edu.tw/NclService/ 3. 全國圖書書目資訊網：http://nbinet3.ncl.edu.tw/screens/opacmenu_cht.html 4. 臺灣博碩士論文知識加值系統：https://reurl.cc/9VE24n https://ndltd.ncl.edu.tw/cgi-bin/gs32/gsweb.cgi/login?o=dwebmge 5. 清大圖書館 資源利用空中補給站: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCcVRJgvF0DFgc9j1zZ7qoXA/playlists 4 國別化教材閱讀文章： 方麗娜（2010），〈國別化教材的設計與編寫——以《悅讀華文，細品文化》為例〉， 《海外華文教育》2。 何寶璋、羅雲（2010），〈漢語國別化教材編寫新嘗試：《Routledge 現代漢語課程》〉， 《國際漢語學報》。 何寶璋、羅雲（2012），〈非目的語環境華語國別教材編撰的思考、設計與實施〉， 《華語文教學研究》 9.3：31-46。 李泉（2015），〈漢語教材的「國別化」問題探討〉，《世界漢語教學》29.4：526- 540。 李祿興、王瑞（2008），〈國別化對外漢語教材的特徵和編寫原則〉，《世界漢語教 學學會》：836 - 341。 徐昌火（2012），〈基於 CEFR 的國別化中文教材編寫芻議〉，《華語文教學研究》 9.4：1-16。 趙金銘（2009），〈教學環境與漢語教材〉，《世界漢語教學》23.2：210-223。 鄭通濤（2012），〈以效果為基礎的對外漢語國別化教材發展〉，《國際漢語學報》 3.1: 1-9。 鄭通濤、方環海、張涵（2010），〈國別化：對外漢語教材編寫的趨勢〉，《海外華 文教育》1：1 - 8。 于海闊、李如龍（2012），〈關於漢語國際教育國別化教材幾個問題的探析〉，《民 族教育研究》6。 方環海（2010），〈語言知識的認知特性語教材的編寫策略〉，《海外華文教育》3： 15-22。

docs.name: 漢語語言學
docs.text: 1 漢語語言學 （114學年度第一學期） 一、教師資訊： 授課教師：陳淑芬 電子信箱：chensf@gapp.nthu.edu.tw 辦 公 室：綜二館 A607 聯絡電話：35167 二、課程資訊： 上課時間： 週五早上 9:10 --- 12:00 p.m. 上課地點：綜二 205 Office Hours: 週四、週五下午 1 - 3（請來信預約） 三、課程說明： 本課程向學生介紹漢語語言學知識，包括語音屬性、音韻結構、構詞與詞彙、 句法結構、語意學、篇章結構、語用現象和漢字教學，涵蓋語言分析的基本概念和 方法。通過對漢語結構的分析，學生將更深入地了解漢語的結構以及人類語言的本 質，從而提高漢語作為第二語言/外語教學之教學知識與研究方法。通過對漢語的全 面理解，學生在成為華語教師後，將能夠回答華語課堂中所遇到的各種語言問題， 並可以提高其學生的學習興趣，並獲得更好的學習成果。 四、課堂用書： 1. 舒兆民，2021，《現代漢語語言學概要》，台北：新學林。 2. 自編講義（請見閱讀清單）。 五、參考資料： Chao, Yuen Ren. 1968. docs.name: 華語學習策略專題
docs.text:
課程內容：
1. 語言學習策略之概念與學理教材介紹與分析
2. 華語的特質與外國學生的難點
3. 華語策略之獲取與開發
4. 自我的語言學習策略探索
5. 華語學習策略之訓練
6. 華語聽力及口說之學習策略探討
7. 華語字詞語法之學習策略探討
8. 華語閱讀之學習策略探討
9. 華語學習策略之教材分析
10. 專業華語之特殊學習策略研討 (例商務華語、導遊華語、新聞華語…等)
11. 華語學習策略之課堂活動
12. 華語學習策略教學法之建構

課程進度：

09/03 課程簡介
華語教學之概念

09/10 華語文學習策略教學的需求背景
閱讀資料：專書第一章

09/17 第二語言學習策略之研究發展
閱讀資料：專書第二章

09/24 語文學習策略的分類
閱讀資料：Rebecca Oxford
※外籍生學習策略探察作業 開始

10/01 華語文的閱讀策略教學探討
閱讀資料：專書第三章

10/08 華語文策略的分類與採集研究
閱讀資料：專書第五章

10/15 閱讀策略訓練之教材評析-1
閱讀資料：專書第四章

10/22 閱讀策略訓練之教材評析-2
閱讀資料：專書第四章
※ 繳交 札記 (1)

10/29 外國學生之華語學習策略之採集 –課堂分享
※繳交 外籍生學習策略探察作業

11/05 外籍生之華語學習策略分享

11/12 閱讀策略的教學規劃－以「分詞」策略為例
閱讀資料：專書第六章
※ 策略教學設計活動

11/19 閱讀策略的教學規劃－以「斷句」策略為例
閱讀資料：專書第七章
※ 期末作業 啟動

11/26 華語聽力策略之規劃範例 – 增進聽力寬度之策略
聽力寬度之自我練習 – 英語及華語

12/03 華語口說策略之範例 -- 口語跟讀策略
※ 繳交期末作業大綱

12/10 閱讀策略教學法之建構
閱讀資料：專書第九章 + 第十章
※ 繳交 札記 (2)
12/18 期末作業討論

12/25 ※ 繳交 期末作業

評量方式：
課程參與 (出席、討論等) 10 %
札記與心得撰寫 (平時) 20 % (評分兩次各 10 %)
文章領讀/教材介紹 10%
外籍生學習策略探察 20%
策略教學設計活動 10 %
期末報告 30 %
Bonus: 現場參加國際型研討會 每個研討會2%.

教材：
1. 本課講義彙編
2. 信世昌 (2020) 華語文閱讀策略之教程發展 (第二版)。台北：五南出版公司。
ISBN 978-957-763-793-2

參考書目：
Oxford, R. L. (1990). Language Learning Strategies. Boston: Heinle & Heinle
Publishers.
Interactions (英語技能系列教材) Cambridge Press.

docs.name: 臺灣與印度工作坊
docs.text:
1. Course Description:

The primary objective of this course is to provide students with exposure to
practical and social experiences outside the university setting. This will
enable students to plan ahead and explore potential career paths after
completing their Master's degree in India studies.

2. References:

Ausaja, S. M. M. contributor, Aikat, Kajori contributor, Bachchan, Amitabh 1942-
writer of foreword. Bollywood: The Films! The Songs! The Stars! London: Dorling
Kindersley Limited, 2017.
Manfield, Christine. Tasting India: Heirloom Family Recipes. Cammeray, N.S.W. :
Simon and Schuster, 2018.

Reshii, Marryam H. The Flavour of Spice: Journeys, Recipes, Stories. Gurgaon:
Hachette India, 2017
Sen, Amartya. The Argumentative Indian- Writings on Indian Culture, History and
Identity. London: Penguin Books, 2005.
Sen, Amartya. Home in the World: A Memoir. London: Allen Lane, 2021.
Shah, Vidya. Jalsa: Indian Women and Their Journeys from the Salon to the
Studio. Chennai: Tulika Books, 2016.

3. Teaching Method:

Teaching Method includes lectures, discussions, and students’ presentations.
Each week, distinguished speakers will share their hands-on experience or
cutting-edge research on specific topics, which will be further analyzed and
discussed in group discussion sessions right after the speeches. Students will
be expected to write their own analysis and summary of the topics and choose a
topic for their term project. Active participation in class is expected.

4. Syllabus

1. Introduction
Prof. Wang, Wei-Chung
Director, Center for India Studies, National Tsing Hua University.
2. India-Taiwan Relations
Speaker: India Taipei Association
3. India-Taiwan Cultural Relations
