Priya Lee Translation & Consulting
4. Taiwan-India Security Cooperation
Speaker: Dr. Shen, Ming-Shih
Acting Deputy CEO, Institute for National Defense and Security Research
5. Group discussion and presentation
6. Taiwan-India Cooperation in ICT Industry
Speaker: Dr. Hu, Tien-Shen
President, Foundation for Commerce and Culture Interchange
7. Taiwan-India’s Economic and Business Interaction
Speaker: Mr. Manik Kumar
Sales Manager, Socle Technology Corporation
8. India-Taiwan in Science and Technology
Speaker: Prof. Wang, Chin-Tsan
Distinguished Professor, Department of Mechanical and Electro-Mechanical
Engineering, National Ilan University; Former Director, Science and Technology
Division in Taiwan Embassy, India
9. Taiwan-India’s Financial Interaction
Speaker: E. Sun Bank
10. Group discussion and presentation
11. Indo-Taiwan Connectivity, Academic Exchange and Service Learning
Initiative Speaker: Prof. Albert Wei-Min Tang
Chair, Department of Communication Arts, Fu Jen University
12. India and Taiwan: a complementary partnership
Speaker: Amb. Ong, Wen-Chyi
Former Taiwanese Ambassador to India
13. Taiwan-India’s Politics and Policy
Speaker: Prof. Chen, Mu-min
Graduate Institute of International Politics, National Chung Hsing University;
Former Deputy Representative, Taipei Economic and Cultural Center in India
14. India-Taiwan Relations
Speaker: Department of East and Asian Affairs, Ministry of Foreign Affairs
15. Group discussion and presentation
16. Term Report

Note:
The course syllabus will be modified further according to the availability and
topics of the invited speakers.

5. Evaluation

1. Class attendance and discussion: 40%
2. Group discussion and presentation: 30%
3. Term project: 30%

docs.name: 跨領域探索
docs.text:
●課程說明
本課程將邀請工學院教師，介紹化學工程、動力機械工程、材料科學、工程及工業工程及醫工所，四系
醫所的學習內容
及未來發展。藉團隊合作的方式，讓同學從資訊分享的過程，探索校內其他專長領域。課程將引導學生
檢視自我性向，從探索自己的特質與優勢，到釐清瞭解適合自己選擇的第二專長。
此外，課程引導學生利用跨界思考的方式，學習探究並提案生活問題及建立解決方案，鼓勵學生以探
索、獨立思考、活用知識及解決問題的能力，讓知識與生活連結，提升學習興趣。

● 成績考核(依第一次上課公告為主)
作業：共2次（30％）
報告：共2次
期中報告：探索專長（30％）
期末報告：團隊跨域創意發想口頭報告（30％）
出席成績及其他（10％）

---------------------------------------
人工智慧倫理聲明
經仔細考量後，本課程授課教師認為不宜於此門課程當中使用生成式人工智慧於課堂學習當中。因本課
程的內容於生成式AI中尚有諸多錯誤，且容易影響學生對基礎核心知識之判讀。

根據本校公布之佈的「大學教育場域AI協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採取禁止使用，以下為相
關的監管機制

查核發現，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。
修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。

3.領航老師輔導方式：
(1)每位老師以帶領 1 組學生為原則。
(2)分享相關經驗，提供學生對產業認識、職能養成、職場體驗及實作等資源。
(3)協助學生職涯發展之輔導與諮詢。

docs.text: 授 課 學 期 114 學年度 第 1 學期 開 課 單 位 □ 跨院國際博士班學位學程 □ 跨院國際碩士學位學程 課 程 名 稱(中文) 科技旅讀：電腦、人工智慧、機器人 課 程 名 稱(英文) Travel and Reading for Technology：Computers, AI, and Robotics 授 課 教 師 陳鴻文、陳俊銘 學分數 2 授 課 教 室 ■校本部綜二___________ □南大_________ 上課時間 授 課 語 言 □英文 ■中文 人數限制 20 課 程 限 制 無 課 程 簡 述 本課程以「科技旅讀」為核心，結合理論講授與企業參訪，帶領學 生深入了解台灣在電腦、人工智慧（AI）與機器人產業中的角色 與轉型挑戰。課程從組織設計、產業結構與國家發展等理論出發， 探討台灣企業如何在全球價值鏈中持續升級，並掌握 AI 與智慧製 造對產業生態的影響。 中 文 暨 英 文 關 鍵 字 （ 五 組） 電腦產業 Computer Industry 人工智慧 Artificial Intelligence (AI) 機器人技術 Robotics 產業策略與國家發展 Industrial Strategy and National Development 科技與社會 Technology and Society 課 程 大 綱 Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程以「科技旅讀」為核心教學方式，結合理論建構與實地 參訪，帶領同學探索台灣科技產業——特別是電腦、人工智慧 （AI）與機器人相關產業——在企業策略、產業結構與全球競爭 體系中的發展脈絡與轉型挑戰。 台灣長年於全球電腦代工產業中扮演關鍵角色，雖然生產線多數外 移中國，但本地廠商憑藉技術整合與供應鏈管理持續鞏固地位。面 對中國崛起與製造外移的壓力，台灣企業如何升級與創新，成為本 課程關注的核心議題。同時，AI 與機器人技術的興起正快速改變 產業生態，進一步牽動半導體與智慧製造等關鍵領域，本課程將帶 領學生從理論與實務雙軌並進，掌握產業變革趨勢。 課程內容分為三大模組： 理論建構：介紹五力分析、全球價值鏈、創新兩難、產業群聚、國 家發展等核心理論，建立學生分析企業與產業的基礎架構。 科技主題探索：聚焦 AI 與機器人的技術演進與產業應用，並探討 其與台灣半導體與製造業的整合關係。 實地參訪與回饋：安排科技企業參訪與業界專家分享，強化學生對 產業現場與實務議題的理解。 本課程適合理工與人文社會領域學生共同修習，並採跨域小組方式 進行學習與專題製作。學生需於期中提出研究提案，並於期末完成 整合報告；每次參訪亦需事前準備提問並繳交心得，以提升批判思 辨與實務觀察能力。透過課堂訓練與現場觀察相結合，培養學生從 科技產業理解社會變遷、從企業決策反思全球結構的綜合能力。 ● 課程單元 週次 課程主題 推薦閱讀 1 課程說明 沈方正（2022）《科技與社會 的交錯：觀點與方法》。左岸 文化。 2 組織設計與核心競爭力 Galloway, R. docs.name: 新生命-混合實境藝術
docs.text: 國立清華大學 114 學年 -上學期 (2025-09) 跨院博密集課程 - 11410IPHD500100 1 / 2 新生命 - 混合實境藝術 New Life - Mixed Reality Art 授課老師 : 陳珠櫻教授 & 李瑞光教授 Pr. CHEN Chu-Yin & Pr. LEE Ray-Kuang 上課時間、地點 : (2 天密集式工作坊) 2025/09/06 (六)，清大校本部 - 綜二 B 側: 204、205 教室 ； 2025/09/20 (六)，桃園科技藝術節展場 - 中原文創園區 https://g.co/kgs/FpFGRdZ 課程學分：1 學分 (16 小時) 授課語言 : 英文/中文 參考圖 : 精緻生命 in XR - 混合實境之共創體驗 關鍵詞 : 科學與藝術，超現實主義、精緻屍骸共創，當代科技藝術，虛擬/擴增/混合實境藝術。 Science & Art, Surrealism, Co-creation of Exquisite Corpses, Contemporary Technological Art, Virtual/Augmented/Mixed Reality Art. 課程簡述： 本課程聚焦於探索未來宇宙及創意生命的無限可能，體驗前所未有的沉浸式科技藝術之旅！ 課程內容主要分為三部份：「科學與藝術」、「精緻生命 in XR」及「參觀桃園科技藝術節」，透過 VR 技術共創模式及沉浸式混合實境體驗，拓展實驗性和趣味性的美感經驗；激發對未來宇宙與新 生命形式的發想，及探索未來世界人類與非人類生命共存的可能性。 國立清華大學 114 學年 -上學期 (2025-09) 跨院博密集課程 - 11410IPHD500100 2 / 2 課程內容說明： 1. 科學與藝術 : 來自一場人類情感智慧與科技力量、藝術想像力的協同合作 ! 探索未來宇宙 : 首先介紹量子科學的最新發展，並以在台灣及日本「黑洞及重力波」展覽為例， 說明如何運用科技藝術、音樂和影像來呈現黑洞和重力波的本質及探測原理。科學如何成為藝術 家的創作靈感，讓觀眾以沉浸式、互動式的藝術聲光效果，進入科學與科技藝術的殿堂了解天文 宇宙的現象，拓展人類的新視野。 開發創意場域: 介紹第二次世界大戰後的「精緻屍骸」共創理念，源自法國超現實主義運動所發起 的創作接龍遊戲，是一種多腦共創形式 ，布魯東、達利和畢卡索等藝術家都是這一運動的積極參 與者。超現實主義者認為這是一種極具挑戰性、但又隱含無限可能的共同創作方式；既是探索集 體無意識的實驗，又能揭示人類心靈深處的想像力。 2. 黑客松 – 精緻生命 in XR： 汲取「精緻屍骸」的共創理念，由法國巴黎第八大學團隊所研發的「精緻生命 in XR」混合實境裝 置模組，提供並賦予了這種獨特的沉浸式集體創作形式。通過 VR 技術及 360°的空間維度，每個 團隊成員在虛擬實境眼鏡裡進行繪圖接龍遊戲，共同創作精美的新生命個體，最後並在虛擬的與 現實的混合實境中，延續富有實驗性和趣味性的美感賞析經驗。 3. 參觀 - 桃園科技藝術節: 2025 年展覽主題為 : 「新生命 New Type」，探索未來的新生命形式。藉由實地觀展、親身體 驗、沉浸作品中，進入藝術家對未來生命演化的想像世界。展覽作品涵蓋 : 「機器（Robot）、人造人（Android）、賽伯格（Cyborg）、混種（Hybrid）、基因改造 （Genetic Modification）、人工智慧（Artificial Intelligence）以及人工生命（Artificial Life）等 全新樣態。[ …. ] 讓我們在科技與生命交融的時代，重新思考生命的本質與邊界，激發對生命形式 演變及倫理挑戰的深刻反思，以及人類與機器未來共存的可能性。」(截自展覽文宣) 教學方式 : 著重跨領域、非邏輯性、非線性思維，對未知好奇、勇於嘗試探討。 共同審思 : 科學和藝術的本質與與現代精神，人類與科技的共生關係。 共創體驗 :「精緻生命 in XR」之多腦共創發想及人機共創協作。 實地參觀 : 桃園科技藝術節 2025「新生命 New Type」。 自我反思 : 未來生命的演化方向及新生命的倫理挑戰。 成績考核 : 上課出席狀況: 30% 異地學習必須全程出席。 分組討論報告: 30% 參與度與創意思維。 心得感想撰寫: 40% 中文為主; A4 紙至少 2 頁 (字體大小 12，每頁至少 1000 字) 。 學生使用 AI 的規則： 本門課程採取禁止使用， 1 國立清華大學 114 學年 -上學期 (2025-09) 跨院博密集課程 - 11410IPHD500100 新生命 - 混合實境藝術 New Life - Mixed Reality Art 陳珠櫻教授 & 李瑞光教授 Pr. docs.name: 透視韓國教育：制度、文化與全球脈動
docs.text: 1 Understanding Korean Education Hwanbo Park, Ph.D. (Professor, Chungnam National University) Course Objectives This course provides a general introduction to Korean education for international students. It will explore four main themes: 1. Korean education system 2. Korea’ educatioanl fever 3. Korean schools and student life 4. The impact of globalization on Korean education Rather than simply presenting factual information, the course explores Korea’s educational system, policies, and challenges as socially and historically constructed phenomena shaped by various actors within Korean society. Students will be encouraged to engage critically with the topics and reflect on similarities and differences between Korean education and their own contexts. Various media will be used to support learning, and class discussions will offer opportunities for students to share their own experiences and perspectives. Readings Course materials will include a variety of sources such as policy documents, videos, newspaper articles, and academic readings. Students are strongly encouraged to attend the first class to receive detailed information about course materials. Class Activities The course consists of lecture and discussion. Each class begins with a short lecture to introduce the topic, followed by interactive discussions. Students are expected to participate actively in every session. They will be grouped in small teams to lead discussions on a rotating basis. Topics, Readings, and Assignments by Class Day Session 1 – Korean Education System - Overview of Korean Educational System - Educational Acheivement (educational expansion and academic achievement) - National Development and the Role of Education in Korea 2 - Key issues and challenges of Korean Education - Comparative Reflections Session 2 – Korea’ educatioanl fever - The meaning and characteristics of educational fever - Root causes: colonial legacy, competition, job market, and college entrance - Family expectations and their influence on education - Comparative Reflections Session 3 – Korean schools and student life - School culture and student in K-drama - Daily life and routines of Korean students - Comparative Reflections Session 4 – Globalization and Korean Education - Internationalization of Korean education - Global citizenship education in Korea - Korea’s role in educational development and cooperation - Comparative Reflections

docs.text: 11320IPHD700100 iPHD Seminar Lecturer: Prof. Hung-Wen Chen hungwen@mx.nthu.edu.tw Course Overview This course is designed for graduate students in iPhD program of NTHU to broaden their horizons in different areas. This course, students will be required to invite speakers from interdisciplinary areas of research to share their cutting-edge results. All students are encouraged to have interactions with the speakers. Please see the Syllabus for more details. Course Policy (Tentative) 1. In this seminar, we have 12 talks in total (12 Attendances). Course introduction and IPhD Orientation are excluded. 2. Students are required to attend the seminar on time (Tues. 16:30) and the TAs will take your attendance. 3. To pass this course, students are required to (1) Attend talks at least 10 times in total (2) Team up, invite a speaker and host the speech on that day as a team. (3) Ask 1 question to at least 2 different speakers during the semester and upload your questions and the responses from the speakers to eeclass platform before the evening of the next day (Thu. 18:00). 4. docs.name: 營運管理
docs.text:
Course objectives

By the end of this course, students will:

Develop a foundational understanding of operations management concepts and their
role in business
strategy, particularly within technology-based and high-growth industries.

Apply quantitative and analytical tools to solve real-world operations problems,
including process design,
capacity planning, and inventory control.

Analyze and evaluate the effectiveness of operational decisions in enhancing
efficiency, quality, and
competitiveness in global and tech-driven markets.

Strengthen communication, teamwork, and problem-solving skills through case
studies, simulations, and
industry-relevant projects.

Course Description

Operations Management is essential to the success of any business, from start-
ups to global enterprises.
This course provides IBBA students with a comprehensive understanding of how to
design, manage, and
improve the systems and processes that deliver value to customers. Students will
learn key topics such as
process flow analysis, supply chain coordination, quality management, capacity
and inventory planning,
and lean operations. Emphasis is placed on the application of analytical tools
and strategic decision-
making in the context of modern, technology-driven organizations.

Designed for students pursuing international business careers, the course
bridges theoretical concepts
with practical business challenges. It equips students with the skills to
evaluate operational trade-offs,
improve efficiency, and align operations with business goals. Whether aiming for
roles in operations,
consulting, entrepreneurship, or management, students will gain valuable
insights into how operational
excellence supports innovation, competitiveness, and growth in dynamic global
markets.

Textbooks

Reid, R. D., & Sanders, N. R. (2010). Operations Management (Fourth edition.).
John Wiley & Sons, Inc.

Teaching Approach

Experiential Learning Focus:
The course emphasizes “learning by doing.” Students will engage in hands-on
simulations, process
mapping exercises, and real-world case analyses to apply operational theories to
practical business
challenges.

Collaborative Activities:
Students will work in small teams to analyze and improve a real or simulated
business operation. Each
team will develop an operations improvement plan, including key metrics and
implementation strategies,
and present their findings to the class for peer and instructor feedback.

Balanced Pedagogy:
While interactive exercises and projects are emphasized, core concepts in
operations management—such
as supply chain design, inventory control, and lean systems—will be introduced
through concise lectures,
case studies, and guided readings to provide a solid theoretical foundation.

Feedback-Driven Iteration:
Ongoing feedback from the instructor and peers will support student development
and iterative refinement
of team projects, with a focus on practical solutions, critical thinking, and
data-driven decision-making.

Assessment:
Grades will be based on participation, group project performance, case
analysis presentations, short
quizzes, and individual written reflections on operational challenges and
learning outcomes.

Grading

Attendance is Critical

1. Success in this course depends heavily on showing up and staying engaged
2. Each session builds sequentially, introducing new tools and applying them to
operational challenges
3. Missing class means missing hands-on exercises, simulations, and critical
team-based activities
4. Regular attendance leads to deeper understanding and better performance
5. Like in real-world operations, consistency and reliability are key

Active Participation is Mandatory

1. This is not a lecture-only course
2. Everyone is expected to contribute to class discussions, group problem-
solving, and simulations
3. You’ll take on various operational roles, just like in a real business
environment
4. Your voice, questions, and insights help shape the learning experience for
the entire class

Final Evaluation is Real-World

1. Final group projects will involve analyzing and improving a real or simulated
business operation
2. You’ll be expected to present your findings and defend your recommendations
to your peers and
instructor
3. This mimics real-world decision-making, where clarity, logic, and
practicality matter
4. Your ability to connect theory to action will be a major part of your final
assessment

Grading Breakdown

1. Class Participation & Attendance: 45%
2. Team Project & Presentation: 25%
3. Case Analyses / Simulations: 20%
4. Final Exam: 10%

Course Schedule

Week 1: Course Introduction & Overview of Operations Management
Course goals, expectations, and deliverables
What is Operations Management (OM)?
OM in manufacturing vs. services
Key decisions, global trends, and challenges
Exercise: Student reflection: “Where do we see OM in everyday life?”

Week 2: Operations Strategy and Competitiveness
Strategic alignment between OM and business goals
Competitive priorities: cost, quality, flexibility, speed
Productivity measurement and improvement
Exercise: Case study: Analyze the strategy of a global tech company (e.g., TSMC,
Apple)

Week 3: Product Design and Process Selection
New product development process
Process types: job shop, batch, continuous, etc.
linking product decisions to process strategy
Exercise: Design a new product and match it to an optimal process layout

Week 4: Supply Chain Management
Components and flows of a supply chain
Supply chains in manufacturing and services
Bullwhip effect and digital transformation
Exercise: Supply chain mapping: Trace a popular tech product from raw material
to customer

Week 5: AI Tools in Operations Management
Role of AI in modern OM: forecasting, quality, scheduling
Predictive analytics and intelligent systems
Opportunities and ethical considerations in AI adoption
Exercise: Tech Lab: Try a free AI-based OM tool (e.g., demand forecasting
platform or smart
scheduler)

Weeks 6: Total Quality Management (TQM)
Principles and philosophies of TQM
ISO standards, quality awards, and continuous improvement
Cost of quality
Exercise: Quality audit: Evaluate a sample firm’s quality system using TQM
principles

Week 7: Statistical Quality Control (SQC)
Control charts for variables and attributes
Variation, process capability, and Six Sigma basics
Exercise: Create and interpret a control chart with real or simulated data

Week 8: Just-in-Time (JIT) and Lean Systems
Lean thinking and the 7 wastes
Pull systems and Kanban
JIT applications in services
Exercise: Process redesign: Identify and eliminate waste in a given scenario

Week 9: Forecasting
Qualitative and quantitative methods
Time series models and causal relationships
Measuring forecast accuracy
Exercise: Build a basic sales forecast in Excel or Google Sheets

Week 10: Capacity Planning and Facility Location
Capacity measurement and planning
Location decision factors and models
Using decision trees for location choices
Exercise: Case analysis: Recommend a facility location based on weighted
criteria

Week 11: Facility Layout and Work System Design
Types of layouts: process, product, fixed-position, cellular
Work system design, job enrichment, and ergonomics
Work measurement techniques
Exercise: Design a layout for a small manufacturing operation

Week 12: Inventory Management
Types and functions of inventory
EOQ, reorder points, and ABC analysis
Safety stock and service-level considerations
Exercise: Solve EOQ and reorder point problems with case data

Week 13: Aggregate and Resource Planning
Aggregate planning strategies: level vs. chase
MRP and ERP systems
Balancing demand and capacity
Exercise: Simulation: Create an aggregate plan for a seasonal business

Week 14: Scheduling
Gantt charts, job sequencing, and bottlenecks
Priority rules and workforce scheduling
Theory of constraints
Exercise: Create a project schedule using sequencing rules and a Gantt chart

Week 15: Project Management
Project life cycle and planning
PERT/CPM and critical path analysis
Crashing and project risk
Exercise: Draw a project network, calculate critical path, and explore crashing
options

Week 16: Final Exam – Real-Time Group Operations Challenge
Students receive an unexpected operations problem (e.g., production delay,
quality failure, inventory
misalignment)
Real-time data updates and time pressure
Each team presents a solution strategy and justifies their decisions
Assessment: Group presentation + action plan report judged on clarity,
feasibility, and logic

Gen AI Conditionally open:

In this course, the use of Generative AI (GenAI) tools is conditionally allowed
and, in some cases,
encouraged—especially where they can enhance analytical thinking, efficiency,
and creativity. As
operations professionals increasingly integrate AI into forecasting, quality
control, and process
improvement, becoming comfortable with such tools will strengthen your practical
skillset.
Permitted Uses of GenAI:

Idea Generation & Brainstorming: Use GenAI to help generate ideas for process
improvements, supply
chain innovations, or operations strategies.
Writing & Clarity Support: You may use GenAI to help structure reports, refine
written content, or
improve presentation slides for professionalism and readability.
Research & Summarization: GenAI may be used to gather insights, summarize
industry trends, or
explore new operational technologies such as AI in scheduling or inventory
management.
Limitations and Considerations:
Original Thought Required: Final submissions must reflect your own analytical
thinking, problem-
solving, and teamwork. Over-reliance on AI-generated content will negatively
impact your learning and
may affect your grade.
Decision-Making and Leadership: GenAI cannot analyze live case data for you
during in-class
exercises or the final group simulation. The ability to interpret information
and make decisions under
pressure is a key learning outcome.

The Importance of the Human Element:

While GenAI is a powerful tool, your success in operations management depends on
skills such as
collaboration, judgment, adaptability, and communication. These human-centered
skills are essential to
lead and implement real-world solutions effectively.

Ethics and Acknowledgment:

If GenAI is used for specific segments of your work, acknowledge its role when
appropriate. For example,
you may include a footnote in your business plan or pitch slides mentioning how
GenAI supported your
process.

Student Leave Policy

In accordance with the National Tsing Hua University Regulations for Student
Leave of Absence

docs.text: National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 科號 Course Number IPMT200600 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Size of Limit 60 中文名稱 Course Title 綠色及轉型金融 英文名稱 Course English Title Green and Transitional Finance 任課教師 Instructor 王自雄 教師聯絡方式 Contact Information thwang@iii.org.tw 上課時間 Time T5T6 上課教室 Room 台積館 204 教室 先修科目 Prerequisite(s) 無 本課程對應之學習目標與核心能力 Aligned Learning Goals and Learning Objectives □ 運用專業管理與科技知識的能力。 Our students will master the knowledge of technology and professional management. ■ 整合與活用第一專長及第二專長的專業知識能力，並具備跨領域規劃、領導與執行 團隊合作的能力。(30%) Our students will be able to integrate expertise from their double specialty and thus plan, execute and lead in an interdisciplinary team setting. (30%) □ 具備中文及英文閱讀寫作商業報告與商業口頭簡報能力。 Our students will be able to read and produce professional business documents as well as deliver a professional oral presentation in English and in Chinese. ■ 認識產業的國際發展趨勢，瞭解管理與科技對環境、社會及全球的影響，並培養自 我學習成長的能力。 (40%) Our students will develop the ability of self-learning by comprehending the international development trend of the industry and by comprehending the impact of management and technology made on the environment, the society and the world. (40%) ■ 理解專業倫理及社會責任的能力。 (30%) Our students will be equipped with understandings of professional ethics and social responsibility. (30%) 課程目標 Course Objectives 本課程將針對授信、投資、資本市場籌資、人才培育、金融商品發展、資訊揭露、審慎 監理、國際鏈結及誘因機制、反漂綠等面向，帶領修課同學深入了解並共同分析國內外 政策、法令、產業實踐，尤其包括川普 2.0 下對於金融業投入永續活動之反動，期能引 領了解此一牽動技術發展、淨零轉型、以及資本移動的重要趨勢。 課程說明 Course Description National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 我國自 2022 年承諾「2050 年淨零排放目標」以來，戮力推動淨零轉型與永續發展，國 家發展委員會 2022 年發布的「2050 淨零排放路徑」已將「綠色金融」列入十二項關鍵 戰略中，運用綠色金融機制與影響力，將資金導引到符合能源轉型、產業轉型、生活轉 型及社會轉型的企業或專案，並促使企業將永續的概念與精神逐步深化於各產業文化。 前（2023）年我國將 2050 淨零排放目標正式納入《氣候變遷因應法》，確立我國氣候治 理法制化，亦突顯我國實踐淨零排放承諾及落實永續相關行動的決心。去（2024）年賴 總統更進一步成立「國家氣候變遷對策委員會」，集結部會首長、產業界及公民代表、跨 領域專家學者共同就氣候變遷議題，提出因應與調適策略，強化國家永續發展的韌性。 金融業在推動永續轉型的過程中所扮演的角色尤其關鍵，不僅透過投融資、金融商品的 設計、議合等影響力，帶動企業重視 ESG 議題與風險，也可透過自身減碳及對低碳產業 的支持，加速企業布局永續行動。國際上有觀點認為「綠色金融」主要僅支持「綠色」、 「永續」的企業或專案，對於尚未達到綠色、永續標準的企業則應限縮資金的提供，以 促使企業減碳及改善。然而，這些尚未達到綠色、永續的企業，其產業雖是溫室氣體排 放的主要來源，卻也是全球經濟的重要支柱，更應協助其淨零轉型，這些產業例如水泥、 鋼鐵、鋁、肥料、電力業等。由於這些產業尚未符合「綠色」標準，過去往往無法獲得 綠色金融的支持。整體而言，綠色及轉型金融是新興發展並極為重要的問題，深入了解 其背後的政策考量、關鍵面向與影響因素等，是永續管理與金融專業的重要內涵。 請輸入課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」至少 5 個, 每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文, 以半形逗 點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 綠色金融 Green Finance, 轉型金融 Transitional Finance, 淨零排放 Net-Zero, 環境、社會、 及治理 ESG, 永續 Sustainability 指定用書 Textbooks 無 參考書籍 References 由於課程主題新興多元、變化迅速，授課教師將依相關政策發展指定最新、前沿閱讀教 材置於課程網站。 教學方式 Teaching Approach 本課程以教師講授為主軸，但重視學生參與課堂討論。教師並將於每週主題補充最新時 事發展，與學生交流意見。另本課程將視需要部分採取同步遠距授課方式。 評分標準 Grading National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 本課程重視參與，修課同學的學期成績會以課程參與（60%）及期末報告（40%）作為 評量。期末報告字數至多八千字（含註腳）。 1. 期末報告題目須與本課程主題相關，但不限於課綱所列議題。請於第九週前提交期末 報告大綱，並約授課教師討論時間，以確認期末報告與本課程之相關性及適切性。 2. 期末報告切勿堆砌英翻中或網站文章。報告內容請以個人意見或論點為主軸，再進一 步尋找佐證之數據或資料。 教學進度 Course Schedule 第一週 課程導覽與介紹 ➢ Lloyds Banking Group, What is green finance?, https://www.lloydsbankinggroup.com/insights/green-finance.html ➢ World Economic Forum, What is green finance and why is it important?, https://www.weforum.org/stories/2020/11/what-is-green-finance/ 第二週 我國綠色及轉型金融政策（1/2） ➢ 金管會「綠色金融行動方案 2.0」八大面向辦理情形 ➢ 金管會「綠色金融行動方案 3.0」 第三週 我國綠色及轉型金融政策（2/2） ➢ 金管會「綠色及轉型金融行動方案」 ➢ 金管會「轉型計畫建議涵蓋事項」 ➢ 第一屆永續金融評鑑 第四週 從審慎監理到盡職治理：中央銀行及機構投資人的角色 ➢ 中央銀行因應氣候變遷策略方案 ➢ 英國盡職治理守則（The UK Stewardship Code） ➢ 證交所「機構投資人盡職治理守則」 第五週 金融業自己綠不綠：範疇三碳排放的盤查 ➢ 證交所「上市櫃公司範疇 3 溫室氣體盤查作業參考指引」 National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus ➢ 金融業範疇三財務碳排放計算指引 ➢ 保險業內控及稽核制度實施辦法第 5、19、41 條修正 第六週 銀行授信的對象綠不綠：永續經濟活動的分類標準 ➢ 金管會「永續經濟活動認定參考指引」第二版 ➢ 歐盟永續分類規則（EU Sustainability Taxonomy Regulation） ➢ 王自雄，永續金融中的企業人權責任—論歐盟永續投資規則之最低限度保障，《台 灣法學雜誌》，411 期，頁 131-147（2021 年 3 月 14 日） 第七週 綠色債券及保險商品及市場 ➢ 綠色債券、社會責任債券、永續發展（連結）債券 ➢ 綠色保險 第八週 企業永續資訊的揭露（1/4） ➢ 歐盟企業永續報告指令（Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive, CSRD） ➢ 歐盟永續報告準則（European Sustainability Reporting Standards, ESRS） 第九週 企業永續資訊的揭露（2/4） ➢ 國際財務報導準則（International Financial Reporting Standards, IFRS）永續揭露準 則第 S1 號－永續相關財務資訊揭露之一般規定 第十週 企業永續資訊的揭露（3/4） ➢ 國際財務報導準則（International Financial Reporting Standards, IFRS）永續揭露準 則第 S2 號－氣候相關揭露 第十一週 企業永續資訊的揭露（4/4） ➢ 金管會，我國接軌 IFRS 永續揭露準則藍圖 ➢ 櫃買中心，IFRS 永續揭露準則問答集 ➢ IFRS 永續揭露準則相關內部控制實務 National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 第十二週 企業的社會投資如何量化 社會投資報酬率（Social Return On Investment, SROI）評估指南 第十三週 企業的永續自白：永續報告書 ➢ 證交所「上市公司編製與申報永續報告書作業辦法」 ➢ 如何採用 TCFD 與 SASB 符合我國揭露要求 ➢ 企業永續報告書評析 第十四週 當永續言過其實：反漂綠 ➢ 金管會「金融機構防漂綠參考指引」 ➢ 永續資訊揭露不實的法律責任 第十五週 永續的反動 ➢ ESG 的川普效應及反 DEI 運動 ➢ 銀行業退出淨零銀行聯盟（NZBA） 第十六週 修課同學期末報告 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則 (Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) (1)完全開放使用且無須註明 Unrestricted use with no disclosure required ☑(2)有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output (3)禁止使用，請註明相關的監管機制 Prohibited use; please specify relevant oversight (4)本課程無涉及 AI 使用 Not applicable 生成式 AI 倫理聲明 基於透明與負責任的原則，本課程鼓勵學生利用 AI 進行協作或互學，以提升本門課產出品質。根據本 校公布之佈的「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採取：「有條件開放，請註明 如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出」 學生須於課堂作業或報告中的「標題頁註腳」或「引用文獻後」簡要說明如何使用生成式 AI 進行議題發 想、程式修改、文句潤飾或結構參考等使用方式。若經查核使用卻無在作業或報告中標明，教師、學校 National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。本門課授課教材或學習資料若有引用自生成 式 AI，教師也將在投影片或口頭標注。修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。 課程相關連接 Course Related Links 隨各周教學進度檢附

docs.text: National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 科號 Course Number IPMT200700 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Size of Limit 100 中文名稱 Course Title 創意思考 英文名稱 Course English Title Creative Thinking 任課教師 Instructor 洪 嘉駿 / Katsun Ang 教師聯絡方式 Contact Information j.ang@mx.NTHU.edu.tw 上課時間 Time 週一 下午第一 節第二節 上課教室 Room 台積館 224 教室 先修科目 Prerequisite(s) 本課程對應之學習目標與核心能力 Aligned Learning Goals and Learning Objectives 此科目對應之系所課程規劃所欲培養之核心能力 運用專業管理與科技知識的能力。 Our students will master the knowledge of technology and professional management. 整合與活用第一專長及第二專長的專業知識能力，並具備跨領域規劃、領導與執行團 隊合作的能力。 Our students will be able to integrate expertise from their double specialty and thus plan, execute and lead in an interdisciplinary team setting. 具備中文及英文閱讀寫作商業報告與商業口頭簡報能力。 Our students will be able to read and produce professional business documents as well as deliver a professional oral presentation in English and in Chinese. 認識產業的國際發展趨勢，瞭解管理與科技對環境、社會及全球的影響，並培養自 我學習成長的能力。 Our students will develop the ability of self-learning by comprehending the international development trend of the industry and by comprehending the impact of management and technology made on the environment, the society and the world. 理解專業倫理及社會責任的能力。 Our students will be equipped with understandings of professional ethics and social responsibility. National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 課程目標 Course Objectives 問對問題，設計創意解決方案！ 透過創意發想與思考，定義問題並設計問題解決模型。透過創新的設計思考 方式，深入了解需求和問題，創造出更具價值和有意義的產品或服務，且激 發創新思維和創造力。 課程說明 Course Description 本課程以人為核心出發，Design Thinking 設計思考為主體，輔以個案分析、 品牌實務研討與業界專家實務演講，培養「危機處理」與「問題解決能力」 之技能。透過以案例分析與創意思維，深入了解使用者的行為和需求，以獲 取更有價值的問題解決方案，讓學生學習在有限的空間和時間內，用簡短的 方式表達創意並解決問題。 請輸入課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」至少 5 個, 每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文, 以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 設計思考（Design Thinking） 設計原則 (Design principles) 創新（Innovation） 設計原則 (Design principles) Brain storming（腦力激盪） 創意發想（Ideate） 定義問題（Define） 指定用書 Textbooks 本課程無特定指定用書，以現代行銷與實務分析探討整合教材，由教師自編 合適之授課題材。 參考書籍 References 無 教學方式 Teaching Approach 1. 個案分析與問題思考。 2. 分組報告與實證反饋討論。 3. 專家演講實務經驗分享。 4. 翻轉學習與情境模擬教學。 評分標準 Grading 1. 課堂參與及討論 (40%) 2. 期中作業(30%) 3. 期末作業(30%) National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 教學進度 Course Schedule 1.創意思維與策略 2.發現問題與技巧實作 3 定義問題 4.問題解決實務研討與設計 5.表達的魅力與舞台技巧 6.行銷策略與市場定位 7.品牌溝通 8.期中評量 9.設計思考 10.廣告文案 11.行銷說服力 12.創新與創意表現 13.廣告創意與案例分析 14.事件行銷與案例分析 15.數位行銷與案例分析 16.期中評量 本課程無涉及 AI 使用 Not applicable 課程相關連接 Course Related Links

docs.name: 統計學一
docs.text: National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 科號 Course Number 11410IPMT2008 00 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Size of Limit 30 中文名稱 Course Title 統計學一 英文名稱 Course English Title Statistics (I) 任課教師 Instructor 賴怡君 教師聯絡方式 Contact Information Email: lai-ic@mx.nthu.edu.tw 上課時間 Time MnM5M6 上課教室 Room TSMC 台積 429 先修科目 Prerequisite(s) 無 本課程對應之學習目標與核心能力 Aligned Learning Goals and Learning Objectives ▪ 學習基礎統計學知識。 Learn foundational knowledge in statistics. ▪ 培養數據統整、處理及分析能力。 Develop skills in data integration, processing, and analysis. ▪ 應用統計方法解讀商業狀況及提出商業洞察。 Apply statistical methods to interpret business situations and provide business insights. 課程目標 Course Objectives ▪ 本系列課程預計包含兩學期，第一學期會以統計學基礎概念為主，並輔以課堂小 組討論，透過實際資料操作，實踐應用統計學解決商業問題的目標。 This course is part of a two-semester series. The first semester focuses on basic statistical concepts, complemented by group discussions. Through hands-on data manipulation, the course aims to apply statistical methods to solve business problems. ▪ 第一學期會協助同學自行下載公開資料、選擇商業問題，涵蓋部分基礎資料操作 (Excel)，並思考適合應用於該商業問題的統計方法。 In the first semester, students will be guided to download publicly available data, select a business problem, perform basic data operations (Excel), and determine the appropriate statistical methods for the identified business problem. ▪ 第二學期進入較多的 Python 操作，完成整個資料前處理、統計處理流程，最後 進行結果分析。 In the second semester, students will focus more on Python for data processing, covering the entire process from data preprocessing to statistical analysis, and results interpretation. 課程說明 Course Description ▪ 作業繳交以小組為單位，第一學期小組討論總共會有四次，每次一小時；過程中 教師會逐一至每一小組了解討論狀態並反饋，協助小組完成任務。 Assignments will be submitted by groups. There will be four group discussions in the first semester, each lasting one hour. Throughout these sessions, the instructor will approach each group to understand their discussion progress and provide feedback to help complete the tasks. ▪ 期中期末考試以個人為單位，試卷內容涵蓋部份模擬資料表，同學以資料表和所 National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 學統計概念為工具，回答試卷問題。 Midterm and final exams will be individual assessments. The exam will include a simulated data table, and students will use the data table and statistical concepts learned in class to answer the exam questions. 課程關鍵字 Course Keywords 統計學、數據分析、量化方法、機率與統計、假設驗證 Statistics, Data Analysis, Quantitative Methods, Probability and Statistics, Hypothesis Testing 指定用書 Textbooks Lind, D. A., Marchal, W. G., & Wathen, S. A. (2021). Basic Statistics in Business and Economics (10th ed.). McGraw-Hill Education. ISBN: 978-1260597578. 參考書籍 References 教學方式 Teaching Approach ▪ 課程包含授課與小組討論，小組討論共四次，每次一小時；小組討論目的為實際 下載公開資料、剖析資料結構，並規劃如何應用統計方法解析資料並解決商業問 題。 The course includes lectures and group discussions, with a total of four group discussions, each lasting one hour. The purpose of these group discussions is to practically download public data, analyze their structure, and plan how to apply statistical methods for data analysis and solving business problems. ▪ 第一學期以統計概念和基礎資料處理為重點(使用 Excel)，第二學期將涵蓋 Python 操作。 The first semester focuses on statistical concepts and basic data handling (using Excel), while the second semester will cover Python programming. 評分標準 Grading ▪ 小組作業 3 次：30% (分別於 Week7, Week 12, Week14 繳交) 3 Group Assignments: 30% (submitted in Week 7, Week 12, and Week 14) ▪ 小組成員互評：10% Peer Evaluation within Group: 10% ▪ 期中考試：30% Midterm exam: 30% ▪ 期末考試：30% Final exam: 30% 教學進度 Course Schedule ▪ Week 1: Course Introduction ▪ Week 2: Data Types and Data Structure ▪ Week 3: Descriptive Statistics ▪ Week 4: Descriptive Statistics & Group Workshop I: Select and download open-source data for the semester and discuss the business problems to be addressed. ▪ Week 5: Probability Concepts ▪ Week 6: Discrete Probability Distributions ▪ Week 7: Continuous Probability Distributions & Group Workshop II: Explore the dataset variables, the variables to be used, and the reasons for the selection. National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus ▪ Week 8: Midterm exam (covering Week 2 to Week 7 content) ▪ Week 9: Sampling and Sampling Methods ▪ Week 10: Estimation and Confidence Intervals ▪ Week 11: Hypothesis Tests ▪ Week 12: Hypothesis Tests & Group Workshop III: Discuss the statistical methods to be used and the rationale behind them. ▪ Week 13: Analysis of Variance ▪ Week 14: Correlation and Linear Regression & Group Workshop IV: Predict the expected results using the selected statistical methods. ▪ Week 15: Multiple Regression Analysis ▪ Week 16: Final exam (covering Week 2 to Week 15 content) 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則 (Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) (2)有條件開放：同學可使用 AI 協助學習，在繳交作業時並註明應用 AI 工具在哪些地 方。期中期末考試不開放應用 AI 工具，讓老師評估每位同學的實際學習狀況。 (2) Conditionally open: Students are allowed to use AI tools to assist with learning. When submitting assignments, students must indicate how AI tools were applied. AI tools will not be allowed during midterm and final exams, so the instructor can accurately assess each student's actual learning progress. 課程相關連接 Course Related Links 國立清華大學 eLearn 數位學習平台 elearn.nthu.edu.tw

科技被運用在產業中？當科技被應用到不同領域(如：行銷、財務、法律、生產、研發、供應 鏈)，管理思維會發生哪些改變？這門課會是你走進這些議題的敲門磚。 本課程由科管院莊慧玲教授發起，目的在於幫助學生了解未來世界的科技變遷與產業發 展。在這門課中，我們設計豐富多元的學習活動，包含書報討論、企業參訪、專題講座、學 長姐採訪、個案討論、小組新興科技報告等。課程不僅著眼於拓展你對產業的宏觀視野，更 希冀能助你精雕細琢未來的履歷，從容銜接企業的真實運營。 課程目標 Course objectives 上過這門課程後，學生將能夠： § 辨別科技產業所面臨的管理議題，並提出前瞻的解決策略。 § 比較學術與實務上的差異，準備好自己的認定(目標定位)與在就業市場的履歷。 § 探索近年的新興科技，預想這些科技如何改變我們的未來工作與生活。 § 分析自己有興趣就業的產業，並與同學分享對於產業的分析與觀察。 docs.name: 人力資源管理
docs.text: NATIONAL TSING HUA UNIVERSITY College of Technology Management Interdisciplinary Program of Management and Technology Human Resource Management (Offered in English) Fall Semester 2025 Professor: Hua-Wei Hung (hwhung@mx.nthu.edu.tw) Teaching Assistant: Pei-Hua (Luna) Tung (tungpeihua0403@gmail.com) Time: Monday 14:20-17:00 (M6M7M8) Classroom: TSMC building Room#406 Office hours: Please email to make an appointment Course Objectives: This course explores HR's central, strategic role in making organizations competitive. This course focuses on the concepts and practices of human resource management, namely recruitment and selection of employees, equal opportunity, training and development, performance appraisals, compensation, and benefits issues. A special focus on the increase of globalization and workforce diversity in the high-performance organization is also included. By the end of this course, students should be able to: 1) Describe the functions of HR management. 2) Provide examples of the new management practices that are changing HR management. 3) Illustrate how building employee commitment can be a cornerstone of an employer's HR philosophy. 4) Present the basic processes for: developing job specifications; recruiting, interviewing, and placement of employees; compensation and benefits plans; and conducting performance appraisals. 5) Outline the organization's role in the career management process. 6) Explain employee mobility. 7) Understand the impact of globalization on HR management. Teaching Arrangements: Class sessions may include lectures and small and large discussion groups. We will strive to clarify, supplement, and analyze text materials. You are responsible for all assigned readings and all materials presented in class. You are also responsible for all information disseminated in class and all course requirements, including deadlines. Lectures: Each lecture is about 1.5 hours. Please note that all lectures will be taught in English. Topic Presentation (30 minutes): • Presentation (20 minutes): All students will come up with topics they are interested in related to human resources. Some potential topics include how to write a resume, how to write a cover letter, how to dress professionally, how to prepare for an interview, MBTI, etc. • Each group will present fruitful information on this topic that helps deepen the understanding of this topic, some key indications, managerial inspiration, and/or any other issues that you want to share with the class. • Activity (10 minutes): Each group will prepare a small activity to allow interaction with audiences that is related to your topic, be creative. Case Presentation (30 minutes): • Case presentation (20 minutes): Each group will choose a case to present in class, which should include the content and solution of a specific managerial situation. Please upload your case presentation 10 pm before the day you are presenting, so the group preparing to ask questions will have time to review your material. • Q&A (10 minutes): Other groups must prepare at least three questions to discuss with the presenting group. Guest Speaker Reflection • Students are required to write a reflection (1-2 pages) that captures their personal learning and critical thinking about the talk. Your reflection should go beyond simply summarizing the talk - it should demonstrate engagement with the ideas presented and connect them to your own knowledge, experience, or future aspirations. • In addition, attendance will be taken at the start of the invited talk. You must be present for the entire session to be eligible to submit your reflection, unless you have notified me in advance and received approval for your absence. Midterm Individual Essay: • Think of a company/job that you wish to go to in the future. • Conduct research on the company’s corporate culture. What kind of talent are they looking for? What is the job design and description of the position you want to apply for? What are your interview strategies to highlight your value? • Develop a one-page company overview (be concise and to the point), a one-page cover letter, a two-page statement of purpose, and one page with 3 expected interview questions and how you would respond (scoring depends on depth of response). • Conditional accept: AI only when the AI screenshot report is attached, which will also affect the grading. Final Group Presentation (30 minutes): • Select two companies from the same industry. Analyze the characteristics of their HRM and what they need to do to find the right people (their HRM strategies). Analyze how their HRM strategies are different (what aspects are the same and what is different). What are the current operational strengths and weaknesses and how can they be improved (learn from other companies in the same industry)? Final Group Report: • In addition to an oral presentation, a printed paper report must also be submitted. This report will put your presentation into words and should be between 8 and 14 pages. • If AI is utilized, screenshots of conversations with the AI must be included. • APA format: 12 font Times New Roman, 1/1.5 leading, PDF file. • No plagiarism; shall also attach with the Turnitin report (acceptable similarity percentage: below 15%) (please register in advance through NTHU Library: https://learning.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/412- 1319-7120.php?Lang=en) • Conditional accept: AI only when the AI screenshot report is attached, which will also affect the grading. Assessment: • Class Participation: 10%, Case Presentation: 15%, Topic Presentation: 15%, Guest Speaker Reflection: 5%, Midterm Individual Essay: 30%, Final Group Presentation: 10%, Final Group Report: 15%. • Assessing materials are required to be uploaded on eeclass in advance, with less tolerance for additional adjustment/improvement after the deadline (need to be discussed). Audience Scoring will be conducted in class, with group-based scoring from other groups to value each criterion; Peer Scoring will be managed within a group, and each group member will evaluate teammates’ contributions individually. No roll-call in class, therefore you get your participation by speak-up during class, or you may also share your ideas on eeclass. • Sometimes there will be spontaneous pop-up quizzes. Nick Wu National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus This course focuses on the management and improvement of supply chain processes and performance, providing a comprehensive foundation for students interested in pursuing a career in various sectors, including consulting, operations, marketing, or finance within manufacturing or distribution firms. Throughout the course, we will delve into essential supply chain metrics that are critical for assessing performance and making informed decisions. Students will learn about the primary trade-offs involved in supply chain decision-making, equipping them with the analytical skills necessary to navigate complex scenarios. Basic tools for effective and efficient supply chain management will be introduced, covering key areas such as production planning, inventory control, order fulfillment, and supply chain coordination. In addition to these foundational elements, we will explore advanced topics that are increasingly relevant in today’s global marketplace. This includes global supply chain design, where students will learn how to strategically structure supply chains to optimize efficiency and responsiveness. We will also examine logistics and outsourcing strategies, discussing how companies can leverage external partnerships to enhance their supply chain capabilities. Furthermore, the course will investigate several recent innovations in supply chain management, including the integration of technology and data analytics, which are transforming traditional practices and driving competitive advantage. By the end of this course, students will have gained a robust understanding of the complexities of supply chain management and will be well-prepared to apply their knowledge in real-world settings, docs.text: 1 NATIONAL TSING HUA UNIVERSITY International Business Bachelor Program 11410IPMT300900 ESG and Social Innovation (Offered in English) Fall Semester 2025 Lecturer: Ari Chen (caoiaoi@gmail.com) Time: Tuesday 13:20-16:20 (M5M6M7) Classroom: TSMC building, R121 Office hours: By appointment Teaching Assistant: Course Objectives: With the setting of SDGs (sustainable development goals) by the United Nations General Assembly in 2015, corporations have been motivated to change the way they operate their businesses, and have started to emphasize their contributions towards a better society and the environment. Along with the global announcement of the ESG (Environmental, Social, Governance) trend, hybrid business organizations are an emerging phenomenon that adopts market strategies to solve social and environmental issues. Social innovation has increasingly attracted academic and practical attention for its contribution to global sustainability. Various innovative collaboration and business models have been constructed to deliver social and business value. One of the key trends in the fast development of social innovation worldwide has been the rise of the third sector and hybrid organizations such as social enterprises. This course is designed for undergraduates who find interest in ESG and social innovation issues and, would like to extend their understanding with in-depth study of related concepts (ESG, CSR, social innovation, social enterprise, Benefit corporation, net zero carbon emission). Also, this course is expected to provide basic guidance for those who consider a sustainability-related job position as their potential future career. This course aims to introduce students to the concepts, theories, tools, and insights necessary for sustainability construction, social innovation, and social entrepreneurship. By the end of this course, students should be able to: 1) Elaborate on the nature of ESG-related concepts and topics 2) Understand the international standard and legitimacy of global ESG construction 3) Provide examples of the international/local management practices of ESG 4) Explain how globalization/localization features (dis) empower ESG 2 5) Illustrate how social innovation is being constructed through social entrepreneurship 6) Outline the relationship between social innovation and ESG 7) Present basic ideas of social innovation practice through fieldwork Weekly Modules Week Date Lecture (13:20-15:00) Key Reading (Chapters) Case Discussion (15:20-16:20) 1 09/02 Course Introduction (Kick-off) 2 09/09 Introduction to ESG: Foundations & Differentiators 1 - 3 09/16 Environmental Factor Deep Dive 4 - 4 09/23 Carbon Management Case A 5 09/30 Environmental Sustainability and Challenges Case B 6 10/07 The Pathways to Decarbonizing Key Sectors 16 Case C 7 10/14 ESG Board Game Activity 8 10/21 Midterm Individual Essay (No-class) 9 10/28 Social Factor Deep Dive 5 Case D 10 11/04 Corporate Role and Social Innovation 6 Case E 11 11/11 Governance Factor Deep Dive Case F 12 11/18 ESG Metrics and Standards 7-9 Midterm sharing 13 11/25 Financial Sector and Stakeholder Ecosystem 11-13 Final Project Initiation 1 14 12/02 Future Trends and Challenges in ESG Final project initiation 2 15 12/09 Future Career Training for Sustainability (Entrepreneur Support, Job Position, Certification, Practical skill) 16 12/16 Final Project Presentation (Discussion, Future for ESG, Wrap-up) Teaching Arrangements: Class sessions may include lectures and small and large discussion groups. We will strive to clarify, supplement, and analyze text materials. You are responsible for all assigned readings and all materials presented in class. You are also responsible for all information disseminated in class and all course requirements, including deadlines. Lectures: Each lecture is 1.5 hours. Please note, all lectures will be taught in English. 3 ● The lecture will be delivered in a highly interactive way, speak-up and idea-sharing/discussion is always welcoming through lecturing, which is also counted as class participation. Case Discussion (40 minutes): ● Case presentation (20 minutes): one group will be assigned a case to present in class, which should include the content and solution of a specific managerial situation in sustainability development. Each group will need to introduce the topic and address the discussion issue accordingly. ● Case discussion (20 minutes): The discussion is open to the audience, adding up valuable comments, insight, debate, and discussion that help deepen the understanding of the case. Case Topic Study Target Insights and Discussion Case A Carbon Management The significance of ESG in shaping modern business practices • Explore different products carbon footprint. • Analyze the lifecycle of various products and their carbon hotspots • How can carbon offsets complement product lifecycle emissions reductions? Case B Greenwashing • Case C High-Tech in Sustainability Introduce one High-tech adoption case to sustainability development • Introduce how AI/Big data/Blockchain or other High-tech adoption in sustainability practice • How High-tech adoption helps sustainability development? • What’s next? Predict the future trend. Case D Social Enterprise and Social Entrepreneurship Introduce one foreign social enterprise and one local social enterprise • Introduce the initiative of the social enterprises, and how they operate, how they benefit society. • What is the potential risk they are facing? • Comparing the similarities and differences of social enterprises. Case E Social Innovation Introduce one social innovation case • Explain how the social innovation occurs, what the actors involved, how the actors collaborate, and how actors benefit from the social innovation. • Demonstrate what are the key factors that (dis)empower the social innovation to expand. Case F Benefit Corporation Introduce one B Corp company • Introduce the initiative of the company, and how it operates, how it benefits society. • Explain how it did well on each B-Corp assessment. • Elaborate how it manage hybridity (business and social conflicts) in internal management. Case Circular Economy Introduce one Circular Economy Case • Introduce the initiative of the circular economy case, and how it operates, how it benefits society. • What is the potential risk it is facing? Do not infringe copyrights.] Marketing Management: Service, Technology & Innovation (行銷管理：整合服務、科技與創新) Interdisciplinary Program of Management and Technology (IPMT) College of Technology Management, National Tsing Hua University Course credit: 3 Class Time: 14:20-17:20, Wednesday Session Location: TSMC Building 223 TA: TBA Instructor: Tonny Menglun Kuo, Ph.D. (郭孟倫) Office: Rm. 617, TSMC Building Tel: (03)571-5131 ext. 42248 Email: tonny@gapp.nthu.edu.tw Office Hours: by appointment Course Description In a world where digital innovation evolves at lightning speed, marketing has become more than just product promotion—it’s about designing experiences, telling compelling stories, and leveraging emerging technologies. This course equips undergraduate students with a solid foundation in marketing strategy, covering essential topics such as STP (Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning), branding, pricing, channel design, and integrated marketing communications (IMC). Beyond the fundamentals, students will explore how livestreaming, AR/VR, chatbots, generative AI, and blockchain technologies are transforming customer engagement. We will read and discuss cutting-edge conceptual papers and strategic frameworks to help shape a forward-thinking blueprint for the ever-evolving world of marketing. The course also addresses critical issues such as sustainability, trust-building, and corporate social responsibility (CSR), helping students understand marketing’s expanding role in both business and society. Through interactive lectures, case studies, hands-on workshops, authentic tasks, and a final team project, students will develop strategic thinking and creative agility to solve real-world marketing challenges—and gain the confidence to lead in the marketing landscape of tomorrow. Course Objectives After taking this course, students will be able to: 1. Understand and apply core marketing strategies such as the 4Ps, 7Ps, STP, customer value, and market orientation to develop customer-centric marketing plans. 2. Analyze consumer behavior and interpret marketing research data (qualitative and quantitative) to make evidence-based marketing decisions. 3. Design marketing strategies related to product lifecycle, brand management, pricing, and omnichannel promotion based on customer insights. 4. Evaluate and implement technological tools (e.g., AI, generative AI, chatbots, AR/VR) to enhance service design, customer experience, and relationship marketing. 5. Critically examine emerging marketing trends such as the Metaverse, NFTs, blockchain, and CSR to propose sustainable and value-driven marketing innovations. 2 Learning Methods The course combines different learning methods: Mini lectures, group discussions, case studies, invited speech, project-based learning. Class Policies § Attendance Policy: Missing two or more classes will result in an automatic failing grade (F) for this course. If you must be absent due to unavoidable circumstances, please notify me in advance. Excused absences will be considered on a case-by-case basis (e.g., medical leave with official documentation from a hospital). § Punctuality: Being late is disruptive to the learning environment and is therefore strongly discouraged. Please make every effort to arrive on time. § Academic Integrity: Any form of academic dishonesty—such as cheating, misrepresentation, or plagiarism—will result in a failing grade. Be sure to properly cite and acknowledge all sources to avoid unintentional plagiarism. There is zero tolerance for academic misconduct. § Communication: I welcome open communication. If you have questions, concerns, or simply want to talk about your learning, please don’t hesitate to reach out to me at any time. § Let’s enjoy this semester together! Looking forward to a meaningful and engaging journey with you all. docs.text: 1 NATIONAL TSING HUA UNIVERSITY College of Technology Management Interdisciplinary Program of Management and Technology Innovation Management (Offered in English) Fall Semester 2025 Professor: Hua-Wei Hung (hwhung@mx.nthu.edu.tw) Teaching Assistant: Pei-Hua (Luna) Tung (tungpeihua0403@gmail.com) Time: Thursday 14:20-17:00 (R6R7R8) Classroom: TSMC building, Room#309 Office hours: Please email to make an appointment Course Objectives: This course covers three main contents and objectives, each crucial for developing a comprehensive understanding of innovation and technology strategies in the modern business landscape. The first objective is to impart the abstract theories and systematic knowledge necessary for understanding innovation and technology strategies. This involves exploring fundamental concepts and frameworks that underpin technological innovation, including but not limited to disruptive innovation theory, technology adoption lifecycle, and strategic management of intellectual property. Students will gain a solid theoretical foundation that will enable them to analyze and develop effective strategies in various technological contexts. Secondly, the course aims to train students' thinking, questioning, and communication abilities through discussions and analyses of practical cases. This hands-on approach will expose students to real-world scenarios, challenging them to apply theoretical knowledge to complex business situations. Through case studies and interactive discussions, students will develop critical thinking skills, learn to ask insightful questions, and enhance their ability to communicate complex ideas effectively. This practical component bridges the gap between theory and application, preparing students for the challenges they may face in their future careers. Finally, the course is designed to cultivate students' team spirit and rapport, as well as their understanding of the relationship between industry practices and management theories. Through group projects and collaborative assignments, students will learn to work effectively in teams, mirroring the collaborative nature of modern business environments. Additionally, the course will emphasize the interconnectedness of academic management theories and real-world industry practices, helping students to develop a holistic view of the business world. This understanding will enable them to navigate the complexities of technological innovation in various organizational contexts and industries. 2 Teaching Arrangements: Class sessions may include lectures and small and large discussion groups. We will strive to clarify, supplement, and analyze text materials. You are responsible for all assigned readings and all materials presented in class. You are also responsible for all information disseminated in class and all course requirements, including deadlines. Lectures: Each lecture is 1 hour. Please note that all lectures will be taught in English. • The lecture will be delivered in a highly interactive way, and speaking up and idea- sharing/discussion are always welcome through lecturing, which is also counted as class participation. Book Review (30 minutes): • Book review sharing (25 minutes): Each group will be assigned to review one book at the beginning of the course, and share their review with the class during the discussion session. Each group will finish the book, and you will present feedback to the class, consisting of book summaries, key insights, managerial inspiration, and/or any other issues you want to share with the class. • Q&A (5 minutes): Other groups must prepare at least three questions to discuss with the presenting group. Innovation Case Analysis (30 minutes) • In this assignment, your group will select a real-world innovation to present - a successful breakthrough or a notable failure -and analyze it through innovation management concepts covered in this course. • The chosen innovation may be a product, service, process, or business model from any industry. It could be a disruptive game-changer like Tesla’s electric vehicle strategy, a widely adopted service like Netflix’s streaming model, or a high-profile failure like Google Glass or Juicero. • Your task is to investigate the story behind the innovation, evaluate the factors that influenced its outcome, and present your findings in a way that helps your classmates learn from its successes and challenges. Guest Speaker Reflection • Students must write a reflection (1-2 pages) that captures their learning and critical thinking about the talk. Your reflection should go beyond simply summarizing the talk - it should demonstrate engagement with the ideas presented and connect them to your own knowledge, experience, or future aspirations. • In addition, attendance will be taken at the start of the invited talk. You must be present for the entire session to be eligible to submit your reflection, unless you have notified me in advance and received approval for your absence. Midterm Project: • In this assignment, you will write an individual analytical essay (1-2 pages) comparing two companies in the same industry, one representing the traditional incumbent model (“old”) and the other representing the disruptive challenger (“new”). • Your goal is to examine how the disruptive company changed the competitive landscape and challenged the incumbent’s market position, using innovation management concepts from this course. 3 Final Project Presentation: • In this assignment, your group will select two companies from the same industry and compare their most recent Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) or Sustainability Reports. While reviewing the reports, focus on the areas each company emphasizes most —stakeholder engagement, environmental sustainability, employee safety, diversity and inclusion, or community development. • Your analysis should go beyond identifying differences in emphasis. You should examine how each company’s CSR priorities influence or align with its innovation strategy. Consider questions such as: • Are CSR commitments leading to new products or services (e.g., eco-friendly product lines, inclusive design)? • Is CSR driving process innovations (e.g., sustainable manufacturing, energy efficiency, waste reduction)? • Does the company use CSR as part of its business model innovation (e.g., circular economy models, social enterprises)? • How do CSR-driven innovations contribute to competitive advantage or differentiation in the market? Final Group Report: • In addition to an oral presentation, a printed paper report must also be submitted. This report will put your presentation into words and should be between 8 and 14 pages. • If AI is utilized, screenshots of conversations with the AI must be included. • APA format: 12 font Times New Roman, 1/1.5 leading, PDF file. • No plagiarism; shall also attach with the Turnitin report (acceptable similarity percentage: below 15%) (please register in advance through NTHU Library: https://learning.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/412- 1319-7120.php?Lang=en) • Conditional accept: AI only when the AI screenshot report is attached, which will also affect the grading. 4 Assessment: This course consists (but is not limited to) the following assessments: Class Participation 10%, Book Review 15%, Innovation Case Analysis 15%, Guest Speaker Reflection 5%, Midterm Project 30%, Final Group Presentation 10%, Final Group Report 15%. Assessing materials must be uploaded on eeclass in advance, with less tolerance for additional adjustment/improvement after the deadline (need to be discussed). Audience Scoring will be conducted in class, with group-based scoring from other groups to value each criterion; Peer Scoring will be managed within a group, and each group member will evaluate teammates’ contributions individually. No roll-call in class, random call is included in class participation, once one fails to answer random calls up to four times, they will be failed. docs.text: National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 科號 Course Number 11410IPMT3013 00 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Size of Limit 50 中文名稱 Course Title 科技價值鏈管理：專利策略與佈局 英文名稱 Course English Title Technology Value Chain Management: Patent Strategy and Portfolio Planning 任課教師 Instructor 賴怡君 教師聯絡方式 Contact Information Email: lai-ic@mx.nthu.edu.tw 上課時間 Time R2R3R4 上課教室 Room TSMC 台積 421 先修科目 Prerequisite(s) 無 本課程對應之學習目標與核心能力 Aligned Learning Goals and Learning Objectives ▪ 培養基礎專利知識。 Develop foundational knowledge in patents. ▪ 了解創新價值和創新保護的重要性，以及如何運用專利進行策略布局。 Understand innovation value and the importance of innovation protection, and how to apply patents for strategic positioning. ▪ 培養如何運用專利來追蹤技術和創新軌跡的概念。 Develop the concept of applying patents to track technology and innovation trajectories. 課程目標 Course Objectives ▪ 本課程為同學奠定專利的基礎知識，了解專利作為智慧財產權保護的一環，對創 新價值有何影響。 This course establishes a foundational understanding of patents, helping students recognize the role of patents as a form of intellectual property protection and their impact on innovation value. ▪ 除了創新價值的保護，並了解如何進行專利管理和佈局，以維持可持續的競爭 力。 In addition to understanding how innovation value is protected, students will learn how to manage and strategically position patents to sustain competitive advantage. ▪ 第二學期會有延伸課程，更深入進入應用專利資料庫進行技術和創新軌跡探索的 資料操作面。 A follow-up course in the second semester will explore hands-on data applications in greater depth, focusing on the use of patent databases to analyze technology and innovation trajectories. 課程說明 Course Description ▪ 課程包含授課與小組報告，報告以小組為單位；學期涵蓋兩次小組討論，每次一 小時。小組過程中教師會逐一至每一小組了解討論狀態並反饋，協助小組完成期 末報告。 The course consists of lectures and group projects. Reports will be submitted by groups. There will be two group discussion sessions during the semester, each lasting National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus one hour. During these sessions, the instructor will approach each group to understand their progress, provide feedback, and support them in completing the final project ▪ 期中報告以小組為單位，每組提案一企業（跨國企業為佳），作為期末報告的分 析標的。報告內容包含標的企業簡介、選擇該企業原因、預期會在期末分析的競 爭者。 The midterm report is group-based. Each group will propose one company (preferably a multinational enterprise) as the subject of analysis for the final project. The report should include a company overview, reasons for selection, and expected competitors to be analyzed in the final report. ▪ 期末報告以小組為單位，分析期中提案企業的專利管理策略；分析內容應包括但 不限於：企業核心技術、專利授權與策略聯盟、訴訟概況、主要競爭者（競爭者 地理分佈、競爭者技術佈局）、未來策略建議。 The final report is also group-based and should analyze the patent management strategy of the selected company. The analysis should include, but is not limited to: core technologies, patent licensing and strategic alliances, litigation status, key competitors (including their geographic distribution and patent strategies), and future strategic recommendations. ▪ 期中報告以投影片檔案繳交，期末報告包含口頭報告與投影片檔案繳交；檔案可 用傳統 PPT、或雲端製作轉 PDF 等形式。 The midterm report should be submitted as a slide deck. The final report includes both an oral presentation and submission of slides. Files may be submitted as traditional PowerPoint presentations or as cloud-based presentations exported to PDF. 課程關鍵字 Course Keywords 專利、智慧財產權、專利佈局、專利策略、創新價值 Patents, Intellectual Property, Patent Portfolio, Patent Strategy, Innovation Value 指定用書 Textbooks Gassmann, O., Bader, M. A., & Thompson, M. J. (2020). Patent Management: Protecting Intellectual Property and Innovation. Springer. ISBN: 9783030590086. 參考書籍 References United States Department of Commerce (2025). Patents and How to Get One: A Practical Handbook. Anson Street Press. ISBN: 9781023586078. 教學方式 Teaching Approach ▪ 課程包含授課與小組報告，報告以小組為單位；學期涵蓋兩次小組討論，每次一 小時。小組過程中教師會逐一至每一小組了解討論狀態並反饋，協助小組完成期 末報告。 The course includes lectures and group projects, with all reports completed in groups. There will be two group discussion sessions during the semester, each lasting one hour. During these sessions, the instructor will approach each group to observe their discussion progress, provide feedback, and assist in the development of their final report. ▪ 第一學期以奠定專利基礎知識和理解專利佈局策略為重點，第二學期後的延伸課 程將進一步應用專利資料庫進行技術和創新軌跡探索。 The first semester focuses on building foundational knowledge of patents and understanding strategic patent portfolio planning. A follow-up course in the second semester will further apply patent databases to explore technology and innovation National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus trajectories. 評分標準 Grading ▪ 小組期中報告(投影片檔案)：20% Group Midterm Report (slide deck): 20% ▪ 小組討論參與：20% Group Discussion Participation: 20% ▪ 小組成員互評：5% Peer Evaluation within Group: 5% ▪ 小組期末報告(口頭+投影片檔案)：55% Group Final Report (oral presentation + slide deck): 55% 教學進度 Course Schedule ▪ Week 1: 課程介紹 ▪ Week 2: 智慧財產權基礎概念：價值與權利 ▪ Week 3: 專利起草：如何撰寫專利；含分組案例解讀練習 ▪ Week 4: 專利保護策略：攻擊型與防禦型策略 ▪ Week 5: 專利保護策略：互補型策略 ▪ Week 6: 專利評估與估值 ▪ Week 7: 專利佈局管理 ▪ Week 8: 專利商業化與小組討論 I：期末標的企業選擇 ▪ Week 9: 專利商業化 ▪ Week 10: 大型組織內的專利處理流程 ▪ Week 11: 各產業專利管理 I ▪ Week 12: 各產業專利管理 II ▪ Week 13: 新科技環境中的專利管理 I ▪ Week 14: 新科技環境中的專利管理 II ▪ Week 15: 專利指標與小組討論 II: 期末報告研討 ▪ Week 16: 期末口頭報告 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則 (Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) (2)有條件開放：同學可使用 AI 協助學習，在繳交報告時應註明應用 AI 工具在哪些地 方，讓老師評估每位同學的實際學習狀況。 (2) Conditionally open: Students are allowed to use AI tools to assist with learning. docs.text: 11410IPT 514000 課程綱要表 課程名稱 (中文) 光電子學一 (英文) Photonics I 開課單位 電機系 授課教師 李依珊 課程代碼 IPT 5140 選課性質 ⎕必修■選修 學分數 3 開課年級 碩博 先修科目或先備能力 Prerequisites Electromagnetic theory 課程概述 本課程全面介紹光電子學與光子學的基本原理與實際應用。學生將深入探討光的 行為及其與物質的交互作用、各類光子元件的運作原理，以及這些元件在現代科技 中的整合應用。課程設計旨在為學生建立紮實的理論基礎與實作能力。 This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the fundamental principles and practical applications of optoelectronics and photonics. Students will explore the behavior of light and its interaction with matter, the operation of photonic devices, and the integration of these components in modern technologies. The curriculum is structured to build a strong foundation in both theoretical concepts and practical device operation. 課程目標 在課程結束時，學生將能夠： 1. 理解並應用光的基本性質包含傳播、發射與偵測的物理原理 2. 分析與建模主要光電子與光子元件的性能 3. 設計基礎的光子系統，用於光通訊、感測與訊號處理等應用 4. 解讀並運用各權威教科書所提供的理論架構 By the end of the course, students will be able to: 1. Understand and apply the physics of light propagation, emission, and detection 2. Analyze and model the performance of key optoelectronic and photonic devices 3. Design basic photonic systems for applications such as optical communication, sensing, and signal processing 4. Interpret and apply the theoretical frameworks provided by leading texts in the field 教科書 自編教材 lecture notes 參考書 1. Principles of Photonics, Liu, Jia-Ming, Cambridge University Press. 2. docs.text: 超快光學−課程大綱 (11410 IPT 543000, Ultrafast Optics) 一、課程說明(Course Description) 本課程旨在介紹超短(10-12~10-15 秒)雷射光脈衝之產生、量測、傳播、色散管理及其應 用。此一技術提供的超精密時間解析度可用以觀測前所未知的分子、准粒子短暫動態。 所產生之巨大亮度(>1023 W/cm2)足以突破原子基本引力，或驅動物質產生顯著之非線 性效應，從而獲得一系列新的(如中紅外光、極紫外光)同調光譜成份。本課程所需要的 背景知識為：傅立葉轉換、電磁平面波，並具備運用數學軟體(如 Matlab)之能力。 This subject is designed to introduce generation, measurement, propagation, dispersion management and applications of ultrashort (10-12-10-15 sec) laser pulses. The ultrahigh temporal resolution enabled by this technique can trace the fleeting dynamics of molecules or quasi particles. The gigantic peak intensity (up to 1023 W/cm2) can overrun the atomic force, or generate a series of new coherent spectral components (e.g. mid-infrared, extreme ultraviolet) by strong nonlinear interaction with materials. The prerequisites include Fourier transform, electromagnetic plane waves and the ability to conduct numerical simulation with package software (e.g. Matlab). 二、教科書(Text Book) 自編講義(Lecture slides, pdf files will be offered at the beginning of semester.) 三、參考書籍(References) Andrew Weiner, Ultrafast Optics, Wiley, 2009. (ISBN: 978-0-471-41539-8) 四、教學方式(Teaching Method) 開放式課程影片預習、隨堂討論及問答、課堂講授、團隊專題 (OpenCourseWare video preview, discussion and Q&A in class, lectures, group project) 五、教學進度(Syllabus) 1. Introduction and review (6 hours) 2. Active mode-locking (1 hour) 3. Light-matter interaction (5 hours) 4. Passive mode-locking (6 hours) 5. Pulse measurement by correlation techniques (4 hours) 6. Pulse measurement by FROG and SPIDER (4 hours) 7. Dispersion and dispersion management (5 hours) 8. Flexible topics on request (6 hours) 9. Term project in the form of group competition 六、成績考核(Evaluation) 教師考核(20%)，期中考(30%)，期末考(25%)，團隊專題(15%)，作業(10%) Instructor’s assessment(20%), midterm exam(30%), final exam (25%), group projects (15%), homework assignments (10%) 七、可連結之網頁位址(Useful links) 數位學習平台(E-learning)：eeclass.nthu.edu.tw 開放式課程(Open Course Ware)：ocw.nthu.edu.tw/ocw/index.php?page=course&cid=206& 八、生成式人工智慧使用規則(Generative Artificial Intelligence access rules) 本課程同意學生利用人工智慧(AI)進行協作或互學。根據本校公布之「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本課程採取有條件開放，以下說明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出。 學生須於課堂作業或報告中的「標題頁註腳」或「引用文獻後」簡要說明如何使用生 成式 AI 進行議題發想、文句潤飾或結構參考等使用方式。若經查核使用 卻無在作業 或報告中標明，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。 本門課授課教材或學習資料若有引用自生成式 AI，教師也將在投影片或口頭標注。 修讀本課程之學生 於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。

docs.nameEn: Deep Learning in Biomedical Optical Imaging
docs.text: National Tsing Hua University Fall 2023 11310IPT 553000 Deep Learning in Biomedical Optical Imaging Lecturer Prof. Hung-Wen Chen Email: hungwen@mx.nthu.edu.tw Course Overview In this course, you will learn: (1) the foundational knowledge of deep learning algorithms, build neural networks from scratch via Python, and furthermore get familiar with different frameworks such as Pytorch, Tensorflow, and Keras. (2) The principle of different biomedical optical imaging technologies will be introduced as well. Finally, (3) a final project on medical imaging is required. We also offer (4) the opportunities of earning free official certificates from Nvidia Deep Learning Institute and DeepLearning.AI from Coursera as well, which might be helpful for your future career development. Grading  Homework (35 %): Assignments to get familiar with basic deep learning programming.  Midterm (30 %): Basic concepts of deep learning and related mathematical derivation.  Final Project Presentation (20 %): A project presentation of a research paper related to the deep learning application in medical imaging and the code implementation of the  Creativity Report (15 %): A Provide a detailed analysis of your model implementation on a given image dataset. References  Goodfellow, Y. Bengio, and A. Courville, "Deep Learning," 2016.  Francois Chollet (creator of Keras), "Deep Learning with Python," 2017.  J. Schmidhube, "Deep Learning in Neural Networks: An Overview," Neural Networks 61: 85-117, 2015.  Y. Bengio, Y. LeCun, and G. Hinton, "Deep Learning," Nature 521: 436-44, 2015. Online Resources  Goodfellow, Y. Bengio, and A. Courville, "Deep Learning," 2016. http://www.deeplearningbook.org  Deep Learning Specialization by Andrew Ng https://www.youtube.com/c/Deeplearningai/playlists  Stanford CS231n: Deep Learning for Computer Vision http://cs231n.stanford.edu/schedule.html  Google: Machine Learning Crash Course with TensorFlow APIs https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course  AI for Medicine Specialization. https://www.coursera.org/specializations/ai-for-medicine  NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/training/ National Tsing Hua University Fall 2023 11310IPT 553000 Deep Learning in Biomedical Optical Imaging  NVIDIA NGC https://www.nvidia.com/zh-tw/gpu-cloud/containers/  TensorFlow 2 quickstart for beginners. https://www.tensorflow.org/tutorials/quickstart/beginner  Python Numpy Tutorial (with Jupyter and Colab) https://cs231n.github.io/python-numpy-tutorial/  Python Basics for Data Science https://www.edx.org/course/python-basics-for-data-science  Python Tutorial https://www.w3schools.com/python/  莫烦 Python https://mofanpy.com/ National Tsing Hua University Fall 2023 11310IPT 553000 Deep Learning in Biomedical Optical Imaging

課程說明 (Course Description)
本課程為光電所書報討論課（IPT Seminar），每週邀請來自國內外研究機構或產業界的專家學者，就
光電相關領域的最新研究進展或應用成果進行分享與交流。演講主題涵蓋精密光譜、量子光學、尖端材
料分析、雷射技術、太空科學、英文論文閱讀與寫作等多元議題。課程旨在拓展學生的學術視野，並鼓
勵與演講者互動，提升研究能力與表達能力。This course is a weekly seminar series (IPT
Seminar) hosted by the Institute of Photonics Technologies. Experts from academia
and industry are invited to share cutting-edge developments and experiences in
various photonics-related fields, including precision spectroscopy, quantum
optics, advanced materials analysis, laser technologies, space science, and
academic paper writing. The course aims to broaden students’ academic exposure and
enhance their research communication skills.

指定用書 (Text Books)

No specific textbook required

教學方式 (Teaching Methods)

Invited lectures and in-class discussion

每週安排一場學術演講，講題與講者資訊將於課前公告
One seminar per week; topics and speakers will be announced in advance

docs.name: 軟X光和極紫外光光源原理與應用
docs.nameEn: Ultrafast Soft X-Rays and Extreme Ultraviolet Radiation Principles and applications
docs.text:
課程說明：
The course provides the essential knowledge to understand the properties of Ultrafast Extreme Ultraviolet
Radiation (EUV). After a comprehensive review of different EUV pulse generation approaches,
different temporal and spatial characterization methods will be discussed in detail.
The EUV mirror coating technique, EUV imaging and a few main Light-matter interaction phenomena will
also be introduced. Some special application topics shall be selected for further discussion at the end of
this class.

教科書：
(1) Soft X-Rays and Extreme Ultraviolet Radiation, Principles and
Applications, David Attwood
(2) Lecture notes

參考資料：
1. "Elements of X-ray Diffraction" 3rd Ed. by B.D. Cullity and S.R.
Stock
2. Ultrashort Laser Pulse Phenomena, Jean-Claude Diels and Wolfgang
Rudolph
3. X-ray Multiple-wave Diffraction: Theory and Application, series in
Solid-State Science, S.-L.Chang

教學進度：

Review of Atom and Molecule Physics
2 weeks
‧ Fundamental postulates of quantum mechanics
‧ Atomic Sturcture
‧ Energy Levels and Emission Processes
‧ Nuclear Motion
‧ Basic Absorption and Emission Process
‧ Laser and Atom interaction
‧ Radiation and Scattering at EUV and Soft X-ray wavelegnth

Wave Propagation at Soft X-rays and EUV Wavelength 2
weeks
‧ The Wave Equation and Refractive index
‧ Phase Varian and Absorption of Waves
‧ Optics Components for X-ray and EUV
‧ Design of Dielectric Mirrors for EUV

Multilayer interference coating
2 weeks
‧ Constructive interference of Scattered Radiation
‧ Computational Model for Calculating Reflection from a Multilayer
Mirror
‧ Multilayer Fabrication
‧ Applications.

Synchrotron Radiation
2 weeks
‧ Characteristics of Bending Magnet Radiation
‧ Undulator Radiation – Power, Brightness, and Harmonics
‧ Wiggler Radiation – Power, Flux
‧ Femtosecond Pulse Generation.

High order Harmonic Generation
2 weeks
‧ History
‧ Theory Background: Semi-classical model
‧ Spatial and Temporal Coherence
‧ Attosecond Pulse generation
‧ HHG scales with driving laser wavelength

Soft X-ray Microscopy with Diffractive Optics
2 weeks
‧ The Fresnel Zone Plate Lens
‧ High Resolution Soft X-ray Microscopy
‧ Applications

Ultrafast Soft X-rays and EUV light source
2 weeks
‧ Synchrotron Radiation
‧ Hot Dense Plasmas
‧ X-rays and EUV Lasers
‧ High Harmonic Generation

Special Topic: EUV pulse characterization and applications 2
weeks
‧ Femtosecond, Attosecond EUV pulse characterization
‧ Microscopy with diffraction optics
‧ Deep Ultraviolet and Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography

教學方式
Powerpoint presentations

成績考核
Homework 70%
Attendance 5%
Project paper and final presentation 25%
