實驗儀容：實驗衣及服裝穿著(ex 包鞋) (c) 實驗過程表現與實驗態度 (d) 實驗器材完善度：打破或毀損將酌量扣分 實驗報告 42% 12 份預報 + 6 份報告 期末考 33% (a) 筆試：70% (b) 操作考：30% 實驗記錄與報告（Laboratory report and note) 學習和養成書寫實驗報告是這門生物實驗課重要的一環，實驗報告可依個人實驗需要稍加增減 個句子。描述實驗目的，探討有趣和重要的生物問題。 III. 方法 （method) : 讓同學有多方了解實驗儀器的機會，培養實際操作之能力，並鼓勵創造新方法。 IV. 結果和討論 （results and discussion) : (a). 有系統的呈現實驗當中所觀察到的現象和記錄下來的 data。 (b). 實驗後所做的計算和圖表。圖表要排序並標示計量單位，如此 ，在寫結果和討論時，才容 易引用 (The information found in Figure 1….) 。 (c). 對 data 的分析和比較及從中所做的推論 (interpretation and unknown identification) 。 (d). 整個實驗的結論。 如果結果未達成目標或不如預期，也請說明可能的原因，及重做時可改進之處。 問題回答（Answers and Questions) : 講義上的問題和老師與助教詢問的問題回答。 實驗規則補充： 1. 上課務必注意時間，請勿喧鬧。 2. 實驗課服裝： 實驗衣、長褲、包腳的鞋子，長髮者必須將頭髮紮起。 3. 預報一單元每人一份，於每次上課時將紙本帶給助教檢查， 參考實驗講義內容整理，亦可另外加自己查到的參考資料，務必註明參考書目。 4. 結報一單元一組一份： a. 繳交日期：該單元結束後、下一次上課日課程開始前統一繳交給助教。 遲交一天扣報告成績 5 分，遲交時間未滿一天者，以一天計。 b. 繳交形式：紙本(列印或手寫均可)，同一組結報裝訂一起繳交。 c. 結報內容：封面— 實驗單元、班別、組別、成員名單與學號、註明分工 實驗目的 實驗方法與流程 實驗結果與分析 結果討論 參考資料及問題回答 （其他可參考科學論文寫作相關書籍） 如有任何疑問，請聯絡助教。

docs.name: 書報討論
docs.text:
Seminar (書報討論)

Instructor:
Chun-Chao Wang (王群超)
Email: ccwang@life.nthu.edu.tw
Phone: +886-3-516-2589 (office)
http://chunchaowang.wix.com/wanglab
Office Location: Life Science Building I, Room 527
Office Hours: By appointment

Course Description:
The Seminar allows students a chance to meet every week to discuss journal articles. The primary goals of this course are to help students keep up with the scientific literature, and help students argue logically, and present newest research in a way that others can follow. We hope everyone takes advantage of this opportunity, as it is a great way to practice speaking in front of a group, critically analyze papers, and be aware of the state-of-the-art advances in the fields of quantitative cell biology and cancer biology.

Course Requirements and Expectations:
R26; Each student must select a paper that they consider to be either important or controversial from a pre-approved list of articles. They should make a case for why it is significant, controversial, etc. and what they find interesting.
R26; Students are required to read all papers. If you read the paper(s) before each class, discussions will be more meaningful, and learning will increase. Expect to spend a minimum of 90¬–120 minutes reading per paper.
R26; Students are expected to construct a lightning talk (3 minutes) and an oral presentation (30 minutes).
R26; When in the audience, you are expected to 1) submit 1 question, 2) present one slide made by the speaker after the oral presentation, in your own word (“Audience presentation”), and 3) ask questions (optional).
R26; You are expected to host a presentation.
R26; Be respectful and professional: remember that your responses are public, so always maintain a respectful and professional tone, even when handling criticism or negative feedback.

As a presenter:
R26; Rehearse your presentation out loud several times, if possible in front of friends or family members, or in front of the mirror. Use your mobile device to record rehearsal. Ask your audience for feedback after you finish your rehearsal.
R26; You will record a lightning talk and upload your YouTube file.
R26; Responding to YouTube comments. Submit a screenshot or PDF of your YouTube comment and its response in eeclass. Keep a record of who submits their comments/questions late.

docs.nameEn: Contemporary Cognitive Neuroscience: Brain and Mind
docs.text: 當代認知神經科學：腦與心智 Contemporary Cognitive Neuroscience: Brain and Mind (通識課程, LS114300, Fall 2025) 加簽者請務必出席第一堂課（9/3，實體或線上都可）以填 寫加簽表單（參與抽籤）及參與課堂小考。 加簽表單填寫時間僅開放 9/3 第一節課程開始後一小時 (15:30~16:30)。 未達上述條件者不列入抽籤資格。 第一堂課直播網址 https://www.youtube.com/live/kyWQhTBU5X4 課程規定: 請另詳閱「2025 課程規定」之投影片（清華數位學習 平台 eeclass）。 Instructor: 焦傳金 Contact info: 生科二館 646, 03-574-2464, ccchiao@life.nthu.edu.tw Classroom: 生科二館華生廳 (Watson Hall)＋YouTube 同步直播 Class time: W7W8W9 (15:30-18:20 pm) Course materials : 清華數位學習平台 eeclass（https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw/） 即時互動系統 slido（https://www.slido.com/index-b?experience_id=2） 課程信箱: brain7mind@gmail.com Course TAs: 葉惠棻 yehhuifen@gmail.com Reference: Cognitive Neuroscience: The Biology of the Mind (Sixth Edition), Michael Gazzaniga, Elizabeth A. Phelps, Dani S. Bassett, George R. Mangun, Richard B. Ivry (2025) Course description: 認知神經科學（Cognitive Neuroscience）是一門新興 的研究領域，主要是探索腦與心智（Brain and Mind）的關連性。從感覺與知 覺（Sensation and Perception）、學習與記憶（Learning and Memory）、注 意力與情緒（Attention and Emotion）、同理與厭惡（Empathy and Disguise）、決策與執行（Decision-making and Execution）、乃至意識 （Consciousness）的產生，都是認知神經科學的範疇。瞭解這些認知行為背 後的神經科學不僅是本世紀最重要的一項科學探索，也與每個人的有密切的關 係。例如：神經經濟學（Neuroeconomics）與消費者行為及市場調查有關， 退化性神經疾病（Neurodegenerative disorders）與老年失智症有關。在本 課程中，我們將依序探討認知神經科學中的主要課題，重點在於介紹最新的研 究發展，並討論這些科學發現對個人及社會的衝擊。本課程將以腦與心智相關 的科普書籍與科學人雜誌過去所發表有關認知神經科學的文章為主，並以影片 及近期發表的期刊論文為輔，搭配課程中互動討論，讓沒有生物學背景的學生 也可輕鬆地學習本課程。 Course schedule: Week Topic Note 1 腦與心智簡介 簡介各週內容，暴力行為在腦中的運作模式 第一週上課使用直播方式，不需前往教室 (加簽規定如上) 2 感覺&知覺 I 視覺的錯視、視覺訊息的處理 3 感覺&知覺 II 奧妙的色彩如何影響大腦認知 4 感覺&知覺 III 原來我們聽到的可能不一樣、基因影響嗅覺辨識! 5 學習&記憶 感官、短期、長期，原來有不同的記憶形式 6 睡眠&夢 我可以都不睡覺嗎? 我為何需要睡覺? 7 報償&成癮 為何毒品這麼難戒除，成癮對腦造成的傷害 8 理性&感性 動物也會難過，不同情緒由不同腦區控制 9 選擇&決策 如何做出選擇，究竟你在選什麼? 10 同理心 網路和面對面的霸凌有何不同，你懂我的痛嗎? 11 全校運動會 12 智力&創造力 天才從何而來? 創意如何產生? 13 發育&可塑性 嬰兒天生會做哪些事?學前教育可以如何進行 14 老化&疾病 如何優雅的老化，能阻止大腦變老嗎? 15 腦科學&科技&社會 男、女頭腦大不同? 16 意識&自由意志 植物人有意識嗎? 繳交期末報告 #本課程同時採用實體上課與同步遠距教學（同學可自由選擇學習方式） Grading policy: 課堂參與：40% (每堂課結束後需將課程心得與自我經驗分享上傳至社群軟體 fb、ig) 課堂小考：30% (每個段落皆有課堂小考，以 slido 進行) 期末報告：30% (個人書面報告或團體影片報告擇一) 課堂參與（加分）：0-5% 課程要求： 1. 攜帶行動載具（手機、平版、筆電）來上課，並確定自己在良好的網路空間 中上課 2. 下載 slido 3. 擁有任一社群軟體 加簽規定： 1. 欲加簽者請參與第一堂線上直播課程，並於課程中填寫加簽表單，將依據人 數抽籤，表單關閉後不再開放加簽 2. 直播連結: https://www.youtube.com/live/wOssI06rW-g 學生使用 AI 規則： 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出

並實地感受豐富植物類群與型態多樣性，如受疫情影響將正課改為線上進行，講師來自國內各單位
之研究人員與大學教授，之後學生植物材料進行短期研究。

有意報名的同學，請來信說明想參與今年的暑期研習課程，索取報名資訊和行前說明。也歡迎同學
轉知相關訊息給有興趣的非生科院同學。聯絡方式如下：
郭立園助理教授- lykuo@life.nthu.edu.tw

1.課堂參與情形：50%
2.期末專題口頭報告：25%
3.專題書面報告：25%

辜嚴倬雲植物保種中心簡介:

財團法人辜嚴倬雲植物保種中心(KBCC)是由本院李家維教授主持的熱帶植物活體異地保育中心，
至今已收集近34,000種活體植物，栽種於17棟溫室內，是全世界蒐藏最豐富的植物園，其中蘭
花、蕨類、秋海棠、鳳梨、苔蘚等類群物種數亦是世界第一。該中心平日不對外開放，僅提供學術
交流或是採集植物以供研究，但每年暑假會開設研習課程，招收有對植物多樣性及保育相關研究有
熱誠的大學生。

docs.name: 計算神經科學導論
docs.text: 國立清華大學 114 學年第 1 學期新開課程課程大綱 科號 Course Number 11410LS 314500 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Class Size 20 中文名稱 Course Title 計算神經科學導論 英文名稱 Course English Title Introduction to Computational Neuroscience 任課教師 Instructor 羅中泉 上課時間 Time T7T8 上課教室 Room 生二 220 一、課程說明 本課程以“理解大腦與神經系統的計算原理”以及“實際動 手操作神經網計算模型”為兩大主軸。希望在目前腦科學與 人工智慧最熱門的時代，提供學生一個跨領域學習的機會。 本課程將概略性介紹計算神經的理論，尺度從認神經網路到 神經細胞乃至於相關的腦功能與認知行為。以實用性角度出 發，讓學生理解日常生活的認知行為背後牽涉到的複雜大腦 計算問題。本課程盡量減少深奧的數學公式，每一個主題皆 佐以神經網路模擬軟體教學以讓學生實際動手與體驗。 本課適合理工與生命科學等科系大三大四同學修讀，並特別 設計給有下列需求的學生： 1. 正在學習認知與心理學，希望能進一步理解相關大腦神 經網路理論，或 2. 正在修讀神經科學與生命科學，希望能學習大腦系統性 的行為及其理論，或 3. 對機器學習與人工智慧有涉略，但希望能更理解相關生 物基礎與理論。 二、指定用書 以授課老師的公開線上課程網站為主要授課內容 https://sites.google.com/view/brain-and- computation/home 三、參考書籍 1. Computational Cognitive Neuroscience. by Michael Frank, Yuko Munakata, Thomas Hazy, Randall O'Reilly. http://a.co/bkNI2Mf (Amazon Kindle edition) https://grey.colorado.edu/CompCogNeuro/index.php/CCNBook /Main (Free online edition) 2. Peter Dayan & L. F. Abbott. Theoretical Neuroscience: Computational and Mathematical Modeling of Neural Systems. The MIT Press (2005) 四、教學方式 本課程以部分線上課程搭配實體課堂講解與電腦上機實作。 本課程分成四個主題，每一主題有2-4個單元。上課的部分 強調與學生的討論與互動，實機操作部分鼓勵學生發揮創 意。實機操作僅需操作軟體，不需要撰寫程式，但若有 Python程式語言的基本能力可增進學習效果。 五、教學進度 教學大綱 L3-1. Networks 1. Network structures 2. Feedforward networks and perceptron * 3. Recurrent network and working memory * 4. Recurrent network and navigation* L3-2. Connections 1. Synapse models: firing rate based & spike based 2. Synapse physiology L3-3. Neurons 1. Leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) model 2. Synaptic inputs in LIF model * 3. The Hodgkin-Huxley model 4. Other neuron models L3-4. Learning and memory 1. Hebbian learning & spike-timing dependent plasticity (STDP)* 2. Conditioning* 3. Reinforcement learning* *為附有電腦實作之單元 教學進度 9/2 Lecture L3-1-1, L3-1-2 9/9 Hands-on L3-1-2-h1, L3-1-2-h2 9/16 (Online) Lecture L3-1-3 9/23 hands-on L3-1-3-h1, L3-1-3-h2 9/30 (Online) Lecture L3-1-4 10/7 Hands-on L3-1-4-h1 10/14 Mid-term exam 10/21 (Online) Lecture L3-2-1, L3-2-2 10/28 (Online) Lecture L3-3-1, L3-3-2 11/4 Hands-on L3-3-1-h1 L3-3-1-h2 11/11 (Online) Lecture L3-3-3, L3-3-4 11/18 (Online) Lecture L3-4-1, 11/25 Hands-on L3-4-1-h1, L3-4-1-h2 12/2 (Online) Lecture L3-4-2, L3-4-3 12/9 Hands-on L3-4-2-h1, L3-4-3-h1 12/16 Final exam 標示 (Online) 者為線上課程，學生須自行觀看指定影片並作線 上測驗。無實體課程。若對於影片內容有疑問，可於課程網站之 留言區詢問，或於下次實體上課時討論。 六、成績考核 1. 每單元線上評量 13 次 x 3% = 39% 2. 課堂互動、討論與電腦實作 6 次 x 4% = 24% 3. 期中考 17% 4. 期末考 20% 七、可連結之網頁 位址(相關網頁) 本課程使用學校的 eeclass 平台為課程網站 另外可參考授課老師的線上課程網站 https://sites.google.com/view/brain-and- computation/home 八、AI 使用規則 學生在撰寫程式、報告與課堂測驗時可使用生成式 AI 或相 關工具。期中考與期末考不得使用任何 AI 工具。

docs.name: 免疫學
docs.text:
一、課程說明(Course Description)
免疫系統是具專一性且高度多樣化之個體防禦系統，在這防禦系統中，各類特定功能的細胞與分子
密切合作形成一動態的網絡，藉以清除致病性微生物與癌細胞。然而免疫系統的失調以及微生物與
癌細胞的反制亦造成感染症、癌症、及自體免疫疾病的惡化，我們該如何設計有效的免疫療法及疫
苗? 近年來，由於免疫學研究有多項突破性的進展，使得這門科學漸趨成熟，已成為二十一世紀之
顯學。無庸至疑地，免疫學是一不可或缺的生命科學課程。

本課程歡迎對免疫學有興趣的大學部學生及研究生修習。亦歡迎非生科系院同學選修。課程內容包
括探討基本的免疫學現象、發育及機制，簡言之，即是分子辨識(molecular recognition) 與反
應
(response)，以及免疫學在生物醫學及產業的應用，如免疫療法(immunotherapy)、單株抗體、疫
苗設計、生物感應器(biosensors)等。

docs.text:
一、課程說明(Course Description)

The SARS-CoV-2 pandemic has shown viruses' significant impact on human health.
This course offers an in-depth introduction to medical virology principles,
covering viral composition and structure, virus classification, and the
molecular replication strategies of both RNA and DNA viruses. Special focus is
put on medically critical human viruses, virus–host cell interactions, the
mechanisms of virulence and pathogenesis, and the development of antiviral drugs
and vaccines. Students will receive a detailed understanding of virology in
clinical applications.

docs.text: 國立清華大學 114 學年第ㄧ學期課程大綱 科號 Course No. 11010LS 545700 組別 group 學分 credit 2 人數限制 Size limit 30 修課年級 For grade ■ 大學部 年級以上 (undergraduate) ■ 碩士班一年級以上(含博士班) graduate ■ 碩士班二年級以上(含博士班) 上課時間 Time T7T8 教室 Room TBA 科目中文名稱 Course title in Chinese 生命科學之模式生物 Model organisms in life sciences 科目英文名稱 Course title in English Model Organisms in Life Sciences 任課教師 Teacher 李以如, 劉姿吟, 王歐力, 王翊青, 江運金, 桑自剛 擋修科目 Prerequisite 擋修分數 credit ※下列各欄由任課教師提供※ 一、課程說明 Course Description 人類基因體定序的完成，方便讓我們更了解所有人類的蛋白 質，但基因體的定序並無法提供足夠的信息來了解蛋白質的 功能、結構以其生物體內的訊號傳遞。現在，研究人員需要 的是，可以了解基因的作用，以及其編碼蛋白在細胞過程中 所扮演的角色。為了回答這些問題，研究員需要依靠一些小 型生物來了解生物體的奧妙，其條件是：容易培養，基因體 定序已完成，已具備突變株，容易被改造，適合顯微鏡觀 察，能快速而精準的篩選突變株，生命週期短，以及遵守人 道精神。 儘管大多數的微小模式生物體與人類毫無共同之處，但是大 部分生物的基因相似性卻是極高的。在許多情況下，某些模 式生物的基因已被成功地被人類基因取代，卻沒有影響其細 胞功能。模式生物，現在被廣泛地用來研究人類的疾病，並 且在較簡單的生物研究疾病，也減少了受爭議的倫理問題。 在這一學期的課程中，我們將介紹常用的一些在世界廣泛被 使用的模式生物，包括：老鼠，斑馬魚，阿拉伯芥，果蠅， 線蟲，酵母菌和大腸桿菌。課堂上，我們將選定一些主題進 行討論，像是解剖，發展（胚胎學），神經生物學（神經解 剖學，行為，mechanosensation，電生理學），遺傳（基因 體計畫），操作和維護這些模式生物，改造與基因的表達， 交配和性別鑑定，突變實驗（顯微注射，基因槍，和化學藥 物EMS），基因定位（SNP定位），RNAi干擾和利用轉位 子(transposons)的基因操作，顯微鏡使用，疾病模式，毒理 學和藥理學，演化和生態學，研究的方法和搜尋網站等等。 更有趣的，學生將有機會參加特定實驗室的操作或是觀摩。 並可學習如何處理和維護選定的模式生物，以及利用顯微鏡 來篩選綠色螢光蛋白的表達和其他變異之間的差異。 Course Description: The completion of the Human Genome Project has improved our understanding of human proteins. However, simply sequencing the genome is not enough to fully understand protein functions, structures, and their roles in cellular signaling. Researchers need methods to understand gene functions and the roles of encoded proteins in cellular processes. To address these questions, researchers rely on model organisms that meet specific criteria: ease of cultivation, completed genome sequencing, available mutants, modifiability, suitability for microscopic observation, rapid and precise mutant screening, short life cycles, and adherence to ethical principles. While it's true that most model organisms don't share direct commonality with humans, many species do exhibit a significant genetic similarity. This similarity has allowed human genes to be successfully replaced in model organisms without disrupting cellular function. As a result, model organisms have become invaluable tools in the study of human diseases, offering a way to investigate simpler biological systems and thereby reducing ethical controversies. Course Objectives: • Introduce commonly used model organisms in biomedical research. • Discuss various biological disciplines using model organisms, including anatomy, embryology, neurobiology, genetics, and more. • Provide hands-on experience and observational opportunities in laboratory settings. • Teach maintenance and handling of model organisms, microscopic screening techniques, and identification of protein expression variations. Model Organisms Covered: • Yeast • Arabidopsis • Nematode • Mouse • Zebrafish • Fruit fly Key Topics: 1. Anatomy and Developmental Biology (Embryology) 2. Neurobiology o Neuroanatomy o Behavior o Mechanosensation o Electrophysiology 3. Genetics o Genome projects o Manipulation and maintenance of model organisms o Gene expression and modification o Mating and sex determination 4. Mutation Experiments o Microinjection o Gene gun technology o Chemical mutagenesis (e.g., EMS) 5. Gene Localization o SNP mapping 6. RNA Interference (RNAi) 7. Transposon-based Gene Manipulation 8. Microscopy Techniques 9. Disease Models 10. Toxicology and Pharmacology 11. Evolution and Ecology 12. Research Methodologies and Database Searching Practical Experience: Students may be able to participate in laboratory work or observations, learning to handle and maintain selected model organisms. Practical sessions will include using microscopes to screen for green fluorescent protein expression and identifying differences among various mutants. This course aims to equip students with the knowledge and skills to utilize model organisms effectively in biomedical research, enhancing their understanding of complex biological processes and their implications for human health. 二、指定用書 Text Books N/A 三、參考書籍 References 授課教師提供講義 Provided by instructors 四、教學方式 Teaching Method 英語授課 The class is offered in English. 五、教學進度 Syllabus Week Date Topic Instructor Week 1 9/2 Yeast I-Ju Lee (李以如老師) Week 2 9/9 Yeast I-Ju Lee (李以如老師) Week 3 9/16 Yeast I-Ju Lee (李以如老師) Week 4 9/23 Arabidopsis Tzu-Yin Theresa Liu (劉姿吟老師) Week 5 9/30 Arabidopsis Tzu-Yin Theresa Liu (劉姿吟老師) Week 6 10/7 Arabidopsis Tzu-Yin Theresa Liu (劉姿吟老師) Week 7 10/14 Worm Oliver Wagner (王歐力老師) Week 8 10/21 Worm Oliver Wagner (王歐力老師) Week 9 10/28 Worm Oliver Wagner (王歐力老師) Week 10 11/4 Mouse I-Ching Wang (王翊青老師) Week 11 11/11 Mouse I-Ching Wang (王翊青老師) Week 12 11/18 Mouse I-Ching Wang (王翊青老師) Week 13 11/25 Zebrafish Yun-Jin Jiang (江運金老師) Week 14 12/2 Drosophila Tzu-Kang Sang (桑自剛老師) Week 15 12/9 Drosophila Tzu-Kang Sang (桑自剛老師) Week 16 12/16 Final Exam (Arabidopsis and C. elegans) 六、成績考核 Evaluation 學生評量: 由個別授課教授決定, 各單元佔比為 20% Instructors will announce the evaluation method in class. docs.text: 科號 Course Number 11410LSBS524700 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Class Size 0 中文名稱 Course Title 幹細胞與細胞治療特論一 英文名稱 Course English Title Special Topics in Stem Cell Biology and Cell Therapy I 任課教師 Instructor 劉懿璇 Yi-Shiuan Liu 上課時間 Time M9Ma 上課教室 Room 育成 319 室 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters 本課程將指導學生研讀幹細胞領域的期刊論文與研究成果報告。課程目的除了 了解幹細胞基礎知識以及幹細胞培養技術外，學生在課程完成後將能夠（1）了 解幹細胞在醫療的應用以及限制性；（2）分析幹細胞相關文獻的研究成果並規 劃具有潛力的研究題目；（3）對幹細胞生物學的科學倫理與醫療政策提出反思。 I will guide students to read journal articles covering regenerative medicine and cell therapy. In addition to understanding the basic knowledge of stem cells, upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to (1) describe how stem cells can be used for medical purposes and understand current limitations; (2) analyze literature and describe potential research topic; (3) develop informed opinions of the science policy and ethics of stem cell biology. 請輸入課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」至少 5 個, 每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文, 以半形逗點分隔 (必填) Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 幹細胞；間質幹細胞；細胞治療；生物力學；分化；外泌體 Stem cell; Mesenchymal stem cell; Cell therapy; Mechanobiology; Differentiation; Exosome 一、課程說明 本課程將指導學生研讀幹細胞領域的期刊論文並進行研究成 果報告，以期能夠了解幹細胞基礎知識以及醫療應用。學生 在課程完成後將能夠分析幹細胞相關文獻的研究成果並規劃 具有潛力的研究題目。 二、指定用書 近期幹細胞以及細胞治療相關之專業期刊 三、參考書籍 近期幹細胞以及細胞治療相關之專業期刊 四、教學方式 課堂報告與討論，包括期刊論文討論與研究結果報告。 五、教學進度 每位學生每學期需負責帶領至少兩次論文導讀與兩次研究結 果報告。授課老師除了組織主題並討論外，會在每階段 (一 次論文導讀與成果報告後)進行分項主題講解。 六、成績考核 1. 報告與導讀內容 50 %。 2. 討論參與 50%。 可使用 AI 相關工具，但需於報告時揭露使用範圍與方法。 七、可連結之網頁 位址(相關網頁)

Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000
letters

Researchers need to have a thorough understanding of the theories and algorithms
behind the computational methods they employ. It's also crucial to actively seek
knowledge about newly proposed methods on a daily basis.
Explaining what one has learned to others when studying methods can enhance
presentation skills and deepen understanding. Similarly, listening to
presentations by others can improve presentation skills and lead to the
discovery
of new interests and ideas.
With this in mind, this course will involve selecting topics related to theories
and algorithms in fields such as machine learning and molecular simulation,
allowing participants to give presentations on their chosen subjects.

docs.nameEn: Special Topics in Wound Healing and Cancer Therapy I
docs.text:
一、課程說明
The ability to repair tissue injuries is essential for
survival and is a prerequisite for all invasive medical intervention. It has
been shown that wound healing and cancer metastasis share common early
signaling pathways that have led to the hypothesis that tumors are “wounds
that do not heal”. In fact, cancer progression and wound healing are
influenced by many common factors, for example, regulators of angiogenesis and
inflammation are instrumental in different types of oncological therapy and
wound healing/regeneration.

With a focus on current research projects in Prof. YJ Chuang;s lab, this
special topics course begins with a systemic review of current topics in wound
healing and cancer therapy, followed by general and then focused discussion of
involved factors that are of interest.

docs.text: Special Topics on Pathogen Evolution (I) 一、課程說明 Course Description This advanced course aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the concepts and methods in pathogen population genetics, a field that is currently undergoing rapid growth. Through reading of primary literature, class participation, oral presentations, and group discussions, students will explore the fundamental population-level processes that shape genetic variation in pathogen populations, as well as the latest statistical methods for analyzing pathogen genetic data. 二、指定用書 Text books Selected papers 三、參考書籍 References • Additional resources (額外學習資源之內容): Molecular Evolution online course from NTU (http://ocw.aca.ntu.edu.tw/ntu-ocw/ocw/cou/100S225) 四、教學方式 Teaching Method All students are required to present and participate in classroom discussion. 五、教學進度 Syllabus This course encourages students to share important new research in the field of pathogen evolution as well as their own research findings, explore areas where current research is lacking, refine their own research projects, identify possible future research directions, and develop skills in oral presentations and Q&A. This course will focus on the following research topics that are currently ongoing in Dr. Chang’s lab. 1. Statistical methods for detecting the presence of natural selection 2. Methods for studying migration and population structure of pathogens 3. Sequence simulations 4. Genetic diversity in pathogen populations 5. Modeling immune selection in pathogens 六、成績考核 Evaluation Class discussion: 30%. Assigned presentation: 50%. Attendance: 20%. docs.nameEn: Special Topics in Microtubule Dynamics and Microtubule Associated Proteins
docs.text:
一、課程說明
自從Mitchison和Kirschner在1984年第一次揭示微管的動態變化特性和調控機制後，一個全新的生物領域
因而誕生。細胞中的微管具有調控細胞分裂、細胞移動、細胞極性、胞器運輸等重要功能；而微管調控失調則
與神經退化性疾病、纖毛相關疾病、癌症息息相關，故微管及其相關蛋白常是新藥開發的標靶。以微管為
例，紫杉醇能有效抑制微管動態變化，在細胞內可以抑制細胞分裂，臨床上是一種抗癌藥物。

本課程旨在使學生了解細胞骨架蛋白微管的生成與調控機制、以及該領域的重要研究主題與最新發現，將藉
由報告討論的方式培養學生在閱讀科學期刊、主動探索進修、以及研究設計與分析的能力。此外，亦訓練學
生使用英文進行簡要的口頭研究報告，並練習問答技巧，進而分享自己的研究成果。

docs.name: 書報討論
docs.text: 科號 Course Number 11410LSBS790101 學分 Credit 1 人數限制 Class Size 10 中文名稱 Course Title 書報討論 英文名稱 Course English Title Seminar 任課教師 Instructor 劉懿璇 Yi-Shiuan Liu 上課時間 Time F5 上課教室 Room LS II 生二 107 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters 本課程目的在於深化同學對專業領域最新研究文獻的掌握與批判性解析能力， 並提升口頭表達與科學討論的技巧。學生將輪流選擇與課程主題相關的研究論 文進行報告，並與全班進行深入討論。透過課堂互動與導師引導，學生將學習 分析研究方法、解讀數據、以及科學論證與回應質疑的技巧。本課程同時鼓勵 學生從文獻中發掘研究動機、建立跨領域連結，進一步提出原創性研究問題的 能力。 請輸入課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」至少 5 個, 每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文, 以半形逗點分隔 (必填) Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 生物醫學 (Biomedicine), 期刊論文(Journal article), 口頭報告(Oral presentation), 科學方法(Scientific methods), 批判性思維(Critical thinking) 一、課程說明 本課程旨在訓練學生閱讀、理解、分析同儕審查文獻。透過 每週指定文獻的報告與討論，學生將培養學術溝通、邏輯表 達、問題提出與論證能力，並加強對研究方法與學術寫作的 掌握。 This course aims to train students in reading, understanding, and analyzing peer-reviewed journal articles. Through weekly oral presentations and discussions of assigned readings, students will develop skills in academic communication and critical thinking, while also deepening their understanding of scientific methods and academic writing. 二、指定用書 無 N/A 三、參考書籍 生命科學領域具代表性的學術期刊 四、教學方式 1. 上課方式以文獻討論為主。學生於課前預習文獻，並於 課堂中輪流提出問題討論。 2. 演講同學於演講前兩週將擬報告之研究論文寄給老師以 徵得老師同意；演講前一週將該論文全文以 PDF 電子檔發 給全班同學，以利預先閱讀與討論準備。 3. 每位同學報告 30 ~ 40 分鐘，10 ~ 20分鐘問題回答。 4. 口頭報告後兩周內繳交書面報告(約 2頁A4)，針對報告 與提問內容做出討論與心得總結。 5. 學期末每位同學另進行 10 分鐘研究自述，分享研究方 法與經驗。 1. The course is primarily conducted through literature presentations and discussions. 2. The presenting student must send the proposed research article to the instructor two weeks before the presentation for approval. One week prior to the presentation, the full article in PDF format should be shared with all classmates. 3. Each student will give a 30–40 minute presentation, followed by 10–20 minutes of Q&A. 4. A written report (approximately 2 A4 pages) should be submitted within two weeks after the oral presentation. 5. At the end of the semester, each student will give a 10- minute research talk, sharing their research experiences. 五、教學進度 每週以 1 位同學進行報告為原則。 In principle, one student will give a presentation each week. 六、成績考核 報告內容與簡報品質 presentation 40% 批判性分析能力 critical thinking 10% 討論互動與提問 participation in discussion 25% 書面摘要 written report 15% 課堂出席 attendance 10% 可使用 AI 相關工具，但需揭露使用範圍與方法。 ※請假規定依清華大學學則辦理。遲到 15 分鐘視為缺席。 七、可連結之網頁 位址(相關網頁)

docs.nameEn: Special Topics of the Nucleus I
docs.text:
一、課程說明
The nucleus is the hallmark of eukaryotic cells that housing DNA in a membrane-enclosed compartment.
The
emergence of nucleus during evolution offered a more sophisticated regulation for decoding genetic
information, which ultimately drove the evolvement of multicellular organisms. Thus, the maintenance of
nuclear structure and organization is key to the function of all eukaryotic cells. In this class, we will discuss
topics relate to (1) the nuclear envelope, (2) the nuclear lamins, (3) the lamin-binding proteins, (4) the
nuclear
pore complex, (5) the nucleoplasm and cytoplasm transport, (6) the functional organization of the
nucleolus,
(7) the nuclear proteolysis, and (8) the nuclear structure maintenance.
二、指定用書
The nucleus, by Tom Misteli and David L. Spector
‧ ISBN-10: 0879698942
三、參考書籍

四、教學方式
Student presentation and paper review (in English)
五、教學進度
(1) nuclear envelope (three weeks)
(2) nuclear lamins (two weeks)
(3) lamin-binding proteins (one week)
(4) the nuclear pore complex (one week)
(5) nucleoplasm and cytoplasm transport (two weeks)
(6) the functional organization of the nucleolus (two weeks) (7) the nuclear proteolysis (two weeks)
(8) the nuclear structure maintenance (two weeks)
40 min presentation and 1 hour discussion/paper review for each class
六、成績考核
Presentation (50%)
Summary report (30%)
Class participation (20%)

and diseased lungs by covering following issues: (1) Lung epithelial development

In this course we will learn: 1) recombinant DNA technology; 2) procedure of
generation of transgenic and gene knock mice; 3) the molecular mechanism of

conditional

docs.text:
This course aims to introduce recent progress and future trends in
biochip/biosensor technologies. To enable a student to do the related research
works, extensive literature studies in microfluidics, biosensing, and
bioengineering will be expected. The course will adopt a hybrid teaching
approach, combining lectures by the instructor, student presentations, and
journal club discussions. A student will learn how to design and incorporate
upstream microfluidics with a downstream biosensing system that is applicable to
various biomedical applications. The course will cover the operating principles
of transducers and biochips, fabrication methods, and their applications in
fields such as diagnostics, health monitoring, and drug development, including
protein profiling arrays, single-cell technologies, multi-omics, and liquid
biopsy.

Various nuclear factors are essential for immune organogenesis, leukocyte lineage development, differentiation, effector functions and immune tolerance. In addition, understanding epigenomic regulation has become an urgent area of study. This course offers an introduction to the discovery, functions, and latest research on these nuclear factors, enhancing students understanding of immune cell biology. ● 指定用書(Text Books) none ● 參考書籍(References) related papers ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) Lecture, presentation and discussion ● 教學進度(Syllabus) Week 1. docs.name: 免疫系統發育與免疫病理
docs.text: 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) The immune system provides essential lifelong protection and maintains homeostasis. While it develops early in life, it gradually declines with aging. Both genetic and environmental factors (such as diet, microbiota, infections, and aging) influence the immune system, potentially leading to pathologies like autoimmunity, allergies, and chronic inflammation. In the first half of the course, lectures will cover an overview of immune system development, immune-related diseases, and factors affecting immune function that are linked to immune-mediated pathologies. The second half will focus on student-led group discussions and presentations based on recent research articles, encouraging deeper engagement with the material and promoting a better understanding of current developments in immunology. Together, this course aims to enhance students' knowledge of immune system function, its dysregulation in diseases, and how ongoing research is shaping our understanding of immune-mediated pathologies. ● 指定用書(Text Books) - none ● 參考書籍(References) - “Cellular and Molecular Immunology 10th edition” by Abbas, Lichtman and Pillai - Published journal papers ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) This course adopts a combination of lectures, interactive discussions, and group presentations to foster active learning. External seminars by guest speakers will provide additional perspectives on cutting-edge research. The course is offered in English. ● 教學進度(Syllabus) Week data (tentative) 1. Course introduction and overview 2-3. Immune response and diseases 4-5. Genetic factors in immune related diseases 6-7. Environmental factors in immune related diseases 8. Exam 9. Special lecture 10-15. Groupwork presentation 16. Lecture and final Discussion - Schedule for groupwork discussion is flexible, and determined depending on number of students enrolled - Special seminars by external speakers are being scheduled ● 成績考核(Evaluation) (tentative) Attendance 30% Exam 20% Presentation/discussion 40% Active participation in discussions, clarity and depth in presentations, and performance on exams will form the basis of evaluation. ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output. docs.name: 書報討論
docs.text:
Course Introduction
“What is the next big question?” is a phrase you might have heard or even often wonder yourselves after reading a paper or a seminar. Although there is no correct answer to this question, given that scientific breakthroughs are often dictated by unexpected technological advances, there are definitely good answers. Impactful papers that move a field forward usually provide such answers. Thus, reading a series of papers that are in progressive order scientifically within a field can give us a sense of how good scientific questions are formulated. In this course, we will read a series of papers in the relatively new field of mitophagy. Because the field began less than 15 years ago and has developed very fast since, we will be able to witness the trajectory of the development of a new field in science from reading these papers. In the class focus will be placed on discussing the impact of a paper to the field, and predicting the thesis of the following paper. At the end of the course we will review every paper and determine their significance under the broad view of the field. Through this exercise students can learn to evaluate scientific questions and, more importantly, formulate good research questions of one’s own.

Course Description
Each week a student will be required to perform tasks, including giving a presentation of a paper and leading a discussion. When not presenting, student audience will be required to read the papers and participate in discussion.

Syllabus
TBD. (Will be discussed and determined at the beginning of the course.)

Evaluation
1. Oral presentation (60%) – Evaluation of this part is based on organization logic and clarity of presentation.
2. Discussion (40%) – Evaluation of this part is based on the questions raised in each of the fellow students’ presentation.
3. More detail requirement and grading criteria will be provided at the beginning of the course.

In this course, we aim to update our knowledge of immunology and develop a deeper understanding of the complexity of the immune system. Each student will select a research article on immunology, and present in the class. Attendance is recorded by submitting a questionnaire sheet for each class. Additionally, each student is required to submit three reports on papers introduced by others. The mentor will help presenters prepare their presentations upon request, assist in understanding the presentation, and facilitate discussions. docs.text:
1. 課目名稱/ Course
(中文) 生長因子訊息專題:於癌症治療之應用
(英文) Special Topics in Growth Factor Signaling: Its Application in Cancer
Therapy
授課老師/Instructor：周裕珽 (Yu-Ting Chou)
學分數/Credit： 2 (須與老師面談後加簽選課)

2. 課程大綱/Course Description
Growth factors play critical roles in tissue homeostasis. Deregulated
expression of growth factors and their receptors contribute to tumor
initiation and progression. Several Targeted therapies blocking deregulated
growth factor signaling achieve successful outcomes in cancer patients. This
course will cover cutting-edge topics including the roles of growth factor
signaling in cell proliferation, differentiation and cancer development. We

docs.text:
Course Introduction
Giving useful critiques to research works is an important skill for not only personal development as a scientist but also for progress of scientific fields as a whole. In this course, students will learn how to critique and evaluate scientific papers. Students will be required to use a standardized method, which will be introduced in the class, to offer critique and evaluation of an assigned paper. Moreover, by applying these skills, reading papers will transform from passively receiving information to an active process. This will enable students to read papers in a more efficient manner.

Syllabus
TBD. (Will be discussed and determined at the beginning of the course.)

Evaluation
1.Oral presentation (60%) – Evaluation of this part is based on organization logic and clarity of presentation.
2.Discussion (40%) – Evaluation of this part is based on the questions raised in each of the fellow students’ presentation.
3.More detail requirement and grading criteria will be provided at the beginning of the course.

Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output

本課程目的是幫助大一新生在學業和個人方面順利從高中過渡到大學，藉由促 進參與大學課程和課外生活，建立對學校的歸屬感，協助學生培養和運用批判 思考技能，以順利適應大學生活，並幫助學生找尋人生目的、意義與方向。 課程目標 A 協助學業成功：透過本課程，學生將能 1. 應用適當的策略來調整他們的課程學習方式 2. 運用有效的方式來進行時間管理 3. 熟悉與他們學習有關的彈性學制 B 認識清華並與清華建立連結：透過本課程，學生將能 1. 使用適當的校園資源，並參與有助於他們在課堂內外學習的機會 2. 與同學、老師和行政同仁建立正向的關係 3. 瞭解清華大學的歷史與傳統 C 促進個人發展、幸福和社會責任：透過本課程，學生將能 1. 建立自己的價值觀和身份認同，並瞭解這些價值觀和身份認同如何形塑 他們的觀點，以及發展與自己相同或不同立場的人的關係 2. 發展促進健康的策略，並理解身心健康如何影響他們的學業和個人成功 3. 進行自我的生涯規劃，並對未來的職場方向有所瞭解 課程閱讀材料 1. 學務處新生領航營新生手冊 2. 保持原來的樣子就很好了(稻垣榮洋 2024/10/09) 課程要求及評分 課堂參與及討論 15% 拜訪教授與撰寫心得 10% 參加校園活動紀錄 10% 探索校園神秘地點 10% 撰寫履歷 10% 期中狀況分享 15% 期末專題 docs.text: 國立清華大學 114 學年第 1 學期新開課程課程大綱 科號 Course Number 11410LSMC514100 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Class Size 中文名稱 Course Title 酵母菌生物學 英文名稱 Course English Title Yeast Biology 任課教師 Instructor 李政昇、廖品超、李清福、張壯榮、李以如 上課時間 Time T34 上課教室 Room (生二 213) 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) 酵母生物學旨在教授學生酵母菌的基本生物學概念、實驗程序和實際應用。強調酵母菌的 基本生物特徵和經典遺傳學方法，如突變體的分離和鑒定、互補性、四分體分析和有絲分 裂重組等。還將探討分子遺傳技術，包括酵母轉化、基因替換、基因融合的構建和分析以 及在克隆出的基因中導入突變等。此外，還將介紹現代細胞學和系統學方法。這些古典、 分子細胞學和系統學酵母方法將有助於學生在將酵母應用作研究模型時獲得洞察力。同 時，還會在適當的課程中討論最新的關於酵母遺傳學重要觀念的論文。 請輸入課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」至少 5 個, 每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文, 以半形逗點分 隔 (必填) Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 酵母菌, yeast, molecular genetics, cell architecture, gene regulation, screening 一、課程說明 The Yeast Biology is designed to teach students basic biological concepts, experimental procedures, and applications of yeast. Basic biological features of yeast and classical genetic approaches, such as the isolation and characterization of mutants, complementation, tetrad analysis, and mitotic recombination, will be emphasized. Molecular genetic techniques, including yeast transformation, gene replacement with plasmids and PCR, construction and analysis of gene fusions, and generation of mutations in cloned genes, will also be addressed. Furthermore, modern cytological and systematical approaches will be covered. These classical, molecular cytological and systematical yeast approaches will benefit students to gain insight information while applying yeast as research model. Latest papers on fundamental aspects of yeast genetics may also be discussed in the corresponding lectures. 二、指定用書 N/A 三、參考書籍  Yeast: Molecular and Cell Biology, Second Edition. Edited by Horst Feldmann. Wiley-VCH Verlag GmbH & Co. KGaA., 2012  Genetic Techniques for Biological Research – A case study approach Corinne A. Michaels John Wiley & Sons, Ltd., 2002  Methods in Yeast Genetics. David C. Amberg, Daniel J. Burke, Jeffery N. Strathern. CSHL Press, 2005 四、教學方式 Lecture combined with discussion. 五、教學進度 週次 日期 課程內容 授課教師 1 09/02 Taxonomy and ecology of yeasts 李清福 2 09/9 Yeast growth and the yeast cell cycle 李政昇 3 09/16 Manipulation of yeast genomes (I) 李政昇 4 09/23 Manipulation of yeast genomes (II) 李政昇 5 9/30 Yeast transformation and protein expression 張壯榮 6 10/07 Isolation of yeast mutants 張壯榮 7 10/14 Yeast X-hybrid system 張壯榮 8 10/21 Yeast screening 李以如 9 10/28 Yeast genomics 李以如 10 11/04 Budding yeast cell architecture and functions 廖品超 11 11/11 Intracellular protein sorting and transport 廖品超 12 11/18 Molecular signaling cascades and gene regulation 廖品超 13 11/25 Studies using fission yeast 李以如 14 12/02 Biotechnological application of yeasts (1) 李清福 15 12/9 Biotechnological application of yeasts (2) 李清福 16 12/16 Final exam 六、成績考核 Class participation & in-class quiz: 30% Assignments: 30% Final exam: 40% 七、可連結之網頁 位址(相關網頁) https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw/ 生成式人工智慧倫理聲明： 「有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於作業或報告」 基於透明與負責任的原則，本課程鼓勵學生利用 AI 進行協作或互學，以提升本門課產出品質。 根據本校公布之佈的「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採取有條 件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於作業或報告，說明如下： • 學生可於課堂作業或報告中的「標題頁註腳」或「引用文獻後」簡要說明如何使用生成式 AI 進行議題發想、文句潤飾或結構參考等使用方式。然而，在本課程的「個人反思報告」、 「小組採訪作業」中，學生不得使用生成式 AI 工具撰寫作業。若經查核使用卻無在作業或 報告中標明，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。 • 本門課授課教材或學習資料若有引用自生成式 AI，教師也將在投影片或口頭標注。 • 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。

docs.nameEn: Special Topics on Pteridophyte Biology II
docs.text:
● 課程說明(Course Description)
Pteridophytes, ferns and lycophytes, contain the second largest lineage
among land plants, but their biology is poorly understood compared to that
of seed plants, a model organism concentrated lineage. An improved
understanding of pteridophyte biology provides the key to uncovering
mysteries behind the evolutionary history of plants. In this lecture, we are
going to focus on several important biological issues that are much unique
in pteridophytes by reading assigned textbook chapters and other scientific
literature.

● 指定用書(Text Books)
Current Advances in Fern Research by Helena Fernández, Springerlink (2018)

● 參考書籍(References)
Selected recent papers from high profile journals such as Science, Nature,
PNAS, New Phytologists, MPE, GBE, American Journal of Botany, American Fern
Journal etc.

● 教學方式(Teaching Method)
All students are required to read all assigned chapters and papers and then
participate in classroom discussion.

LIFE HISTORY

Apomixis
Apospory

PHENOLOGY
Sporing phenology
Leaf life span

ECOPHYSIOLOGY
C3 and CAM

Nutrient relations

SYSTEMATICS & DIVERSITY
Phylogeny
Classification systems
Diversity in Taiwan

GENOME BIOLOGY
Plastome
Nuclear genome

Schedule:

Dirk Haller. 2018. The Gut Microbiome in Health and Disease. Springer Cham. 2. Om Prakash, Dilip R. Ranade. 2021. Anaerobes and Anaerobic Processes 1ed. Routledge and CRC Press. ● 教學方式 (Teaching Method) 前半段基礎知識及研究方法部分以講授為主，佐以影片及校外參訪進行輔助教學。後半段微生物體於各領域之應 用則會以部分講授搭配學生報告的方式來進行。 ● 教學進度 (Syllabus)* 本課程將涵蓋以下主題： 1. 人類微生物體簡介/ Microbiome through the lifespan in our body 2. 以 16S 序列研究微生物菌相之方法-檢體之收集與核酸萃取及放大/ Sequencing-based techniques to analyze microbiome- sample collection, DNA, RNA extraction, and amplification 3. 研究微生物體之生物資訊方法/ Bioinformatics tools to analyze microbiome composition and the interactions 4. 以多體學方法研究功能性微生物體/ Integrated multi-omics to analyze the functional microbiome 5. 培養體學/ Culturomics 6. 厭氧操作技術簡介/Anaerobic microbial techniques 7. 校外參訪*/ Off-campus Visit 8. 無菌動物模式/ Gnotobiology and animal models to study microbiome 9. 環境微生物體與健康一體之概念/ Environmental microbiome and the One-health 10. 動物微生物體與農業及野生動物保育之應用/ Animal microbiome in agriculture and wildlife conservation 11. 腸道微生物與免疫/ Gut microbiota and immunity 12. 腸道微生物與營養代謝/ Gut microbiota and nutrition metabolism 13. 腦腸軸研究/ The gut-brain axis 14. 固醇與內分泌微生物體/ Sterolbiome and endobolome 15. 糞菌移植治療/ Fecal microbiota transplantation 16. 真菌體及病毒體/ Mycobiome and Virome ● 成績考核(Evaluation) 書面報告 40% 口頭報告* 40% 課堂參與 (出席+課程問答討論) 20% *教學進度會依照修課人數及專家演講時程進行調整。 *校外參訪事宜及口頭報告順序將會在第一堂課時決定。 ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output 可參考下列網頁範例 See the following web page for examples. https://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1208-248357.php?Lang=zh-tw ● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website)

Applied microbiology focuses on harnessing microbial processes for practical applications, spanning industrial microbiology, biopharmaceuticals, environmental microbiology, food and fermentation technology, and microbial contributions to human health. This course will explore key topics in applied microbiology, emphasizing both fundamental principles and cutting-edge innovations and applications. 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 代謝工程、發酵、合成生物學、培養基優化、細菌代謝多樣性 Metabolic engineering, fermentation, synthetic biology, medium optimization, bacterial metabolic diversity 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) This advanced course is designed to span two semesters. Stevens, Jayna L. Ditty, Rebecca E. Parales, Susan M. Merkel. 2024. Microbial Physiology: Unity and Diversity. ASM Press. ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) All students will be assigned to present the selected papers and join the in-class discussion. ● 教學進度(Syllabus) Major topics will be included in this course: 1. docs.name: 分子辨識與細胞訊號傳導特論
docs.nameEn: Special Topics in Molecular Recognition and Cellular Signaling
docs.text:
● 課程說明(Course Description)
本課程旨在介紹分子辨識與細胞訊號傳導的基本概念和機制，幫助學生深入理解細胞內外如何通過分
子之間的相互作用來傳遞信號，並引發細胞的生理反應。學生將學習分子辨識在細胞功能調控中的關
鍵作用，並探索這些過程如何影響細胞生理、發育以及疾病狀態。
課程的重點將放在兩個主要的分子辨識過程：G蛋白偶聯受體（GPCR）配體的結合機制和抗體-抗原的
相互作用，並深入探討這些相互作用如何在細胞訊號傳導中發揮重要作用。學生將學習如何從分子結
構的角度解釋受體-配體的結合過程，並分析這些過程在細胞內訊號傳遞中的具體功能。
此外，課程將探討分子辨識和訊號傳導在生物醫學中的應用，特別是在藥物開發和疾病治療中的角
色。例如，學生將學習到如何利用GPCR和抗體-抗原互動的知識開發新型藥物，並討論這些技術在治療
癌症、免疫疾病以及神經退行性疾病中的應用潛力。
本課程適合對細胞生物學、分子生物學、藥理學及生物醫學研究有興趣的學生。課程將通過講授、案
例分析和討論，幫助學生掌握分子辨識與細胞訊號傳導的核心概念，並理解其在現代生物醫學研究中
的重要性。

● 指定用書(Text Books)
無

● 參考書籍(References)
近兩年內之期刊論文

● 教學方式(Teaching Method)
上課前，學生需事先研讀選定之期刊論文，並於課堂中作口頭報告及進行討論。除了選定之期刊論
文，學生亦須將實驗之結果作報告及討論

● 教學進度(Syllabus)
每二週一位學生報告期刊論文，每週二位學生報告實驗結果

● 成績考核(Evaluation)
口頭報告：70％; 課堂討論情形：20％; 作業：10％
授課教師保留依學生在學期中的進步情形、出席狀況、或其他可以觀察的表現，以調整學期總成績

docs.text: 國立清華大學 114 學年度第 1 學期課程大綱 科號 Course Number 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Class Size 0 中文名稱 Course Title 核酸技術開發特論 英文名稱 Course English Title Special Topics on Nucleic Acid Technology Development 任課教師 Instructor 王慧菁 Lily Wang 上課時間 Time M8M9 上課教室 Room LSII 213 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) This lecture provides an in-depth exploration of the latest advancements and applications in nucleic acid technology. Students will delve into topics such as nucleic acid synthesis and modification, detection technologies, gene editing (CRISPR/Cas9), nucleic acid therapeutics, RNA-based technologies, DNA nanotechnology, and the application of lipid-nanoparticle (LNP) delivery. Through lectures, discussions, and project presentations, students will gain a comprehensive understanding of the advances in nucleic acid technology development. 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) Nucleic acid, mRNA, CRISPR/Cas9, LNP, LncRNA 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) This lecture provides an in-depth exploration of the latest advancements and applications in nucleic acid technology. Students will delve into topics such as nucleic acid synthesis and modification, detection technologies, gene editing (CRISPR/Cas9), nucleic acid therapeutics, RNA-based technologies, DNA nanotechnology, and the application of lipid-nanoparticle (LNP) delivery. In addition, this lecture involves practical on-site training on mRNA synthesis and quantification. Through lectures, discussions, and project presentations, students will gain a comprehensive understanding of the advances in nucleic acid technology development. ● 指定用書(Text Books) NA ● 參考書籍(References) NA ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) In-class lecture, practical training, and journal discussion ● 教學進度(Syllabus) Week Lecture Key concepts 1 Introduction to Nucleic Acid Technology DNA, RNA, nucleotides, and their roles in biology. 2 Nucleic Acid Synthesis-1 Vector design and enzymes used in DNA/RNA synthesis 3 Nucleic Acid Synthesis-2 In vitro transcription, amplification, and purification 4 Nucleic Acid Detection Technologies 1. Mechanisms of action, delivery challenges. 11 Nucleic Acid Drug Delivery Systems Challenges and strategies for nucleic acid delivery, including lipid nanoparticles (LNP) and viral vectors. 12 Practical training-3 LNP package and quality control 13 Practical training-4 mRNA delivery and efficiency optimization 14 New updates in NA therapy Student journal presentation of new advances 15 New updates in NA therapy Student journal presentation of new advances 16 Final report ● 成績考核(Evaluation) Course participation: 10% Practical training: 45% Journal report: 45% ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output

docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 11410LSMC546500 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Class Size 0 中文名稱 Course Title CRISPR-Cas 之基因編輯特論一 英文名稱 Course English Title Special Topics in gene editing by CRISPR-Cas I 任課教師 Instructor 李政昇 上課時間 Time F7F8 上課教室 Room 生科一館 421A 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) 這門課程將介紹 CRISPR/Cas 領域的主要概念與方法。學生將學習 CRISPR/Cas 的運作原理，以 及如何利用該系統進行基因組編輯。課程內容包括分子生物學的基本背景知識以及多種不同應 用的詳細操作流程。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) CRISPR/Cas, 基因編輯, 基因治療, gene disruption, genetic screening 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) This class will introduce the major concepts and methods in CRISPR/Cas field. Both conceptual background in molecular biology and detailed protocol of multiple different applications will be covered. ● 指定用書(Text Books): CRISPR-Cas: A Laboratory Manual Edited by Jennifer Doudna & Prashant Mali ISBN 978-1-621821-31-1 ● 參考書籍(References): Selected papers from high-profile journals ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) All students are required to read all assigned chapters and papers and then participate in classroom discussion. ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 1-2. Large-Scale Single Guide RNA Library Construction and Use for CRISPR-Cas9-Based Genetic Screens 9-10. Adeno-Associated Virus–Mediated Delivery of CRISPR-Cas Systems for Genome Engineering in Mammalian Cells 11-12. Detecting Single-Nucleotide Substitutions Induced by Genome Editing 13-14. docs.name: 神經元內傳輸及病理特論二
docs.nameEn: Special Topics on Intra-neuronal Trafficking and Diseases II
docs.text: 生命科學系 114 學年度下學期課程大綱 科號 LSMC576600 組別 學分 2 人數限制 0 修課年級 For grade ■ 大學部 年級以上 (undergraduate) ■ 碩士班一年級以上(含博士班) graduate ■ 碩士班二年級以上(含博士班) 科目中文名稱 神經元內傳輸及病理一 教室 505A LSBI 科目英文名稱 Intra-neuronal trafficking and diseases (part II) 任課教師 王歐力 Oliver Wagner 上課時間 F7F8 擋修科目 擋修分數 一、課程說明 The neuron is a highly polarized cell, possessing dendrites that are specialized for signal reception, and an axon for signal conduction and transmission. Long and thin axons are densely packed with mitochondria, synaptic vesicles, microtubules and neurofilaments, molecular motors and cargo. Cargos include synaptic precursors, membranous organelles, cytoskeletal elements, signaling molecules, growth factors and more. Considering the extensive length and the small diameter coupled with the amount of material that must be transported, it is not surprising that disruption in axonal transport lead to defects causing numerous neurodegenerative diseases. Many of these neurodegenerative diseases are related to defects in microtubule-based motors and their cargos. For example, a mutation in the molecular motor dynein rescues axonal transport defects and extends the life span of ALS (Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis) mice. Alzheimer's disease occurs based on accumulation of amyloid precursor proteins (APP) which is a cargo for the molecular motor KIF5A. LIS1 is associated with dynein while a mutation in LIS causes lissencephaly. A mutation in the molecular motor KIF1B causes Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A. A single base-pair change in the p150Glued subunit of the dynein adaptor-protein dynactin causes LMN and senile dementia is based on neuronal cell death caused by defects in the transport of synaptic precursors by the molecular motor KIF1A. Recent progress on Huntington’s Disease demonstrates that axonal polyglutamine (polyQ) aggregates could physically block microtubule-based cargo transport while Huntingtin and huntingtin-associated protein-1 (HAP1) interacts with dynein/dynactin and kinesin. To understand how defects in the axonal transport system lead to neurodegenerative diseases, we need to know the mechanisms of motor-cargo interaction and how the movement of molecular motors is regulated in the nervous system. In this class we discuss most recent studies on this at the present time central topic in neuroscience. 二、指定用書 Recent textbooks and papers related to this topic. 三、教學方式 Special seminar for graduate and undergraduate students. 四、教學進度 2 hourly seminar 五、成績考核 Attendance: 30%. Performance (general performance and discussion of papers): 30%. Presentation (individual journal presentation): 40% 六、講義位址 http:// http://life.nthu.edu.tw/~laboiw AI Unrestricted use with no disclosure required

課程簡述
心血管系統是人體主要的循環系統，本課程從生理學和基礎病理學介紹心血管的調控機制，再
導入基礎藥理學和介紹臨床藥物透過何種機制來治療疾病，並由病例討論使學生瞭解疾病和臨
床藥物使用的實際情形。使學生對心血管領域有基礎的知識並對相關學術論文具有判讀分析能
力。

讀。利用案例討論和論文導讀以及口頭報告，可提升學生高密度自主性學習，培養學生主
動、積極、獨立思考的學習精神，增進學生溝通及獨立思考的能力。本課程目標為建立學生

docs.text: 國立清華大學 114 學年第 1 學期新開課程課程大綱 科號 Course Number 11410LSMC581000 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Class Size 中文名稱 Course Title 區塊鏈在生物醫療的應用 英文名稱 Course English Title Blockchain Applications in Biomedical Healthcare 任課教師 Instructor 趙以選/王慧菁 上課時間 Time R8R9RaRb (8 周密集上課) 9/4~10/23 上課教室 Room 217 一般教室 220 電腦教室 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters 區塊鏈技術是一種去中心化的分散式資料庫技術，它基於密碼學原理和分佈 式系統技術，可以實現多個節點共同維護和更新數據庫，而無需依賴單一中 央機構。區塊鏈技術中最重要的概念是「區塊」，每個區塊都包含了數據、 時間戳、和前一個區塊的數字簽名，並且所有區塊按照時間戳順序排列，形 成了一個不斷增長的鏈狀數據結構，因此稱為「區塊鏈」。 在生物醫療領域，區塊鏈可以應用於許多面向，例如醫療記錄管理，藥物追 溯，醫學研究資料的完整保存，醫療保險，或是生物醫療產品的加密識別及 認證。 本課程的教育目標是讓完全不懂區塊鏈的學員，上完課之後理解區塊鏈的智 慧合約，區塊鏈帳本，並有能力製作出基本智能合約。最後輔以實例介紹區 塊鏈技術在生物醫療的應用。 本堂課程學員不需要具有程式語言背景，課程將在電腦教室教學。上課時可 以自己準備的手機，平板或是個人筆記型電腦一起上課。 請輸入課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」至少 5 個, 每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文, 以半形逗點分隔 (必填) Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 分散式數據庫, 去中心化, 數字簽名, 智能合約, 加密貨幣 Decentralized database, Decentralization, Digital signature, Smart contract, Cryptocurrency 一、課程說明 本課程結合區塊鏈基礎教學及實作。 目標是讓完全不懂區塊鏈的學員，上完課之後理解區塊鏈的 智慧合約，區塊鏈帳本，並輔以實例介紹區塊鏈技術在生物 醫療的應用。 哪些學生適合修課: 1. 對區塊鏈有興趣想深入瞭解應用 2. 不需具備程式撰寫經驗及程式語言能力 3. 學生無須自備區塊鏈技術。 4. 想知道關於區塊鏈領域的生物醫療的應用。 5. 想知道如何針對實驗數據進行加密處理 6. 想知道如何針對科研產品建立不可被竄改的產品編號 二、指定用書 自編講義 三、參考書籍 Nakamoto, S. (2008). Bitcoin: A peer-to-peer electronic cash system. Decentralized business review. 四、教學方式 本課程結合區塊鏈基礎教學及實作。 學員將學習如何利用區塊鏈創設出個人專屬之帳本及智能合 約。並學習如何建構無法竄改的資料及資料庫，並瞭解何為 挖礦，及加密貨幣。最後提出該區塊鏈技術應用在生物醫療 領域的實作成果。 本堂課由兩位老師同時授課，在解說區塊鏈技術的時候，會 同時搭配說明該技術在生物醫療領域的應用範圍及限制。理 論課程說明後，會直接到電腦教室進行應用實作。 五、教學進度 周次 日期 時間 講題 授課教師 一 9/4 16:30-20:30 課程介紹及區塊鏈技術簡介 區塊鏈在生物醫療應用概論 趙以選 王慧菁 二 9/11 16:30-20:30 區塊鏈如何建立連結： 雜湊函數運算 雜湊值(Hash 值哈希值) 區塊鏈實地演練： 建立個人帳本，挖礦 生醫科技的金流 趙以選 王慧菁 三 9/18 16:30-20:30 區塊鏈特色： 去中心化，分散式處理，匿名化 簽署及儲存生醫資訊 區塊鏈難以破解的原因： 礦工的責任，區塊鏈加密，驗證交 易 研究資料的驗證與加密 區塊鏈輔助專利保護 趙以選 王慧菁 四 9/25 16:30-20:30 區塊鏈建立個人錢包： 建立錢包，轉帳，區塊鏈錢包交易 智能合約 smart contract： 利用智能合約加密醫療資訊 趙以選 王慧菁 五 10/2 16:30-20:30 區塊鏈建立個人紀錄與儲存 區塊鏈在生物醫療的應用實例 保單，冷鏈運輸，臨床試驗解盲等 趙以選 王慧菁 六 10/09 16:30-20:30 區塊鏈 加密方法 錢包 挖礦成果發表 趙以選 王慧菁 七 10/16 16:30-20:30 區塊鏈 智能合約生物醫療的應用 成果發表 趙以選 王慧菁 八 10/23 16:30-20:30 期末綜合討論/期末考 趙以選 王慧菁 六、成績考核 1. 作業 (40%)：利用區塊鏈製作出生物醫療相關之智能 合約 2. 期末成果發表 (40%)：口頭報告+影片製作，關於區 塊鏈在生物醫療之未來應用方向及想像 3. 課堂參與/小考/出席 (20%) 4. AI 使用規則：本課堂作業開放使用 AI, 但報告內容須 說明哪些部分內容由 AI 產出，是否經過後續人工修 正，且佔比例為多少百分比。原則上 AI 產出報告內 容不得超過 80%。 七、可連結之網頁 位址(相關網頁)

docs.text: 114 學年度第一學期 書報討論 Seminar 分子與細胞生物研究所 學科號：11410LSMC590101 時間：Wed 13:20~14:10 (視修課同學共同決定是否更改為 13:20~15:10) 地點：LS II 生二 206 負責教師：蕭尊先 (thhsiao@mx.nthu.edu.tw ; 分機：35881；清華實驗室 620) 課程目標： 本課程目標為培養學生透過科學論文的選讀及報告，學習如何有效整合、詮釋與表 達論文和實驗的內容，同時於課程內練習如何提出問題、參與討論及評論科學文 章，並藉由報告內容了解現今最新生命科學領域相關的知識及進展。 課程進行方式：  於課程開始前 (8/29) 與負責教師討論後選定報告 paper (須選自發表一年內於生 命科學相關領域之重要期刊兩篇：Impact Factor ≧ 5 或領域排名前 15%，主 題需與生命科學領域相關，和負責教師討論後選擇一篇當作報告 paper)。  報告與評論順序於開學後第一堂課討論或抽籤決定。  學期內每位同學都必須進行演講及當 Commentator 各一次。  報告方式：50 分鐘，30 分鐘演講、20 分鐘回答問題與討論以及 10 分鐘 Commentator 的補充和評論。  Commentator 必須針對報告者表現、論文內容進行評論，並協助補充回答報告 者被提問的問題。  報告者需於一週前將報告論文全文及摘要上傳至eeClass供同學及教師參考。  報告者可和負責教師另約定時間討論報告內容。 評分： 報告表現 (包括演講內容、問題回答、摘要，60%)、同學互評 (10%)、評論表現 (包括當 commentator 及針對論文內容當 reviewer 進行評斷，各 5%，共 10%)、提出問 題與討論 (學期內必須提出至少五個問題或是討論，10%)、出席 (10%)，無故缺席 超過兩次以上則不及格。 加分：學期內，當提出問題或參與討論已滿五次，之後每提問或參與討論一次即加 一分，至多十分。 教學進度 (Syllabus)： 週次 日期 報告人 評論人 題目 1 9/3 課程規則講解、報告順序決定 2 9/10 - 3 9/17 - 4 9/24 5 10/1 6 10/8 7 10/15 8 10/22 9 10/29 10 11/5 - 11 11/12 全校運動大會 (停課一週) 12 11/19 13 11/26 14 12/3 15 12/10 16 12/17 進度以實際選課人數及是否改為每週兩堂課再進行調整 AI 使用規則：有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 學生互評問卷範例： 1. 投影片完成度 (內容是否清晰、整體呈現精緻度) (10 分) 2. 報告內容清晰度 (報告者所表達的內容是否易懂並完整) (10 分) 3. 報告者與聽眾的交流 (報告者在報告時是否有注意報告音量或與聽眾有眼神交 流) (10 分) 4. 回答問題的能力 (報告者是否有充分回答問題或應對) (10 分) 5. 摘要 (內容是否完整清晰) (10 分) 如果今天你是這篇 paper 的 peer-reviewer，請盡你所能地寫下你對這篇 paper 的評 斷：包括簡略描述這篇研究做了什麼、有什麼重大的發現、作者是否針對他們所下 的結論提供足夠的結果來支持？是否有不足的部分可以改進？如何改進？請寫下你 的建議。

docs.text: 114 學年度第一學期 書報討論_分子與細胞生物研究所 科號: 11410LSMC590102 時間: W5 (星期三 13:20-15:20) 地點: LS II 生二 218 負責老師：徐子勝 課程設計與目標： 本課程將著重於分子生物學/醫學相關課題，透過期刊論文的討論，學習生醫領域相關研究的實驗 模式、方法以及當今研究的最新發現，培養學生閱讀、查詢、整合及表達科學文獻的能力。 課程要求及進行方式： • 全採實體上課：若因疫情變化需求，將採用 google meet 進行遠距同步。 • 報告者按照每週預訂的主題，選擇一篇 2024-2025 年發表的期刊論文，作詳盡的報告。 指定期刊: • Journal of cell biology (JCB) • Journal of Experimental Medicine (JEM) • Journal of Clinical Investigation (JCI) • 學生於第一週出席確認報告時間與順序。 • 9/22 (五)前與老師確認報告論文。 • 中文講演；以投影片呈現。 • 報告時間包括 30 分鐘的論文講演，以及 10-15 分鐘的討論及提問。 • 每周兩名同學報告，當週同學互為引言人。 • 每位同學需提出四次 (70 分)，每多提問一次+15 分，至多 100 分 (佔學期成績 30%)；提問者於下 課後在 eeclass 討論區主題串記錄提問內容。若已於課堂上獲得解答，請在問題後面括弧註記已回 答。未在 eeclass 討論區記錄提問內容視同未提問。 • 如有被問問題無法於課堂上回答，必須於演講完一週內於 eeclass 回答問題。 成績: • 評分方式：個人報告佔 70% (老師:50%；同學互評: 20%)、發言提問及討論 30%。 • 扣分: 每次遲到總成績扣 2 分；補報告者總成績扣 20 分。 其他注意事項: 無法如期報告而與其他同學互換，須於報告前兩週完成，並徵得授課老師同意。無故不報告者， 成績為零分。除非老師及其餘同學均同意補作報告，否則不另增補報時段。補報告者另行扣學期總 分 20 分。 週次 日期 報告者 1 9/3 Introduction 2 9/10 準備周 3 9/17 準備周 4 9/24 5 10/1 6 10/8 7 10/15 8 10/22 9 10/29 10 11/05 11 11/12 全校運動大會(停課一天) 12 11/19 13 11/26 14 12/3 15 12/10 16 12/17 期末考周

docs.text: 114.6.24 更新 1 國立清華大學生命科學暨醫學院 專題討論課程規範 【114 學年第 1 學期】 一、宗旨︰邀請國內外優秀學者至本院演講，分享生命科學與醫學 相關研究領域最新發展，並讓學生親炙優秀學者風範。 二、各所負責老師︰ 分生所︰黃千瑜老師、傅化文老師 分醫所︰陳韋靜老師、高茂傑老師 生技所︰林亦凡老師、邱于芯老師 生資所︰林珮君老師、葉善茹老師 系神所︰林郁婷老師 三、講員的邀請以國內外有傑出表現之優秀學者及學界巨擘為佳。 四、學生繳交報告規定︰ 1.學生需繳交 2 份報告，期中及期末各一次，報告評分方式為期 中、期末各佔 30 分，期末報告內容為繳交期中報告後演講內 容為限。博士班學生必須以英文撰寫，碩士班學生報告內容中 英文皆可，報告內容需包含總結及討論，討論內容至少佔 1/4。 2.專討報告禁止抄襲(含網路抄襲、不當翻譯軟體抄襲及互相抄 襲)或不當引用，一經證實報告內容抄襲，則該份報告以零分 計算。並請於報告後註明 Turnitin 線上偵測剽竊系統比對相似 度百分比（Turnitin score= %）及報告字數（Word count= ）。此外，課程助教會使用其它偵測剽竊系統進行相 似度比對。 3.報告繳交規定︰ 114.6.24 更新 2 a.期中報告(114 年 10 月 23 日繳交)，期末報告(114 年 12 月 23 日繳交)，報告遲交扣學期總分 2 分/日。 b.修課同學在繳交期限前將報告電子檔(檔案名稱「學號-姓名」， 檔案格式為.doc)送至「Turnitin 線上偵測剽竊系統」檢查。 4.需繳交文件：「期中及期末報告（完整版，含參考文獻部分）」 與「Turnitin 的檢查結果」，若使用生成式 AI 修改報告，必須 上傳 AI 修改前檔案。 5.演講者的投影片不會公開亦不上傳，請自行做筆記。 五、課程出席規定︰(如因應防疫措施調整規定，會公告在 eeclass) 1.請同學務必坐在定位，點名三次不到者，以不及格論。 2.因故未能出席需請假，應以書面簡述事由後請論文指導教授及 授課教授簽名，並於二日前 (週二下午五點前) 交給所辦公室 林小姐(生命科學二館 205 室)。如有緊急情事無法出席，需於 課後一週內補交請假單，逾期不受理。 六、評分依據︰ 項目 評分 說明 期中及期 末報告 各 30 報告請依格式規定撰寫，報告格式會列入 評量，報告遲交扣學期總分 2 分/日。報告 格式說明檔案請於 eeclass 下載。 口頭或信 件提問 10 1. 評分方式為提問 1 次得學期總分 7 分、2 至 4 次得 8 分、5 至 7 次得 9 分、8 次以 上得 10 分。 2. 需於課後一週內將問題與演講者回答填 114.6.24 更新 3 項目 評分 說明 入線上表單 (連結會公告在 eeclass)，否 則視同未發問。 3. 信件提問僅限於遠距教學課程，提問後 將提問與演講者回答信件轉寄給助教。 出席率 30 1. 遲到、早退、上課看書看報告或課間睡 覺扣學期總分(-2 分/次)、缺席扣學期總 分(-6 分/次)、缺席三次出席分數 0 分。 2. 超過上午 10：10 入場為遲到，上午 10： 20 後入場為缺席。 總分 100 七、演講公告方式︰ 1. 網頁公告︰演講題目、演講日期、演講者姓名等資訊齊備後 於清大生醫學院網頁 https://cls.site.nthu.edu.tw/公告。 2. 紙本公告︰演講日前一週放置於生命科學一、二館公佈欄。 3. E-mail 公告︰演講前一週發佈全院師生 E-mail 通知。 4. 演講公告電子檔和 E-mail 格式依照現有格式製作。 註 1：除該場次演講主持人要求加發「再次通知信件」外，E-mail 公告以演講前一週 通知本院師生一次為主（演講者 CV 僅提供教師參閱）。 八、業務承辦人員︰ 所辦公室林小姐(分機 42463) 課程助教待公告於 eeclass 若要詢問課程相關問題，可透過 eeclass 或課程信箱 114.6.24 更新 4 seminar@life.nthu.edu.tw 2025.6.24 1 College of Life Sciences and Medicine, National Tsing Hua University Guidelines for Colloquium (Fall 2025) 1. Purpose: Invite outstanding scholars from nationwide or abroad to give lectures, share the most updated researches in the life science and medicine related field, and to let students learn the values from outstanding scholars. 2. Teachers: IMCB: Chien-Yu Huang, Tsun-Hsien Hsiao IMM: Wei-Ching Chen, Mou-Chieh Kao IBT: Yi-Fan Lin, Yu-Hsin Chiu IBSB: Pei-Chun Lin, Shan-Ju Yeh ISN: Yu-Ting Lin 3. It is best to invite speakers with outstanding achievements or authority person with credentials on specific topic and knowledge from nationwide or abroad. 4. Requirements for report submission: A. docs.text: Graduate Seminar LSMC790100 Meeting time & place: Friday 13:20-14:10, LS II Room218 Instructor: Huang Chine Yu (黃千瑜) cyhuang@life.nthu.edu.tw; Phone: 35991; Office: NTHU LAB R920 Course Language: English This course is meant to give students organizing presentations and practice speaking in front of a scientific audience. The students will also be engaged participant by analyzing, constructing, and evaluating information presented in scientific journals. This course provides educational experience that enhances graduate students' research and professional skills, encourages critical thinking, and prepares them for successful careers in academia, industry, or other scientific pursuits. General lecture policies: 1. Please send two manuscript options (and indicate which one is preferred) to Dr. Huang Chine Yu by E-mail at least two weeks before your talk. 2. Please upload your final manuscript to the eeClass four days (i.e. Monday) before your scheduled talk. 3. Prepare a one-page abstract and upload to eeClass system before your talk (format provided in below). 4. Organization of the seminar: (1) Commentator introduction: 1 min (2) Presentation 25-30 minutes (3) Questionnaire and discussion 5-10 minutes (4) Final comment 2 minutes. 5. Evaluation: Attendance: 20%; audiences: 40%; Dr. Huang Chien Yu: 40% Choice of manuscript/paper for presentation: 1. Manuscripts published in 2021-2023 2. Topic related to personal research interests is preferred but not restricted. 3. Journal impact factor should above 7 or ranking 20 % (Q1) (Please check Journal Citation Index). Presentation guidelines: 1. Introduction of the senior author 2. Key question to be solved in this study 3. How do authors address their points? 4. Experimental design, approaches, and results 5. Technical support: Explain key experimental approach is necessary 6. Discussion. Such as what do you expect the author will do in the following study. 7. Explain again how this study may contribute to the field of your research interest. 8. Take home message! Format of one-page abstract Speaker: Manuscript title: Author: Journal information&PMID: Abstract Information outline (please answer the following question) 1. What is already known on this subject? 2. What is the scientific question this manuscript is addressing? 3. What are the key findings? 4. How might it impact on clinical practice in the foreseeable future or, what significance does this study have for this field?

docs.text: 國立清華大學 113 學年第 1 學期課程大綱 科號 Course Number LSMM528400 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Class Size 0 中文名稱 Course Title 細胞核膜特論 II 英文名稱 Course English Title Special Topics in Nuclear Envelope II 任課教師 Instructor 李以如 上課時間 Time F7F8 上課教室 Room 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters 細胞核膜是將細胞核中的遺傳物質與細胞質分開的重要構造。失去了此分隔 作用會造成基因體的不穩定，也與許多疾病(例如癌症及早衰症)息息相關。在 這個課程中，將會由同學上台報告近期有關於細胞核膜的科學論文及分享實 驗進度，並帶領討論，學習到細胞在不同狀態下是如何維持細胞核膜的完整 性。 The nuclear envelope separates the genome from the rest of the cell, which is critical to the function and stability of the genome. The loss of nuclear envelope integrity is associated with various diseases including cancers and progeria, etc. In this course, students will learn about how cells establish and maintain the integrity of the nuclear envelope under different conditions via reading, presenting, and discussing journal articles as well as discussing the latest research progress. 請輸入課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」至少 5 個, 每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文, 以半形逗點分隔 (必填) Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 細胞核膜,基因體穩定性,核膜組合,核膜破裂, 膜重組 nuclear envelope, genome stability, nuclear envelope assembly, nuclear envelope rupture, membrane remodeling 一、課程說明 本課程的目標為全面性的了解細胞核膜的組合和重組。學生 需要閱讀相關文獻並上台報告，並且參與討論。 需與授課教師討論後加簽選課。 The objective of this course will be to comprehensively understand the assembly and remodeling of nuclear envelope in the cell. This will be achieved by reading and presenting classic and current literature on nuclear envelope integrity, and discussion in an interactive environment. Permission from the instructor is required. 二、指定用書 無 N/A 三、參考書籍 分子細胞生物學教科書相關章節及期刊文章 Molecular Cell Biology textbook chapters and current literature 四、教學方式 學生們將閱讀期刊文章並輪流上台報告，並參與由指導老師 帶領的討論。 The students will read assigned literature and take turns presenting the paper. The students are also expected to participate in discussions. 五、教學進度 本課程將會包含以下的主題: • 細胞核膜的研究方法 • 當下對核模組合的了解 • 細胞核膜不正常表徵與基因體穩定性 Major topics that will be included in this class: • Methodologies for studying nuclear envelope remodeling. • Current understanding of nuclear envelope assembly and knowledge gaps. • Nuclear atypia and genome stability. 六、成績考核 10% 出席，50% 上台報告，40% 討論。 10% attendance, 50% presentation, 40% discussion. 七、可連結之網頁 位址(相關網頁)

本課程的目標為了解子宮內膜異位症的致病機轉，需要徹底了解其相關科學文獻，透過閱讀和討論學
習
到疾病的病因和進程。
This course will explore the pathogenesis of endometriosis through reading the
scientific literature and discussion to learn the etiology and disease
progression.

需與授課教師討論後加簽選課。
Permission from the instructor is required.

無
None

The teacher will organize the etiology, clinical symptoms, and epidemiology of
endometriosis. Through literature research and discussion with students, the

docs.text: 2025 Autumn Course: Seminar Teacher: Lin, Yu-Chun 林玉俊 Time: Wednesday 13:20~14:10 or 12:30~14:10 Location: LSII, 217 or online 1. Course Description Students in the course need to read original papers and present the related contents in the courses. The goal of this course aims to teach students how to search for academic papers, and the skills of presentation and discussion as well as the latest discoveries in the field of cell biology. AI: unrestricted use with no disclosure required. 2. References The original papers published in prestigious journals including Science, Science series, Nature, Nature series, Cell, Cell series, PNAS, JCB, MCB, MBC, JCS, JBC or any journals with over ten impact factor last three years (2023-2025) in the field of cell biology. 3. Teaching Method Student oral presentation and group discussion 4. Syllabus 1st class-3rd class: The teacher will teach students how to search for and read academic papers and how to presentation it well. 4th class-16th class: One student presents an academic paper every week: ~20 or 25 minutes presentation, ~10 minutes Questions and Answers, ~5 minutes Students’ discussion, ~10 minutes Teacher’s comments Note: Presenters should e-mail their PDF files of academic papers to teacher’s email: ycl@life.nthu.edu.tw two weeks before presentation. The files will be uploaded to NTHU eeclass website (https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw) or line group Presenters should e-mail their PowerPoint files to teacher’s email: ycl@life.nthu.eud.tw three days before presentation. For online presentation, presenter should organize a Google meeting and share the link one day before presentation. Rehearsal: Original score +2 6. Evaluation: Student’s presentation: 60% (Teacher 40% + Students 20%) Other activities including Q&A, attendance, discussion, comment sheet, etc: 40% Presentation and Q&A in English: 105% of original score Note: Unexplained absence: original score -3 Late for 5 minutes will be considered absence.

docs.text: 11410LSMM590102 書報討論(Seminar) 1. Time: Wednesday, 13:20 ~ 14:10, Classroom: LSII-107 2. Instructor:  Mou-Chieh Kao (高茂傑) mckao@life.nthu.edu.tw LS-I 307 ext. 42472 3. Office hours: By appointment only 4. Lecture information website: 清華大學 eeclass 數位學習平台 (https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw/) 5. Course description:  This is a course with a practical purpose, which is intended to allow students to practice their skills in scientific presentation and acquire new knowledge in the field of biological research. The format, presentation layout, and the speaker’s clarity, organization, and devotion will be specifically emphasized. The course will be conducted using a seminar format given by students in the class.  At least one week before the class, the speaker of the week should send the abstract (written by the speaker himself/herself after thoughtful reading. Please include both the English and Chinese versions) in a “WORD” file and the chosen paper in a “PDF” file to the instructor by E-mail. The information collected will be posted on the aforementioned E-learning system for students’ reference. 6. Topic selection: The topic chosen for the presentation should be focused on “Mitochondria.” Any interesting scientific paper related to them (e.g., apoptosis, mitochondrial genetics, proteomics, the function and structure of the component proteins, electron transport chain, the oxidative phosphorylation system, fission and fusion, reactive oxygen species, aging, mitophagy, cancer, pathogen infection, mitochondria-related diseases/therapeutic invention and much more) will be welcome. If you are not quite sure what you have selected, please contact the instructor! 7. Journal selection: The article chosen for presentation should be published in a well-recognized, peer-reviewed journal in the past 3 years (2022~ 2025). The list of the journals includes (but not limited to) Science, Nature, Cell, PNAS, JBC, Mitochondria and EMBO J etc. If you are not quite sure what you have selected, please contact the instructor! 8. Grading  50% evaluation given by the instructors  30% evaluation given by all the students in the class (an evaluation sheet which includes your comment will be given in each class)  20% participation (asking questions!) 2  2 points deduction for being late in attending the class.  5 points deduction for absence from class without notice in advance.  After the seminar, the speaker of the week is welcome (but not necessary) to write a “story, Chinese or English” on this topic. This story will be posted on the E-learning system to share with other students in the class, and the author writing this story will be given extra bonus points!  Students using English to present his/her seminar will be given extra bonus points! 9. 根據本校公布之佈的「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門 課程採取禁止使用，以下為相關的監管機制︰  修讀本門課程之學生應注意本門課不得繳交使用生成式人工智慧所產出的 作業、報告或個人心得。若經查核發現，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針 對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。  修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。 9. Purpose: Invite outstanding scholars from nationwide or abroad to give lectures, share the most updated researches in the life science and medicine related field, and to let students learn the values from outstanding scholars. 2. Teachers: IMCB: Chien-Yu Huang, Tsun-Hsien Hsiao IMM: Wei-Ching Chen, Mou-Chieh Kao IBT: Yi-Fan Lin, Yu-Hsin Chiu IBSB: Pei-Chun Lin, Shan-Ju Yeh ISN: Yu-Ting Lin 3. This course guides students in reading journal articles in the field of

course are:

Participation in discussions.

were used during their oral presentations.

docs.text: 11410LSSN575100 神經心理藥物學 Neuropsychopharmacology Instructor: 張鈞惠(changch@life.nthu.edu.tw) Lectures: Friday 10:10-13:00 @ LSII 218 Textbook: Psychopharmacology: Drugs, the Brain, and Behavior, Fourth Edition (by Meyer, Farrar, Biezonski, Yates) Grading (Total 100%) 1. Take-home essays (25%) 2. Chapter discussion (25%) 3. Literature discussion (total 50%) • Literatures should be selected from Science, Nature, PNAS, Nature Neuroscience, Neuron, Journal of Neuroscience, Molecular Psychiatry, Biological Psychiatry, or Neuropsychopharmacology. • They need to be published after July 1, 2024 • Oral presentation (25%) ~ 35 min presentation + ~15 min discussion (Q&A) • Q&A (5%) Other than the presenter, everyone needs to prepare one critical comment or question regarding the literature during Q&A. • Journal Club style Commentary (in English, 20%) In general, Journal Club articles should have three components: a short overview of the topic and questions addressed in the reviewed paper; a description of the key findings; and a brief discussion of the significance of the paper. Authors should discuss how the highlighted paper expands knowledge about the field:for example, how it fits into an existing or new conceptual model. The Journal Club must offer more than a summary of what was stated in the original article. For example, it might present a broader interpretation of the results in the context of work that the author did not discuss. Presentation of unpublished work or modeling results is not acceptable, however. Journal Clubs may also provide constructive criticism of the work and discussion of more experiments that could be done. But these criticisms and suggestions must be accurate, well- reasoned (preferably with supporting citations), and diplomatic. Inappropriately harsh or glowing reviews will not be considered. Moreover, the focus should be on what was learned, rather than what might have been done differently. Finally, although we expect that authors of Journal Clubs will be working on a topic related to that of the reviewed paper and thus will be familiar with the experimental approach, Journal Clubs should not focus on the author's own work. Journal Club submissions must be concise and should be limited to 1,500 words. They should be written in a style that is understandable to all readers of JNeurosci. Avoid using jargon and unnecessary abbreviations. References are strictly limited to 10, including the highlighted article. A single, original schematic or explanatory figure is acceptable. The figure caption must appear in the main document after the references. Do not duplicate figures that were in the reviewed paper: links to any figures you cite will be placed in the published Journal Club. In the text, refer to the cited figures with the author's name, e.g., “(Author et al., Figure 1A).” A title page must be included with your submission. The title page should include: title; citation of article being reviewed; list of authors and affiliations (graduate students’ affiliations should be listed as the graduate program or department); corresponding author and contact information (address, phone, and email address); abbreviated title; name, affiliation, and email address of mentor; and additional acknowledgments. docs.text:
一、課程說明(Course Description)
行政法是法律體系中重要的一支。在難以勝數的現存法規中，有很大部分屬於行政法規，規制
吾人生活的各個層面。因此，在這門課當中所學習的許多基本概念、體系與方法，將有助於未來從事
法律工作乃至法律生活，必然會面對到的各種行政法規之解釋、適用，以及行政法律關係之理解與爭
端之解決。
本課程遵循行政法總論之一般體系，分為行政法之理論、行政組織法、行政作用法、行政救濟
法等四大部分。其中本學期（上學期）之進度，主要涵蓋前二大部分，另依進度可能進入第三部分行
政作用法的部分內容，其餘則留待留待下學期探討。在行政法之理論部分，本課程將從權力分立之觀
點開始，再進入行政與行政法概念之認識。其後介紹行政法之法源、行政法之一般法律原則、行政之
羈束性與自由性、行政法之解釋適用、行政法之法律關係等重要主題。期盼能為同學往後行政法之理
解，建立良好的基礎。在行政組織法部分，則包含行政組織之型態、行政組織之權限、中央與地方行
政組織、公務員法、公物等項目。期盼能協助同學初步認識行政組織相關法律議題。
