docs.text: 「普通物理實驗」課程大綱 Syllabus of General Physics Laboratory 課程網站(Website)：國立清華大學普通物理實驗室 一、 課程說明： 本課程除透過實驗驗證普通物理課程中所學習到的各種物理定律和物理現象外，並 訓練學生熟悉實驗的測量方法和操作技術，以及學習如何解決實驗時所遭遇的各種困難 與建立實驗數據分析的能力。 上學期主要著重在基本度量、運動學、力學、熱力學和力學波動等古典物理學領域 的基本物理實驗，下學期則在電學、磁學、電磁學、基本電子儀表之工作原理、電路學和 光學等基礎物理實驗的學習。同時藉由實驗的實作，培養學生對實驗研究應有的嚴謹態 度和好奇好學的精神，使同學能夠熟用各種基本量測工具、相關儀器及器材。此外，在 課程中亦安排一些無法讓全部學生同時實作的物理演示實驗和物理演示觀摩影片，以強 化課程的內涵和提升學生的學習興趣和範圍。 二、 課程目的： 1.驗證並了解基本物理定律和現象。 2.熟悉各種基本量測工具、儀器及器材，並培養愛護儀器及正確使用儀器的方法和態 度。 3.強化實驗的基本技能。 4.學習實驗數據擷取、處理與分析的能力，加強使用工程計算機及電腦數據分析軟體 之應用能力，如學習熟用 Microsoft Office 的 Excel 試算軟體 。 5.訓練撰寫實驗報告和簡報的能力，特別是書面文字的撰寫、圖表和簡報製作的技 巧，並培育上台簡報的技巧和能力。學習熟用 MS word 文書處理軟體和 MS power point 簡報軟體。 6.加強學生對物理定理的深入瞭解、歷史發展和技術演變的過程及在日常生活上的應 用原理和操作。 7.訓練學生發掘問題、解決問題和思考分析，並強化創造力的啟發與靈活運用。 8.培養學生面對科學實驗與研究應有的好奇心和嚴謹態度，與重視團隊合作的實驗精 神和態度。 三、實驗單元： 上下學期共有 17 個與運動學、力學、熱力學、力學波動、電學、磁學和近代物理有關 的典型物理實驗單元及六個相關的物理演示實驗: 上學期實驗如下： 實驗 1 基本度量與數據分析 (Fundamental Measurements and Data Analysis) 實驗 2 運動軌跡和相關物理量測量 (Newton's Second Law) 實驗 3 向心力實驗(Centripetal Force) 實驗 4 演示實驗 A：運動學與力學篇 (Demonstration A: Kinetics and Mechanics) 實驗 5 轉動慣量(Rotational Inertia) 實驗 6 碰撞運動與守恆定律 (Collision Motions and Laws of Conservation) 實驗 7 一維與二維力學振盪及駐波實驗 (Mechanical Oscillation & Standing Waves) 實驗 8 演示實驗 B：轉動力學篇 (Demonstration B:Rotation Dynamics) 實驗 9 簡諧運動 (Simple Harmonic Motion) 實驗 10 熱力學實驗 (Thermodynamics) 實驗 11 演示實驗 C：力學波動篇與熱力學篇 (Demonstration C: Mechanical Waves and Thermodynamics) 四、課程進度 上課方式採實驗講解、統一實作的典型實驗、自由探索演示實驗和影片觀摩等 四種 方式，每一班級的課程進度由普物實驗課程小組統一規劃，本學年度上學期的實驗 輪班表見實驗室課程網站公告。 五、指定用書、參考資料和補充資料 (1) 典型物理實驗： 1. 實驗講義、講解簡報和參考資料見普物實驗網站 (2) 物理演示實驗與影片觀摩： 六、教學方式上課方式採實驗課堂講解、統一的典型實驗、自由探索演示實驗和影片觀摩等 四種方式，以及適時地安排校外學者來校進行演示教學演講或校外觀摩活動： (1) 課堂講解：講解實驗原理及實驗進行的方法、步驟和注意事項。 (2) 典型物理實驗：主要實驗目的和內容為驗證普物課堂上所學的物理定律和現象，實 驗過程採兩人一組，共用一套實驗器材，每一實驗共備有 30 套設備。實驗時，按實驗 課本中的實驗步驟進行一系列有系統的數據測量，實驗後每位同學自行 根據所測得 的實驗數據進行數據分析和物理原理的比較與驗證分析。部份修課 人數超過 60 人 的班級，將會有部份同學是三人一組。 (3) 物理演示實驗與影片觀摩：同學不分組，演示實驗室中將擺置多種不同的物理演示 教具，大部份的教具僅一套，故請小心使用，避免破壞，以免後來學習的同學無法 使用。學生抵達實驗室後，先由講師或助教對每一物理演示展品作一簡單扼要的講 解，然後才讓學生自由探索每一展示教具工作原理和設計時所使用的物理原理。並 要求學生回去後，針對每一演示教具自行查詢相關資料，探索較具的工作詳細原理， 並撰寫探索報告，此演示報告的評分視為一般的實驗報告。 (4) 物理演示百科 DVD 影片的演示實驗觀摩：由講師和助教適當地安插於實驗課程、實 驗講解課中進行，亦可安排學生自行觀看後，製作簡報，上台報告。 七、實驗操作： 1. 實驗操作時，原則上採兩人一組，分組進行實驗。修課人數超過 60 人的班級，會有 部份同學是三人一組。 2. 實驗時，同學須自備筆電，實驗時記錄實驗數據用；並高度建議每次實驗應備有數位 相機或數位攝影機，以利實驗裝置和圖形 的存取。 3. 每位學生需自己撰寫，並繳交自己的實驗預報、結報和各式報告。 4. 實驗開始前，同學需先繳交實驗預習報告及前一次實驗的結報。 5. 任課教師和助教得以根據預習報告和講解課時的授課內容進行隨堂小考。 6. 實驗結束前，學生需完成數據的初步處理(先以計算機處理)及初步作圖(先繪於方格 紙上)，經任課教師或助教檢查無誤後，並請助教於數據資料上簽名後，才算完成實驗， 方可離開實驗室。 7. 實驗所得數據需經電腦的 EXCEL 或相關數據分析及作圖軟體處理、分析和作圖。 8. 期末將以操作考及筆試評核學生的實驗學習成果。 八、 成績計算 由任課教師和助教於學期末依下列各項成績而定。 1. 實驗報告成績：含實驗預報和結報，以及演示實驗探索報告和演示實驗影片觀摩報 告，一學期共 11~12 份報告。實驗報告成績至少佔學期成績的 70%。 2. 平時的實驗精神和態度。 3. 筆試成績：如預習考、隨堂考、期中考、期末考等各種筆試。 4. 實驗操作考成績。 5. 其他：期末需繳交本學期所有實驗報告之電子檔和書面裝訂本，需含封面、校外教 學或參觀活動之報告等等。 九、上課規定 1.請準時到堂上課和實驗，並簽到(請勿代簽)。 2.繳交實驗預報及上次實驗的結報，結報請隔週即繳交。即使隔週為講解課，亦得繳 交前一週的實驗結報，不接受遲交之報告。 3.實驗課時請務必攜帶自己的實驗講義和筆電。 4.實驗流程：老師和助教先講解實驗大綱和注意事項，同學開始做實驗，整理數據， 實驗數據檢查。 5.請教師和助教檢查數據：實驗數據未經教師和助教認核簽名前，請不要先收儀器。 6.依規定收拾儀器、整理實驗桌，清除垃圾後，請助教檢查，始可簽退，並離開實驗 室。 7.實驗室內禁止帶入食物及飲食，若需飲食，請至實驗室外享用。

docs.name: 普通物理實驗一
docs.text: 「普通物理實驗」課程大綱 Syllabus of General Physics Laboratory 課程網站(Website)：國立清華大學普通物理實驗室 一、 課程說明： 本課程除透過實驗驗證普通物理課程中所學習到的各種物理定律和物理現象外，並 訓練學生熟悉實驗的測量方法和操作技術，以及學習如何解決實驗時所遭遇的各種困難 與建立實驗數據分析的能力。 上學期主要著重在基本度量、運動學、力學、熱力學和力學波動等古典物理學領域 的基本物理實驗，下學期則在電學、磁學、電磁學、基本電子儀表之工作原理、電路學和 光學等基礎物理實驗的學習。同時藉由實驗的實作，培養學生對實驗研究應有的嚴謹態 度和好奇好學的精神，使同學能夠熟用各種基本量測工具、相關儀器及器材。此外，在 課程中亦安排一些無法讓全部學生同時實作的物理演示實驗和物理演示觀摩影片，以強 化課程的內涵和提升學生的學習興趣和範圍。 二、 課程目的： 1.驗證並了解基本物理定律和現象。 2.熟悉各種基本量測工具、儀器及器材，並培養愛護儀器及正確使用儀器的方法和態 度。 3.強化實驗的基本技能。 4.學習實驗數據擷取、處理與分析的能力，加強使用工程計算機及電腦數據分析軟體 之應用能力，如學習熟用 Microsoft Office 的 Excel 試算軟體 。 5.訓練撰寫實驗報告和簡報的能力，特別是書面文字的撰寫、圖表和簡報製作的技 巧，並培育上台簡報的技巧和能力。學習熟用 MS word 文書處理軟體和 MS power point 簡報軟體。 6.加強學生對物理定理的深入瞭解、歷史發展和技術演變的過程及在日常生活上的應 用原理和操作。 7.訓練學生發掘問題、解決問題和思考分析，並強化創造力的啟發與靈活運用。 8.培養學生面對科學實驗與研究應有的好奇心和嚴謹態度，與重視團隊合作的實驗精 神和態度。 三、實驗單元： 上下學期共有 17 個與運動學、力學、熱力學、力學波動、電學、磁學和近代物理有關 的典型物理實驗單元及六個相關的物理演示實驗: 上學期實驗如下： 實驗 1 基本度量與數據分析 (Fundamental Measurements and Data Analysis) 實驗 2 運動軌跡和相關物理量測量 (Newton's Second Law) 實驗 3 向心力實驗(Centripetal Force) 實驗 4 演示實驗 A：運動學與力學篇 (Demonstration A: Kinetics and Mechanics) 實驗 5 轉動慣量(Rotational Inertia) 實驗 6 碰撞運動與守恆定律 (Collision Motions and Laws of Conservation) 實驗 7 一維與二維力學振盪及駐波實驗 (Mechanical Oscillation & Standing Waves) 實驗 8 演示實驗 B：轉動力學篇 (Demonstration B:Rotation Dynamics) 實驗 9 簡諧運動 (Simple Harmonic Motion) 實驗 10 熱力學實驗 (Thermodynamics) 實驗 11 演示實驗 C：力學波動篇與熱力學篇 (Demonstration C: Mechanical Waves and Thermodynamics) 四、課程進度 上課方式採實驗講解、統一實作的典型實驗、自由探索演示實驗和影片觀摩等 四種 方式，每一班級的課程進度由普物實驗課程小組統一規劃，本學年度上學期的實驗 輪班表見實驗室課程網站公告。 五、指定用書、參考資料和補充資料 (1) 典型物理實驗： 1. 實驗講義、講解簡報和參考資料見普物實驗網站 (2) 物理演示實驗與影片觀摩： 六、教學方式上課方式採實驗課堂講解、統一的典型實驗、自由探索演示實驗和影片觀摩等 四種方式，以及適時地安排校外學者來校進行演示教學演講或校外觀摩活動： (1) 課堂講解：講解實驗原理及實驗進行的方法、步驟和注意事項。 (2) 典型物理實驗：主要實驗目的和內容為驗證普物課堂上所學的物理定律和現象，實 驗過程採兩人一組，共用一套實驗器材，每一實驗共備有 30 套設備。實驗時，按實驗 課本中的實驗步驟進行一系列有系統的數據測量，實驗後每位同學自行 根據所測得 的實驗數據進行數據分析和物理原理的比較與驗證分析。部份修課 人數超過 60 人 的班級，將會有部份同學是三人一組。 (3) 物理演示實驗與影片觀摩：同學不分組，演示實驗室中將擺置多種不同的物理演示 教具，大部份的教具僅一套，故請小心使用，避免破壞，以免後來學習的同學無法 使用。學生抵達實驗室後，先由講師或助教對每一物理演示展品作一簡單扼要的講 解，然後才讓學生自由探索每一展示教具工作原理和設計時所使用的物理原理。並 要求學生回去後，針對每一演示教具自行查詢相關資料，探索較具的工作詳細原理， 並撰寫探索報告，此演示報告的評分視為一般的實驗報告。 (4) 物理演示百科 DVD 影片的演示實驗觀摩：由講師和助教適當地安插於實驗課程、實 驗講解課中進行，亦可安排學生自行觀看後，製作簡報，上台報告。 七、實驗操作： 1. 實驗操作時，原則上採兩人一組，分組進行實驗。修課人數超過 60 人的班級，會有 部份同學是三人一組。 2. 實驗時，同學須自備筆電，實驗時記錄實驗數據用；並高度建議每次實驗應備有數位 相機或數位攝影機，以利實驗裝置和圖形 的存取。 3. 每位學生需自己撰寫，並繳交自己的實驗預報、結報和各式報告。 4. 實驗開始前，同學需先繳交實驗預習報告及前一次實驗的結報。 5. 任課教師和助教得以根據預習報告和講解課時的授課內容進行隨堂小考。 6. 實驗結束前，學生需完成數據的初步處理(先以計算機處理)及初步作圖(先繪於方格 紙上)，經任課教師或助教檢查無誤後，並請助教於數據資料上簽名後，才算完成實驗， 方可離開實驗室。 7. 實驗所得數據需經電腦的 EXCEL 或相關數據分析及作圖軟體處理、分析和作圖。 8. 期末將以操作考及筆試評核學生的實驗學習成果。 八、 成績計算 由任課教師和助教於學期末依下列各項成績而定。 1. 實驗報告成績：含實驗預報和結報，以及演示實驗探索報告和演示實驗影片觀摩報 告，一學期共 11~12 份報告。實驗報告成績至少佔學期成績的 70%。 2. 平時的實驗精神和態度。 3. 3.實驗課時請務必攜帶自己的實驗講義和筆電。 4.實驗流程：老師和助教先講解實驗大綱和注意事項，同學開始做實驗，整理數據， 實驗數據檢查。 5.請教師和助教檢查數據：實驗數據未經教師和助教認核簽名前，請不要先收儀器。 6.依規定收拾儀器、整理實驗桌，清除垃圾後，請助教檢查，始可簽退，並離開實驗 室。 7.實驗室內禁止帶入食物及飲食，若需飲食，請至實驗室外享用。

實驗所得數據需經電腦的 EXCEL 或相關數據分析及作圖軟體處理、分析和作圖。 8. 期末將以操作考及筆試評核學生的實驗學習成果。 八、 成績計算 由任課教師和助教於學期末依下列各項成績而定。 1. 實驗報告成績：含實驗預報和結報，以及演示實驗探索報告和演示實驗影片觀摩報 告，一學期共 11~12 份報告。實驗報告成績至少佔學期成績的 70%。 2. 平時的實驗精神和態度。 3. 筆試成績：如預習考、隨堂考、期中考、期末考等各種筆試。 4. 實驗操作考成績。 5. 其他：期末需繳交本學期所有實驗報告之電子檔和書面裝訂本，需含封面、校外教 學或參觀活動之報告等等。 九、上課規定 1.請準時到堂上課和實驗，並簽到(請勿代簽)。 2.繳交實驗預報及上次實驗的結報，結報請隔週即繳交。即使隔週為講解課，亦得繳 交前一週的實驗結報，不接受遲交之報告。 3.實驗課時請務必攜帶自己的實驗講義和筆電。 4.實驗流程：老師和助教先講解實驗大綱和注意事項，同學開始做實驗，整理數據， 實驗數據檢查。 5.請教師和助教檢查數據：實驗數據未經教師和助教認核簽名前，請不要先收儀器。 6.依規定收拾儀器、整理實驗桌，清除垃圾後，請助教檢查，始可簽退，並離開實驗 室。 7.實驗室內禁止帶入食物及飲食，若需飲食，請至實驗室外享用。

Our primary focus is to provide a solid foundation of basic knowledge through various approaches, including in-class lectures, office hours, TA sessions, homework, and exams. To enhance and support student learning for these fundamental knowledge in science, we will utilize mathematical tools such as calculus and differential equations etc. To personalize the content for each student, we will introduce the application of Artificial Intelligence as a personal TA, called Little TAI, for self-study, homework, and mini- project preparation. This will allow students to receive tailored assistance and guidance. We believe that highly motivated and self-disciplined students will excel in this class. However, we hope even students with less motivation will still have the opportunity to learn important methods and basic knowledge, which could prepare them better for their future studies and careers. 2/2 三、指定用書與參考書(Textbook and References) R.A. docs.text:
Classical Mechanics (I) 2025 Fall

* Course Meeting Times: W3W4F3

* Prerequisite:
It is strongly recommended that you complete Caculas I and II before
enrolling in this course.

This 2-semester course in Classical Mechanics offers a comprehensive exploration
of dynamical systems, spanning from Newtonian Mechanics to Lagrangian and
Hamiltonian dynamics. Students delve into the principles governing simple and
complex systems, mastering foundational concepts like Virtual Work and
Conservation Laws. Through classical examples such as oscillations and central
forces, this course bridges the gap between undergraduate and graduate physics
training, offering a glimpse into the profound beauty and universal principles
of modern physics.

* 課程用書: 筆記 及 參考書目1 為主

* 參考書目:
1. "Classical Dynamics of Particles and Systems" by S. T. Thornton and J. B.
Marion
2. "Analytical Mechanics" by L. N. Hand and J. D. Finch
3. "Mechanics" by L. D. Landau and M. Lifshitz

* TA: To be announced

* Subjects explored over the span of these two semesters include:

Kinematics Mathematical description of motion
Newtonian Mechanics
Oscillations and Chaotic Motions
Calculus of Variations and action principle
Hamilton's principle and the Lagragian/Hamiltonian dynamics
Gravitation and Central-Force Motion
Dynamics of a system of particles
Dynamics of rigid bodies
Coupled oscillations: perturbation and diagonalization
Hamiltonian mechanics:
Canonical transformations
Hamilton-Jacobi theory
Poisson brackets and symmetries
Lagrangian and Hamiltonian formulations for continuous systems and fields
Special relativity
... and more ( depending on time )

* 成績考核: Problem sets, quiz during classtime, mid-term examination, and
final examination

* Problem sets are essential for this course, aiding in a profound understanding
of the material and the development of crucial analytical skills. While
collaboration is encouraged, it's imperative that you tackle each problem
independently before discussing it with peers. Submitted solutions must be your
own original work to avoid plagiarism, which is easily identifiable and
constitutes a serious offense.

Problem sets are normally posted on the EEClass course website and will be due
in one week.
Any late problem set [[ will not be accepted]].

* 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁 EEClass

utilize AI to enhance your learning.

英語授課(EMI計畫)

I. Course Description

General Astronomy (I) is aimed at undergraduate/beginner’s level. Students from
all colleges are welcome. Although a general college physics background is
helpful, this course will be self-contained. It will provide students a general
introduction to astronomy, as might be helpful in the modern world.
To complete the introductory course, students are encouraged to take the course
General Astronomy (II) (PHYS242000) afterwards. Students with further interest
may then take other astronomy and astrophysics courses at junior and senior
levels and those offered by the Institute of Astronomy.

This course starts with a journey from our Earth to the whole Universe as we
know
today. We will introduce celestial coordinate systems and the face of the sky as
we see from the Earth. This concludes Part 1 of this course, which is practical
in our daily life and provides a first-time encounter with terminology and
conventions in astronomy.

Part 2 includes brief reviews of planet motion and Newtonian gravity, properties
of EM waves and atomic spectra, various observational tools and techniques.

Part 3 is the core of this course and will take the second half of the whole
lecture time. From stellar spectral classification, variable stars, giant stars,
the solar system, and planets. Our approach will be observation-oriented with
discussion of interpretations.

This course is expected to end with students left longing for knowing more about
the Galaxy and beyond.

Course Pages:
Google Classroom The course will go with classroom lectures. Discussion in
classroom is very much encouraged. There are no midterms and/or finals. We will
quizzes either every week or bi-weekly.

Office Hours: tentative – Tuesdays 14:00 – 15:00. Most of the time after class,
or by appointment, or post your questions in the Google Classroom.

II. Text books

The main textbook is the same as previous general astronomy courses: Author:
Geller, Freedman, & Kaufmann title: Universe, 11th edition (2019) Publisher:
W.
H. Freeman ISBN-13: 978-1319039448 ISBN-
10: 1319039448

III. References

Other textbooks at an introductory level:
R26; Seeds & Backman: ’Foundations of Astronomy’
R26; Kaler: ’Astronomy!’
R26; Chaisson & McMillan: ’Astronomy Today’
R26; Zeilik: ’Astronomy: the Evolving Universe’
R26; Arny & Schneider: ’Explorations, An Introduction to Astronomy’
Some textbooks which are ’more astrophysical’:
R26; Shu: ’The Physical Universe – An Introduction to Astronomy’
R26; Carroll & Ostlie: ’An Introduction to Modern Astrophysics’
R26; Bowers & Deeming: ’Astrophysics’
A fundamental, practical textbook for observations is by Birney: ’Observational
Astronomy’ A more
advanced book concerning observations and astrophysics is by Smith:
’Observational Astrophysics’

IV. Course schedule

Introduction and overview
Coordinate systems
Telescopes and magnitude systems
Sun, Earth Moon
Planets
Gravity and planetary motion
EM spectrum
Astronomy observations
Stars
Solar system
Exoplanets and astrobiology

V. Evaluation
80% based on quizzes where questions are based on voluntary assignments
(videos,
online lectures) and previous lecture. 20% is based on
participations/attendance.

There are NO make-up quizzes, and no make-up exams.

VI. Teaching methods

The course will be mainly based on lectures. It also includes some
discussions
where student participations will be crucial. Some parts of the class will be
focused on quizzes.

There are no homeworks, midterms, and/or final exams.

VII. Leaves and regulations

a. Attendance: Students are allowed to have 3--4 leaves (including sick leave,
funeral, business, etc.) *with information/these requests are communicated
clearly to the TAs or instructors*. Students will fail the course if they have
less than 8 quizzes recorded or have more than 5 absences. You are welcome to
come in late as long as you can make it to the quiz.

This course covers three core technical aspects of experimental physics: (1)
fundamental electronics and applications of operational amplifiers, (2) principles
and methods of data acquisition, and (3) programming with graphical control software
such as LabVIEW. In the final part of the course, students will undertake a project
to integrate these three fundamental skills by designing and implementing a custom-
built system for experimental control and measurement.

docs.text: National Tsing Hua University / Department of Physics / PHYS3080 應用電子學實驗 113 上學期 課程大綱 教師： 童世光 Office: 413, E-mail: zekest@phys.nthu.edu.tw 上課時間: Thursday, 上課地點: 物506 課程目標與內容 著重電子電路實作訓練，驗證電子學課本之知識。實驗內容涵蓋雙 極性接面電晶體（BJT）之特性，BJT 偏壓電路，BJT 放大器，場效 電晶體特性、運算放大器（OP）的特性，OP 之頻率響應，OP 之應 用（加法、積分、微分、低通濾波與高通濾波），精密溫控器，精 密電流供應器，雙向電流放大器。 課程說明 • 實驗課時，不得缺席、遲到、瞌睡或進行與實驗無關的工作。助 教將嚴格考核實驗課的表現。無法出席實驗課必須事先請假並核 准。任何一次實驗課無故缺席或未事先核准，學期成績扣10 分。 • 實驗課前先預習，但無須繳交預習報告。 • 實驗課兩位同學一組。實驗數據須助教簽可後方可結束實驗。 • 每次實驗課的二個實驗必須由同組的兩位同學分別撰寫。撰寫報 告重點如下： (1) 文字清晰、工整。報告中應有封面、原始數據或其影本、數據 的詳細分析過程、實驗結果與理論的比較、討論、心得與總結。 (2) 實驗結果一目瞭然(列表或作圖)，表達不失真(電腦繪圖)，標 示誤差。 (3) 對數據的評論及說明評論的理由(例如誤差的由來)。根據實驗 結果提出不同或相同於實驗原理的觀點。以實驗結果作進一步的預 測或推論。實驗中觀察到不預期現象的解釋。建議或新的構想。 • 實驗報告抄襲者與配合者皆依校規懲處。 AI 使用規則 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式AI於課程產出 成績計算 實驗課表現 40%，實驗報告 60% 參考書籍 1. 電子學實驗 陳瓊興、陳竹正 著 2. docs.text:
這是清華大學物理系大學部的選修課程，本課程的目的是為學生提供常用於解決物理問題的數值方法的基本知識和技

能，Python是本課程主要使用的程式語言，本課程適合具備Python基本程式能力的學生。

數值方法和程式語言最佳的學習方式就是實作，因此課堂上將結合數值方法的概念講解和課堂中的實作練習，另外也

透過作業與期末報告來增加實作與應用的練習。

評分標準：

-- 課堂實作（30%）

-- 作業（40%）

-- Term project（30%）

Term project旨在讓學生將本課所學的數值方法應用於解決一個物理問題。Term project將基於問題的創新性與複雜

性（10%）、程式的完成度（10%）以及期末口頭報告（每人約15分鐘，10%）進行評分。

課程暫定主題：

-- Overview of the course, programming basics and tools

-- Introduction to numerical analyses (stability, convergence, errors)

-- Solutions of equations in one variable (bisection method, Newton’s method)

-- Interpolation

-- Numerical differentiation and integration

-- Monte Carlo methods

-- Linear systems and matrix algebra

-- ODEs: initial value problems, boundary value problems

-- PDEs: hyperbolic equations, elliptic equations

參考書目：

1. "Numerical Recipe" by Press, W. H. (http://www.nr.com)

2. "Scientific Computing: An Introductory Survey" by Michael Heath

3. “Numerical Analysis” by Burden, R. and Faires, J. D.

4. "Introduction to Computational Astrophysical Hydrodynamics" by Zingale, M. (https://github.com/python-

hydro/hydro_examples)

5. “A student’s Guide to Numerical Methods” by Ian H. Hutchinson

(https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/students-guide-to-numerical-

methods/06C4F9638E645EC28567DD4BDCEDD875)

6. “Computational Physics: Problem Solving with Computers, 2nd Edition” by R. Landau

(https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/book/10.1002/9783527618835)

AI policy：

Conditionally open. Provided that there are many AI tools available for more efficient programming, we will

partially incorporate some of them into the course and discuss the best practices. For course outputs

(exercises/homework/project), please explicitly specify how the AI tools are used. No credits will be given in

case of violation of the AI policy and course guidelines discussed at the beginning of the semester.

docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 數位智慧科技實作與程式控制 (Implementation and Program Coding of Digital Smart Technology) 科 號 11410PHYS370000 組別 學 分 3 人數限制 70 人 上 課 時 間 週一 第 A, B, C 節 教 室 普通物理實驗室 130 室 科目中文名稱 數位智慧科技實作與程式控制 科目英文名稱 Implementation and Program Coding of Digital Smart Technology 任 課 教 師 戴明鳳 擋 修 科 目 無 擋修分數 無 請勾選 此科目對應之系所課程規畫所欲培養之核心能力 Core capability to be cultivated by this course 權重（百分比） Percentage 自我瞭解與溝通表達 Self-awareness, expressions & communication % 邏輯推理與批判思考能力 Logical reasoning & critical thinking20 % 科學思維與反思 Scientific thinking & reflection30 % 藝術與人文涵養 Aesthetic & humanistic literacy20 % 資訊科技與媒體素養 Information technology & media literacy30 % 多元觀點與社會實踐 Diverse views & social practices % 一、課程說明 邁入 21 世紀數位科技的紀元，師生們在科學實驗教學上有更多數位 科技的教學媒介與技術可以選用，近日 AI 與 ChatGPT 快速竄紅讓科學 傳遞與教育推廣工作有了全新的平台與詮釋方法。但傳統科學實驗中， 每一實驗步驟、每一環節的講究，都須建立在學生對科學的基本原理、定 律和概念有相當程度的理解，並透過實務操作實驗培養學生具備實驗技 能和邏輯判斷、測量技術和數據分析的能力。然而，這些技能的養成是無 法被 AI 和 ChatGPT 全然取代的。 若邏輯推理的養成與實驗技能的實務操作也都交給 AI 代勞，則在不 久的未來恐對人腦與手巧的退化產生一定的風險，也勢必對未來人類科 學的發展產生不確定性的影響。 如何結合現代科技帶來的便利與精確性，減少實驗上不必要的錯誤， 提升學生的學習興趣與科學素養的養成，但卻依舊能保持最重要的實驗 探究精神?本課程透過機電整合、數位科技與程式設計的相輔相成，與老 師們分享如何在數位時代中仍能保有傳統的實驗精隨。 21 世紀互動科技的成長不僅快速且高度趨向普及化，並以各種形式 融入人類的日常生活中，也使能研發新科技互動科技產品已不再需侷限 於少數具有特殊專業背景知識的群組才能研發製作。故本課程目的在讓 沒有程式基礎、數位控制、微電腦、電子 DIY、交互裝置與電子電路等 等基礎背景的學生，能夠透過本課程規劃的跨領域實作教案與進階專案 的設計與實作，建立學生自我實作組裝數位電子電路自動控制器件、設 計與撰寫自動控制程式的技能和自信心，並引導具有 STEAM 的理念和 設計能力。近年來我們團隊陸續完成許多項運用 Arduino 及智慧型手機 進行科學實驗的設計研發，並將之引入本校大學普物實驗課程內使用。 本課程希望將此研發成果也能分享給校內學生，將透過讓學生自己親自 動手組裝由簡入繁、由淺入深的各種實用且具趣味探究的電子電路，及 自己撰寫自動控制程式以控制 Arduino 微控制板和各種感測元件的連結， 以及比較不同電路接法間的差異比較，以期同學生也能實質理解電路中 各式電子元件的功能、學習認識各種電子電路元件規格差異與比較、如 何將電子電路元件善用於適當的地方、、等等。進而能夠自行設計具創意 且實用的智慧型生活電子器具。 期望研習結束，同學們可善用研習所學習到的各種技能，進行其他 軟、硬體結合後，即可自製多種不同的電子偵測儀器，以期發揮更多功 能，故本次課程請自備筆電。(平板電腦和 Chrome 筆電不適合) 二、指定用書 無指定用書，採用自行編製的課程簡報檔。 需自備筆記型電腦(課程中無法提供筆電借用) 三、上課器材 本課程以課堂上現場實作及當場撰寫程式為主，故每堂課都會使用到筆電、 相關感測器模組與電子設備。 但學校無補助此課程的實作費用，故同學可自行購買或由跨領域科學教育 中心協助團購所需的電子材料與模組。 四、教學方式 1. 簡報授課 2. 課堂中實作 3. 程式設計與編寫 五、教學進度 請參見下列課程主題表 六、成績考核 以下為暫訂標準，開課後會依實際修課學生的系級別、人數與學生已有的 相關之知識背景和未來應用的潛力與現場授課時的學習成效做更適性的調 整。以下比例為暫訂參考： 1. 課堂實作：20% 2. 課後作業： 20 % 3. 期中實作報告：0-20 % 4. 期末實作報告與成品：40-60 % 七、講義位址 1. 本課程校方之數位教學網站（開課後才會有） 八、參考書籍 /網頁 1. https://sites.google.com/site/csjhmaker/arduino-ji-chu/arduino-ru-men 2. http://coopermaa2nd.blogspot.com/2011/05/arduino.html 3. http://yehnan.blogspot.com/search/label/Arduino%E6%96%87%E7%AB% docs.text:
一、課程說明(Course Description)

相對論導論(一)(二)為介紹廣義相對論的一門課程. 適合大三（含）

以上及研究所同學. 第一學期著重廣義相對論理論之建立. 雖然

狹義相對論開始, 但以為廣義相對論做準備為目的. 狹義相對論的

基礎極為重要. 建議同學務必先自行複習狹義相對論,

如普物,理論力學,電磁學書中的狹義相對論.

第二學期著重廣義相對論之應用. 如: 重力波,黑洞,宇宙論.

Reading Guideline Before Lectures:

This course is on General Relativity. Although the course begins with a review on

Special Relativity, it adopts the geometric approach for the preparation for General Relativity.

It assumes that you are familiar with:

1. Special Relativity, especially in the four-dimensional form,

2. Electromagnetism in the four-dimensional form,

3. Electromagnetism in Gaussian units.

If you are not familiar with the above subjects, you need to review or study them

before the class begins in September, in order to catch up with the lectures.

The suggested references are:

‧ M. A. Heald & J. B. Marion: Classical Electromagnetic Radiation (3rd ed.), Chapter 14.

‧ J. D. Jackson: Classical Electrodynamics, Chapters 11, 12.

The lectures are in Chinese.

二、指定用書(Text Books)

B. F. Schutz, "A First Course in General Relativity" (2nd ed., Cambridge University Press).

三、參考書籍(References)

1. A. Einstein, "The Principle of Relativity" (1952, Dover).

2. A. Einstein, "The Meaning of Relativity" (1922).

3. C. W. Misner, K. S. Thorne, and J. A. Wheeler, "Gravitation" (1973)

4. S. Weinberg, "Gravitation and Cosmology" (1972)

5. L. D. Landau and E. M. Lifshitz, "The Classical Theory of Fields"

6. M.P. Hobson, G. Efstathiou, and A.N. Lasenby, "General Relativity" (2006)

四、教學方式(Teaching Method)

Lecture in Chinese

五、教學進度(Syllabus)

作業 (可能加考試, 視情況而定）

Homework (possibly + exam)

● 課程說明(Course Description)
Teach the basic knowledge of elementary particle physics. Introduce the historical
developments and current research status, for example, the structure of Standard
Model, various dark matter candidates, how to search new particles at collider,
and other particle phenomenology. The students can learn the fundamental
computations of particle processes, like Feynman diagrams, decay rate, scattering
cross section, preparing for advance research skill. On top of that, help students
develop interests in particle physics. Furthermore, I will do computer programing
to demonstrate the numerical calculations during the class.

● 指定用書(Text Books) Introduction to Elementary Particles (David Griffiths)
● 參考書籍(References) Collider Physics (Vernon Barger and Roger Phillips)
● 教學方式(Teaching Method) Blackboard or slides. Teach mostly in English.

properties of ordered matter structures with a special emphasize on experimental
methods.

We will have EVERY MONDAY a brief written questionary (5-10 min) about the content
of the previous weeks.

The first semester will cover the first 8 chapters in Kittel's book; and the
contents will be enriched to a more sophisticated level.

一、課程說明(Course Description)

光電實驗是物理系碩士班光電物理組必修的實驗課程，內容以雷射特性及光譜為主。學生將學習雷

本學期實驗共計10個，實驗項目由下列實驗選擇：

modern interferometer
He-Ne 雷射 --- Transverse modes and Gaussian beam
He-Ne 雷射 --- Longitudinal modes and Lamb dip
He-Ne 雷射 --- mode locking
He-Ne 雷射及CO2 雷射--- Laser alignment
DPSS 雷射 --- Q-switching and SHG
Spectrometer and lock-in amplifier
Acusto-optical modulator (AOM)
Saturation spectroscopy
Raman spectroscopy

docs.text: Syllabus for Statistical Mechanics (II) – PHYS522000 Contents Basic information Evaluation: Final projects Homework policies Textbook Prerequisites Course Description References Basic information Time: Thursday 13:20-16:20 Classroom: Physics building, Room 208 Instructor: Yi-Ping Huang TA: <+TBA+>, Room <+TBA+> Office hours: After the course or by appointment (Online or at Room 517) Final project presentation date: <+TBA+> The course will be offered in English. We encourage everyone to interact in English. If some conceptual questions are difficult to be described in English, one can ask the question in Mandarin, and I will translate that into English. If I forgot to do that, please remind me to do so. Teaching method: Lectures Evaluation: Homework (60%), Final project (40%) Final projects Final project guideline Homework policies It is encouraged to discuss homework or the content of the lectures with your classmates. However, the point of discussion is to form one’s own opinion instead of following someone’s idea. Don’t copy the homework. Copied homework will get no points. That is, we will use a very one-sided rule. If two homework looks very similar, both of them get zero points. Copied homework from the internet is also disallowed. If the homework looks similar to any online resources: solution manual or anything, the homework will also get zero points. I will put the pdf file of the homework on google classroom. The pdf file will specify the due date of the homework. One-day delay is allowed (By Friday 5 pm). If you need more time to finish the homework, please send an email to me and explain why you need an extension and when you expect to turn in your homework. Late homework(within a week) without reasoning gets 70% of the scores. Late homework without reasoning for more than a week will get 0 points. The purpose of homework is to help you learn the subject. Please give yourself some time to think independently first, then discuss with your classmates or TA. TA has no responsibility to do the homework for you. Please start doing the homework early. Textbook None Prerequisites Basic knowledge in statistical mechanics (I) Course Description This course explores the collective behavior of interacting many-body systems, extending beyond the topics covered in Statistical Mechanics I. We begin with the classification of phases of matter using the Ginzburg–Landau theory and introduce the conceptual framework and physical meaning of the renormalization group. Equipped with these tools, we revisit phase transitions in bosonic and fermionic systems and examine exotic phases of matter that lie beyond the conventional Ginzburg–Landau paradigm, including topological phases and symmetry-protected topological order. In the second part of the course, we delve into modern developments in quantum statistical mechanics. We will discuss the dynamics of isolated quantum systems, the emergence of thermalization through the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis (ETH), and mechanisms of ergodicity breaking. Special attention will be given to quantum many-body scars, a novel class of atypical eigenstates that evade thermalization despite interactions. These topics highlight the rich interplay between quantum dynamics, entanglement, and statistical behavior in many-body systems. References For background knowledge of statistical mechanics 1. Statistical Mechanics in a Nutshell, Luca Peliti [Pel11] 2. (2nd Edition)Statistical Mechanics: Entropy, Order Parameters, and Complexity: Second Edition (Oxford Master Series in Physics), James P. Sethna [Set21] For statistical mechanics II 1. Quantum Field Theory of Many-body Systems: From the Origin of Sound to an Origin of Light and Electrons, Xaio-Gang Wen [Wen04] 2. Lectures on phase transitions and the renormalization group, Nigel Goldenfeld [Gol18] 3. Scaling and renormalization in statistical physics, John Cardy [Car96] 4. Statistical physics of fields, Mehran Kardar [Kar07] 5. Principles of condensed matter physics, P. M. Chaikin and T. C. Lubensky [CL00] A good reference is the one that you are willing to read. Course plan (2025-fall, <+ means to be updated +>) Date Contents 09.05 Course overview – Basic information, course description, and review of essential physics in statistical mechanics (I). 09.12 Review of mean field theory: Ising model and the Van der Waals equation. Motivation for a more general framework: Landau theory. Landau theory: Postulates, construction of Landau free energy, discrete and continuous phase transitions in Landau theory, critical exponents from Landau theory, coarse graining and the microscopic meaning of Landau theory. 09.19 <+(Continue) Landau theory: Landau free energy as a functional of the coarse grained field. Correlation functions for Landau theory. Critical exponents for Landau theory.+> 09.26 <+(Continue) Microscopic meaning for the phenomenological constants in Landau theory. Correlation function for Landau theory in general $d$ dimensional systems. Fluctuations and the breakdown of Landau theory.+> 10.03 <+(Discussion) How to understand fluctuations in mean-field theory? How to calculate the probability distribution for interacting systems in principle? How to tell whether probability distribution for many-body system can be factorized into one-body problem? How to estimate the fluctuation for a distribution function and the Ginsburg criteria in different dimensions. Introduction of the Gaussian approximation.+> 10.17 <+The Gaussian approximation and its correction to the Landau theory.+> 10.24 <+(Continue) The Gaussian approximation and its correction to the Landau theory. Perturbation theory for the $\phi^4$ theory in $d$ dimensions. Concept of asymptotic series.+> 10.31 <+Dimension analysis and the critical exponents. Conflicts between the dimension analysis and the experiment and the need to have a deeper theoretical understanding. The scaling hypothesis.+> 11.07 <+The scaling hypothesis and the Kadanoff’s renormalization group: the postulates and the insights.+> 11.14 <+Review of what we have done till now. From mean field theory, to fluctuation, to Landau theory and its breakdown, the anomalous dimension and the conflicts between common dimension analysis to Kadanoff’s insight. The formal structure/idea of renormalization group transformation: Why renormalization group idea is useful? Including fluctuations systematically on different scales.+> 11.21 <+Renormalization group step, renormalization group flow, the concept of fix points, the local and global structure of renormalization group flow.+> 11.28 <+Stable fix points, critical fix points, relevant, irrelevant and marginal couplings. The renormalization group flow near critical fix points and its relation to the critical exponents.+> 12.05 Renormalization group transformation for two-dimensional ferromagnetic Ising model. 12.12 <+Final presentation (1/2)+> 12.19 <+Final presentation (2/2)+>

Description: We have studied electromagnetism in two courses before: General Physics II (freshman) and Electromagnetism (sophomore). What is new in this course? Syllabus for Quantum Mechanics I (Fall, 2025)

(I) Course Overview
This course provides a comprehensive introduction to quantum mechanics, following
the structure and pedagogical approach of Principles of Quantum Mechanics by R.
Shankar. Beginning with a review of the necessary mathematical tools, such as
linear algebra and operator theory, the course progresses to foundational
postulates, the Schodinger equation, and the formalism of Hilbert spaces. In the
first semester, we would cover Chapter 1-13 with key topics including wave
functions, observables, commutation relations, path integral, symmetries and
angular momentum.

on-site course lectures (80%), online course components (20%).

Condensed Matter Physics (I) (凝態物理 I) 2019-2020

Course description (課程目標):
Condensed matter physics is a broad subject that is closely related to experiments. This course is an
elmentary course particularly designed for physics graduates. Its purpose is to develop students'
understanding of common principles involved in condensed matter so that students can further grasp and
understand phenomena involved in condensed matter experiments.
(凝態物理是一個範圍極廣並且與實驗關連性強的領域，本課程為物理所的基礎課程，主要的目標是在使
學生能掌握凝體物理共通之基本原理，因而能進一步掌握與了解凝體相關的實驗現象。)

Instructor:
Chung-Yu Mou (牟中瑜) (X42537) email: mou@phys.nthu.edu.tw

Lecture notes: see course webpage
Reference(參考書): 1.Solid State Physics, Ashcroft/Mermin (main textbook, 主要教科書)
2.Condensed Matter Physics, Michael P. Marder
3.Principles of Condensed Matter Physics, Chaikin/Lubenksy
Grading (成績): 40% homework+report、30% midterm、30% final

Syllabus
(1) Introduction to condensed matter physics
(2) Description of orders and atomic structures
-- Crystal Lattices and Structures
-- Experimental determination
-- Surfaces、interface and superstructures
-- alloy、liquids and glass
-- Liquid crystals、polymer and quasi-crystals
(4) Mechanical and dynamical properties of atomic structures
-- Ginzburg-Landau theory of phase transition
-- defect、dislocations and melting: solids versus crystal 2D melting
-- elasticity
-- lattices waves、second quantization and phonons
(5) Electronic structures
-- Failure of free-electron model in crystal
-- Bloch theorem and non-interacting electrons
-- methods for calculating band structures
-- effects of electron-electron interactions:
-- Hartree-Fock equations
-- Density functional theory
-- Correlation effects: metals、insulators and Mott physics

Course Description
This course is designed for students who are curious about the fundamental
workings of nature or are considering a future in high-energy physics. It provides
a solid foundation in the Standard Model (SM) of particle physics, with an
emphasis on both theoretical understanding and practical computation.

Topics include a review of quantum field theory, the structure and features of the

docs.text:
一、課程說明(Course Description)

各位同學好:

歡迎您加入設計製圖的行列, 本課程的主要目標是建立傳統圖學設計製圖基礎，學習電腦輔
助繪圖工具的操作與應用，整合圖學理論、繪圖軟體與設計實務。學習過程中將給各位相當的壓
力,相對的,一學期(年)下來,您將有更大的收獲,在您與學長學姐的家聚時,不妨問問他(她)們的意
見,意者趕緊接受老師的挑戰吧!

課程的撰寫重點在於：將工程實務、圖學理論、工具軟體三者結合成為一體，以迎接新世代的
電腦輔助設計與繪圖。

傳統工程圖學介紹著重基礎製圖規範與圖學理論之介紹，以及平面視圖與立體視圖之理論解說
及繪製，內容偏重製圖規範及理論傳授；而傳統之電腦輔助設計 (CAD) 繪圖軟體課程，多以強調
軟體的操作為主，輔以圖形範例進行繪圖之示範。然而，隨著電腦輔助設計繪圖軟體的日趨成熟，
如何將基礎圖學與電腦輔助設計繪圖軟體進行適切的融合，已成為當務之急。

因此，本課程特色將朝以下的目標發展：從『設計實務』的觀點，進行『圖學理論』的介紹，
清晰表達圖學的內涵；從『軟體應用』的觀點，進行『設計繪圖』的操作，完整發揮軟體的特色；
並進一步加以整合構成『電腦輔助設計圖學』，並規劃實際之計畫範例，進行整合的工作，期使本
課程能夠成為兼具學術及工程價值。

本課程由設計繪圖的實務觀點開始圖學的簡介；接著，對圖學的規範進行系列的介紹，以
建立深厚的圖學基礎，包括基礎圖學內容之工程圖的標準、線條的種類與用途、正投影、立體圖
與三視圖、剖面圖、尺寸標註、公差與配合...等等；

然後，便是電腦輔助設計繪圖軟體 AutoCAD 的操作基礎培訓，此乃經由系統性的分類及整
理，從基本之繪圖編輯指令示範，發展到高階之應用指令介紹；之後，便是應用幾何與投影幾何的
解說，至此建立起設計圖學與繪圖軟體之根基；緊接著，進行電腦輔助設計製圖的整合，從平面的
正投影圖繪製，一直到立體之等角圖、斜視圖，以及透視圖的電腦輔助繪製；最後，並另以獨立之
章節，透過實際設計範例，展現項電腦輔助製圖觀念與技巧的應用成果，期使能夠兼顧理論與實
務。

自從 91 學年度開始，圖學教室導入參數式的 3D 系統，因此，整個學年度將教學的層級由
2D 提升到 3D，也就是說，本學期將為下學期的 3D 參數是設計打下札實的基礎，本學期課程的
學習將以 Autodesk AutoCAD 2D 系統的學習應用為主軸，下學期則將衍生發展到 Autodesk
Inventor 3D/2D 系統，此舉將會對大家有非常正面的學習成效，期待與大家共同來完成這一學
年的訓練

二、指定用書(Text Books)

待定

三、參考書籍(References)

1.劉俊賢, "AutoCAD 2002/2000工程圖學實務導航 - 登堂入室篇", 2002.10, 宏友圖書
2.劉俊賢, "AutoCAD 2002/2000工程圖學實務導航 - 進階應用篇", 2002.10, 宏友圖書

四、教學方式(Teaching Method)

學生以紙本簡報學習，講師以簡報方式闡述，進行課程說明、綜合討論、操作訓練、報告規劃與
寫作、實務設計製圖、創意與設計

五、教學進度(Syllabus)

詳見第一堂課的課程簡介

六、成績考核(Evaluation)

6.1 設計製圖報告：期中、期末報告.....
6.2 實習測驗：課堂測驗與競賽、課程作業與練習....
6.3 研究記錄：筆記、小組討論、會議.....
6.4 課堂參與：到課、學習、發問....狀況
6.5 課後參與：預習、複習、eeclass 上線.....狀況
6.6 課後挑戰：學生依程度進行挑戰，選擇升級更上一層樓

七、可連結之網頁位址

docs.name: 工場實習一
docs.text: 工場實習(一) Work Shop Practices (I) — 課程大綱 114 學年上學期 課號：11410PME101500 上課時間：W5W6W7 地點：工一 214 授課講師：動機系 一、課程概述： 本課程結合理論及實務，讓學生在科儀中心以工廠實習的方式學習工場環境與加 工技術。課程中將介紹：工廠安全與環境衛生、實習規則及自我保護，尺寸量測， 實作車床/銑床/鑽床/鉗工/CNC 加工中心機/電銲/氣銲，以及了解目前用於特殊材 料產品之製作加工的先進製造技術方法。 二、教學目標： 1. 讓學生了解工場實習安全規則之重要性。 2. 讓學生學習各種製造加工方法，了解其中的差異與適應性。 3. 讓學生學習精度、公差的概念。 4. 讓學生實際於科儀中心操作車床/銑床/鑽床/鉗工/CNC 加工中心機/電銲/氣 銲等，使學生了解各種加工儀器，選擇正確加工設備。 三、參考書籍： 1. 張甘棠、機工學、三文出版社 2. 蔡德藏、工廠實習：機工實習(第七版)、全華圖書 3. 上課投影片. 四、教學內容: 週數 日期 主要課程 實作課程 Week 1 9/3 課程規定簡介 -- Week 2 9/10 工場安全規則及基本知識 實作一 Week 3 9/17 尺寸量測工具原理介紹與使用教學 實作二 Week 4 9/24 加工精度、公差及工程圖介紹 實作三 Week 5 10/1 機械加工方法介紹：車床、CNC 車 床、銑床、CNC 銑床 實作四 Week 6 10/8 工業物聯網與產業案例 實作五 Week 7 10/15 工具機和半導體製造設備 實作六 Week 8 10/22 智慧製造概論 實作七 Week 9 10/29 智慧製造產業案例介紹 實作八 Week10 11/5 智慧製造產業案例介紹 實作九 Week11 11/12 全校運動會(停課) -- Week12 11/19 智慧製造產業案例介紹 實作十 Week13 11/26 小組期末報告 實作十一 Week14 12/3 小組期末報告 實作十二 Week15 12/10 期末考準備 -- Week16 12/17 期末考 -- 五、成績考核： 平常成績：學習態度、出席狀況 (師傅評分及老師斟酌加減) [30%] 實習報告：[20 %] 個人期末報告：[10 %] 小組期末報告：[20 %] 期末考試：[20 %] ※ 實習期間若嚴重違反工廠安全規定，本課程將不予以通過！ 六、AI 使用規則 有條件開放：於指定條件下使用，使用時須註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出。 七、安全事項： 1. 應注意逃生口、警鈴、滅火器的位置。 2. 實習時請戴安全眼鏡(護目鏡)。 3. 實習時請穿著包鞋(止滑、防護性強為佳)。 4. 使用適當的工具，不可馬虎差不多。 5. 機器運轉時，手應遠離轉動部分，不可拿布接近轉動或運動範圍。 6. 量測工件、清理機器時，必須停機。 7. 長髮要綁起。 8. 禁止穿著寬鬆衣物，以防袖子被機器捲入。 9. 禁止穿戴手錶、項鍊等任何可能為機械絆住之物品。 10. 禁止穿著拖鞋或涼鞋。 11. 禁止兩人操作一部機器。

。課程說明 (Course Description)
This course introduces fundamental concepts of general-purpose programming. No
prior experience is required. We will focus on procedural programming, using a
widely adopted high-level language. While the exact language may vary, it will
serve as a tool to help students understand core programming principles that apply
across many languages. The goal is not only to write correct code, but also to
write good code—efficient, readable, and maintainable. More advanced topics, such
as object-oriented programming, will be covered in future courses. This course
emphasizes learning how to think like a programmer, so students can confidently
learn other languages on their own.

docs.text:
一、課程說明(Course Description)

本課程的對象是程式設計初學者。
我們將以C語言來介紹程式設計的基本概念、基本技巧以及熟練C語言的使用。目標使學生能將腦中的演
算法轉換成為電腦程式，利用電腦來解決問題。

本課程將著重在C語言程式的實際編寫能力，請務必要有花費心力及時間寫程式的準備。修課學生必
須要通過線上的程式驗證考試及完成期末程式專題作業。期末程式專題作業需由同學親自向授課老師
展示繳交，繳交時會就程式原始碼做討論及問答。

本課程的核心重點是讓程式初學者理解程式語言的運作及訓練自己有能力將想法編寫成程式碼，而非單
純的要求程式執行結果。繳交的程式均需要由學生自行完成，使用AI生成、他人代寫及抄襲均不予計
分。

二、指定用書(Text Books)
NA

四、教學方式(Teaching Method)

2.Variables and Data types
3.Control statement
4.expressions
5.Formatted I/O
6.File Processing
7.Functions
8.Array
9.Pointer
10.Structure
11.Recursion

2.期末測驗(包含上機考): 20%
3.作業：20%

docs.name: 機器人技術與實作

一、課程說明

docs.text:
●課程說明(Course Description)

This "Mechanics of Materials" lecture addresses the question, “How much does an
object of finite size deform when a force is applied to it?” This practical study
is widely used in the design of micromachines, robots, buildings, bridges,
automobiles, and more. The lecture covers the deformation of objects in the
elastic region caused by bending, shear, tension, compression, and torsion.

The main issues that this lecture covers are as follows:
(1) What do stress, strain, yield and strength mean in Mechanics of materials?
(2) The basics of deformation caused by axial load and torsion.
(3) Bending: How to calculate the deflection of the beams and shafts using the
moment of inertia of the cross-section.
(4) Combined load: How to calculate internal stresses when multiple forces are
applied simultaneously by Mohr’s strain circle, principal strain.
(5) Energy methods: More effecient methods to calculate the deflection using
Maxwell’s reciprocal theorem and Castigliano’s theorem.

We have an midterm exam and a final exam.

However, it does not address “Plastic Mechanics" such as plastic deformation and
fracture. It also does not include "Dislocation theory" which attempts to
understand the atomic structure in deformation.

● 指定用書(Text Books)
Russell Hibbeler “Mechanics of Materials 11th Edition in SI unit” Pearson
Education Limited, 2023

● 參考書籍(References)
B. J. Goodno, J.M. Gere, "Mechanics of Materials 9th Edition” Cengage Learning,
2018

● 教學方式(Teaching Method)
The lecture will proceed as follows: (1) Listen to explanations in the classroom,
(2) Take notes, (3) Solve the problems given during the lecture, and (4) Listen to
the answers to the problems. We also have a question and answer period in each
class. The lecture is not available online.

● 教學進度(Syllabus)
(1) Stress, (2) Strain, (3) Mechanical Properties of Materials, (4) Axial Load,
(5) Torsion, (6) Bending, (7) Transverse Shear, (8) Combined Loadings, (9) Stress
Transformation, (10) Strain Transformation, (11) Design of Beams and Shafts, (12)
Deflection of Beams and Shafts,

● 成績考核(Evaluation)
(1) Short quizzes (you can see the textbooks): 20%, (2) Midterm exam: 30%, (3)
Final exam: 50%

課程說明 (Course Description)
機械製造是將設計概念轉化為實體產品的關鍵環節，對產品性能與製造效率有決定性影響。本課程旨
在使學生了解與機械工程相關的主要產品及其零組件的生產方式，包括可採用的各類加工方法、其基
本原理與特性、所需設備、以及提升生產力的各種工程方法。
Manufacturing is the critical stage in transforming design concepts into
physical products, playing a decisive role in both product performance and
production efficiency. This course aims to equip students with a comprehensive
understanding of the production methods for major products and components
related to mechanical engineering, including various applicable manufacturing
processes, their fundamental principles and characteristics, required equipment,
and engineering methods for improving productivity.

docs.text:
一、課程說明(Course Description)
線性代數為工程問題分析的重要工具，此課程將大二的工程數學中的線性代數不足部份做一個完
整的介紹，此課程主要探討linear equations, vectors and matrices; vector spaces;

docs.name: 能源工程
docs.text:
Course description:
This course aims to lead students to further strengthen their knowledge in
thermophysical principles and transport phenomena. The theme is the
application of those fundamental principles in energy systems engineering.
Students should leave the course with confidence and sufficient abilities to
readily apply techniques as engineers on the design and analysis encountered
in a variety of emerging sustainable and renewable energy systems. A hands-
on project will be carried out as the platform for students to learn by
doing. Students should also be able to readily use the basic computer
software in solving energy related problems, as well as having a clear concept
when utilizing advanced commercial software in solving engineering problems.
The skills developed in this course will be applied in the semester-long
project to practice the detailed design of a complete sustainable energy
system. The objective is to translate the statement of an energy system
analysis and design problem into a series of tasks and step-by-step practices.

References:
1. Y.A. Çengel and M.A. Boles, Thermodynamics: An Engineering Approach
(McGraw-Hill)
2. B.R. Munson and T. H. Okiishi et al., Fluid Mechanics (Wiley)
3. F.P. Incropera and D. P. DeWitt et al., Principles of Heat and Mass
Transfer (Wiley)
4. R.A. Dunlap, Sustainable Energy 2nd edition (Cengage Learning)

Topics:
1. Introduction of course, The basics of energy conversion
2. Review of basic thermodynamics and thermosystems
3. Review of fluid dynamics
4. Review of fundamental heat transfer
5. Overview of HVAC system and thermal comfort, Green building
6. Solar thermal energy systems
7. Wind, Hydropower, Wave and Tidal energy systems
8. Oceanthermal and Geothermal energy systems
9. Hydrogen energy, Biomass energy
10.Nanotechnology for renewable and sustainable energy

Evaluation:
Homework, Midterm exam, Final project, Labs and quiz, Class participation

一、課程說明(Course Description)
實際的工程與科學問題往往相當複雜，不易用理論方法來處理；另一方面，因為電腦的進步，數值方
法成為處理工程與科學問題最經濟而有效的方法。在相關數值方法中，有限單元法是最被廣泛使用的
方法，尤其在固體力學領域。相關的軟體功能也日益完備，已成為有效而方便的工具。學生可透過基
礎理論的介紹與實際的操作練習，熟悉一個有用的工具(以ANSYS為例)，提升往後解決工程與科學問

本課程將介紹機械元件的基本構造及選用機械元件的方法，以及機械系統設計時機械強度設計的理
論基礎。課程內容涵蓋機械設計的基礎知識，包括工程力學和材料力學，靜態和可變載荷下的故障
預防，以及主要機械元件的特性與原理。
This course will introduce the basic structure of mechanical components, the
method of selecting mechanical components and the theoretical basis of the
design of mechanical strength during design. The content covers the basics of
machine design, including engineering mechanics and materials, failure
prevention under static and variable loading, and characteristics of the
principal types of mechanical elements.

Richard G. Budynas and J. Keith Nisbett, Shigley's Mechanical Engineering
Design , eleventh Edition,Mc,Graw Hill 2020

中文授課

7. Lubrication and Journal Bearing (Chapter 12)

9. Flexible Mechanical Element (Chapter 17)

docs.text: PME 343700 Innovations in Engineering Design Department of Power Mechanical Engineering Instructor: Wei-Chih Wang, Ph.D. Office: Delta 319 tel: 03-5742488 abong@u.washington.edu Class Time: M 3:20-5:10PM and Th 2:20-3:10 PM Objectives Through engineering projects, students learn the design process and associated skills: communicating, creative problem solving, computing, and working in teams. Students also see first-hand how math and science relate to the field of engineering. The small class size allows instructors to provide students with extensive feedback, and students are encouraged to learn from one another. By taking this class, students gain engineering design experience through hands-on projects and practical oral and written presentation skills, team work and possibly working with industry for their final project to demonstrate the skills they learn in class. Course Description This exciting 18-week class will introduce you to engineering design and communication principles through a project-based approach which stresses teamwork, design process, specialties and tools of engineering, creative and analytical thinking, professionalism, and open‐ended problems. Students taking this course design and build a variety of machines and structures to learn hands-on the basic engineering design principles as well as getting career advises from visiting professionals from industrial and students and faculties from academia. The design projects vary each semester and may include:  Building a bridge for maximum strength and minimum cost  Dissecting a lawn mower engine to see how it works  Designing and programming a robot to maneuver in an obstacle course  Designing "Rube Goldberg" machines  Learning smart materials and design various interesting smart sensors and actuators  Learning Labview program for a musical instrument project  Learning basic electricity through simple 2way, 3way and four way switches and application in digital eletronics  More! Prerequisite: Junior standing undergraduate students are preferred, but there is no actual prerequisite except creativity and willingness to participate in the class projects. Text: Reading packets and assignments are available on the course web site: (TBA) Supplemental reading materials will be handed out in class. digital electronics through simple switch design project) Week 10 Basic Electricity (introduction to power system, basic analog and digital electronics through simple switch design project) Week 10 Career Presentation (inviting special speakers from industry to speak to students about career in engineering and other options besides engineering) Week 11 Fundamental of Sensors & Actuators (Introduction to light sources and detectors) Week 12 Optical transducer project (week long design project, oral and final report in the end of the project) Week 13 Fundamental of Sensors & Actuators (Introduction to smart structures and materials) Week 14 SMA Design project (Application of shape memory alloy actuator in engineering design, oral and final report in the end of the project) Week 15 Robot Design (Lego Mindstorms or Arduino controller based robot design project, involves programming , sensory, control, and mechanical design) Week 16 Robot Design (Lego Mindstorms or Arduino docs.text: Updated on July 19, 2025. 1 PME400500: Numerical Analysis (in English conditionally; X-class) Fall 2025 Department of Power Mechanical Engineering, National Tsing Hua University I. Course Description (課程說明) Error analysis (Chap. 1), solutions of equations in one variable (Chap. 2), interpolation and polynomial approximation (Chap. 3), numerical differentiation and integrating (Chap. 4), initial-value problems for ordinary differential equations (Chap. 5), direct methods for solving linear systems (Chap. 6), and iterative technique in matrix algebra (Chap. 7). The approximation theory (Chap. 8) might be delivered provided we have sufficient time. Other chapters in the textbook will NOT be covered. II. Prerequisite (預修課程) Engineering Mathematics (I) III. Textbooks (指定用書) 1. R.L. Burden, and J.D. Faires, Numerical Analysis, 10th ed., Thomson Brooks/Cole, Belmont, CA, USA, 2016. (for theory) IV. References (參考書籍) 1. G.R. Lindfield, and J.E.T. Penny, Numerical Methods: Using MATLAB, 4th ed., Academic Press, Cambridge, MA, USA, 2019. (for coding) 2. T. Sauer, Numerical Analysis, 3rd ed., Pearson Education Inc., Edinburgh Gate, United Kingdom, 2023. (for examples and homework) V. Time and Location (教學時間與地點) 1. Lectures (in English) / Lectures review (in Mandarin) / Coding exercises 2. Written exams (9:00 – 12:00 on Tuesday at Room 209, ENG_I) 3. NTHU MOOCs https://mooc.nthu.edu.tw/ (https://mooc.nthu.edu.tw/course/info/339) 4. Videos of last year are provided on eLearn https://elearn.nthu.edu.tw/ by permitted request VI. Instructor (授課教師) Dr. Yu-Bin Chen (陳玉彬 教授); ybchen@pme.nthu.edu.tw Updated on July 19, 2025. 2 Room 512 in Engineering Building I 03-5715131 (ext. 33767) Office hour: Wednesday 13:10 – 13:30 or reserved via e-mail VII. Teaching Assistants (助教) 1. Mr. Chang-Li Zheng (鄭長力) l6509eo@gmail.com 2. Mr. Shang-Wei Liu (劉上偉) sean910830@gmail.com Office hour: Tuesday 14:10 – 16:00 or reserved via e-mail Room 430 in Engineering Building I 03-5715131 (ext. 33743) VIII. Evaluation (成績考核) Homework: 150 (sum of 5 assignments) Tests: 240 (1.4  higher + 1.0  lower) Bonus: 80 (attendance, answering to in-class questions) Grade guidelines are given according to the rules described in the following. Assume student A gets the highest score x in the class. Student B gets the score y, which is higher than 280. Student C gets the score z, which is lower than 280. Then, student A will get 97 in Numerical Analysis as the final grade. Student B will get the score “60 + 37(y  280)/(x  280).” Student C will get the score “55  z/280.” For example, we assume that student A gets the highest original score 430, student B gets 400, and student C gets the score 260. The final grade of student A, B, and C will be 97, 60 + 37(400  280)/(430  280) = 89.6 = 90, and 55260/280 =51.07 = 51, respectively. Note: A student will fail in this course even he or she gets the original score 279, unless more than 15% of students are flunked. The criteria 279 can only be slightly adjusted till less than 15% of students are flunked and the average score of whole class can be curved to 70 -79. Note: The average score of whole class will be curved to 70 – 79, which is requested by PME. Homework: Please read the relevant sections of the references before each lecture. Read the book examples carefully before doing homework also. There will be five homework assignments, due before the class as indicated on the schedule page. Solutions will be announced after the due date. The steps Score Range  280 < 280 Actual Grade  60  55 Updated on July 19, 2025. 3 of solution should be detail enough and clear; otherwise you will not receive full credit even if your answers are correct. Discussion among classmates is encouraged; however, you are expected to solve problems independently. Homework grading will be largely based on efforts and whether you have used the procedures correctly, rather than the numbers. You will receive a penalty for each unsolved problem. All assignments will be counted. Examination: There will be two exams in the semester. See the tentative schedule for examination dates. Please see the instructor immediately if a conflict arises. 量測、視流與風洞實驗、蒸汽渦輪動力實驗、太陽電池測試。

理、裝置、步驟，以及分析實驗結果的方法。

任何熱力學、熱傳與質傳、流體力學相關教科書均可參考。

台，內容及圖表須為電腦打字，不可手寫手繪，進行方式如下：

評分。

3.實驗當週的星期五晚上23:59前上傳實驗結報。

docs.name: 人體再生能源收集技術概述
docs.nameEn: Introduction to human renewable energy harvesting technologies
docs.text:
一、課程說明 (Course Description)
在微電子和材料技術高速發展的今日，大量新型多功能和高度集成化的微型電子器件不斷推陳出
新，在日常生活的各個方面展現出前所未有的應用前景，感測器便是其中一種新興的研究項目。然
而，一般感測器皆需外接電源來驅動其運作，而且主要以充電或一次性電池作為主要電力來源，這
些電源的體積較大、能源耗用量高，致使感測器的應用範圍受到嚴重限制；此外，廢棄電池也會對
環境造成汙染，種種因素驅使著科學家努力尋找更為環保的動力來源。綜觀動力發電研究的歷程，
從風力、水力、火力發電等等技術不斷演進，建造出許多設計複雜精密的發電設施，但如果將研究
回歸到最基礎且本質的「人類」自身，我們每天的活動及體溫即會不斷產生各種機械能和熱能，如
何將這些微小但卻最易取用的能量轉變為日常所需的驅動力來源，正是科學家持續研究的課題之
一。在本課程中，將會介紹同學有關用來收集人體所產生機械能及熱能的技術；配合奈米材料的優
點，這些所製成元件將不再笨重，高度提升其應用潛力。另外，也會利用讓同學實作的機會，鼓勵
同學將課堂上所學的知識，學以致用。

二、指定用書 (Text Books)
Triboelectric Nanogenerators、Nanogenerators for Self-powered Devices and
Systems

三、參考書籍 (References)
Journal Papers

四、教學方式 (Teaching Method)
投影片、實作

五、教學進度 (Syllabus)
1. 可用於人體能源收集技術簡介
2. 熱電效應及常見材料介紹
3. 熱電奈米元件及其實際應用
4. 壓電與熱釋電效應及常見材料介紹
5. 壓電與熱釋電奈米元件及其實際應用
6. 摩擦起電現象及常見材料介紹
7. 摩擦起電奈米元件及其工作原理
8. 複合元件設計及其實際應用
9. 自供電感測器及系統
10. 元件實作

六、成績考核 (Evaluation)
期中考 (40%)、分組期末實作報告 (40%)、期末文獻書面報告 (20%)

七、AI使用規則 (Principle of using AI)
有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式AI於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how
generative AI will be used in course output

docs.name: 層流理論
docs.text: Power Mechanical Engineering, National Tsing Hua University 1 PME 511100: Laminar Flow Theory (層流理論) Fall, 2025 offered in English Prerequisites: advanced fluid dynamics, differential equations This is a graduate-level course aiming to offer students the knowledge on fluid dynamics. We will go over fundamental concepts of fluid motions and dynamics, followed by a derivation of the (in)famous Navier-Stokes equations. Then we will obtain some analytic solutions where viscosity is balanced by some other forces such as inertia, pressure, and body force that determine the flow dynamic. The Stokes flow and lubrication theory in which viscosity dominates will also be discussed. Finally, we wrap up in laminar boundary layer theory, where self-similar solution and an integral approach will be covered. Stability of fluid flows is optional and will be introduced based on the availability of time. docs.name: 流體不穩定性控制理論
docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number PME 511400 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 無 中文名稱 Course Title 流體不穩定性控制理論 英文名稱 Course English Title Flow Instability Control Theory 任課教師 Instructor 胡相宸 上課時間 Time F5F6F7 上課教室 Room 工一 209 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Fluid instability plays a significant role in fluid dynamics and is particularly critical in the contexts of electronic cooling and semiconductor processing. In recent years, the rising demand for high- performance immersion liquid cooling—driven by high-power chips and the rapid evolution of semiconductor fabrication technologies—has intensified the need to understand and manage thermo- flow effects. These effects directly impact the quality of epitaxial thin films and the performance of high-performance computing (HPC) and artificial intelligence (AI) chips. One of the most urgent challenges in the metal-organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) epitaxial process is achieving the uniformity and stability of reactive gas flows. Addressing this challenge is essential for improving thin film quality and ensuring reliable device operation. This course integrates the fundamentals of flow instability and thermal convection with an active flow-field stabilization strategy known as the Kelly-Hu Mechanism. Within this framework, students will explore innovative approaches to stabilizing flow behavior in the MOCVD process and to overcoming thermal management challenges posed by next-generation high-power chips. The course is designed for master’s and doctoral students, as well as advanced undergraduates (junior or senior level), who have completed an introductory course in fluid mechanics. 流體穩定性與不穩定性是流體動力學中最核心且廣泛被探討和研究的課題，尤其在電子冷却與半導體製程中更顯 關鍵。流場從穩定層流(Laminar Flow)發展成不穩定紊流（Turbulence）的物理現象廣泛存在於各種應用科學領 域。因此，深入理解流體不穩定性的觸發機制，對基礎科學研究和工程應用具有極其重要的意義。近年來，隨著 高耗能晶片對高效能浸沒式液體冷卻技術需求的迅速攀升，以及半導體製程設備因應高階運算與人工智慧（AI） 晶片爆炸性需求而快速成長，晶片製程中的熱流效應已成為影響薄膜磊晶層品質與晶片效能的關鍵挑戰。因此， 在有機金屬化學氣相沉積（MOCVD, Metal-Organic Chemical Vapor Deposition）磊晶過程中，如何有效控制 反應氣體的均勻性與穩定性，已成為半導體產業亟待克服的重要議題。本課程將結合熱流擾動特性與流場穩定之 主動控制機制 (Kelly-Hu Mechanism)，提出創新且高效的解決方案，主動調控 MOCVD 製程中的流場穩定度， 同時應對高耗能晶片的散熱挑戰。課程內容設計涵蓋流體穩定與不穩定流場現象與其基本原理，並深入探討觸發 流體擾動的關鍵物理機制和控制方法，例如 Kelly-Hu Mechanism。同時，課程將探討應用主動式控制機制來調 節流場的穩定性，為解決實際工程問題提供理論基礎與技術支援。本課程適合碩士與博士研究生研習，以及已修 習基礎流體力學課程的大三或大四學生選修。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) Flow Instability, Floquet Theory, Galerkin Method, Boussinesq Approximation, Rayleigh-Taylor Instability, Kelvin-Helmholtz Instability, Orr-Sommerfeld Equation, Rayleigh-Bénard Convection, Rotating flow and Centrifugal Instabilities, Finite Amplitude, Thermal Convection, Taylor Vortex Flow, Modulated Fluid Motions, MOCVD Flow 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) 流體穩定性與不穩定性的控制，是流體力學中最核心且關鍵的研究課題之一, 尤其在電子冷却與半導體製程中更顯 關鍵。百餘年來，科學家觀察到流體在流動過程中，受到外力擾動或幾何邊界突然改變的影響，可能導致流場劇 烈變化，使原本穩定的層流（Laminar Flow）轉變為混亂且高度不穩定的紊流（Turbulence）。此類流場轉變的 物理現象廣泛存在於化工製程、熱流系統、航太工程與半導體製程設備中，同時也普遍出現在大氣、海洋、天文 與地球物理等自然界中。因此，深入理解穩定（Steady）與不穩定（Unsteady）流場的物理機制，不僅對基礎科 學研究至關重要，更是實現精準控制流體擾動、提升工程系統性能的關鍵，尤其近年來針對高階晶片和半導體製 程領域。 流體動力學與半導體製程的融合，是一項高度跨領域的前瞻性研究，涵蓋工程力學、材料科學與物理化學等領 域。有效掌握流體不穩定性的控制理論與方法，並結合人工智慧技術進行流場擾動的預測與主動控制，將是推動 高效能晶片製程與散熱技術發展的關鍵。隨著高耗能晶片對高效能浸沒式液體冷卻技術需求的快速增長，以及高 階運算與人工智慧（AI）晶片市場的蓬勃發展，半導體製程中熱流效應已成為影響薄膜磊晶層品質與晶片效能的 主要挑戰。在有機金屬化學氣相沉積（MOCVD, Metal-Organic Chemical Vapor Deposition）磊晶過程中，如 何穩定並均勻地控制反應氣體的流場，已成為半導體產業亟需克服的技術瓶頸。本課程將聚焦於熱流擾動特性與 穩定流場之主動控制機制，並結合 Kelly-Hu 機制（Kelly-Hu Mechanism），提出創新且高效的控制方法，應對 MOCVD 製程中流場的不穩定性，同時滿足高耗能晶片所引起的散熱挑戰。 本課程內容設計將系統性介紹穩定與不穩定流場的基本特性與關鍵物理機制，深入探討引發流體擾動的成因與控 制方法，特別強調 Kelly-Hu 機制在流場控制中的應用。此外，課程亦將探討多種調控流場穩定性的方法，提供 學生解決實際工程問題的理論基礎與技術工具。本課程適合碩士與博士研究生研習，亦歡迎已完成基礎流體力學 課程的大三或大四學生選修。 課程內容包括：  Stability problems and the dynamic control of modulated systems based on Floquet theory and the Kelly-Hu Mechanism  Instabilities involving interfaces and disturbance energy equations  The Orr–Sommerfeld and vorticity equations  Rayleigh–Bénard convection and centrifugal instabilities  Finite-amplitude thermal convection and rotating flows  Active control strategies for modulated fluid motions  Thermal management in cooling systems and MOCVD (Metal-Organic Chemical Vapor Deposition) flow control The control of fluid stability and instability is one of the most fundamental and critical research areas in fluid mechanics, particularly in the contexts of electronic cooling and semiconductor processing. For over a century, scientists have observed that fluid flows are highly sensitive to external disturbances and sudden changes in geometric boundaries, which can trigger transitions from stable laminar flow to chaotic, turbulent regimes. Such flow instabilities are commonly observed in chemical processes, thermal systems, aerospace engineering, and semiconductor fabrication equipment, as well as in natural phenomena such as atmospheric dynamics, ocean currents, astrophysics, and geophysics. A comprehensive understanding of the physical mechanisms governing both steady and unsteady flows is therefore essential—not only for advancing the theoretical foundations of fluid dynamics but also for enabling precise control over flow disturbances. This knowledge is particularly critical for enhancing the reliability and performance of engineering systems affected by thermo-flow effects, especially in advanced integrated circuits (ICs) and semiconductor manufacturing processes. In recent years, the rapidly growing demand for high-performance immersion liquid cooling driven by high-power chips and the accelerated advancement of semiconductor fabrication technologies to support the explosive growth of high-performance computing and artificial intelligence (AI) chips have made thermo-flow effects during chip manufacturing a critical challenge. These effects significantly impact the quality of epitaxial thin films and the overall performance of semiconductor devices. As a result, achieving uniform and stable reactive gas flows in the metal-organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) epitaxial process has become an urgent priority for the semiconductor industry. The integration of fluid dynamics with semiconductor manufacturing represents a cutting-edge, multidisciplinary research frontier that spans engineering mechanics, materials science, and physical chemistry. Effectively managing flow instabilities, particularly through the application of artificial intelligence for predictive modeling and active flow control, is essential for advancing next-generation chip fabrication and thermal management technologies. This course will integrate the characteristics of thermal flow disturbances with an active flow-field stabilization strategy known as the Kelly-Hu Mechanism. Through this framework, the course aims to introduce innovative and effective solutions for stabilizing flow fields in the MOCVD process, while also addressing the thermal management challenges posed by next-generation high-power chips. This course is suitable for master's and doctoral students, as well as advanced undergraduates (junior or senior year) who have completed an introductory course in fluid mechanics. ● 指定用書(Text Books) None ● 參考書籍(References) 1. S. Chandrasekhar “Hydrodynamics and Hydromagnetic Stability”(1961) 2. P. G. Drazin and W. H. Reid “Hydrodynamic Stability”(1981) 3. R. E. Kelly and H.-C. Hu, "The Onset of Rayleigh-Bénard Convection in Non-Planar Oscillatory Flows," Journal of Fluid Mechanics, Vol. 249, pp. 373-390, 1993. 4. H.-C. Hu and R. E. Kelly, "The Effect of a Time-Periodic Axial Shear Flow upon the Onset of Taylor Vortices," Physical Review E, Vol. 51, pp. 3242-3251, 1995. 5. Philip Hall, "Finite-Amplitude Convection in the Presence of an Unsteady Shear Flow," Journal of Fluid Mechanics, Vol. 287, pp. 225-249, 1995. 6. Trudi A. Shortis and Philip Hall, “On the Effect of Feedback Control on Bénard Convection in a Boussinesq Fluid,” ICASE Report No. 96-9, NASA Langley Research Center, 1996. 7. H.-C. Hu and R. E. Kelly, “Stabilization of Longitudinal Vortex Instabilities by Means of Transverse Flow Oscillations,” Physics of Fluids, Vol. 9, pp. 648-654, 1997. 8. A. Weisberg, I. Kevrekidis and A. J. Smits, "Delaying transition in Taylor-Couette flow with axial motion of the inner cylinder," Journal of Fluid Mechanics, Vol. 348, pp. 141-151, 1997. 9. F. Marques and J. M. Lopez, "Taylor–Couette flow with axial oscillations of the inner cylinder: Floquet analysis of the basic flow," Journal of Fluid Mechanics, Vol. 348, pp. 153-175, 1997. 10. J. M. Lopez and F. Marques, "Modulated Taylor–Couette flow: Onset of Spiral Modes," Theoretical and Computational Fluid Dynamics, Vol. 19, pp. 59-69, 2002. ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) Lecture Notes & Class ppt ● 教學進度(Syllabus) Syllabus 課程大綱 Lecture Contents I Introduction to Flow Stability I.1. docs.name: 燃燒學概論
docs.text:
一、課程說明(Course Description)

燃燒學在機械、化工以及航太工程問題上存在著很多有趣的應用，其所牽涉到的基礎學科很
廣，包括：流體力學、熱力學、熱傳學、質傳學、化學動力學、多相流以及工程數學等等。燃
燒學概論的課程，一開始先以專章介紹關於一個反應系統之反應流體的保守方程式和其之簡
化，接著分章介紹基礎火焰反應行為：第二章層流預混火焰結構與應用；第三章預混火焰於爆
燃現象之應用；第四、第五章為層流非預混火焰（或稱擴散火焰）結構及其於噴流火焰與油滴
燃燒的應用。在上述主要內容的介紹中隨時輔以質傳學、流體力學、熱傳學、化學動力學、多
相流以及氣體動力學等基礎學科之補充教材。

二、指定用書(Text Books)

Turns, S.R., “An Introduction to Combustion—Concepts and Applications,” 3E(IE),
McGraw Hill,2012.

docs.name: 線性系統理論
docs.text:
A. Course Description: This course introduces the fundamental concepts of linear system theory and builds
proficiency in the mathematical techniques and tools used to analyze the intrinsic dynamics of lumped-parameter
dynamical systems. Emphasis is placed on both continuous-time models of physical systems and discrete-time
models of sampled-data control systems. Real-world engineering systems are used as examples to gain deeper
understanding and insight into the relationship between the internal dynamics of physical systems and their
mathematical representations.

Students will explore both the input-output (transfer function) and state-space descriptions of dynamical systems.
MATLAB will be used extensively to perform analytical and numerical computations throughout the course.

B. Textbooks: There is no required textbook.

C. References: 1) C-T Chen, Linear System Theory and Design, HRW, 1984.
2) Robert H. Cannon, Dynamics of Physical Systems, 1967.

D. Teaching Method: Use PowerPoint presentations and chalkboards for lectures.

E. Course Outline:
1. Mathematical model representation of lumped parametric dynamic systems
2. Equilibrium state and linearization
3. Input-output description and transfer functions
4. Output response of linear time-invariant systems
5. Discrete-time modeling and analysis of sampled-data systems
6. State-variable description of continuous-time systems
7. Analysis of linear state equations/eigen analysis and modal decomposition
8. Stability, controllability, and observability of continuous-time linear dynamic systems
9. Discrete-time state-variable description of sampled-data systems
10. Stability, controllability, and observability of discrete-time linear dynamic systems
11. State feedback/Pole placement and state estimators
12. Augmented state estimators (disturbance observer and real-time estimation of process parameters)

F. Grading: Homework 25%
Exam I 25%
Exam II 25%
Exam III (Final Exam) 25%

G. Ethical Statement on Generative Artificial Intelligence: Prohibition on Use.
The course instructor believes that it is not appropriate to use generative AI in the learning of this course.
Students enrolled in this course should note that the use of AI models to generate assignments, reports, or
personal reflections is strictly prohibited. If such use is detected, the course instructor, the university, or the
relevant authority reserves the right to re-evaluate or not grade the assignment or report. Students who enroll
in this course are deemed to have agreed to the above Ethics Statement at the time of course selection.

docs.text: Prof. Jen-Yuan (James) Chang Telephone: +886-03-574-2498  Office: Engineering Building I – R509  Email: jychang@pme.nthu.edu.tw Page 1/2 PME 534200 Advanced Mechanical Vibrations 高等振動學 Fall Semester, 2025 Instructor: NTHU Chair Professor Jen-Yuan (James) Chang 張禎元 清華講座教授 Credits: 3 credits. Language: This course will be offered in English Class meetings: M7M8M9 Engineering Building I – R216 Office hours: Monday 18:30-19:00 PM in Prof. Chang’s office Course description: The subject area for this course is mechanical vibration, at a level appropriate for master and doctoral graduate students. Classical techniques in mechanical vibration are developed for the modeling and analysis of discrete and continuous linear dynamic systems. Continuous systems are described within the broader context of operator theory to emphasize the physical and mathematical analogies with discrete systems. Specific topics include: Discrete systems. Equations of motion for multiple degree of freedom systems through Lagrange’s method; linearization about equilibrium; symmetry and definiteness properties; free vibration; matrix eigenvalue problems; orthogonality; Rayleigh quotient; generalized coordinates; transient and forced response through modal analysis. Continuous systems. Classical rod, shaft, string, beam, membrane and plate models; Hamilton’s principle; equations of motion and boundary conditions through variational methods; essentials of functional analysis; exact solution of eigenvalue problems; Galerkin’s method; essential and suppressible boundary conditions; Kamke quotient; introduction to elastic wave propagation and vibrations of rotors. Prerequisites: PME 332000 “Mechanical Vibrations,” or its equivalent. Textbooks: L. Meirovitch, Analytical Methods in Vibrations, Macmillan Lecture notes/materials provided by Professor Chang. References: S.S. Rao, Vibration of Continuous Systems, Wiley. L.A. Pars, A Treatise on Analytical Dynamics, Oxbow. F.S. Tse, I.E. Morse, and R.T. Hinkle, Mechanical Vibrations, Prentice-Hall. D. Newland, Mechanical Vibration Analysis and Computation, Longman. Teaching Method: Classroom lectures in English with teaching materials posted in Moodle. Assessments: Homework & Labs 30% Term Project 10% Midterm Exams 30% Final Exam 30% Homework Policy: Problem sets will be assigned regularly and will usually be due one week later. Usually combination of analytical, computational, and graphical approaches will be expected in homework. Copy of homework is not allowed. However, you are allowed to discuss homework problems with one another in order to teach each other how to solve problems. You are NOT allowed to copy work from someone else OR to work step-by-step through a problem with someone else. The work you hand in with your name on it must be your attempt to work through the problem. As a general guideline, oral communication regarding the homework is allowed, whereas written communication is not allowed. Because of the fast pace of the class, please avoid handing in late homework. If homework is submitted after solution set is distributed, 50% of the grade will be taken off. Prof. Jen-Yuan (James) Chang Telephone: +886-03-574-2498  Office: Engineering Building I – R509  Email: jychang@pme.nthu.edu.tw Page 2/2 Course Outline and Reading Schedule Discrete Systems: 1. Review of Single Degree of Freedom Systems (Meirovitch, Chapter 1) a. Free vibrations b. Response through transform methods c. Frequency response function 2. Equations of Motion for Multi-Degree of Freedom Systems (Chapter 2, 3) a. Definitions and concepts b. Derivation of Lagrange’s equation c. Small oscillations around equilibrium 3. Free Vibration (Chapter 4) a. Matrix eigenvalue problems b. Properties of the eigenvalue problem c. Solution methods d. Expansion techniques e. Rayleigh’s quotient 4. Modal Analysis (Chapter 7.1-7.6 and 9.1-9.5) a. Response problems b. General solutions c. Steady State Harmonic Response d. Damped system response Mechanism of dissipation; Viscous damping; Rayleigh proportional damping; Modal damping Continuous Systems: 5. Equations of Motion for Continuous Systems (Course notes and Chapters 5, and 10.1-10.5) a. Transition from discrete system to continuous system b. Infinitesimal element approach Torsional Rod, longitudinal rod, and string models; Euler-Bernoulli, Rayleigh, and Timoshenko Models; Membranes c. Variational approach Hamilton’s principle for a conservative discrete system; Extended Hamilton’s principle; Extension to continuous systems; Applications 6. Eigenvalue Problems of Continuous Systems (Course notes and Chapter 5) a. Formulation and solution of eigenvalue problems One-dimensional, 2nd-order problems; One-dimensional, 4th order problems; Two-dimensional, 2nd-order problems; Two-dimensional, 4th-order problems. b. Structure of the eigenvalue problem Essentials of functional analysis; Properties of linear operators, symmetric, and positive- definiteness. 7. Modal Analysis (Course notes and Chapter 7.7-7.17) a. General development b. Steady state harmonic response c. Static response d. Transformations for inhomogeneous boundary conditions 8. Special topics a. Introduction to global discretization (Course notes and Chapter 6.1-6.6) b. Introduction to constrained systems (Course notes) c. Introduction to elastic wave propagation (Course notes and Chapter 8.1-8.8) d. Vibrations of rotors (Course notes)

全球製造業朝向巨量化降低單價及客製化提供差異化產品兩端發展，透過IIoT與AI以實現工業

docs.text: PME 5371 Elastic Wave Devices and Applications Instructor: Ming-Huang Li Objectives: The goal of this course is to discuss the fundamentals of elastic waves in solids and their engineering applications. This is a theoretical course focused on the development of equivalent circuit models for various elastic wave devices. The course begins with the theoretical background of ultrasonic wave propagation in solids and crystals. This is followed by an exploration of the design methodologies of RF microdevices (such as FBAR and Lamb wave resonators), as well as various micromachined ultrasonic transducers (CMUT and PMUT). The final part of the course covers circuit and subsystem design based on these devices. Students are expected to gain general knowledge of integrated ultrasonic microsystems. Commercial software tools (COMSOL Multiphysics, MATLAB, and Keysight ADS) will be used for homework assignments. Prerequisites: Mechanics of Materials, General Physics Language: This course is offered in English, but some important concepts will be repeated in Mandarin. Grading: Assignments + Experiments (35%) Final Exam (45%) Final Project Presentation and Report (20%) Textbook: No textbook. Lecture notes will be distributed weekly. Key References: 1. J. F. Rosenbaum, Bulk Acoustic Wave Theory and Devices, Artech House, 1988. 2. B. A. Auld, Acoustic Fields and Waves in Solids, vol. 1, Wiley, New York, 1973. 3. D. Royer, E. Dieulesaint, and D. P. Morgan, Elastic Waves in Solids I - Free and Guided Propagation, Springer-Verlag Berlin Heidelberg, 2000. 4. S. Senturia, Microsystem Design, Kluwer Academic Publishers, 2001. Course Outline: (1) Introduction of vibrations and waves (2) Bulk waves in solids and crystals (3) Film bulk acoustic wave resonators (FBAR) (4) Plate wave resonators (PWR) (5) RF filters and oscillators based on elastic wave devices (6) Micromachined ultrasonic transducers: CMUT and PMUT (Optional) (7) Electronic circuit design for MUTs (Optional) 生成式人工智慧倫理聲明：禁止使用 經仔細考量後，本課程授課教師認為不宜於此門課程當中使用生成式人工智慧於課堂學習當中。因本 課程的內容於生成式 AI 中尚有諸多錯誤，且容易影響學生對基礎核心知識之判讀。 根據本校公布之「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採取禁止使用，以下為相 關的監管機制。 修讀本門課程之學生應注意本門課不得繳交使用生成式人工智慧所產出的作業、報告或個人心得。若 經查核發現，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。 Ethical Statement on Generative Artificial Intelligence: Prohibition on Use After careful consideration, the course instructor believes that it is not appropriate to use generative AI in learning for this course. Students taking this course should be aware that assignments, reports, or personal reflections generated using AI models are strictly prohibited. If such use is detected, the course instructor, university, or relevant authority reserves the right to re-evaluate or not score the assignment or report. Students who enroll in this course are deemed to have agreed to the above ethical statement at the time of course selection.

docs.name: 飛秒雷射微加工導論
docs.text:
一、課程說明(Course Description)
Femtosecond laser is a type of laser that emits light in a pulsed format with
durations shorter than one picosecond. This property enables it to deliver
ultrahigh optical power to a micro- or even nanoscale region in a material,
while keeping thermal effects minimized. Consequently, efficient nonlinear
absorption of photons can occur in the exposed region of the material, causing
extremely localized and unique material modifications. Such modifications,
including ablation, densification, molecule crosslinking, and formation of
self-organized patterns, have found promising applications in microfabrication
for manufacturing useful structures and devices that are otherwise challenging
to realize. Consequently, femtosecond laser has become a highly relevant tool
for various application fields such as electronics, integrated photonics, micro-
optics, MEMS, microfluidics, and life science.

This course aims to provide students with (1) basic knowledge of the
fundamentals of femtosecond lasers and the interactions between femtosecond
laser pulses and different materials, (2) a comprehensive understanding of
femtosecond laser microfabrication techniques, and (3) an overview of
established and potential applications of those techniques in different fields
of research and industry. Upon completing this course, students are expected to
(1) have a clear idea of the unique and various capabilities of a femtosecond
laser as a tool for microfabrication, (2) be capable of identifying
opportunities that femtosecond laser microfabrication can be applied to solving
engineering challenges or facilitating scientific investigations in their own
research field, and (3) be able to suggest a project to evaluate and develop
such opportunities with the consideration of experiment design, material/device
characterization, limitations, and alternative techniques.

二、指定用書及參考書籍(Text Books and References)
1. Steen, William M. & Mazumder, Jyotirmoy., Laser Material Processing, 4th ed.
2010. ed. (London: Springer London, 2010).
2. Osellame, Roberto, Cerullo, Giulio & Ramponi, Roberta, Femtosecond Laser
Micromachining: Photonic and Microfluidic Devices in Transparent Materials, 1.
Aufl. ed. (Berlin, Heidelberg: Springer Nature, 2012).
3. Baldacchini, Tommaso, Three-dimensional microfabrication using two-photon
polymerization, Second edition. ed. (Oxford, England ; William Andrew, 2020).
4. Selected journal publications

三、教學方式(Teaching Method)
Lecture, in-class discussion, course project

四、教學進度(Syllabus)
1. Introduction to microfabrication
2. Basic principles of continuous-wave lasers and pulsed lasers
3. Laser-material interactions
4. Precise micromachining of opaque materials
●Underlying mechanism
●Ablation
●Applications
5. Additive manufacturing
●Multiphoton lithography
●Patterning strategy
●Material design
●Laser-induced forward transfer
●Applications
6. Controlled modification of transparent materials
●Femtosecond laser-assisted etching
●Refractive index changing
●Formation of self-organized structures
●Applications
7. Summary & outlook

五、成績考核(Evaluation)
Class attendance & involvement: 15%, Assignments: 40%,
Final report: 30%, Final presentation: 15%
